items.en: They housed eight adult rats with two types of robotic rat—one social and one asocial—for four days.The robot rats were quite minimalist, resembling a chunkier version of a computer mouse with wheels to move around and colourful markings.
items.zh: 他们在四天内将八只成年老鼠与两种机器人老鼠一起饲养，一种是具有社会性的，另一种是缺乏社会性的。这些机器人老鼠设计非常简约，类似于一个更粗壮的电脑鼠标，配有轮子以便移动，还有色彩鲜艳的标记。

items.en: During the experiment, the social robot rat followed the living rats around, played with the same toys, and opened cage doors to let trapped rats escape.
items.zh: 在实验过程中，具有社会性的机器人老鼠会跟随活老鼠四处走动，玩相同的玩具，并打开笼门让被困的老鼠逃脱。

items.en: Meanwhile, the asocial robot simply moved forwards and backwards and side to side.
items.zh: 与此同时，缺乏社会性的机器人老鼠只是来回移动和左右摆动。

items.en: Next, the researchers trapped the robots in cages and gave the rats the opportunity to release them by pressing a lever.Across 18 trials each, the living rats were 52 per cent more likely on average to set the social robot free than the asocial one.
items.zh: 接下来，研究人员将机器人老鼠关进笼子，并给活老鼠一个机会，通过按下杠杆来释放它们。在每组18次试验中，活老鼠平均有52%更高的可能性释放具有社会性的机器人老鼠，而不是缺乏社会性的那一个。

items.en: This suggests that the rats perceived the social robot as a genuine social being, says Quinn.
items.zh: 昆恩表示，这表明老鼠将具有社会性的机器人老鼠视为真正的社会存在。

items.en: The rats may have bonded more with the social robot because it displayed behaviors like communal exploring and playing.
items.zh: 这些老鼠可能更倾向于与社交机器人建立联系，因为它表现出了一些类似群体探索和玩耍的行为。

items.en: This could lead to the rats better remembering having freed it earlier, and wanting the robot to return the favour when they get trapped, she says.
items.zh: 她说，这可能导致老鼠更好地记住之前曾释放过这个机器人，并在自己被困时希望机器人回报它们的恩情。

items.en: Rats have been shown to engage in multiple forms of reciprocal help and cooperation, including what is referred to as direct reciprocity where a rat will help another rat that has previously helped them,” says Quinn.
items.zh: Quinn说：'研究表明，老鼠会参与多种形式的互惠帮助与合作，包括所谓的直接互惠，即一只老鼠会帮助之前帮助过自己的另一只老鼠。'

items.en: The readiness of the rats to befriend the social robot was surprising given its minimal design.The robot was the same size as a regular rat but resembled a simple plastic box on wheels.
items.zh: 考虑到这个社交机器人的设计非常简单，老鼠竟然愿意与它交朋友，这一点令人惊讶。这个机器人和普通老鼠一样大小，但看起来就像一个装有轮子的简单塑料盒子。

items.en: We’d assumed we’d have to give it a moving head and tail, facial features, and put a scent on it to make it smell like a real rat, but that wasn’t necessary,”says Janet Wiles at the University of Queensland in Australia, who helped with the research.
items.zh: 澳大利亚昆士兰大学的Janet Wiles表示：'我们原本以为必须给它装上可动的头部和尾巴、面部特征，并让它散发出类似真实老鼠的气味，才能让它看起来更像一只老鼠，但事实证明这并不必要。' 她参与了这项研究。

items.en: The finding shows how sensitive rats are to social cues, even when they come from basic robots. says Wiles.
items.zh: Wiles说，这一发现表明，即使社交信号来自基础的机器人，老鼠对社交线索也非常敏感。

items.en: Similarly, children tend to treat robots as if they are fellow beings, even when they display only simple social signals.
items.zh: 同样地，孩子们往往会把机器人当作同类来对待，即使它们只表现出简单的社交信号。

items.en: We humans seem to be fascinated by robots, and it turns out other animals are too,” says Wiles.
items.zh: Wiles说：'人类似乎对机器人着迷，结果发现其他动物也是如此。'

items.en: It is true that CEO pay has gone up—top ones may make 300 times the pay of typical workers on average, and since the mid-1970s, CEO pay for large publicly traded American corporations has, by varying estimates, gone up by about 500%.
items.zh: 的确，CEO的薪酬已经上涨了——顶尖的CEO平均薪酬可能是普通工人的300倍，而且自20世纪70年代中期以来，美国大型上市公司CEO的薪酬，根据不同的估算，已经上涨了大约500%。

items.en: The typical CEO of a top American corporation now makes about $18.9 million a year.
items.zh: 如今，美国顶尖公司的CEO年薪约为1890万美元。

items.en: The best model for understanding the growth of CEO pay is that of limited CEO talent in a world where business opportunities for the top firms are growing rapidly.
items.zh: 理解CEO薪酬增长的最佳模型是：在一个顶级企业商业机会迅速增长的世界里，CEO人才却十分有限。

items.en: The efforts of America’ s highest-earning 1% have been one of the more dynamic elements of the global economy.
items.zh: 美国收入最高的1%人群的努力已成为全球经济中更具活力的要素之一。

items.en: It’s not popular to say. but one reason their pay has gone up so much is that CEOs really have upped their game relative to many other workers in the u.s. economy.
items.zh: 说这话并不受欢迎，但CEO薪酬大幅上涨的一个原因在于，与美国经济中许多其他工人相比，CEO们的确提升了他们的能力。

items.en: Today’ s CEO, at least for major American firms, must have many mere skills than simply being able to “run the company.” CEOs must have a good sense of financial markets and maybe even how the company should trade in them.They also need better public relations skills than their predecessors, as the costs of even a minor slipup can be significant.
items.zh: 如今的CEO，至少对于美国大型公司而言，需要具备比仅仅‘经营公司’更多的技能。他们必须具备良好的金融市场感知能力，甚至可能还需要了解公司应该如何在这些市场中进行交易。此外，他们还需要比前任更强的公关能力，因为即使是轻微的失误，其代价也可能非常巨大。

items.en: Then there’s the fact that large American companies are much more globalized than ever before, with supply chains spread across a larger number of countries.
items.zh: 此外，美国大型公司如今比以往任何时候都更加全球化，其供应链也遍布更多的国家。

items.en: To lead in that system requires knowledge that is fairly mind-boggling.
items.zh: 要在这样的体系中领导企业，需要具备相当令人难以置信的知识。

items.en: Plus, virtually all major American companies are becoming tech companies, one way or another.
items.zh: 此外，几乎所有大型美国公司都正在以这样或那样的方式转变为科技公司。

items.en: Beyond this, major CEOs still have to do all the day-to-day work they have always done.
items.zh: 除此之外，主要的首席执行官们仍然必须完成他们一直以来所做的日常事务性工作。

items.en: The common idea that high CEO pay is mainly about ripping people off doesn’t explain history very well.
items.zh: 普遍认为高额的首席执行官薪酬主要是剥削他人，这一观点并不能很好地解释历史情况。

items.en: By most measures, corporate governance has become a lot tighter and more rigorous since the 1970s.
items.zh: 从大多数指标来看，自20世纪70年代以来，公司治理已经变得严格得多，也更加严谨了。

items.en: Yet it is principally during this period of stronger governance that CEO pay has been high and rising.That suggests it is in the broader corporate interest to recruit top candidates for increasingly tough jobs.
items.zh: 然而，正是在公司治理更为严格的这一时期，首席执行官的薪酬才变得较高并持续上涨。这表明，从更广泛的企业利益来看，公司需要为日益艰难的工作招募顶尖人才。

items.en: Furthermore, the highest CEO salaries are paid to outside candidates, not to the cozy insider picks, another sign that high CEO pay is not some kind of depredation at the expense of the rest of the company.
items.zh: 此外，最高的首席执行官薪酬是给予外部候选人，而不是给予那些关系密切的内部挑选的人，这又是一个迹象，表明高额的首席执行官薪酬并非是以牺牲公司其他部分的利益为代价的掠夺行为。

items.en: And the stock market reacts positively when companies tie CEO pay to, say, stock prices, a sign that those practices build up corporate value not just for the CEO.
items.zh: 当公司把首席执行官的薪酬与股票价格等挂钩时，股市会作出积极反应，这表明这些做法不仅提升了首席执行官的个人利益，也增加了企业的价值。

items.en: Madrid was hailed as a public health beacon last November when it rolled out ambitious restrictions on the most polluting cars.
items.zh: 去年11月，当马德里推出针对污染最严重的汽车的严厉限制措施时，曾被誉为公共卫生领域的灯塔。

items.en: Seven months and one election day later, a new conservative city council suspended enforcement of the clean air zone, a first step toward its possible demise.
items.zh: 七个月加一天选举日后，一个新的保守派市议会暂停了清洁空气区的执行，这是该区域可能被废除的第一步。

items.en: Mayor José Luis Martinez-Almeida made opposition to the zone a centrepiece of his election campaign, despite its success in improving air quality.
items.zh: 何塞·路易斯·马丁内斯-阿尔梅达市长将反对该区域作为其选举活动的核心内容，尽管该区域在改善空气质量方面取得了成功。

items.en: A judge has now overruled the city’s decision to stop levying fines, ordering them reinstated.
items.zh: 但现在一位法官推翻了该市停止征收罚款的决定，下令恢复罚款。

items.en: But with legal battles ahead, the zone’s future looks uncertain at best.
items.zh: 然而，随着法律斗争的展开，该区域的未来至少看起来是不确定的。

items.en: Among other weaknesses, the measures cities must employ when left to tackle dirty air on their own are politically contentious, and therefore vulnerable.
items.zh: 除了其他弱点外，当城市被迫独自应对空气污染时所采取的措施在政治上存在争议，因此容易受到攻击。

items.en: That’s because they inevitably put the costs of cleaning the air on to individual drivers—who must pay fees or buy better vehicles—rather than on to the car manufacturers whose cheating is the real cause of our toxic pollution.
items.zh: 这是因为这些措施不可避免地将治理空气污染的成本转嫁给个人司机——他们必须支付费用或购买更好的车辆——而不是转嫁给那些因作弊而真正导致我们有毒污染的汽车制造商。

items.en: It’s not hard to imagine a similar reversal happening in London.
items.zh: 很难想象伦敦也会发生类似的逆转。

items.en: The new ultra-low emission zone (Ulez) is likely to be a big issue in next year's mayoral election.
items.zh: 新的超低排放区（Ulez）很可能成为明年市长选举中的一个重大议题。

items.en: And if Sadiq khan wins and extends it to the North and South Circular roads in 2021 as he intends, it is sure to spark intense opposition from the far larger number of motorists who will then be affected.
items.zh: 如果萨迪克·汗获胜，并如他所计划的在2021年将该措施扩展到北环路和南环路，那么势必会引发大量受到影响的司机的强烈反对。

items.en: It's not that measures such as London’s Ulez are useless.
items.zh: 并不是说像伦敦的超低排放区（Ulez）这样的措施毫无作用。

items.en: Local officials are using the levers that are available to them to safeguard residents’ health in the face of a serious threat.
items.zh: 地方官员正在利用他们现有的手段，在面对严重威胁时努力保障居民的健康。

items.en: The zones do deliver some improvements to air quality, and the science tells us that means real health benefits—fewer heart attacks, strokes and premature births, less cancer, dementia and asthma.
items.zh: 这些区域确实带来了一些空气质量的改善，而科学告诉我们，这意味着真正的健康益处——减少心脏病发作、中风和早产，降低癌症、痴呆和哮喘的发生率。

items.en: Fewer untimely deaths.
items.zh: 减少意外死亡的数量。

items.en: But mayors and councilors can only do so much about a problem that is far bigger than any one city or town.
items.zh: 但市长和市议员们对于一个远比任何一座城市或城镇更为庞大的问题，也只能做这么多。

items.en: They are acting because national governments—Britain’s and others across Europe—have failed to do so.
items.zh: 他们之所以采取行动，是因为国家政府——英国的以及欧洲其他国家的——未能履行这一职责。

items.en: Restrictions that keep highly polluting cars out of certain areas—city centres, “school streets”, even individual roads—are a response to the absence of a larger effort to properly enforce existing regulations and require auto companies to bring their vehicles into compliance.
items.zh: 限制高污染车辆进入某些区域——市中心、‘学校街道’，甚至个别道路——是对国家层面未能有效执行现有法规、并要求汽车公司使其车辆符合标准这一更大努力的缺失所作出的回应。

items.en: Wales has introduced special low speed limits to minimise pollution.
items.zh: 威尔士已经引入了特殊的低速限制，以最大限度地减少污染。

items.en: We’re doing everything but insist that manufacturers clean up their cars.
items.zh: 我们正在做一切努力，但坚持要求汽车制造商清理他们的车辆。

items.en: Now that members of Generation Z are graduating college this spring—the most commonly-accepted definition says this generation was born after 1995, give or take a year—the attention has been rising steadily in recent weeks.
items.zh: 如今，Z世代的成员正在今年春天毕业，这是最普遍接受的定义：该世代出生于1995年后，上下一年左右——最近几周，对此的关注度稳步上升。

items.en: Gen Zs are about to hit the streets looking for work in a labor market that’s tighter than it's been in decades.
items.zh: Z世代即将进入劳动力市场寻找工作，而目前的劳动力市场比几十年来都要紧张。

items.en: And employers are planning on hiring about 17 percent more new graduates for jobs in the u.s. this year than last, according to a survey conducted by the National Association of Colleges and Employers.
items.zh: 根据美国大学与雇主协会进行的一项调查，今年美国雇主计划聘用的新毕业生人数将比去年增加约17%。

items.en: Everybody wants to know how the people who will soon inhabit those empty office cubicles will differ from those who came before them.
items.zh: 每个人都想知道，即将占据那些空置办公隔间的人，与他们之前的世代会有什么不同。

items.en: If “entitled” is the most common adjective, fairly or not, applied to millennials (those born between 1981 and 1995), the catchwords for Generation Z are practical and cautious.
items.zh: 如果说‘自以为是’是最常被用来形容千禧一代（1981年至1995年间出生的人）的形容词，无论公平与否，那么Z世代的关键词则是实际和谨慎。

items.en: According to the career counselors and experts who study them, Generation Zs are clear-eyed, economic pragmatists.
items.zh: 据研究他们的职业顾问和专家所说，Z世代的人目光敏锐，是经济实用主义者。

items.en: That’s a big change from the previous generation.
items.zh: 这与上一代人相比发生了巨大的变化。

items.en: Millennials wanted more flexibility in their lives,” notes Tanya Michelsen, Associate Director of YouthSight, a UK-based brand manager that conducts regular 60-day surveys of British youth, in findings that might just as well apply to American youth.
items.zh: 英国品牌管理公司YouthSight的助理总监Tanya Michelsen指出，千禧一代希望在生活中拥有更多的灵活性，该公司定期对英国青年进行60天的调查，其调查结果同样适用于美国青年。

items.en: Generation Zs are looking for more certainty and stability, because of the rise of the gig economy.
items.zh: Z世代由于零工经济的兴起，正在寻求更多的确定性和稳定性。

items.en: They have troubles seeing a financial future and they are quite risk averse.
items.zh: 他们难以看到自己未来的财务前景，并且对风险相当厌恶。

items.en: How can the train operators possibly justify yet another increase to rail passenger fares?
items.zh: 铁路运营商怎么可能再次合理化提高铁路乘客票价呢？

items.en: It has become a grimly reliable annual ritual: every January the cost of travelling by train rises, imposing a significant extra burden on those who have no option but to use the rail network to get to work or otherwise.
items.zh: 这已成为一种令人沮丧但每年都会发生的惯例：每年一月，火车出行的成本都会上涨，给那些别无选择只能依靠铁路网络通勤或出行的人带来显著的额外负担。

items.en: This year's rise, an average of 2.7 per cent, may be a fraction lower than last year's, but it is still well above the official Consumer Price Index (CPI) measure of inflation.
items.zh: 今年的涨幅平均为2.7%，虽然比去年略低一些，但仍远高于官方消费者价格指数（CPI）衡量的通货膨胀率。

items.en: Successive governments have permitted such increases on the grounds that the cost of investing in and running the rail network should be borne by those who use it, rather than the general taxpayer.
items.zh: 历届政府都允许此类涨价，理由是铁路网络的投资和运营成本应由使用者承担，而不是由全体纳税人承担。

items.en: Despite graduating into the best economy in the past 50 years, Gen Zs know what an economic train wreck looks like.
items.zh: 尽管进入了过去50年中最繁荣的经济环境，Z世代的人却知道经济崩溃是什么样子的。

items.en: They were impressionable kids during the crash of 2008, when many of their parents lost their jobs or their life savings or both.
items.zh: 他们在2008年经济危机期间还是容易受影响的孩子，当时许多父母失去了工作或耗尽了积蓄，甚至两者皆有。

items.en: They aren't interested in taking any chances.
items.zh: 他们对冒险不感兴趣。

items.en: The booming economy seems to have done little to assuage this underlying generational sense of anxious urgency, especially for those who have college debt.
items.zh: 繁荣的经济似乎并未缓解这一代人根深蒂固的焦虑和紧迫感，尤其是对于那些有大学债务的人来说更是如此。

items.en: College loan balances in the u.s. now stand at a record $1.5 trillion, according to the Federal Reserve.
items.zh: 根据美联储的数据，目前美国的大学贷款余额已达到创纪录的1.5万亿美元。

items.en: One survey from Accenture found that 88 percent of graduating seniors this year chose their major with a job in mind.
items.zh: 一项来自埃森哲的调查显示，今年88%的应届毕业生在选择专业时都考虑到了就业前景。

items.en: In a 2019 survey of University of Georgia students, meanwhile, the career office found the most desirable trait in a future employer was the ability to offer secure employment (followed by professional development and training, and then inspiring purpose).
items.zh: 与此同时，一项对佐治亚大学学生的2019年调查显示，职业办公室发现，未来雇主最受青睐的特质是能提供稳定的工作（其次是职业发展和培训，然后是能激发使命感）。

items.en: Job security or stability was the second most important career goal(work-life balance was number one), followed by a sense of being dedicated to a cause or to feel good about serving the greater good.
items.zh: 工作稳定或保障是第二重要的职业目标（工作与生活平衡是第一位），其次是能够为某种事业奉献或为服务更大的社会目标而感到自豪。

items.en: Why, the argument goes, should a car-driving pensioner from Lincolnshire have to subsidise the daily commute of a stockbroker from Surrey?
items.zh: 为什么，论据如此，林肯郡的一位开车领取养老金的老人却要补贴萨里郡一位股票经纪人的日常通勤费用呢？

items.en: Equally, there is a sense that the travails of commuters in the South East, many of whom will face among the biggest rises, have received too much attention compared to those who must endure the relatively poor infrastructure of the Midlands and the North.
items.zh: 同样地，人们有一种感觉，即东南部通勤者的困境，其中许多人将面临最大的票价上涨，相比那些不得不忍受中 Midlands 和北方相对落后基础设施的通勤者，受到了过多的关注。

items.en: However, over the past 12 months, those commuters have also experienced some of the worst rail strikes in years.
items.zh: 然而，在过去12个月里，这些通勤者也经历了数年来最严重的铁路罢工。

items.en: It is all very well train operators trumpeting the improvements they are making to the network, but passengers should be able to expect a basic level of service for the substantial sums they are now paying to travel.
items.zh: 尽管铁路运营商大肆宣传他们对网络进行的改进，但乘客理应能期望在如今支付的高额费用下获得基本的服务水平。

items.en: The responsibility for the latest wave of strikes rests on the unions.
items.zh: 最新一轮罢工的责任应归咎于工会。

items.en: However, there is a strong case that those who have been worst affected by industrial action should receive compensation for the disruption they have suffered.
items.zh: 然而，有一个强有力的论点认为，那些受工业行动影响最严重的乘客，应因其所遭受的干扰而获得补偿。

items.en: The Government has pledged to change the law to introduce a minimum service requirement so that, even when strikes occur, services can continue to operate.
items.zh: 政府已承诺修改法律，引入最低服务要求，以确保即使发生罢工，服务仍能继续运营。

items.en: This should form part of a wider package of measures to address the long-running problems on Britain's railways.
items.zh: 这应成为一套更广泛措施的一部分，以解决英国铁路长期存在的问题。

items.en: Yes, more investment is needed, but passengers will not be willing to pay more indefinitely if they must also endure cramped, unreliable services, punctuated by regular chaos when timetables are changed, or planned maintenance is managed incompetently.
items.zh: 是的，需要更多的投资，但如果乘客还必须忍受拥挤、不可靠的服务，以及在时刻表变更或计划中的维护管理不善时频繁出现的混乱，他们也不会无限期地愿意支付更多费用。

items.en: The threat of nationalisation may have been seen off for now, but it will return with a vengeance if the justified anger of passengers is not addressed in short order.
items.zh: 国有化的威胁虽然目前已被遏制，但如果不能迅速解决乘客合理的愤怒情绪，它将以更猛烈的方式卷土重来。

items.en: Last year marked the third year in a row of when Indonesia's bleak rate of deforestation has slowed in pace.
items.zh: 去年标志着印度尼西亚森林砍伐率连续第三年放缓。

items.en: One reason for the turnaround may be the country's antipoverty program.
items.zh: 这一转变的一个原因可能是该国的扶贫计划。

items.en: In 2007, Indonesia started phasing in a program that gives money to its poorest residents under certain conditions, such as requiring people to keep kids in school or get regular medical care.
items.zh: 2007年，印度尼西亚开始逐步实施一项计划，在一定条件下向最贫困的居民提供资金，例如要求人们让儿童继续上学或定期接受医疗服务。

items.en: Called conditional cash transfers or CCTs, these social assistance programs are designed to reduce inequality and break the cycle of poverty.
items.zh: 这些被称为有条件现金转移（CCTs）的社会援助计划旨在减少不平等并打破贫困的循环。

items.en: They're already used in dozens of countries worldwide.
items.zh: 目前，这些计划已在全球数十个国家得到应用。

items.en: In Indonesia, the program has provided enough food and medicine to substantially reduce severe growth problems among children.
items.zh: 在印度尼西亚，该计划已提供了足够的食物和药品，显著减少了儿童严重的生长问题。

items.en: But CCT programs don't generally consider effects on the environment.
items.zh: 但CCT项目通常不会考虑对环境的影响。

items.en: In fact, poverty alleviation and environmental protection are often viewed as conflicting goals, says Paul Ferraro, an economist at Johns Hopkins University.
items.zh: 约翰霍普金斯大学的经济学家保罗·费拉罗表示，实际上，扶贫与环境保护往往被视为相互冲突的目标。

items.en: That's because economic growth can be correlated with environmental degradation, while protecting the environment is sometimes correlated with greater poverty.
items.zh: 这是因为经济增长可能与环境退化相关，而保护环境有时又与更大的贫困相关。

items.en: However, those correlations don't prove cause and effect.
items.zh: 然而，这些相关性并不能证明因果关系。

items.en: The only previous study analyzing causality, based on an area in Mexico that had instituted CCTs, supported the traditional view.
items.zh: 唯一一项此前分析因果关系的研究，基于墨西哥一个实施了CCT项目的地区，支持了传统观点。

items.en: There, as people got more money, some of them may have more cleared land for cattle to raise for meat, Ferraro says.
items.zh: 费拉罗说，在那里，随着人们获得更多金钱，其中一些人可能清理了更多土地来饲养牲畜以生产肉类。

items.en: Such programs do not have to negatively affect the environment, though.
items.zh: 然而，这类项目并不一定对环境产生负面影响。

items.en: Ferraro wanted to see if Indonesia's poverty-alleviation program was affecting deforestation.
items.zh: 费拉罗想看看印尼的扶贫项目是否正在影响森林砍伐。

items.en: Indonesia has the third-largest area of tropical forest in the world and one of the highest deforestation rates.
items.zh: 印度尼西亚拥有世界第三大的热带雨林面积，同时也是森林砍伐率最高的国家之一。

items.en: Ferraro analyzed satellite data showing annual forest loss from 2008 to 2012 — including during Indonesia's phase-in of the antipoverty program — in 7,468 forested villages across 15 provinces.
items.zh: 费拉罗分析了2008年至2012年期间的卫星数据——包括印度尼西亚实施扶贫计划的过渡阶段——覆盖了15个省份的7,468个有森林的村庄，显示了每年的森林损失情况。

items.en: We see that the program is associated with a 30 percent reduction in deforestation," Ferraro says.
items.zh: 费拉罗说：‘我们看到该计划与森林砍伐率下降30%相关。’

items.en: That's likely because the rural poor are using the money as makeshift insurance policies against inclement weather, Ferraro says.
items.zh: 费拉罗表示，这可能是因为农村贫困人口将这笔钱用作应对恶劣天气的临时保险。

items.en: Typically, if rains are delayed, people may clear land to plant more rice to supplement their harvests.
items.zh: 通常情况下，如果降雨延迟，人们可能会清理土地以种植更多的水稻，来补充他们的收成。

items.en: Whether this research translates elsewhere is anybody's guess.
items.zh: 这项研究是否适用于其他地区，目前尚无定论。

items.en: Ferraro suggests the results may transfer to other parts of Asia, due to commonalities such as the importance of growing rice and market access.
items.zh: 费拉罗认为，由于诸如水稻种植的重要性以及市场准入等共同因素，研究结果可能适用于亚洲其他地区。

items.en: And regardless of transferability, the study shows that what's good for people may also be good for the environment.
items.zh: 无论该研究结果是否具有可移植性，这项研究都表明，对人有益的事情可能也对环境有益。

items.en: Even if this program didn't reduce poverty, Ferraro says, "the value of the avoided deforestation just for carbon dioxide emissions alone is more than the program costs.
items.zh: 即使这个项目没有减少贫困，费拉罗说，"仅就二氧化碳排放量而言，避免森林砍伐的价值就超过了该项目的成本。"

items.en: As a historian who's always searching for the text or the image that makes us re-evaluate the past, I've become preoccupied with looking for photographs that show our Victorian ancestors smiling (what better way to shatter the image of 19th-century prudery?).
items.zh: 作为一名总是寻找能让我们重新审视过去的文本或图像的历史学家，我开始着迷于寻找那些展示我们维多利亚时代祖先微笑的照片（还有什么比这更能打破19世纪保守刻板的印象呢？）。

items.en: I've found quite a few, and — since I started posting them on Twitter — they have been causing quite a stir.
items.zh: 我已经找到了不少这样的照片，而且——自从我开始在推特上发布它们以来——这些照片引起了相当大的轰动。

items.en: People have been surprised to see evidence that Victorians had fun and could, and did, laugh.
items.zh: 人们看到维多利亚时代的人们也有乐趣，并且能够、也确实会笑，感到很惊讶。

items.en: They are noting that the Victorians suddenly seem to become more human as the hundred-or-so years that separate us fade away through our common experience of laughter.
items.zh: 他们指出，随着将我们与维多利亚时代相隔的百余年逐渐消逝，通过共同的笑声体验，维多利亚时代的人们突然显得更加人性化。

items.en: Of course, I need to concede that my collection of 'Smiling Victorians' makes up only a tiny percentage of the vast catalogue of photographic portraiture created between 1840 and 1900, the majority of which show sitters posing miserably and stiffly in front of painted backdrops, or staring absently into the middle distance.
items.zh: 当然，我必须承认，我收集的‘微笑的维多利亚人’只占1840年至1900年间创作的大量摄影作品中的一小部分，大多数照片中的人物则是在画布背景前痛苦而僵硬地摆姿势，或者茫然地盯着远处。

items.en: How do we explain this trend?
items.zh: 我们如何解释这一趋势？

items.en: During the 1840s and 1850s, in the early days of photography, exposure times were notoriously long: the daguerreotype photographic method (producing an image on a silvered copper plate) could take several minutes to complete, resulting in blurred images as sitters shifted position or adjusted their limbs.
items.zh: 在1840年代和1850年代，摄影的早期阶段，曝光时间非常长：达盖尔银版摄影法（在镀银铜板上成像）可能需要几分钟才能完成，导致人物在移动或调整姿势时产生模糊的图像。

items.en: From the early days of broadband, advocates for consumers and web-based companies worried that the cable and phone companies selling broadband connections had the power and incentive to favor affiliated websites over their rivals'.
items.zh: 从宽带网络发展的早期阶段开始，消费者和基于网络的公司的支持者就担心，提供宽带连接的有线和电话公司拥有偏袒关联网站而损害竞争对手的权力和动机。

items.en: That's why there has been such a strong demand for rules that would prevent broadband providers from picking winners and losers online, preserving the freedom and innovation that have been the lifeblood of the Internet.
items.zh: 这就是为什么一直存在如此强烈的要求，希望制定规则来防止宽带提供商在网上挑选赢家和输家，从而保护互联网赖以生存的自由和创新。

items.en: Yet that demand has been almost impossible to fill — in part because of pushback from broadband providers, anti-regulatory conservatives and the courts.
items.zh: 然而，这一需求几乎无法实现——部分原因是宽带提供商、反监管的保守派和法院的抵制。

items.en: A federal appeals court weighed in again Tuesday, but instead of providing a badly needed resolution, it only prolonged the fight.
items.zh: 周二，一家联邦上诉法院再次介入此案，但与其提供急需的解决方案，不如说它只是延长了这场斗争。

items.en: At issue before the u.s. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit was the latest take of the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) on net neutrality, adopted on a party-line vote in 2017.
items.zh: 美国哥伦比亚特区上诉法院面前的问题，是联邦通信委员会（FCC）于2017年以党派路线投票通过的最新关于网络中立性的立场。

items.en: The Republican-penned order not only eliminated the strict net neutrality rules the FCC had adopted when it had a Democratic majority in 2015, but rejected the commission's authority to require broadband providers to do much of anything.
items.zh: 这份由共和党起草的命令不仅废除了FCC在2015年拥有民主党多数席位时所采纳的严格网络中立规则，还否定了该委员会要求宽带提供商做很多事情的权力。

items.en: The order also declared that state and local governments couldn't regulate broadband providers either.
items.zh: 该命令还宣称州和地方政府也不能监管宽带提供商。

items.en: The commission argued that other agencies would protect against anti-competitive behavior, such as a broadband-providing conglomerate like AT&T favoring its own video-streaming service at the expense of Netflix and Apple TV.
items.zh: 委员会辩称，其他机构将负责防止反竞争行为，例如像AT&T这样的宽带提供商 conglomerate 偏袒其自身的视频流媒体服务，而损害Netflix和Apple TV等竞争对手。

items.en: The thought of holding a fixed grin as the camera performed its magical duties was too much to contemplate, and so a non-committal blank stare became the norm.
items.zh: 想到在相机完成其神奇任务时必须保持固定的笑容，这让人难以想象，因此不置可否的空白眼神成了常态。

items.en: But exposure times were much quicker by the 1880s, and the introduction of the Box Brownie and other portable cameras meant that, though slow by today's digital standards, the exposure was almost instantaneous.
items.zh: 但到了1880年代，曝光时间已经大大缩短，而盒式布朗尼相机和其他便携式相机的出现意味着，尽管与今天的数码标准相比仍然缓慢，但曝光几乎可以瞬间完成。

items.en: Spontaneous smiles were relatively easy to capture by the 1890s, so we must look elsewhere for an explanation of why Victorians still hesitated to smile.
items.zh: 到了1890年代，捕捉自发的笑容已经相对容易，因此我们必须从其他方面寻找解释，说明维多利亚时代的人为何仍然犹豫于露出笑容。

items.en: One explanation might be the loss of dignity displayed through a cheesy grin.
items.zh: 一个可能的解释是，露出傻笑会显得失去尊严。

items.en: Nature gave us lips to conceal our teeth," ran one popular Victorian maxim, alluding to the fact that before the birth of proper dentistry, mouths were often in a shocking state of hygiene.
items.zh: 有一句流行的维多利亚时代的格言说："大自然赋予我们嘴唇，是为了遮掩牙齿，" 这句话暗示了在正规牙科诞生之前，人们的口腔卫生状况常常令人震惊。

items.en: A flashing set of healthy and clean, regular 'pearly whites' was a rare sight in Victorian society, the preserve of the super-rich (and even then, dental hygiene was not guaranteed).
items.zh: 在维多利亚时代社会中，一口洁白、干净、整齐的牙齿是罕见的景象，只有超级富有的人（即使如此，口腔卫生也并不一定有保障）才拥有。

items.en: A toothy grin (especially when there were gaps or blackened gnashers) lacked class: drunks, tramps, and music hall performers might gurn and grin with a smile as wide as Lewis Carroll's gum-exposing Cheshire Cat, but it was not a becoming look for properly bred persons.
items.zh: 露出牙齿的笑容（尤其是当有牙缝或发黑的牙齿时）显得缺乏教养：醉汉、流浪汉和音乐厅的表演者可能会像刘易斯·卡罗尔笔下露出牙龈的柴郡猫一样咧嘴大笑，但对真正有教养的人来说，这种笑容并不合适。

items.en: Even Mark Twain, a man who enjoyed a hearty laugh, said that when it came to photographic portraits there could be "nothing more damning than a silly, foolish smile fixed forever".
items.zh: 即使是喜欢开怀大笑的马克·吐温，也说过在拍摄肖像照时，"没有什么比永恒定格的傻笑和愚蠢笑容更令人不齿的了。"

items.en: Yet the FCC also ended the investigations of broadband providers that imposed data caps on their rivals' streaming services but not their own.
items.zh: 然而，FCC还结束了对那些对其竞争对手的流媒体服务实施数据上限但不对自身服务实施数据上限的宽带提供商的调查。

items.en: On Tuesday, the appeals court unanimously upheld the 2017 order deregulating broadband providers, citing a Supreme Court ruling from 2005 that upheld a similarly deregulatory move.
items.zh: 周二，上诉法院一致维持了2017年取消对宽带提供商监管的决定，并援引了2005年最高法院的一项裁决，该裁决支持了类似取消监管的举措。

items.en: But Judge Patricia Millett rightly argued in a concurring opinion that "the result is unhinged from the realities of modern broadband service," and said Congress or the Supreme Court could intervene to "avoid trapping Internet regulation in technological anachronism.
items.zh: 但帕特里夏·米勒特法官在一份附议意见中正确指出，"这一结果与现代宽带服务的现实脱节了"，并表示国会或最高法院可以介入，以"避免将互联网监管困在技术上的过时观念中"。

items.en: In the meantime, the court threw out the FCC's attempt to block all state rules on net neutrality, while preserving the commission's power to preempt individual state laws that undermine its order.
items.zh: 与此同时，法院驳回了FCC试图阻止所有州制定网络中立性规则的尝试，但保留了该委员会阻止个别州法律削弱其命令的权力。

items.en: That means more battles like the one now going on between the Justice Department and California, which enacted a tough net neutrality law in the wake of the FCC's abdication.
items.zh: 这意味着将会有更多像美国司法部与加利福尼亚州之间正在进行的那样的斗争，加州在FCC放弃监管后通过了一项严格的网络中立性法律。

items.en: The endless legal battles and back-and-forth at the FCC cry out for Congress to act.
items.zh: FCC无休止的法律斗争和反复无常的决策，迫切需要国会采取行动。

items.en: It needs to give the commission explicit authority once and for all to bar broadband providers from meddling in the traffic on their network and to create clear rules protecting openness and innovation online.
items.zh: 国会需要明确赋予该委员会一次性和最终的权力，以禁止宽带提供商干预其网络上的流量，并制定明确的规则来保护网络的开放性和创新性。

items.en: Reskilling” is something that sounds like a buzzword but is actually a requirement if we plan to have a future where a lot of would-be workers do not get left behind.
items.zh: “再培训”听起来像是一个流行术语，但如果我们要实现一个不让大量潜在工人落后的未来，它实际上是一项必要措施。

items.en: Critically, another group was asked to spend a minute writing down reasons for their judgment, before giving the rating.Accuracy dropped dramatically.
items.zh: 关键的是，另一组被要求在评分前花一分钟写下他们做出判断的原因。准确性急剧下降。

items.en: Ambady suspected that deliberation focused them on vivid but misleading cues, such as certain gestures or utterances, rather than letting the complex interplay of subtle signals form a holistic impression.She found similar interference when participants watched 15-second clips of pairs of people and judged whether they were strangers, friends, or dating partners.
items.zh: Ambady怀疑，深思熟虑使他们关注于某些生动但具有误导性的线索，比如特定的手势或言语，而不是让微妙信号的复杂互动形成整体印象。当参与者观看15秒的两人互动片段并判断他们是陌生人、朋友还是恋爱伴侣时，她发现了类似的影响。

items.en: Other research shows we’re better at detecting deception from thin slices when we rely on intuition instead of reflection.
items.zh: 其他研究表明，当我们依赖直觉而不是反思时，更能从短暂的片段中检测出欺骗行为。

items.en: It’s as if you’re driving a stick shift,” says Judith Hall, a psychologist at Northeastern University, “and if you start thinking about it too much, you can’t remember what you’re doing.
items.zh: 东北大学的心理学家Judith Hall说："这就像你在驾驶手动挡汽车，如果你过度思考，就会忘记自己在做什么。"

items.en: But if you go on automatic pilot,you’re fine.Much of our social life is like that.
items.zh: 但如果你自动驾驶，你就会没问题。我们的大部分社交生活都是这样的。

items.en: Thinking too much can also harm our ability to form preferences.College students’ ratings of strawberry jams and college courses aligned better with experts’ opinions when the students weren’t asked to analyze their rationale.And people made car-buying decisions that were both objectively better and more personally satisfying when asked to focus on their feelings rather than on details, but only if the decision was complex—when they had a lot of information to process.
items.zh: 过度思考也会损害我们形成偏好的能力。当大学生没有被要求分析他们的理由时，他们对草莓果酱和大学课程的评分更符合专家的意见。此外，当人们被要求关注自己的感受而不是细节时，他们在购买汽车时做出的决定既在客观上更好，也更符合他们个人的满意度，但这种情况只发生在决策较为复杂时——也就是他们需要处理大量信息的时候。

items.en: Intuition’s special powers are unleashed only in certain circumstances.In one study,participants completed a battery of eight tasks, including four that tapped reflective thinking (discerning rules, comprehending vocabulary) and four that tapped intuition and creativity (generating new products or figures of speech).Then they rated the degree to which they had used intuition (“gut feelings,” “ hunches,” “my heart”).Use of their gut hurt their performance on the first four tasks, as expected, and helped them on the rest.
items.zh: 直觉的特殊力量只在特定情况下被释放。在一项研究中，参与者完成了一系列八个任务，包括四个需要反思性思维的任务（识别规则、理解词汇）和四个需要直觉和创造力的任务（生成新产品或言语比喻）。然后他们评估自己在多大程度上使用了直觉（"直觉感受"、"预感"、"我的心"）。正如预期的那样，使用直觉会影响他们在前四个任务中的表现，但有助于完成其余的任务。

items.en: Sometimes the heart is smarter than the head.
items.zh: 有时候，心比头脑更聪明。

items.en: The country produces only about 60 per cent of the food it eats, down from almost three-quarters in the late 1980s.A move back to self-sufficiency ， the argument goes, would boost the farming industry, political sovereignty and even the nation’s health.Sounds great — but how feasible is this vision?
items.zh: 这个国家目前仅能生产其消耗食物的约60%，而这一比例在20世纪80年代末期还接近75%。有人认为，重新实现自给自足将有助于提升农业产业、政治主权，甚至改善国民健康。听起来不错——但这种愿景是否切实可行呢？

items.en: According to a report on UK food production from the University of Leeds,UK,
items.zh: 根据利兹大学关于英国食品生产的报告，

items.en: 85 per cent of the country’s total land area is associated with meat and dairy production.That supplies 80 per cent of what is consumed, so even covering the whole country in livestock farms wouldn’t allow us to cover all our meat and dairy needs.
items.zh: 英国约85%的国土面积与肉类和乳制品生产相关。这些产品供应了英国80%的消费量，因此即使将全国土地都用于养殖农场，也无法满足英国全部的肉类和乳制品需求。

items.en: There are many caveats to those figures,but they are still grave.To become much more self-sufficient, the UK would need to drastically reduce its consumption of animal foods, and probably also farm more intensively — meaning fewer green fields and more factory-style production.
items.zh: 尽管这些数据有许多限制因素，但它们仍然令人担忧。为了实现更高的自给自足率，英国需要大幅减少动物性食品的消费，还可能需要进行更集约化的耕作——这意味着将有更少的绿色田野，而更多地采用工厂化生产方式。

items.en: But switching to a mainly plant-based diet wouldn’t help.There is a good reason why the UK is dominated by animal husbandry: most of its terrain doesn’t have the right soil or climate to grow crops on a commercial basis.Just 25 per cent of the country’s land is suitable for crop-growing, most of which is already occupied by arable fields.Even if we converted all the suitable land to fields of fruit and veg — which would involve taking out all the nature reserves and removing thousands of people from their homes — we would achieve only a 30 per cent boost in crop production.
items.zh: 然而，转向以植物为主的饮食方式也无济于事。英国之所以以畜牧业为主，是有充分理由的：其大部分地形不具备商业种植作物所需的土壤或气候条件。只有25%的国土适合种植农作物，其中大部分已经被用于耕作。即使我们将所有适合种植的地区都改种水果和蔬菜——这将意味着要清除所有的自然保护区，并让成千上万的人离开家园——我们的农作物产量也只能提高30%。

items.en: Just 23 per cent of the fruit and vegetables consumed in the UK are currently home-grown, so even with the most extreme measures we could meet only 30 per cent of our fresh produce needs.That is before we look for the space to grow the grains, sugars, seeds and oils that provide us with the vast bulk of our current calorie intake.
items.zh: 目前英国消费的水果和蔬菜中，仅有23%是本地种植的，因此即使采取最极端的措施，我们也只能满足30%的新鲜农产品需求。这还不包括寻找种植为我们当前大部分热量摄入提供来源的谷物、糖、种子和油的空间。

items.en: When Microsoft bought task management app Wunderlist and mobile calendar Sunrise in 2015,it picked two newcomers that were attracting considerable buzz in Silicon Valley.Microsoft’s own Office dominates the market for “productivity” software, but the start-ups represented a new wave of technology designed from the ground up for the smartphone world.
items.zh: 当微软在2015年收购任务管理应用Wunderlist和移动日历应用Sunrise时，它选择了两个在硅谷引起广泛关注的新晋应用。微软自家的Office产品在‘生产力’软件市场占据主导地位，但这两家初创公司代表了专为智能手机时代设计的新一代技术。

items.en: Both apps, however, were later scrapped, after Microsoft said it had used their best features in its own products.Their teams of engineers stayed on,making them two of the many “ acqui-hires”that the biggest companies have used to feed their great hunger for tech talent.
items.zh: 然而，这两款应用后来都被微软取消了，因为微软表示已经将其最佳功能整合到自家产品中。它们的工程师团队继续留任，成为大型公司用来满足对技术人才巨大需求的众多‘收购兼并’（acqui-hires）案例之一。

items.en: We know we are moving into a period where the jobs in demand will change rapidly, as will the requirements of the jobs that remain.Research by the World Economic Forum finds that on average 42 per cent of the“core skills”within job roles will change by 2022.That is a very short timeline.
items.zh: 我们知道，我们正进入一个需求岗位将迅速变化的时期，剩余岗位的要求也将随之迅速变化。世界经济论坛的研究发现，到2022年，平均而言，工作中42%的“核心技能”将发生变化。这是一个非常短的时间框架。

items.en: The question of who should pay for reskilling is a thorny one.For individual companies, the temptation is always to let go of workers whose skills are no longer in demand and replace them with those whose skills are.That does not always happen.
items.zh: 谁应该为再培训付费这个问题是一个棘手的问题。对于个别公司来说，总是有诱惑力去解雇那些技能不再被需要的员工，并用具备所需技能的员工来替代他们。但这种情况并不总是发生。

items.en: AT&T is often given as the gold standard of a company who decided to do a massive reskilling program rather than go with a fire-and-hire strategy.Other companies including Amazon and Disney had also pledged to create their own plans.When the skills mismatch is in the broader economy though, the focus usually turns to government to handle.Efforts in Canada and elsewhere have been arguably languid at best, and have given us a situation where we frequently hear of employers begging for workers, even at times and in regions where unemployment is high.
items.zh: AT&T经常被作为公司的典范，该公司决定实施大规模的再培训计划，而不是采取裁员并雇佣新员工的策略。包括亚马逊和迪士尼在内的其他公司也承诺制定自己的计划。然而，当技能错配出现在整个经济领域时，焦点通常会转向政府来处理。加拿大及其他地方的努力可以说至多是迟缓的，这导致我们经常听到雇主在失业率高的时候和地方恳求工人。

items.en: With the pandemic, unemployment is very high indeed.
items.zh: 随着疫情的爆发，失业率确实非常高。

items.en: In February,at 3.5 per cent and 5.5 per cent respectively, unemployment rates in Canada and the United States were at generational lows and worker shortages were everywhere.As of May, those rates had spiked up to 13.3 per cent and 13.7 per cent,and although many worker shortages had disappeared, not all had done so.In the medical field, to take an obvious example, the pandemic meant that there were still clear shortages of doctors, nurses and other medical personnel.
items.zh: 2月份，加拿大和美国的失业率分别达到3.5%和5.5%，处于代际低点，而劳动力短缺现象随处可见。到了5月份，这些失业率飙升至13.3%和13.7%，尽管许多劳动力短缺现象已经消失，但并非全部如此。以显而易见的医疗领域为例，疫情意味着医生、护士和其他医疗人员仍然存在明显的短缺。

items.en: Of course, it is not like you can take an unemployed waiter and train him to be a doctor in a few weeks, no matter who pays for it.But even if you cannot close that gap, maybe you can close others, and doing so would be to the benefit of all concerned.That seems to be the case in Sweden: When forced to furlough 90 per cent of their cabin staff, Scandinavian Airlines decided to start up a short retraining program that reskilled the laid-off workers to support hospital staff.The effort was a collective one and involved other companies as well as a Swedish university.
items.zh: 当然，你不能指望在几周内将一名失业的服务员培训成医生，无论谁来支付这笔费用。但即使你无法弥补这个差距，也许可以弥补其他一些差距，而这样做对所有相关方都有好处。在瑞典似乎就是这样：当被迫解雇90%的客舱工作人员时，北欧航空决定启动一个短期的再培训计划，将被解雇的员工重新培训，以支持医院工作人员。这项努力是集体性的，还涉及其他公司以及一所瑞典大学。

items.en: With the global population predicted to hit close to 10 billion by 2050, and forecasts that agricultural production in some regions will need to nearly double to keep pace, food security is increasingly making headlines.In the UK, it has become a big talking point recently too, for a rather particular reason: Brexit.
items.zh: 随着全球人口预计到2050年将达到近100亿，以及一些地区农业产量需要几乎翻倍才能跟上步伐的预测，粮食安全问题正日益受到关注。在英国，最近也因一个特别的原因成为热议话题：脱欧。

items.en: Brexit is seen by some as an opportunity to reverse a recent trend towards the UK importing food.
items.zh: 一些人将脱欧视为一个机会，可以扭转英国近期越来越依赖进口食品的趋势。

items.en: To Microsoft’s critics,the fates of Wunderlist and Sunrise are examples of a remorseless drive by Big Tech to chew up any innovative companies that lie in their path.
items.zh: 在微软的批评者看来，Wunderlist 和 Sunrise 的命运是大科技公司无情地吞并任何挡在他们面前的创新企业的例子。

items.en: They bought the seedlings and closed them down,” complained Paul Arnold, a partner at San Francisco-based Switch Ventures, putting an end to businesses that might one day turn into competitors.Microsoft declined to comment.
items.zh: ‘他们买下这些初创公司然后关闭它们，’旧金山的 Switch Ventures 风险投资公司合伙人保罗·阿诺德抱怨道，他认为这终结了可能有一天成为竞争对手的企业。微软拒绝对此发表评论。

items.en: Like other start-up investors, mr. Arnold’s own business often depends on selling start-ups to larger tech companies, though he admits to mixed feelings about the result: “I think these things are good for me, if I put my selfish hat on.But are they good for the American economy?I don’t know.
items.zh: 和其他初创企业投资者一样，阿诺德自己的业务经常依赖于将初创公司卖给更大的科技公司，尽管他承认对此结果感到矛盾：‘如果从自私的角度来看，这些事情对我是有好处的。但它们对美国经济好吗？我不知道。’

items.en: The US Federal Trade Commission says it wants to find the answer to that question.This week, it asked the five most valuable US tech companies for information about their many small acquisitions over the past decade.Although only a research project at this stage, the request has raised the prospect of regulators wading into early-stage tech markets that until now have been beyond their reach.
items.zh: 美国联邦贸易委员会表示，它希望找到这个问题的答案。本周，它向美国五大最有价值的科技公司索取了过去十年中大量小型收购的信息。尽管目前这只是一个研究项目，但这一请求引发了监管机构可能介入此前一直无法触及的早期科技市场的前景。

items.en: Given their combined market value of more than $5.5 trillion, rifling through such small deals—many of them much less prominent than Wunderlist and Sunrise—might seem beside the point.Between them, the five biggest tech companies have spent an average of only $3.4 billion a year on sub- $ 1 billion acquisitions over the past five years—a drop in the ocean compared with their massive financial reserves, and the more than $130 billion of venture capital that was invested in the US last year.
items.zh: 考虑到这五家公司的总市值超过 5.5 万亿美元，审查这些小规模交易——其中许多都不如 Wunderlist 和 Sunrise 那样知名——似乎无关紧要。在过去五年中，这五家最大的科技公司每年平均仅花费 34 亿美元用于收购金额低于 10 亿美元的公司——与他们庞大的财务储备相比，以及去年美国投入的 1300 多亿美元风险投资相比，这简直是九牛一毛。

items.en: However, critics say the big companies use such deals to buy their most threatening potential competitors before their businesses have a chance to gain momentum, in some cases as part of a“ buy and kill”tactic to simply close them down.
items.zh: 然而，批评者认为，这些大公司利用这些交易在这些企业有机会获得发展势头之前，就买下最具威胁的潜在竞争对手，有时甚至采用‘收购并关闭’的策略，直接将它们关闭。

items.en: We’re fairly good at judging people based on first impressions, thin slices of experience ranging from a glimpse of a photo to five-minute interaction, and deliberation can be not only extraneous but intrusive.In one study of the ability she called“thin slicing,” the late psychologist Nalini Ambady asked participants to watch silent 10-second video clips of professors and to rate the instructor’s overall effectiveness.Their ratings correlated strongly with students’ end-of-semester ratings.
items.zh: 我们在根据第一印象判断他人方面相当擅长，这些印象可能来自一张照片的短暂一瞥，或五分钟的互动，而深思熟虑不仅多余，有时甚至会干扰判断。在一项她称之为‘薄切片’能力的研究中，已故心理学家纳莉妮·安巴迪让参与者观看教授的无声10秒视频片段，并对授课教师的整体效果进行评分。他们的评分与学生期末的评分高度相关。

items.en: Another set of participants had to count backward from 1,000 by nines as they watched the clips, occupying their conscious working memory.Their ratings were just as accurate, demonstrating the intuitive nature of the social processing.
items.zh: 另一组参与者在观看视频片段的同时，需要从1000开始每次减去9，占用他们的意识工作记忆。他们的评分同样准确，这表明这种社会判断是直觉性的。

items.en: People often complain that plastics are too durable.
items.zh: 人们常常抱怨塑料过于耐用。

items.en: Water bottles, shopping bags, and other trash litter the planet, from Mount Everest to the Mariana Trench, because plastics are everywhere and don't break down easily.
items.zh: 水瓶、购物袋和其他垃圾遍布全球，从珠穆朗玛峰到马里亚纳海沟，这是因为塑料无处不在且不易分解。

items.en: But some plastic materials change over time.
items.zh: 但是一些塑料材料会随着时间而发生变化。

items.en: They crack and frizzle.
items.zh: 它们会开裂和起皱。

items.en: They "weep" out additives.
items.zh: 它们会渗出添加剂。

items.en: They melt into sludge.
items.zh: 它们会融化成污泥。

items.en: All of which creates huge headaches for institutions, such as museums, trying to preserve culturally important objects.
items.zh: 所有这些现象都给试图保存具有文化重要性物品的机构（如博物馆）带来了巨大的困扰。

items.en: The variety of plastic objects at risk is dizzying: early radios, avant-garde sculptures, celluloid animation stills from Disney films, the first artificial heart.
items.zh: 面临风险的塑料制品种类繁多：早期的收音机、先锋派雕塑、迪士尼电影中使用赛璐珞制作的动画静态画面，以及第一颗人造心脏。

items.en: It's especially vulnerable to light damage, and by the mid-1990s, Gilardi's pumpkins, roses, and other figures were splitting and crumbling.
items.zh: 它尤其容易受到光照损害，到20世纪90年代中期，吉拉尔迪的南瓜、玫瑰和其他雕塑开始开裂并碎裂。

items.en: Museums locked some of them away in the dark.
items.zh: 博物馆将其中一些作品锁在黑暗中保存。

items.en: So van Oosten and her colleagues worked to preserve Gilardi's sculptures.
items.zh: 因此，范·奥斯特恩和她的同事致力于保护吉拉尔迪的雕塑。

items.en: They infused some with stabilizing and consolidating chemicals.
items.zh: 他们向其中一些雕塑注入了稳定和加固化学物质。

items.en: Van Oosten calls those chemicals "sunscreens" because their goal was to prevent further light damage and rebuild worn polymer fibers.
items.zh: 范·奥斯特恩将这些化学物质称为"防晒霜"，因为它们的目标是防止进一步的光照损害并修复磨损的聚合物纤维。

items.en: She is proud that several sculptures have even gone on display again, albeit sometimes beneath protective cases.
items.zh: 她为自己感到自豪，因为有几件雕塑甚至再次展出，尽管有时需要放在保护性展柜中。

items.en: Despite success stories like van Oosten's, preservation of plastics will likely get harder.
items.zh: 尽管有范·奥斯特恩这样的成功案例，塑料制品的保存工作可能会变得更加困难。

items.en: Old objects continue to deteriorate.
items.zh: 旧物件仍会持续劣化。

items.en: Certain artifacts are especially vulnerable because some pioneers in plastic art didn't always know how to mix ingredients properly, says Thea van Oosten, a polymer chemist who, until retiring a few years ago, worked for decades at the Cultural Heritage Agency of the Netherlands.
items.zh: 某些文物尤其脆弱，因为一些塑料艺术的先驱者并不总是懂得如何正确地混合原料，荷兰文化 heritage 机构的聚合物化学家 Thea van Oosten 说，她几年前退休前一直在该机构工作了数十年。

items.en: It's like baking a cake: If you don't have exact amounts, it goes wrong." she says.
items.zh: 这就像是在做蛋糕：如果你没有精确的分量，结果就会出错。

items.en: The object you make is already a time bomb.
items.zh: 你制作的物品本身就是一个定时炸弹。

items.en: And sometimes, it's not the artist's fault.
items.zh: 有时，问题并不在于艺术家本身。

items.en: In the 1960s, the Italian artist Piero Gilardi began to create hundreds of bright, colorful foam pieces.
items.zh: 20世纪60年代，意大利艺术家 Piero Gilardi 开始创作数百件色彩鲜艳、丰富多彩的泡沫制品。

items.en: Those pieces included small beds of roses and other items as well as a few dozen "nature carpets"—large rectangles decorated with foam pumpkins, cabbages, and watermelons.
items.zh: 这些作品包括小床玫瑰和其他物品，以及几十件被称为"自然地毯"（nature carpets）的大型矩形装饰品，上面装饰着泡沫雕刻的南瓜、卷心菜和西瓜。

items.en: He wanted viewers to walk around on the carpets—which meant they had to be durable.
items.zh: 他希望观众能在地毯上行走——这意味着地毯必须足够耐用。

items.en: Unfortunately, the polyurethane foam he used is inherently unstable.
items.zh: 不幸的是，他使用的聚氨酯泡沫本身就不稳定。

items.en: Worse, biodegradable plastics designed to disintegrate, are increasingly common.
items.zh: 更糟糕的是，那些设计用来分解的可生物降解塑料如今也越来越常见了。

items.en: And more is at stake here than individual objects.
items.zh: 在这里，所涉及的远不止是单个物品的问题。

items.en: Joana Lia Ferreira, an assistant professor of conservation and restoration at the NOVA School of Science and Technology, notes that archaeologists first defined the great material ages of human history—Stone Age, Iron Age, and so on—after examining artifacts in museums.
items.zh: 新大学科学与技术学院的文物保护与修复助理教授Joana Lia Ferreira指出，考古学家最初是在博物馆中研究文物后，才定义了人类历史上的主要材料时代——石器时代、铁器时代等等。

items.en: We now live in an age of plastic, she says, "and what we decide to collect today, what we decide to preserve... will have a strong impact on how in the future we'll be seen.
items.zh: 她说，我们现在正处于塑料时代，"今天我们决定收集什么，决定保存什么，将对未来如何看待我们产生重大影响。"

items.en: As the latest crop of students pen their undergraduate application form and weigh up their options, it may be worth considering just how the point, purpose and value of a degree has changed and what Generation Z need to consider as they start the third stage of their educational journey.
items.zh: 当最新一批学生填写他们的本科申请表并权衡选择时，或许值得考虑一下学位的要点、目的和价值究竟发生了怎样的变化，以及Z世代在开始他们教育旅程的第三阶段时需要考虑哪些因素。

items.en: Millennials were told that if you did well in school, got a decent degree, you would be set up for life.
items.zh: 千禧一代被告知，只要你在学校表现好，获得一个不错的学位，你就能为一生奠定基础。

items.en: But that promise has been found wanting.
items.zh: 但这一承诺已被证明是站不住脚的。

items.en: As degrees became universal, they became devalued.
items.zh: 随着学位变得普遍，它们的价值也逐渐降低。

items.en: Education was no longer a secure route of social mobility.
items.zh: 教育不再是一条通往社会流动的可靠途径。

items.en: Today, 28 per cent of graduates in the UK are in non-graduate roles, a percentage which is double the average among OECD countries.
items.zh: 如今，在英国，28%的毕业生从事的是非毕业生岗位，这一比例是经合组织（OECD）国家平均水平的两倍。

items.en: This is not to say that there is no point in getting a degree, but rather stress that a degree is not for everyone, that the switch from classroom to lecture hall is not an inevitable one and that other options are available.
items.zh: 这并不是说获得学位没有意义，而是强调学位并不适合每个人，从教室转向讲堂并非必然的选择，还有其他可行的选项。

items.en: Thankfully, there are signs that this is already happening, with Generation Z seeking to learn from their millennial predecessors, even if parents and teachers tend to be still set in the degree mindset.
items.zh: 幸运的是，已有迹象表明这种情况正在发生，Z世代正在努力从千禧一代前辈身上学习，尽管父母和教师们往往仍固守着学位至上的观念。

items.en: Employers have long seen the advantages of hiring school leavers who often prove themselves to be more committed and loyal employees than graduates.
items.zh: 长期以来，雇主们就看到了雇佣应届中学毕业生的优势，这些毕业生通常比毕业生表现出更高的敬业度和忠诚度。

items.en: Many too are seeing the advantages of scrapping a degree requirement for certain roles.
items.zh: 许多人也看到了取消某些职位的学位要求所带来的优势。

items.en: For those for whom a degree is the desired route, consider that this may well be the first of many.
items.zh: 对于那些将学位视为理想路径的人来说，这可能只是众多选择中的第一个。

items.en: In this age of generalists, it pays to have specific knowledge or skills.
items.zh: 在这个通才的时代，拥有特定的知识或技能是有价值的。

items.en: Postgraduates now earn 40 per cent more than graduates.
items.zh: 硕士毕业生现在的收入比本科毕业生高出40%。

items.en: When more and more of us have a degree, it makes sense to have two.
items.zh: 当越来越多人拥有学位时，拥有两个学位就变得合情合理了。

items.en: It is unlikely that Generation Z will be done with education at 18 or 21; they will need to be constantly up-skilling throughout their career to stay employable.
items.zh: Z世代在18岁或21岁完成教育的可能性不大；他们需要在整个职业生涯中不断提升技能，以保持就业竞争力。

items.en: It has been estimated that this generation, due to the pressures of technology, the wish for personal fulfilment and desire for diversity, will work for 17 different employers over the course of their working life and have five different careers.
items.zh: 据估计，由于技术压力、对个人实现的渴望以及对多样性的追求，这一代人一生中可能会为17个不同的雇主工作，并拥有五个不同的职业。

items.en: Education, and not just knowledge gained on campus, will be a core part of Generation Z's career trajectory.
items.zh: 教育，而不仅仅是校园内获得的知识，将是Z世代职业生涯的核心组成部分。

items.en: Older generations often talk about their degree in the present and personal tense: 'I am a geographer.' or 'I am a classicist.
items.zh: 年长一代通常用现在时和人称代词谈论他们的学位：'我是一名地理学家。' 或 '我是一名古典学者。'

items.en: Their sons or daughters would never say such a thing; it's as if they already know that their degree won't define them in the same way.
items.zh: 他们的子女或孩子绝不会这么说；就好像他们已经知道学位不会像以前那样定义自己。

items.en: Enlightening, challenging, stimulating, fun.
items.zh: 启人深思，富有挑战，激发灵感，充满乐趣。

items.en: These were some of the words that Nature readers used to describe their experience of art-science collaborations in a series of articles on partnerships between artists and researchers.
items.zh: 这些是《自然》读者在一系列关于艺术家与研究人员合作的文章中用来描述他们对艺术与科学合作体验的词语。

items.en: Nearly 40% of the roughly 350 people who responded to an accompanying poll said, they had collaborated with artists, and almost all said they would consider doing so in future.
items.zh: 在一项配套调查中，大约350名受访者中有近40%表示，他们曾与艺术家合作，几乎所有受访者都表示未来会考虑这样做。

items.en: Such an encouraging result is not surprising.
items.zh: 这样令人鼓舞的结果并不令人意外。

items.en: Scientists are increasingly seeking out visual artists to help them communicate their work to new audiences.
items.zh: 科学家们越来越倾向于寻求视觉艺术家的帮助，以向新的受众传达他们的研究成果。

items.en: Artists help scientists reach a broader audience and make emotional connections that enhance learning.
items.zh: 艺术家帮助科学家触及更广泛的受众，并建立能增强学习效果的情感联系。

items.en: One respondent said.
items.zh: 一位受访者表示。

items.en: One example of how artists and scientists have together rocked the scenes came last month when the Sydney Symphony Orchestra performed a reworked version of Antonio Vivaldi's The Four Seasons.
items.zh: 艺术家与科学家共同引发轰动的一个例子是上个月悉尼交响乐团演奏了安东尼奥·维瓦尔第《四季》的重新编排版本。

items.en: They reimagined the 300-year-old score by injecting the latest climate prediction data for each season—provided by Monash University's Climate Change Communication Research Hub.
items.zh: 他们通过注入每个季节最新的气候预测数据，对这部300年前的乐谱进行了重新想象，这些数据由莫纳什大学气候变迁传播研究中心提供。

items.en: The performance was a creative call to action ahead of November's United Nations Climate Change Conference in Glasgow, UK.
items.zh: 这场表演是为11月在英国格拉斯哥举行的联合国气候变化大会所做的一次创意呼吁行动。

items.en: But a genuine partnership must be a two-way street.
items.zh: 但真正的合作伙伴关系必须是双向的。

items.en: Fewer artists than scientists responded to the Nature poll; however, several respondents noted that artists do not simply assist scientists with their communication requirements.
items.zh: 回应《自然》杂志调查的艺术家人数少于科学家；然而，一些受访者指出，艺术家不仅仅是协助科学家满足他们的传播需求。

items.en: Nor should their work be considered only as an object of study.
items.zh: 他们的作品也不应仅仅被视为研究对象。

items.en: The alliances are most valuable when scientists and artists have a shared stake in a project, are able to jointly design it and can critique each other's work.
items.zh: 当科学家和艺术家在一个项目中拥有共同的利益，能够共同设计该项目，并能相互批评彼此的作品时，这种联盟最有价值。

items.en: Such an approach can both prompt new research as well as result in powerful art.
items.zh: 这种方法既能激发新的研究，也能产生震撼人心的艺术作品。

items.en: More than half a century ago, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology opened its Center for Advanced Visual Studies (CAVS) to explore the role of technology in culture.
items.zh: 半个世纪以前，麻省理工学院开设了高级视觉研究中心（CAVS），以探索技术在文化中的作用。

items.en: The founders deliberately focused their projects around light—hence the "visual studies" in the name.
items.zh: 创始人们有意将他们的项目围绕光线展开——因此名字中才有"视觉研究"一词。

items.en: Light was a something that both artists and scientists had an interest in and therefore could form the basis of collaboration.
items.zh: 光是艺术家和科学家都感兴趣的领域，因此可以成为合作的基础。

items.en: As science and technology progressed, and divided into more sub-disciplines, the centre was simultaneously looking to a time when leading researchers could also be artists, writers and poets, and vice versa.
items.zh: 随着科学和技术的进步，并进一步细分为更多的子学科，中心同时也在展望一个时代，即领先的科研人员也可以是艺术家、作家和诗人，反之亦然。

items.en: Nature's poll findings suggest that this trend is as strong as ever, but, to make a collaboration work, both sides need to invest time and embrace surprise and challenge.
items.zh: 《自然》的调查结果表明，这一趋势依然强劲，但要使合作成功，双方都需要投入时间，并接受惊喜和挑战。

items.en: The reach of art-science tie-ups needs to go beyond the necessary purpose of research communication, and participants.
items.zh: 艺术与科学的合作范围需要超越科研传播这一必要目的，以及参与者的范畴。

items.en: Artists and scientists alike are immersed in discovery and invention, and challenge and critique are core to both, too.
items.zh: 艺术家和科学家都沉浸在发现和发明之中，挑战和批评也是两者的核心要素。

items.en: The personal grievance provisions of New Zealand's Employment Relations Act 2000 (ERA) prevent an employer from firing an employee without good cause.
items.zh: 新西兰《2000年雇佣关系法》（ERA）中的个人申诉条款规定，雇主不得无正当理由解雇员工。

items.en: Instead, dismissals must be justified.
items.zh: 相反，解雇必须有正当理由。

items.en: Employers must both show cause and act in a procedurally fair way.
items.zh: 雇主必须既说明理由，又在程序上做到公平。

items.en: Personal grievance procedures were designed to guard the jobs of ordinary workers from "unjustified dismissals.
items.zh: 个人申诉程序的设立是为了保护普通工人的工作免受"不公正解雇"的影响。

items.en: The premise was that the common law of contract lacked sufficient safeguards for workers against arbitrary conduct by management.
items.zh: 其前提是，合同的普通法缺乏足够的保障措施，以防止管理层的任意行为对工人造成损害。

items.en: Long gone are the days when a boss could simply give an employee contractual notice.
items.zh: 过去那种老板只需简单地给员工发出合同通知就能解雇他们的时代早已一去不复返了。

items.en: But these provisions create difficulties for businesses when applied to highly paid managers and executives.
items.zh: 但这些规定在应用于高薪经理和高管时，会给企业带来困难。

items.en: As countless boards and business owners will attest, constraining firms from firing poorly performing, high-earning managers is a handbrake on boosting productivity and overall performance.
items.zh: 正如无数董事会成员和企业主所证实的那样，限制企业解雇表现不佳但高薪的经理，会成为提高生产力和整体业绩的障碍。

items.en: The difference between C-grade and A-grade managers may very well be the difference between business success or failure.
items.zh: C级经理与A级经理之间的差异，可能正是企业成败之间的差异。

items.en: Between preserving the jobs of ordinary workers or losing them.
items.zh: 在保护普通工人工作与失去工作之间。

items.en: Yet mediocrity is no longer enough to justify a dismissal.
items.zh: 然而，平庸本身已不再足以成为解雇的理由。

items.en: Consequently—and paradoxically—laws introduced to protect the jobs of ordinary workers may be placing those jobs at risk.
items.zh: 因此——并且具有讽刺意味的是——为了保护普通工人的工作而制定的法律，可能会使这些工作面临风险。

items.en: If not placing jobs at risk, to the extent employment protection laws constrain business owners from dismissing under-performing managers, those laws act as a constraint on firm productivity and therefore on workers' wages.
items.zh: 即使这些法律没有直接危及工作岗位，只要就业保护法限制了企业主解雇表现不佳的管理人员，这些法律就会对企业生产力造成制约，从而也制约了工人的工资。

items.en: Indeed, in "An International Perspective on New Zealand's Productivity Paradox" (2014), the Productivity Commission singled out the low quality of managerial capabilities as a cause of the country's poor productivity growth record.
items.zh: 事实上，在《从国际视角看新西兰的生产率悖论》（2014年）中，生产率委员会特别指出，管理人员能力低下是该国生产率增长记录不佳的原因之一。

items.en: Nor are highly paid managers themselves immune from the harm caused by the ERA's unjustified dismissal procedures.
items.zh: 而且，高薪管理人员本身也无法免受ERA（雇佣关系法）中不合理解雇程序造成的伤害。

items.en: Because employment protection laws make it costlier to fire an employee, employers are more cautious about hiring new staff.
items.zh: 由于就业保护法使得解雇员工的成本更高，雇主在雇佣新员工时会更加谨慎。

items.en: This makes it harder for the marginal manager to gain employment.
items.zh: 这使得那些处于边缘地位的管理人员更难找到工作。

items.en: And firms pay staff less because firms carry the burden of the employment arrangement going wrong.
items.zh: 此外，由于企业承担了雇佣关系出错的负担，企业会支付给员工更少的工资。

items.en: Society also suffers from excessive employment protections.
items.zh: 社会也会因过度的就业保护而受到损害。

items.en: Stringent job dismissal regulations adversely affect productivity growth and hamper both prosperity and overall well-being.
items.zh: 严格的解雇法规会对生产率增长产生负面影响，并阻碍繁荣和整体福祉。

items.en: Across the Tasman Sea, Australia deals with the unjustified dismissal paradox by excluding employees earning above a specified "high-income threshold" from the protection of its unfair dismissal laws.
items.zh: 在塔斯曼海的另一边，澳大利亚通过将收入超过特定“高收入门槛”的员工排除在不公平解雇法的保护范围之外，来应对无正当理由解雇的悖论。

items.en: In New Zealand, a 2016 private members' Bill tried to permit firms and high-income employees to contract out of the unjustified dismissal regime.
items.zh: 在新西兰，2016年的一项私人议员法案试图允许企业和高收入员工通过合同方式退出无正当理由解雇制度。

items.en: However, the mechanisms proposed were unwieldy and the Bill was voted down following the change in government later that year.
items.zh: 然而，该法案提出的机制过于繁琐，同年政府更迭后，该法案被投票否决。

items.en: On a recent sunny day, 13,000 chickens roam over Larry Brown’s 40 windswept acres in Shiner, Texas.
items.zh: 在最近的一个阳光明媚的日子里，13,000只鸡在德克萨斯州欣纳的拉里·布朗的40英亩被风吹过的土地上自由漫步。

items.en: Some rest in the shade of a parked car.
items.zh: 一些鸡在停着的汽车的树荫下休息。

items.en: Others drink water with the cows.
items.zh: 另一些则和牛一起喝水。

items.en: This all seems random, but it's by design, part of what the $ 6.1 billion u.s. egg industry bets will be its next big thing: climate-friendly eggs.
items.zh: 这一切似乎很随意，但实际上是有计划的，是价值61亿美元的美国鸡蛋行业押注的下一个大趋势：气候友好型鸡蛋。

items.en: These eggs, which are making their debut now on shelves for as much as $ 8 a dozen, are still labeled organic and animal-friendly, but they’re also from birds that live on farms using regenerative agriculture—special techniques to cultivate rich soils that can trap greenhouse gases.
items.zh: 这些鸡蛋现在以每打8美元的价格首次出现在货架上，它们仍然标有有机和动物友好的标签，但同时也来自那些生活在采用再生农业的农场里的家禽——这是一种特殊的技术，用于培育能够捕获温室气体的肥沃土壤。

items.en: Such eggs could be marketed as helping to fight climate change.
items.zh: 这类鸡蛋可以被宣传为有助于应对气候变化的产品。

items.en: I’m excited about our progress,” says Brown, who harvests eggs for Denver- based Nest Fresh Eggs and is adding more cover crops that draw worms and crickets for the chickens to eat.
items.zh: 布朗表示，他为丹佛的Nest Fresh Eggs公司收集鸡蛋，并正在增加更多吸引蚯蚓和蟋蟀的覆盖作物供鸡食用，他对目前的进展感到兴奋。

items.en: The birds’ waste then fertilizes fields.
items.zh: 然后，家禽的粪便可以用来为农田施肥。

items.en: Such improvements “allow our hens to forage for higher-quality natural feed that will be good for the land, the hens, and the eggs that we supply to our customers.
items.zh: 这样的改进使我们的母鸡能够觅食到质量更高的天然饲料，这对土地、母鸡以及我们供应给顾客的鸡蛋都有好处。

items.en: The egg industry’s push is the first major test of whether animal products from regenerative farms can become the next premium offering.
items.zh: 蛋类行业的这一举措是首次重大测试，看再生农场生产的动物产品是否能成为下一个高端产品。

items.en: In barely more than a decade, organic eggs went from being dismissed as a niche product in natural foods stores to being sold at Walmart.
items.zh: 仅仅在不到十年的时间里，有机鸡蛋就从被当作天然食品商店中的小众产品，发展到在沃尔玛销售。

items.en: More recently there were similar doubts about probiotics and plant-based meats, but both have exploded into major supermarket categories.
items.zh: 最近，益生菌和植物基肉类也曾面临类似的质疑，但这两类产品都迅速发展成为大型超市的主要商品类别。

items.en: If the sustainable-egg rollout is successful, it could open the floodgates for regenerative beef, broccoli, and beyond.
items.zh: 如果可持续鸡蛋的推广取得成功，它可能会打开通往再生牛肉、西兰花及其他产品的闸门。

items.en: Regenerative products could be a hard sell, because the concept is tough to define quickly, says Julie Stanton, associate professor of agricultural economics at Pennsylvania State University Brandywine.
items.zh: 宾夕法尼亚州立大学布兰迪葡萄酒分校的农业经济学副教授朱莉·斯坦顿表示，再生产品可能难以推销，因为这一概念很难迅速明确定义。

items.en: Such farming also brings minimal, if any, improvement to the food products (though some producers say their eggs have more protein).
items.zh: 这种农业方式对食品产品带来的改善微乎其微，甚至根本没有（尽管一些生产商声称他们的鸡蛋蛋白质含量更高）。

items.en: The industry is betting that the same consumers paying more for premium attributes such as free-range, non-GMO, and pasture-raised eggs will embrace sustainability.
items.zh: 该行业押注于那些愿意为自由放养、非转基因和放牧饲养等高端属性支付更高价格的消费者，也会接受可持续性产品。

items.en: Surveys show that younger generations are more concerned about climate change, and some of the success of plant-based meat can be chalked up to shoppers wanting to signal their desire to protect the environment.
items.zh: 调查显示，年轻一代更关注气候变化，一些植物基肉类的成功可以归因于购物者希望通过购买行为表达他们保护环境的愿望。

items.en: Young adults “ really care about the planet,” says John Brunnquell, president of Egg Innovations.
items.zh: ‘年轻人真的非常关心地球，’蛋类创新公司总裁约翰·布鲁恩奎尔表示。

items.en: They are absolutely altering the food chain beyond what I think even they understand what they’re doing.
items.zh: 他们正在彻底改变食品链，甚至可能自己都没有意识到他们正在做的事情。

items.en: More Americans are opting to work well into retirement, a growing trend that threatens to upend the old workforce model.
items.zh: 越来越多的美国人选择工作到退休年龄之后，这一日益增长的趋势可能会颠覆传统的劳动力模式。

items.en: One in three Americans who are at least 40 have or plan to have a job in retirement to prepare for a longer life, according to a survey conducted by Harris Poll for TD Ameritrade.
items.zh: 据哈里斯民调为TD Ameritrade进行的一项调查显示，三分之一的至少40岁的美国人目前有工作或计划在退休后继续工作，以应对更长的寿命。

items.en: Even more surprising is that more than half of “unretirees”—those who plan to work in retirement or went back to work after retiring—said they would be employed in their later years even if they had enough money to settle down, the survey showed.
items.zh: 更令人惊讶的是，调查显示，超过一半的“非退休者”——即计划退休后继续工作或在退休后重新工作的人——表示即使他们有足够的钱安享晚年，也仍会在晚年继续工作。

items.en: Financial needs aren’t the only culprit for the “unretirement” trend.
items.zh: 财务需求并不是“非退休”趋势的唯一原因。

items.en: Other reasons, according to the study, include personal fulfillment such as staying mentally fit, preventing boredom or avoiding depression.
items.zh: 根据研究，其他原因包括个人满足感，例如保持心理健康、防止无聊或避免抑郁。

items.en: About 72% of “unretiree” respondents said that they would return to work once retired to keep mentally fit while 59% said it would be tied to making ends meet.
items.zh: 约72%的“非退休者”受访者表示，退休后他们会重返工作岗位以保持心理健康，而59%的人则表示这是为了维持生计。

items.en: The concept of retirement is evolving,” said Christine Russell, senior manager of retirement at TD Ameritrade.
items.zh: TD Ameritrade的退休业务高级经理克里斯汀·拉塞尔表示：‘退休的概念正在演变。’

items.en: It’s not just about finances.
items.zh: 它不仅仅关乎财务问题。

items.en: The value of work is also driving folks to continue working past retirement.
items.zh: 工作的价值也促使人们在退休后继续工作。

items.en: Among the most popular ways they are doing this, the company said, is by reducing their overall expenses, securing life insurance or maximizing their contributions to retirement accounts.
items.zh: 该公司表示，他们正在采取的最受欢迎的方式之一是减少总体开支、购买人寿保险或最大限度地向退休账户缴款。

items.en: Unfortunately, many people who are opting to work in retirement are preparing to do so because they are worried about making ends meet in their later years, said Brent Weiss, a co-founder at Baltimore-based financial-planning firm Facet Wealth.
items.zh: 巴尔的摩金融规划公司Facet Wealth的联合创始人布伦特·韦斯表示，不幸的是，许多选择退休后继续工作的人之所以准备这样做，是因为他们担心晚年难以维持生计。

items.en: He suggested that preretirees should speak with a financial adviser to set long-term financial goals.
items.zh: 他建议即将退休的人应与财务顾问沟通，以制定长期的财务目标。

items.en: The most challenging moments in life are getting married, starting a family and ultimately retiring,” Weiss said.
items.zh: 韦斯说：'人生中最具有挑战性的时刻是结婚、组建家庭，最终是退休。'

items.en: It’s not just a financial decision, but an emotional one.
items.zh: 这不仅仅是一个财务决定，更是一个情感上的决定。

items.en: Many people believe they can’t retire
items.zh: 许多人认为他们无法退休

items.en: We have all encountered them, in both our personal and professional lives.
items.zh: 我们在个人生活和职业生涯中都遇到过这样的人。

items.en: Think about the times you felt tricked or frustrated by a membership or subscription that had a seamless sign-up process but was later difficult to cancel.
items.zh: 回想一下你曾经因为某个会员资格或订阅服务而感到被欺骗或沮丧的时刻，这些服务的注册流程非常顺畅，但后来却很难取消。

items.en: One reason for the change in retirement patterns: Americans are living longer.
items.zh: 退休模式发生变化的一个原因：美国人寿命更长了。

items.en: The share of the population 65 and older was 16% in 2018, up 32% from the prior year, according to the US.
items.zh: 据美国统计，2018年65岁及以上人口占总人口的比例为16%，比前一年增长了32%。

items.en: That’s also up 302% since 2010.
items.zh: 这一比例自2010年以来已增长了302%。

items.en: Older Americans are also the fastest-growing segment of the US. workforce, and boomers are expected to live longer than previous generations.
items.zh: 美国老年人也是劳动力中增长最快的群体，而且婴儿潮一代预计比前几代人寿命更长。

items.en: The percentage of retirement-age people in the labor force has doubled over the past three decades.
items.zh: 过去三十年间，退休年龄人口在劳动力中的比例翻了一番。

items.en: About 20% of people 65 and older were in the workforce in February, up from an all-time low of 10% in January 1985, according to money manager United Income.
items.zh: 据资产管理公司United Income的数据显示，2023年2月，有约20%的65岁及以上人口在劳动力中，这一比例比1985年1月的历史最低点10%有所上升。

items.en: Because of longer life spans, Americans are also boosting their savings to preserve their nest eggs, the TD Ameritrade study showed, which surveyed 2000 adults between 40 to 79.
items.zh: 由于寿命延长，美国人的储蓄也在增加，以保障他们的养老积蓄，TD Ameritrade的一项研究显示，该研究调查了40至79岁之间的2000名成年人。

items.en: Six in 10 “unretirees” are increasing their savings in anticipation of a longer life, according to the survey.
items.zh: 调查显示，10名“未退休者”中有6人正在增加储蓄，以应对更长的寿命。

items.en: Something that should be simple and transparent can be complicated, intentionally or unintentionally, in ways that impair consumer choice.
items.zh: 一些本应简单透明的事情，可能会有意或无意地变得复杂，从而损害消费者的自主选择能力。

items.en: These are examples of dark patterns.
items.zh: 这些都是‘暗黑模式’的实例。

items.en: First coined in 2010 by user experience expert Harry Brignull, “ dark patterns” is a catch-all term for practices that manipulate user interfaces to influence the decision-making ability of users.
items.zh: ‘暗黑模式’这一术语最早于2010年由用户体验专家Harry Brignull提出，它是一个涵盖所有通过操纵用户界面来影响用户决策能力的实践的统称。

items.en: Brignull identifies 12 types of common dark patterns, ranging from misdirection and hidden costs to “roach motel,” where a user experience seems easy and intuitive at the start, but turns difficult when the user tries to get out.
items.zh: Brignull识别出12种常见的暗黑模式，从误导和隐藏费用到‘蟑螂旅馆’，即用户界面在开始时看似简单直观，但当用户试图退出时却变得困难。

items.en: In a 2019 study of 53,000 product pages and 11,000 websites, researchers found that about one in 10 employs these design practices.
items.zh: 在2019年对53,000个产品页面和11,000个网站的研究中，研究人员发现大约每10个网站中就有1个使用了这些设计手法。

items.en: Though widely prevalent, the concept of dark patterns is still not well understood.
items.zh: 尽管暗黑模式非常普遍，但这一概念仍不被广泛理解。

items.en: Business and nonprofit leaders should be aware of dark patterns and try to avoid the gray areas they engender.
items.zh: 企业和非营利组织的领导者应了解暗黑模式，并努力避免它们引发的灰色地带。

items.en: Where is the line between ethical, persuasive design and dark patterns?
items.zh: 伦理说服设计与暗黑模式之间的界限在哪里？

items.en: Businesses should engage in conversations with IT, compliance, risk, and legal teams to review their privacy policy, and include in the discussion the customer/user experience designers and coders responsible for the company’s user interface, as well as the marketers and advertisers responsible for sign-ups, checkout baskets, pricing, and promotions.
items.zh: 企业应与IT、合规、风险和法律团队进行对话，以审查其隐私政策，并在讨论中包括负责公司用户界面的客户/用户体验设计师和程序员，以及负责注册、购物车、定价和促销的营销和广告人员。

items.en: Any or all these teams can play a role in creating or avoiding “digital deception.
items.zh: 这些团队中的任何一个或全部都可以在创建或避免“数字欺骗”中发挥作用。

items.en: Lawmakers and regulators are slowly starting to address the ambiguity around dark patterns, most recently at the state level.
items.zh: 立法者和监管机构正在逐步开始解决围绕“暗黑模式”的模糊性，最近一次是在州一级层面。

items.en: In March, the California Attorney General announced the approval of additional regulations under the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) that “ensure that consumers will not be confused or misled when seeking to exercise their data privacy rights.” The regulations aim to ban dark patterns—this means prohibiting companies from using confusing language or unnecessary steps such as forcing them to click through multiple screens or listen to reasons why they shouldn’t opt out.
items.zh: 3月，加州总检察长宣布批准了《加州消费者隐私法》（CCPA）下的额外规定，以确保消费者在行使数据隐私权利时不会感到困惑或被误导。这些规定旨在禁止“暗黑模式”——这意味着禁止公司使用令人困惑的语言或不必要的步骤，例如迫使用户点击多个屏幕或聆听为何不应退出的解释。

items.en: As more states consider promulgating additional regulations, there is a need for greater accountability from within the business community.
items.zh: 随着越来越多的州考虑颁布额外的规定，企业界内部需要更高的责任感。

items.en: Dark patterns also can be addressed on a self-regulatory basis, but only if organizations hold themselves accountable, not just to legal requirements but also to industry best practices and standards.
items.zh: “暗黑模式”也可以通过自我监管的方式加以解决，但前提是组织要对自己负责，不仅遵守法律要求，还要遵循行业最佳实践和标准。

items.en: Although ethics classes are common around the world, scientists are unsure if their lessons can actually change behavior; evidence either way is weak, relying on contrived laboratory tests or sometimes unreliable self-reports.
items.zh: 尽管伦理课程在全球范围内很常见，但科学家们不确定这些课程是否真的能改变行为；无论哪方面的证据都很薄弱，依赖于人为设计的实验室测试，或者有时不可靠的自我报告。

items.en: But a new study published in Cognition found that, in at least one real-world situation, a single ethics lesson may have had lasting effects.
items.zh: 但一项发表在《认知》（Cognition）期刊上的新研究发现，在至少一种现实世界的情境中，一次伦理课程可能产生了持久的影响。

items.en: The researchers investigated one class session’s impact on eating meat.
items.zh: 研究人员调查了一堂课对学生吃肉行为的影响。

items.en: They chose this particular behavior for three reasons, according to study co-author Eric Schwitzgebel, a philosopher at the University of California, Riverside: students’ attitudes on the topic are variable and unstable, behavior is easily measurable, and ethics literature largely agrees that eating less meat is good because it reduces environmental harm and animal suffering.
items.zh: 根据该研究的合著者、加州大学河滨分校的哲学家埃里克·施维茨格尔布（Eric Schwitzgebel）的说法，他们选择这一特定行为有三个原因：学生在这个话题上的态度具有可变性和不稳定性，行为容易被测量，而且伦理学文献普遍认为减少吃肉是好的，因为它能减少环境危害和动物痛苦。

items.en: Half of the students in four large philosophy classes read an article on the ethics of factory-farmed meat, optionally watched an 11-minute video on the topic and joined a 50-minute discussion.
items.zh: 四门大型哲学课中的一半学生阅读了一篇关于工业化养殖肉类伦理的文章，可选择观看一个关于该主题的11分钟视频，并参与一个50分钟的讨论。

items.en: The other half focused on charitable giving instead.
items.zh: 另一半学生则专注于慈善捐赠。

items.en: Then, unknown to the students, the researchers studied their anonymized meal-card purchases for that semester—nearly 14,000 receipts for almost 500 students.
items.zh: 然后，在学生不知情的情况下，研究人员研究了他们该学期匿名的餐卡消费记录——几乎500名学生的近14000张收据。

items.en: Schwitzgebel predicted the intervention would have no effect; he had previously found that ethics professors do not differ from other professors on a range of behaviors, including voting rates, blood donation and returning library books.
items.zh: 施维茨格尔布预测这种干预不会有任何效果；他之前发现，伦理学教授在一系列行为上与其他教授没有区别，包括投票率、献血和归还图书馆书籍。

items.en: But among student subjects who discussed meat ethics, meal purchases containing meat decreased from 52 to 45 percent—and this effect held steady for the study’s duration of several weeks.
items.zh: 但在讨论了肉类伦理的学生群体中，包含肉类的餐食购买比例从52%下降到了45%——而且这一效果在整个研究持续的几周内保持稳定。

items.en: Purchases from the other group remained at 52 percent.
items.zh: 而另一组学生的肉类购买比例则保持在52%。

items.en: That’s actually a pretty large effect for a pretty small intervention,” Schwitzgebel says.
items.zh: 施维茨格尔贝尔说：'这实际上是一个相当大的效果，来自于一个相当小的干预措施。'

items.en: Psychologist Nina Strohminger at the University of Pennsylvania, who was not involved in the study, says she wants the effect to be real but cannot rule out some unknown confounding variable.
items.zh: 未参与这项研究的宾夕法尼亚大学心理学家尼娜·斯特罗姆明格表示，她希望这个效果是真实的，但也不能排除某些未知的混杂变量的影响。

items.en: And if real, she notes, it might be reversible by another nudge: “Easy come, easy go.
items.zh: 她指出，如果这个效果是真实的，可能通过另一个'推动'来逆转：'来得容易，去得也快。'

items.en: Schwitzgebel suspects the greatest impact came from social influence- classmates or teaching assistants leading the discussions may have shared their own vegetarianism, showing it as achievable or more common.
items.zh: 施维茨格尔贝尔怀疑最大的影响来自于社会影响——进行讨论的同学或助教可能分享了他们自己的素食主义，展示了它是一种可实现的或更常见的选择。

items.en: Second, the video may have had an emotional impact.
items.zh: 其次，视频可能产生了情感上的影响。

items.en: Least rousing, he thinks, was rational argument, although his co-authors say reason might play a bigger role.
items.zh: 他认为最不具激励作用的是理性论证，尽管他的合著者表示理性可能发挥更大的作用。

items.en: Now the researchers are probing the specific effects of teaching style, teaching assistants’ eating habits and students’ video exposure.
items.zh: 现在研究人员正在探讨教学风格、助教的饮食习惯以及学生观看视频的具体影响。

items.en: Meanwhile, Schwitzgebel—who had predicted no effect—will be eating his words.
items.zh: 与此同时，施维茨格尔贝尔——他曾预测没有效果——将不得不收回自己的言论。

items.en: The weather in Texas may have cooled since the recent extreme heat, but the temperature will be high at the State Board of Education meeting in Austin this month as officials debate how climate change is taught in Texas schools.
items.zh: 德克萨斯州的天气可能自从最近的极端高温之后有所降温，但本月在奥斯汀举行的州教育委员会会议上，随着官员们就如何在德克萨斯州的学校中教授气候变化问题展开辩论，会议现场的温度将会很高。

items.en: Pat Hardy, who sympathises with the views of the energy sector, is resisting proposed changes to science standards for pre-teen pupils.
items.zh: 帕特·哈迪同情能源行业的观点，她正在抵制针对青少年科学课程标准的拟议修改。

items.en: There are as many scientists working against all the panic of global climate change as there are those who are pushing it," she claims.
items.zh: 她声称，有和那些推动全球气候变化恐慌论调一样多的科学家在反对这种观点。

items.en: Texas is an energy state and we need to recognise that.
items.zh: 德克萨斯州是一个能源大州，我们需要认识到这一点。

items.en: You need to remember where your bread is buttered.
items.zh: 你要记住你的面包是用黄油涂抹的。

items.en: Most scientists and experts sharply dispute Hardy's views.
items.zh: 大多数科学家和专家都强烈反驳哈迪的观点。

items.en: Board members like her "casually dismiss the career work of scholars and scientists as just another misguided opinion," says Dan Quinn, senior communications strategist at the Texas Freedom Network, a non-profit group that monitors public education.
items.zh: 德克萨斯自由网络（Texas Freedom Network）的高级传播战略师丹·昆恩表示，像她这样的委员会成员"随意地将学者和科学家的职业成果轻蔑地视为另一种错误的观点"。德克萨斯自由网络是一个非营利组织，负责监督公共教育。

items.en: Such debates reflect fierce discussions across the US, as researchers, policymakers, teachers and students step up demands for a greater focus on teaching about the facts of climate change in schools.
items.zh: 此类辩论反映了全美范围内关于气候变化事实教学的激烈讨论，研究人员、政策制定者、教师和学生都在呼吁学校更加重视这一议题的教学。

items.en: A study last year by the National Center for Science Education, a non-profit group of scientists and teachers, looking at how state public schools across the country address climate change in science classes, gave barely half of US states a grade B+ or higher.
items.zh: 去年，由非营利组织国家科学教育中心（由科学家和教师组成）进行的一项研究，调查了全国各州公立学校在科学课程中如何应对气候变化问题，结果显示仅有不到一半的美国州获得了B+或更高的成绩。

items.en: Among the 10 worst performers were some of the most populous states, including Texas, which was given the lowest grade (F) and has a disproportionate influence because its textbooks are widely sold elsewhere.
items.zh: 在表现最差的10个州中，包括一些人口最多的州，如德克萨斯州，它获得了最低的评分（F），并且由于其教科书在其他地方广泛销售，因此具有不成比例的影响力。

items.en: Glenn Branch, the centre's deputy director, cautions that setting state-level science standards is only one limited benchmark in a country that decentralises decisions to local school boards.
items.zh: 该中心的副主任格伦·布兰奇警告说，在将决策权下放给地方学校委员会的国家里，制定州级科学标准只是有限的一个基准。

items.en: Even if a state is considered a high performer in its science standards, "that does not mean it will be taught", he says.
items.zh: 即使一个州在科学标准方面被认为是表现优异的，"这也不意味着它会被教授", 他说。

items.en: Another issue is that while climate change is well integrated into some subjects and at some ages—such as earth and space sciences in high schools—it is not as well represented in curricula for younger children and in subjects that are more widely taught, such as biology and chemistry.
items.zh: 另一个问题是，尽管气候变化在某些学科和某些年龄段（如高中阶段的地球与空间科学）已经很好地融入了教学内容，但在面向年幼儿童的课程以及更广泛教授的学科（如生物和化学）中，其内容表现得不够充分。

items.en: It is also less prominent in many social studies courses.
items.zh: 在许多社会研究课程中，气候变化的内容也显得不那么突出。

items.en: Branch points out that, even if a growing number of official guidelines and textbooks reflect scientific consensus on climate change, unofficial educational materials that convey more slanted perspectives are being distributed to teachers.
items.zh: 布兰奇指出，即使越来越多的官方指南和教科书反映了科学界对气候变化的共识，一些非官方的教育材料却正在向教师分发，这些材料传达了更加偏颇的观点。

items.en: They include materials sponsored by energy industry associations.
items.zh: 这些材料包括由能源行业协会资助的内容。

items.en: Short-term rentals themselves are not the crux of the issue, said Keren Horn, an expert on affordable housing policy.
items.zh: 短期租赁本身并不是问题的关键，负担得起住房政策专家凯伦·霍恩表示。

items.en: I think individuals being able to rent out their second home is a good thing.
items.zh: 我认为个人能够出租自己的第二套住房是一件好事。

items.en: If it's their vacation home anyway, and it's just empty, why can't you make money off it?
items.zh: 如果这本来就是他们的度假屋，而且一直空置着，为什么不能从中赚钱呢？

items.en: Issues arise, however, when developers attempt to create large-scale short-term rental facilities—de facto hotels—to bypass taxes and regulations.
items.zh: 然而，当开发商试图创建大规模的短期租赁设施——实际上就是酒店——以规避税收和监管时，问题就出现了。

items.en: I think the question is, shouldn't a developer who's really building a hotel, but disguising it as not a hotel, be treated and taxed and regulated like a hotel?
items.zh: 我认为问题是，如果一个开发商实际上是在建造酒店，但却伪装成不是酒店，那他不应该像酒店一样被对待、征税和监管吗？

items.en: At the end of 2018, Governor Charlie Baker of Massachusetts signed a bill to rein in those potential investor-buyers.
items.zh: 到2018年底，马萨诸塞州州长查理·贝克签署了一项法案，以限制那些潜在的投资购房人。

items.en: The bill requires every rental host to register with the state, mandates they carry insurance, and opens the potential for local taxes on top of a new state levy.
items.zh: 该法案要求每一位租赁房东向州政府注册，必须持有保险，并且在新的州级税收基础上，还可能征收地方税。

items.en: Boston took things even further, requiring renters to register with the city's Inspectional Services Department.
items.zh: 波士顿更进一步，要求房东向市环境卫生部门注册。

items.en: Communities throughout New England have been attempting to regulate short-term rentals since sites like Airbnb took off in the 2010s.
