items.zh: 自2010年代以来，随着Airbnb等平台的兴起，新英格兰各地的社区一直在试图规范短期租赁。

items.en: Now, with record-high home prices and historically low inventory, there's an increased urgency in such regulation, particularly among those who worry that developers will come in and buy up swaths of housing to flip for a fortune on the short-term rental market.
items.zh: 如今，随着房价创历史新高且房源库存处于历史低位，这种监管的紧迫性显著增加，尤其是在那些担心开发商会大量购入住房并在短期租赁市场中高价转售的人群中。

items.en: In New Hampshire, where the rental vacancy rate has dropped below 1 percent, housing advocates fear unchecked short-term rentals will put further pressure on an already strained market.
items.zh: 在新罕布什尔州，该州的租房空置率已降至1%以下，住房倡导者担心不受控制的短期租赁将进一步加剧本已紧张的住房市场。

items.en: The state Legislature recently voted against a bill that would've made it illegal for towns to create legislation restricting short-term rentals.
items.zh: 该州立法机构最近投票否决了一项法案，该法案原本将禁止城镇制定限制短期租赁的法规。

items.en: We are at a crisis level on the supply of rental housing," said Nick Taylor, executive director of the Workforce Housing Coalition of the Greater Seacoast.
items.zh: 新英格兰大海岸地区劳动力住房联盟的执行主任尼克·泰勒表示："我们在租赁住房供应方面已经达到了危机水平。"

items.en: Without enough affordable housing in southern New Hampshire towns, "employers are having a hard time attracting employees, and workers are having a hard time finding a place to live," Taylor said.
items.zh: 泰勒表示："如果没有足够的可负担住房，南部新罕布什尔州的城镇将难以吸引雇主，而工人也难以找到住处。"

items.en: However, short-term rentals also provide housing for tourists, pointed out Ryan Castle, CEO of a local association of realtors.
items.zh: 然而，当地房地产协会的首席执行官瑞安·卡斯特指出，短期租赁也为游客提供了住房。

items.en: A lot of workers are servicing the tourist industry, and the tourism industry is serviced by those people coming in short term," Castle said, "and so it's a cyclical effect.
items.zh: 卡斯特表示："许多工人服务于旅游业，而旅游业又依赖这些短期入住的人，因此这是一个循环效应。"

items.en: Horn said similar registration requirements could benefit struggling cities and towns, but "if we want to make a change in the housing market, the main one is we have to build a lot more.
items.zh: 霍恩表示，类似的注册要求可能对陷入困境的城市和城镇有益，但"如果我们想在住房市场上做出改变，最主要的是我们必须建造更多的住房。"

items.en: If you're heading for your nearest branch of Waterstones, the biggest book retailer in the UK, in search of the Duchess of Sussex's new children's book The Bench, you might have to be prepared to hunt around a bit; the same may be true of The President's Daughter, the new thriller by Bill Clinton and James Patterson.
items.zh: 如果你正前往英国最大的图书零售商沃特尔斯通斯（Waterstones）最近的门店，寻找苏塞克斯公爵夫人新出版的儿童读物《The Bench》，你可能需要多找找；同样地，寻找比尔·克林顿和詹姆斯·帕特森合著的新惊悚小说《The President's Daughter》也可能如此。

items.en: Both of these books are published next week by Penguin Random House (PRH), a company currently involved in a stand-off with Waterstones.
items.zh: 这两本书将于下周由企鹅兰登书屋（Penguin Random House，简称PRH）出版，而这家公司目前正与沃特尔斯通斯处于僵持状态。

items.en: The problem began late last year, when PRH confirmed that it had introduced a credit limit with Waterstones "at a very significant level".
items.zh: 问题始于去年年底，当时PRH确认它已与沃特尔斯通斯"在非常显著的水平上"引入了信用额度限制。

items.en: The trade magazine The Bookseller reported that Waterstones branch managers were being told to remove PRH books from prominent areas such as tables, display spaces and windows, and were "quietly retiring them to their relevant sections".
items.zh: 贸易杂志《The Bookseller》报道称，沃特尔斯通斯的门店经理被指示将PRH的书籍从显眼的位置如桌子、展示区和橱窗中移除，并被要求"悄悄地将它们归还到相应的书架区域"。

items.en: PRH declined to comment on the issue, but a spokesperson for Waterstones told me: "Waterstones are currently operating with reduced credit terms from PRH, the only publisher in the UK to place any limitations on our ability to trade.
items.zh: PRH拒绝就此事发表评论，但沃特尔斯通斯的一位发言人告诉我："沃特尔斯通斯目前从PRH获得的信用条款有所减少，而PRH是英国唯一一家对我们交易能力施加限制的出版商。"

items.en: We are not boycotting PRH titles but we are doing our utmost to ensure that availability for customers remains good despite the lower overall levels of stock.
items.zh: 我们并不是在抵制PRH的图书，但我们会尽最大努力确保在库存总量较低的情况下，顾客仍能获得良好的供应。"

items.en: We are hopeful with our shops now open again that normality will return and that we will be allowed to buy appropriately.
items.zh: 我们希望随着门店重新开放，正常情况能够恢复，并且我们会被允许适当采购。

items.en: After all, many of the most interesting books in recent years have come from small publishers.
items.zh: 毕竟，近年来许多最有趣的书籍都是由小型出版社出版的。

items.en: We shall see whether that plurality is a casualty of the current need among publishers to be big enough to take on all-comers.
items.zh: 我们将看到，这种多样性是否会成为当前出版商为了足够强大以应对所有竞争者而产生的牺牲品。

items.en: Scientific papers are the recordkeepers of progress in research.
items.zh: 科学论文是科研进展的记录者。

items.en: Each year researchers publish millions of papers in more than 30,000 journals.
items.zh: 每年研究人员在3万多种期刊上发表数以百万计的论文。

items.en: The scientific community measures the quality of those papers in a number of ways, including the perceived quality of the journal (as reflected by the title's impact factor) and the number of citations a specific paper accumulates.
items.zh: 科学界通过多种方式衡量这些论文的质量，包括期刊的感知质量（如期刊标题的影响因子所反映的）以及某篇具体论文所积累的引用次数。

items.en: The careers of scientists and the reputation of their institutions depend on the number and prestige of the papers they produce, but even more so on the citations attracted by these papers.
items.zh: 科学家的职业生涯及其所在机构的声誉，取决于他们发表的论文数量和声望，但更取决于这些论文所吸引的引用次数。

items.en: Citation cartels, where journals, authors, and institutions conspire to inflate citation numbers, have existed for a long time.
items.zh: 引用 cartel（卡特尔）——期刊、作者和机构合谋抬高引用次数的现象——已经存在了很长时间。

items.en: In 2016, researchers developed an algorithm to recognize suspicious citation patterns, including groups of authors that disproportionately cite one another and groups of journals that cite each other frequently to increase the impact factors of their publications.
items.zh: 2016年，研究人员开发了一种算法，用于识别可疑的引用模式，包括相互之间引用比例异常高的作者群体，以及频繁相互引用以提高其出版物影响因子的期刊群体。

items.en: Recently, another expression of this predatory behavior has emerged: so-called support service consultancies that provide language and other editorial support to individual authors and to journals sometimes advise contributors to add a number of citations to their articles.
items.zh: 最近，这种掠夺性行为的另一种表现形式出现了：所谓的支持服务咨询公司，它们为个人作者和期刊提供语言及其他编辑支持，有时会建议投稿者在他们的文章中增加若干引用。

items.en: The advent of electronic publishing and authors' need to find outlets for their papers resulted in thousands of new journals.
items.zh: 电子出版的兴起以及作者寻找发表论文渠道的需求，导致了数千种新期刊的诞生。

items.en: The birth of predatory journals wasn't far behind.
items.zh: 掠夺性期刊的出现也紧随其后。

items.en: These journals can act as milk cows where every single article in an issue may cite a specific paper or a series of papers.
items.zh: 这些期刊可以充当‘奶牛’，每期中的每篇文章都可能引用某篇特定的论文或一系列论文。

items.en: In some instances, there is absolutely no relationship between the content of the article and the citations.
items.zh: 在某些情况下，文章内容与所引用的文献之间完全没有关联。

items.en: The peculiar part is that the journal that the editor is supposedly working for is not profiting at all—it is just providing citations to other journals.
items.zh: 奇怪的是，编辑 supposedly 为之工作的期刊实际上并没有从中获利——它只是为其他期刊提供引用。

items.en: Such practices can lead an article to accrue more than 150 citations in the same year that it was published.
items.zh: 此类行为可能导致一篇文章在发表的同年就获得超过150次的引用。

items.en: How insidious is this type of citation manipulation?
items.zh: 这种引用操纵行为有多恶劣？

items.en: In one example, an individual—acting as author, editor, and consultant—was able to use at least 15 journals as citation providers to articles published by five scientists at three universities.
items.zh: 在其中一个例子中，某个人——同时担任作者、编辑和顾问——能够使用至少15种期刊作为引用来源，这些期刊引用了三位大学里五位科学家发表的文章。

items.en: The problem is rampant in Scopus, a citation database, which includes a high number of the new "international" journals.
items.zh: 这个问题在Scopus（一个引文数据库）中尤为严重，它包含了大量新的"国际"期刊。

items.en: In fact, a listing in Scopus seems to be a criterion to be targeted in this type of citation manipulation.
items.zh: 事实上，在这种引文操纵行为中，被Scopus收录似乎已成为一个目标标准。

items.en: Scopus itself has all the data necessary to detect this malpractice.
items.zh: Scopus本身拥有检测这种不当行为所需的所有数据。

items.en: Red flags include a large number of citations to an article within the first year.
items.zh: 红色预警信号包括一篇文章在第一年内被引用次数异常多。

items.en: And for authors who wish to steer clear of citation cartel activities: when an editor, a reviewer, or a support service asks you to add inappropriate references, do not oblige and do report the request to the journal.
items.zh: 对于希望避免参与引文卡特尔活动的作者来说：如果编辑、审稿人或支持服务要求你添加不恰当的参考文献，请不要顺从，并将这一要求报告给期刊。

items.en: In the quest for the perfect lawns, homeowners across the country are taking a shortcut -- and it is the environment that is paying the price.
items.zh: 在追求完美草坪的过程中，全国各地的房主们正在走捷径——而环境却为此付出了代价。

items.en: About eight million square meters of plastic grass is sold each year but opposition has now spread to the highest gardening circles.
items.zh: 每年约有八百万平方米的塑料草被售出，但如今反对的声音已经蔓延到了最高级别的园艺界。

items.en: The Chelsea Flower Show has banned fake grass from this year’s event, declaring it to be not part of its ethos.
items.zh: 切尔西花展今年禁止使用人造草坪，称其不符合自身的理念。

items.en: The Royal Horticultural Society (RHS), which runs the annual show in west London, says it has introduced the ban because of the damage plastic grass does to the environment and biodiversity.
items.zh: 负责在伦敦西部举办年度花展的英国皇家园艺学会（RHS）表示，由于人造草坪对环境和生物多样性造成损害，因此引入了这一禁令。

items.en: Ed Horne of the RHS said: we launched our sustainability strategy last year and fake grass is just not in line with our ethos and views on plastic.
items.zh: RHS的埃德·霍恩表示：我们去年推出了可持续发展战略，人造草坪显然不符合我们的理念和对塑料的看法。

items.en: We recommend using real grass because of its environment benefits, which include supporting wildlife, alleviating flooding and cooling the environment.
items.zh: 我们建议使用真正的草坪，因为它具有环境效益，包括支持野生动物、缓解洪水和降低环境温度。

items.en: The RHS’s decision comes as campaigners try to raise awareness of the problem fake grass causes.
items.zh: RHS的这一决定正值活动人士试图提高人们对人造草坪所造成问题的认识之际。

items.en: A Twitter account, which claims to “cut through the greenwash” of artificial grass, already has more than 20,000 followers.
items.zh: 一个声称要“揭露人造草坪绿色洗白”的推特账号已经拥有超过20,000名关注者。

items.en: It is trying to encourage people to sign two petitions, one calling for a ban on the sale of plastic grass and another calling for an “ecological damage” tax on such lawns.
items.zh: 它正在鼓励人们签署两项请愿书，一项呼吁禁止销售塑料草坪，另一项则呼吁对这类草坪征收‘生态损害’税。

items.en: They have gathered 7,276 and 11,282 signatures.
items.zh: 这两项请愿书已分别收集到7,276和11,282个签名。

items.en: Certainly, our shops are exceptionally busy.
items.zh: 当然，我们的书店异常繁忙。

items.en: The sales for our May Books of the Month surpassed any month since 2018.
items.zh: 我们五月份的“本月推荐书”销售业绩超过了自2018年以来的任何一个月。

items.en: In the meantime, PRH authors have been the losers.
items.zh: 与此同时，PRH的作者们却成了输家。

items.en: Big-name PRH authors may suffer a bit, but it's those mid-list authors, who normally rely on Waterstones staff's passion for promoting books by lesser-known writers, who will be praying for an end to the dispute.
items.zh: 知名PRH作者可能会受到一些影响，但那些中等知名度的作者，他们通常依赖于沃特尔斯通书店员工对推广不知名作家作品的热情，才会祈求这场纠纷早日结束。

items.en: It comes at a time when authors are already worried about the consequences of the proposed merger between PRH and another big publisher, Simon & Schuster—the reduction in the number of unaligned UK publishers is likely to lead to fewer bidding wars, lower advances, and more conformity in terms of what is published.
items.zh: 这发生在作者们已经担忧PRH与另一家大型出版商西蒙与舒斯特（Simon & Schuster）拟议合并的后果之时——英国独立出版商数量的减少可能会导致竞价战减少、预付稿酬降低，以及在出版内容方面更加趋同。

items.en: This is all part of a wider change towards concentration of power and cartels.
items.zh: 所有这些都属于更广泛的变化趋势，即权力集中和出版商卡特尔的形成。

items.en: Literary agencies are getting bigger to have the clout to negotiate better terms with publishers, publishers consolidating to deal with Amazon," says Lownie.
items.zh: 文学经纪公司正在变得更大，以拥有与出版商谈判更好条件的影响力，出版商也在合并以应对亚马逊，”洛尼说。

items.en: The publishing industry talks about diversity in terms of authors and staff but it also needs a plurality of ways of delivering intellectual contact, choice and different voices.
items.zh: 出版业谈论作者和员工的多样性，但同时也需要多种方式来提供思想交流、选择和不同声音。

items.en: However, supporters of fake grass point out that there’s also an environmental impact with natural lawns, which need mowing and therefore usually consume electricity or petrol.
items.zh: 然而，人造草的支持者指出，天然草坪同样会对环境造成影响，因为它们需要修剪，因此通常会消耗电力或汽油。

items.en: The industry also points out that real grass requires considerable amounts of water, weed killer or other treatments and that people who lay fake grass tend to use their garden more.
items.zh: 该行业还指出，天然草坪需要大量的水、除草剂或其他处理，并且铺设人造草的人往往更频繁地使用他们的花园。

items.en: The industry also claims that people who lay fake grass spend on average of £500 trees or shrubs for their garden, which provides habitat for insects.
items.zh: 该行业还声称，铺设人造草的人平均会在他们的花园中花费500英镑购买树木或灌木，这为昆虫提供了栖息地。

items.en: In response to another petition last year about banning fake lawns, which gathered 30,000 signatures, the government responded that it has "no plans to ban the use of artificial grass.
items.zh: 针对去年另一项关于禁止使用人造草坪的请愿书，该请愿书获得了3万名签名者，政府回应称，它"没有计划禁止使用人造草坪"。

items.en: It added:"We prefer to help people and organizations make the right choice rather than legislating on such matters, However the use of artificial grass must comply with the legal and policy safeguards in place to protect biodiversity and ensure sustainable drainage, while measures such as the strengthened biodiversity duty should serve to encourage public authorities to consider sustainable alternatives.
items.zh: 它补充道："我们更倾向于帮助人们和组织做出正确的选择，而不是就这类问题进行立法。然而，使用人造草坪必须遵守现有的法律和政策保障，以保护生物多样性和确保可持续排水，同时加强生物多样性责任等措施应鼓励公共机构考虑可持续的替代方案。"

items.en: It's easy to dismiss as absurd the federal government's ideas for plugging the chronic funding gap of our national parks.
items.zh: 很容易将联邦政府为弥补我们国家公园长期资金缺口而提出的设想视为荒谬。

items.en: Can anyone really think it's a good idea to allow Amazon deliveries to your tent in Yosemite or food trucks to line up under the redwood trees at Sequoia National Park?
items.zh: 谁能真的认为，允许亚马逊将包裹送到约塞米蒂国家公园的帐篷里，或让食品卡车在红杉国家公园的红杉树下排队，是个好主意呢？

items.en: But the government is right about one thing: u.s. national parks are in crisis.
items.zh: 但政府有一点是对的：美国的国家公园正处于危机之中。

items.en: Collectively, they have a maintenance backlog of more than $12 billion.
items.zh: 总体而言，它们的维护积压任务超过120亿美元。

items.en: Roads, trails, restrooms, visitor centers and other infrastructure are crumbling.
items.zh: 道路、小径、卫生间、游客中心和其他基础设施正在逐渐破败。

items.en: But privatizing and commercializing the campgrounds would not be a cure-all.
items.zh: 但将露营地私有化和商业化并不是万能的解决方案。

items.en: Campgrounds are a tiny portion of the overall infrastructure backlog, and businesses in the parks hand over, on average, only about 5% of their revenues to the National Park Service.
items.zh: 露营地仅占整体基础设施积压任务的一小部分，而且公园内的企业平均只将其收入的约5%交给国家公园管理局。

items.en: Moreover, increased privatization would certainly undercut one of the major reasons why 300 million visitors come to the parks each year: to enjoy nature and get a break from the commercial drumbeat that overwhelms daily life.
items.zh: 此外，增加私有化程度无疑会削弱每年有3亿游客来到公园的一个主要原因：享受自然并逃离充斥日常生活的商业节奏。

items.en: The real problem is that the parks have been chronically starved of funding.
items.zh: 真正的问题是，这些公园长期缺乏资金支持。

items.en: An economic survey of 700 u.s. taxpayers found that people would be willing to pay a significant amount of money to make sure the parks and their programs are kept intact.
items.zh: 一项针对700名美国纳税人进行的经济调查显示，人们愿意支付大笔钱来确保公园及其项目得以完整保留。

items.en: Some 81% of respondents said they would be willing to pay additional taxes for the next 10 years to avoid any cuts to the national parks.
items.zh: 约81%的受访者表示，他们愿意在未来10年内缴纳额外税款，以避免对国家公园的任何削减。

items.en: Half of the participants were told the information would be erased, while the other half were told it would be saved.
items.zh: 一半的参与者被告知信息将会被删除，而另一半则被告知信息会被保存。

items.en: The latter group made no effort to recall the information when quizzed on it later, because they knew they could find it on their computers.
items.zh: 后来在被提问时，后者没有努力回忆这些信息，因为他们知道可以在自己的电脑上找到它们。

items.en: In the same study, a group was asked to remember both the information and the folders it was stored in.
items.zh: 在同一项研究中，一组被要求记住信息以及信息存储在哪些文件夹中。

items.en: They didn't remember the information, but they remembered how to find the folders.
items.zh: 他们记不住信息本身，但记得如何找到这些文件夹。

items.en: In other words, human memory is not deteriorating but "adapting to new communications technology," Sparrow says.
items.zh: 换句话说，人类的记忆并没有退化，而是"适应了新的通讯技术"，斯帕罗说。

items.en: In a very practical way, the Internet is becoming an external hard drive for our memories, a process known as "cognitive offloading.
items.zh: 从非常实际的角度来看，互联网正在成为我们记忆的外部硬盘，这一过程被称为"认知卸载"。

items.en: Traditionally, this role was fulfilled by data banks, libraries, and other humans.
items.zh: 传统上，这一角色由数据库、图书馆和其他人来完成。

items.en: Your father may never remember birthdays because your mother does, for instance.
items.zh: 例如，你父亲可能永远记不住生日，因为你的母亲记得。

items.en: The national parks provide great value to u.s. residents both as places to escape and as symbols of nature.
items.zh: 国家公园为美国居民提供了巨大的价值，既是逃离喧嚣的地方，也是自然的象征。

items.en: On top of this, they produce value from their extensive educational programs, their positive impact on the climate through carbon sequestration, their contribution to our cultural and artistic life, and of course through tourism.
items.zh: 此外，它们还通过广泛的教育项目、通过碳封存对气候的积极影响、对我们的文化和艺术生活的贡献，以及当然还有旅游业，产生价值。

items.en: The parks also help keep America's past alive, working with thousands of local jurisdictions around the country to protect historical sites and to bring the stories of these places to life.
items.zh: 公园还通过与全国各地数千个地方政府合作，保护历史遗址并让这些地方的故事重现于世，从而帮助美国保留其历史。

items.en: The parks do all this on a shoestring.
items.zh: 公园在经费极其有限的情况下完成了所有这些工作。

items.en: Congress allocates only 3 billion a year to the national park system — an amount that has been flat since 2001 ( in inflation-adusted dollars) with the exception of a onetime boost in 2009.
items.zh: 国会每年只向国家公园系统拨款30亿美元——这一数额自2001年以来（按通货膨胀调整后的美元计算）一直保持不变，除了2009年曾有一次性增加。

items.en: Meanwhile, the number of annual visitors has increased more than 50% since 1980, and now stands at 330 million visitors per year.
items.zh: 与此同时，自1980年以来，每年的游客人数已增长超过50%，目前每年达到3.3亿人次。

items.en: The Internet may be changing merely what we remember, not our capacity to do so, suggests Columbia University psychology professor Betsy Sparrow.
items.zh: 哥伦比亚大学心理学教授贝蒂·斯帕罗指出，互联网可能只是改变了我们记住的内容，而不是我们记住的能力。

items.en: In 2011, Sparrow led a study in which participants were asked to record 40 factoids in a computer ("an ostrich's eye is bigger than its brain," for example).
items.zh: 2011年，斯帕罗领导了一项研究，研究中参与者被要求将40个事实性信息记录在电脑中（例如："鸵鸟的眼睛比大脑大"）。

items.en: At this point, we don't know.
items.zh: 此时，我们尚不清楚。

items.en: Teenagers are paradoxical.
items.zh: 青少年是矛盾的。

items.en: That’s a mild and detached way of saying something that parents often express with considerably stronger language.
items.zh: 这是一种温和而超然的说法，用来表达父母们常常使用更为强烈措辞表达的内容。

items.en: But the paradox is scientific as well as personal.
items.zh: 但这种矛盾不仅存在于个人层面，也存在于科学层面。

items.en: In adolescence, helpless and dependent children who have relied on grown-ups for just about everything become independent people who can take care of themselves and help each other.
items.zh: 在青春期，那些几乎完全依赖成年人的无助儿童，会成长为能够自立并互相帮助的独立个体。

items.en: At the same time, once cheerful and compliant children become rebellious teenage risk-takers.
items.zh: 同时，曾经愉快顺从的孩子变成了具有叛逆性格的、喜欢冒险的青少年。

items.en: A new study published in the journal Child Development by Eveline Crone of the University of Leiden and colleagues, suggests that the positive and negative sides of teenagers go hand in hand.
items.zh: 由莱顿大学的埃维琳·克罗内及其同事发表在《儿童发展》期刊上的一项新研究指出，青少年的积极面和消极面是相伴而生的。

items.en: The study is part of a new wave of thinking about adolescence.
items.zh: 这项研究是关于青春期的一种新思潮的一部分。

items.en: Some worry that this is having a destructive effect on society but Sparrow sees an upside.
items.zh: 一些人担心这会对社会产生破坏性的影响，但斯帕罗看到了其中的积极面。

items.en: Perhaps, she suggests, the trend will change our approach to learning from a focus on individual facts and memorization to an emphasis on more conceptual thinking - something that is not available on the Internet.
items.zh: 她认为，这一趋势可能会改变我们对学习的态度，从关注个别事实和记忆转向更强调概念性思维——而这一点在互联网上是无法获得的。

items.en: I personally have never seen all that much intellectual value in memorizing things," Sparrow says, adding that we haven't lost our ability to do it.
items.zh: 我个人从未在记忆事物中看到太多智力价值，斯帕罗说道，并补充说我们并没有失去这种能力。

items.en: Still other experts say it's too soon to understand how the Internet affects our brains.
items.zh: 还有其他专家表示，现在还为时过早，无法理解互联网对我们大脑的影响。

items.en: There is no experimental evidence showing that it interferes with our ability to focus, for instance, wrote psychologists Christopher Chabris and Daniel J.
items.zh: 心理学家克里斯托弗·查布里斯和丹尼尔·J. 写道，目前还没有实验证据表明它会干扰我们集中注意力的能力。

items.en: And surfing the web exercised the brain more than reading did among computer-savvy older adults in a 2008 study involving 24 participants at the Semel Institute for Neuroscience and Human Behavior at the University of California, Los Angeles.
items.zh: 在2008年一项涉及24名参与者的研究中，加州大学洛杉矶分校塞梅尔神经科学与人类行为研究所发现，对于精通电脑的老年人来说，上网冲浪比阅读更能锻炼大脑。

items.en: There may be costs associated with our increased reliance on the Internet, but I'd have to imagine that overall the benefits are going to outweigh those costs," observes psychology professor Benjamin Storm.
items.zh: 心理学教授本杰明·斯托姆观察到："我们对互联网的依赖增加可能会带来一些代价，但我觉得总体而言，益处应该会超过这些代价。"

items.en: It seems pretty clear that memory is changing, but is it changing for the better?
items.zh: 似乎很明显，我们的记忆正在发生变化，但这种变化是向好的方向发展吗？

items.en: For a long time, scientists and policy makers concentrated on the idea that teenagers were a problem needed to be solved.
items.zh: 长期以来，科学家和政策制定者都集中于这样一个观念，即青少年是一个需要解决的问题。

items.en: The new work emphasizes that adolescence is a time of opportunity as well as risk.
items.zh: 这项新研究强调，青春期既是充满机会的时期，也是充满风险的时期。

items.en: The researchers studied "prosocial" and rebellious traits in more than 200 children and young adults, ranging from 11 to 28 years old.
items.zh: 研究人员对200多名年龄在11至28岁之间的儿童和年轻人进行了研究，考察了他们的"亲社会"和叛逆特质。

items.en: The participants filled out questions about how often they did things that were altruistic and positive, like sacrificing their own interests to help a friend or rebellious and negative, like getting drunk or staying out late.
items.zh: 参与者填写了关于他们多经常做利他和积极的事情（比如牺牲自己的利益去帮助朋友）以及做叛逆和消极的事情（比如喝醉酒或深夜外出）的问卷。

items.en: Other studies have shown that rebellious behavior increased as you become a teenager and then fades away as you grow older.
items.zh: 其他研究表明，随着你进入青春期，叛逆行为会增加，而随着年龄增长，这种行为又会逐渐减少。

items.en: But the new study shows that, interestingly, the same pattern holds for prosocial behavior.Teenagers were more likely than younger children or adults to report that they did things like unselfishly help a friend.
items.zh: 但这项新研究显示，有趣的是，亲社会行为也呈现出同样的模式。青少年比年幼的儿童或成年人更有可能报告说他们做过诸如无私地帮助朋友这样的事情。

items.en: Most significantly,there was a positive correlation between prosociality and rebelliousness.
items.zh: 最重要的是，亲社会性与叛逆性之间存在正相关关系。

items.en: The teenagers who were more rebellious were also more likely to help others.
items.zh: 那些更叛逆的青少年也更有可能帮助他人。

items.en: The good and bad sides of adolescence seem to develop together.
items.zh: 青春期的好与坏似乎是一起发展的。

items.en: Is there some common factor that underlies these apparently contradictory developments?
items.zh: 是否存在某种共同因素在背后推动这些看似矛盾的发展？

items.en: One idea is that teenager behavior is related to what researchers call” reward sensitivity.
items.zh: 一个想法是，青少年的行为与研究人员所说的“奖励敏感性”有关。

items.en: Decision-making always involves balancing rewards and risks, benefits and costs “Reward sensitivity” 'measures how much reward it takes to outweigh risk.
items.zh: 决策过程总是涉及奖励与风险、利益与成本之间的权衡，“奖励敏感性”衡量的是需要多大的奖励才能抵消风险。

items.en: Teenagers are particularly sensitive to social rewards-winning the game, impressing a new friend, getting that boy to notice you.
items.zh: 青少年对社交奖励特别敏感——比如赢得比赛、给新朋友留下好印象、让那个男孩注意到你。

items.en: Reward sensitivity, like prosocial behavior and risk-taking, seems to go up in adolescence and then down again as we age.
items.zh: 奖励敏感性，就像亲社会行为和冒险行为一样，在青春期会上升，然后随着年龄增长再次下降。

items.en: Somehow, when you hit 30, the chance that something exciting and new will happen at that party just doesn’t seem to outweigh the effort of getting up off the couch.
items.zh: 不知何故，当你到了30岁，那种在聚会上发生令人兴奋的新事情的可能性，似乎不再能抵消你从沙发上站起来所付出的努力了。

items.en: Nearly 2000 years ago, as the Romans began to pull out of Scotland, they left behind a curious treasure: 10 tons of nails, nearly a million of the things.
items.zh: 近2000年前，当罗马人开始从苏格兰撤军时，他们留下了一件奇特的宝藏：10吨钉子，几乎有百万枚。

items.en: The nail hoard was discovered in 1960 in a four-metre-deep pit covered by two metres of gravel.
items.zh: 这枚钉子堆是在1960年被发现的，位于一个深四米、被两米厚的砾石覆盖的坑中。

items.en: Why had the Romans buried a million nails?
items.zh: 为什么罗马人埋葬了一百万枚钉子？

items.en: The likely explanation is that the withdrawal was rushed, and they didn't want the local Caledonians getting their hands on 10 tons of weapons-grade iron.
items.zh: 可能的解释是，这次撤退是仓促进行的，他们不想让当地的卡莱多尼亚人得到十吨用于制造武器的铁。

items.en: The Romans buried the nails so deep that they would not be discovered for almost two millennia.
items.zh: 罗马人将这些钉子埋得如此之深，以至于它们几乎在两千年之后才被发现。

items.en: Later civilizations would value the skilled blacksmith's labour in a nail even more than the raw material.
items.zh: 后来的文明会更加重视钉子中熟练铁匠的劳动，而不是原材料本身。

items.en: As Roma Agrawal explains in her new delightful book Nuts and Bolts, early 17th-century Virginians would sometimes burn down their homes if they were planning to relocate.
items.zh: 正如罗玛·阿格拉瓦尔在她新出版的有趣书籍《螺栓与螺母》中所解释的那样，17世纪早期的弗吉尼亚人有时会烧毁自己的房屋，如果他们计划搬迁的话。

items.en: This was an attempt to recover the valuable nails, which could be reused after sifting the ashes.
items.zh: 这是试图回收那些宝贵的钉子，这些钉子在灰烬中筛过后可以再次使用。

items.en: The idea that one might burn down an entire house just to reclaim the nails underlines how scarce, costly and valuable the simple-seeming technology was.
items.zh: 一个人可能会为了回收钉子而烧毁整栋房子的想法，凸显了这种看似简单的技术是多么稀缺、昂贵和有价值。

items.en: The price of nails fell by 90% between the late 1700s and mid-1900s, as economist Daniel Sichel points out in a research paper.
items.zh: 如经济学家丹尼尔·西格尔在一篇研究论文中所指出的那样，钉子的价格在18世纪末到19世纪中期之间下降了90%。

items.en: According to Sichel, although the falling price of nails was driven partly by cheaper iron and cheaper energy, most of the credit goes to nail manufacturers who simply found more efficient ways to turn steel into nails.
items.zh: 根据西格尔的说法，尽管钉子价格的下降部分是由于铁和能源成本的降低，但大部分功劳应归于钉子制造商，他们只是找到了更有效的方法将钢转化为钉子。

items.en: Nails themselves have changed over the years, but Sichel studied them because they haven't changed much.
items.zh: 钉子本身在这些年里已经发生了变化，但西格尔研究它们是因为钉子的变化不大。

items.en: Roman lamps and Roman chariots are very different from LED strips and sports cars, but Roman nails are still clearly nails.
items.zh: 罗马的油灯和战车与LED灯带和跑车截然不同，但罗马的钉子仍然是明显的钉子。

items.en: It would be absurd to try to track the changing price of sports cars since 1695, but to ask the same question of nails makes perfect sense.
items.zh: 试图追踪自1695年以来跑车价格的变化是荒谬的，但对钉子提出同样的问题却完全合情合理。

items.en: I make no apology for being obsessed by a particular feature of everyday objects: their price.
items.zh: 我对日常物品的某个特定特征着迷，对此我毫不道歉：它们的价格。

items.en: I am an economist, after all.
items.zh: 毕竟，我是一名经济学家。

items.en: After writing two books about the history of inventions, one thing I've learnt is that while it is the enchantingly sophisticated technologies that get all the hype, it's the cheap technologies that change the world.
items.zh: 在写了两本关于发明历史的书之后，我学到的一件事是，虽然那些迷人而复杂的科技总能引起轰动，但真正改变世界的却是那些廉价的科技。

items.en: The residents help to look after the children, an arrangement akin to alloparenting.
items.zh: 居民们帮助照顾孩子，这种安排类似于代际抚育。

items.en: Another measure could be encouraging friendships between children in different school years to mimic the supervised mixed-age playgroups in hunter-gatherer communities.
items.zh: 另一种措施可以是鼓励不同年级的孩子建立友谊，以模仿采集狩猎社会中由成人监督的混龄游戏小组。

items.en: In a paper published in the Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry, researchers said that the western nuclear family was a recent invention which broke with evolutionary history.
items.zh: 在发表于《儿童心理与精神病学杂志》的一篇论文中，研究人员表示，西方的核心家庭是一种近期的发明，它与进化历史相悖。

items.en: This abrupt shift to an "intensive mothering narrative" which suggests that mothers should manage child care alone, was likely to have been harmful.
items.zh: 这种突然转向的"密集育儿叙事"，暗示母亲应独自承担育儿责任，很可能会带来伤害。

items.en: Such narratives can lead to maternal exhaustion and have dangerous consequences," they wrote.
items.zh: 他们写道，这种叙事可能导致母亲精疲力竭，并产生危险的后果。

items.en: By contrast, in hunter-gatherer societies adults other than the parents can provide almost half of a child's care.
items.zh: 相比之下，在采集狩猎社会中，除了父母之外的成年人都可以为孩子提供几乎一半的照顾。

items.en: One previous study looked at the people of the Democratic Republic of Congo.
items.zh: 之前的一项研究曾观察了刚果民主共和国的居民。

items.en: It found that infants had an average of 14 alloparents a day by the time they were 18 weeks old and were passed between caregivers eight times an hour.
items.zh: 研究发现，当婴儿满18周时，他们平均每天有14个代养者，并且每小时会被传递给照料者八次。

items.en: The Gutenberg printing press transformed civilisation not by changing the nature of writing but by changing its cost - and it would have achieved little without a parallel collapse in the price of surfaces to write on, thanks to an overlooked technology called paper.
items.zh: 古腾堡印刷机通过改变书写成本而非书写本身的性质，改变了文明；如果没有一种被忽视的技术——纸张——使得书写表面的价格大幅下降，它也不会取得太大成就。

items.en: Solar panels had a few niche uses until they became cheap; now they are transforming the global energy system.
items.zh: 太阳能板在变得便宜之前只有少数利基用途；如今它们正在改变全球能源系统。

items.en: Parenting tips obtained from hunter-gatherers in Africa may be the key to bringing up more contented children, researchers have suggested.
items.zh: 研究人员提出，从非洲的采集狩猎者那里获得的育儿建议可能是培养更快乐孩子的关键。

items.en: The idea is based on studies of communities such as the Kung of Botswana, where each child is cared for by many adults.
items.zh: 这个想法基于对像博茨瓦纳的库恩（Kung）这样的社区的研究，在这些社区中，每个孩子都由许多成年人照顾。

items.en: Kung children as young as four will help to look after younger ones and "baby-wearing", in which infants are carried in slings, is considered the norm.
items.zh: 库恩的孩子们，小到四岁，都会帮忙照顾更年幼的孩子，而‘背带育儿’（即用背带携带婴儿）则被视为常态。

items.en: According to Dr Nikhil Chaudhary, an evolutionary anthropologist at Cambridge University, these practices, known as alloparenting, could lead to less anxiety for children and parents.
items.zh: 剑桥大学的进化人类学家尼希尔·乔杜里（Dr Nikhil Chaudhary）认为，这些被称为‘共同育儿’（alloparenting）的做法，可能会减少孩子和父母的焦虑。

items.en: Dr Annie Swanepoel, a child psychiatrist, believes that there are ways to incorporate them into western life.
items.zh: 儿童精神科医生安妮·斯瓦内波尔（Dr Annie Swanepoel）认为，有办法将这些做法融入西方生活。

items.en: In Germany, one scheme has paired an old people's home with a nursery.
items.zh: 在德国，有一个项目将养老院与托儿所配对。

items.en: The tool, along with other popular image-generation AI models, allows anyone to create impressive images based on text prompts.
items.zh: 该工具与其他流行的图像生成AI模型一起，允许任何人根据文本提示生成令人印象深刻的图像。

items.en: For example, type in "Wizard with sword and a glowing orb of magic fire fights a fierce dragon Greg Rutkowski" and the system will produce something that looks not a million miles away from works in Rutkowski's style.
items.zh: 例如，输入"一位手持剑和发光魔法火球的巫师与一只凶猛的龙搏斗，Greg Rutkowski"，系统将生成一幅看起来与Rutkowski风格的作品相去不远的图像。

items.en: But these open-source programs are built by scraping images from the Internet, often without permission and proper attribution to artists.
items.zh: 但这些开源程序是通过从互联网上抓取图像构建的，通常未经艺术家许可，也未正确署名。

items.en: As a result, they are raising tricky questions about ethics and copyright.
items.zh: 结果，它们引发了关于伦理和版权的棘手问题。

items.en: And artists like Rutkowski have had enough.
items.zh: 像Rutkowski这样的艺术家已经忍无可忍了。

items.en: According to the website Lexica, which tracks over 10 million images and prompts generated by Stable Diffusion, Rutkowski's name has been used as a prompt around 93,000 times.
items.zh: 根据追踪Stable Diffusion生成的超过1000万张图像和提示的网站Lexica，Rutkowski的名字已被用作提示约93000次。

items.en: Some of the world's most famous artists, such as Michelangelo, Pablo Picasso, and Leonardo da Vinci, brought up around 2,000 prompts each or less.
items.zh: 世界上一些最著名的艺术家，如米开朗基罗、巴勃罗·毕加索和列奥纳多·达·芬奇，每人带来的提示数量大约在2000次或更少。

items.en: Rutkowski's name also features as a prompt thousands of times in the Discord of another text-to-image generator, Midjourney.
items.zh: Rutkowski的名字也作为提示在另一个文本到图像生成器Midjourney的Discord平台上出现了数千次。

items.en: Rutkowski was initially surprised but thought it might be a good way to reach new audiences.
items.zh: Rutkowski 最初感到惊讶，但认为这可能是一种接触新受众的好方法。

items.en: Then he tried searching for his name to see if a piece he had worked on had been published.
items.zh: 然后他尝试搜索自己的名字，看看他参与创作的作品是否已被发表。

items.en: The online search brought back work that had his name attached to it but wasn't his.
items.zh: 网络搜索结果返回了一些附着他名字的作品，但那些并不是他创作的。

items.en: It's been just a month.
items.zh: 这仅仅过去了一个月。

items.en: What about in a year?
items.zh: 那一年之后呢？

items.en: I probably won't be able to find my work out there because [the internet] will be flooded with AI art," Rutkowski says.
items.zh: “可能到时候我就无法在互联网上找到自己的作品了，因为（网络）将被 AI 生成的艺术作品淹没，”Rutkowski 说。

items.en: That's concerning.
items.zh: 这令人担忧。

items.en: There is a coalition growing within artist industries to figure out how to tackle or mitigate this," says Ortiz.
items.zh: “艺术行业内部正在形成一个联盟，试图找出应对或缓解这一问题的方法，”Ortiz 说。

items.en: Chaudhary said that parents now had less child care support from family and social networks than during most of humans' evolutionary history, but introducing additional caregivers could reduce stress and maternal depression, which could have a "knock-on" benefit to child's wellbeing.
items.zh: 查杜里表示，现在父母从家庭和社会网络中获得的育儿支持比人类大部分进化历史时期要少，但引入更多的照顾者可以减轻压力和母亲的抑郁情绪，这可能会对孩子福祉产生"连锁反应"的积极影响。

items.en: An infant born to a hunter-gatherer society could have more than ten caregivers - this contrasts starkly to nursery settings in the UK where regulation can allow for a ratio of one carer to four children aged two to three.
items.zh: 一个在采集狩猎社会中出生的婴儿可能拥有超过十位照顾者——这与英国的托儿所环境形成鲜明对比，在英国托儿所的监管规定允许每名照顾者照顾两名至三名年龄在两到三岁的儿童。

items.en: While hunter-gatherer children learn from observation and imitation in mixed-age playgroups, researchers said that western "instructive teaching", where pupils are asked to sit still, may contribute to conditions such as attention deficit hyperactivity disorder.
items.zh: 虽然采集狩猎社会的儿童在混龄游戏小组中通过观察和模仿学习，但研究人员表示，西方的"指导式教学"，要求学生保持安静坐定，可能会导致注意力缺陷多动障碍等状况。

items.en: Chaudhary said that Britain should explore the possibility that older siblings helping their parents might also enhance their own social development.
items.zh: 查杜里表示，英国应该探索让年长的兄弟姐妹帮助父母的可能性，这或许也能促进他们自身的社会发展。

items.en: Rutkowski is a Polish digital artist who uses classical painting styles to create dreamy fantasy landscapes.
items.zh: 鲁特科夫斯基是一位波兰数字艺术家，他运用古典绘画风格创作出梦幻般的幻想风景画。

items.en: He has made illustrations for games such as Sony's Horizon Forbidden West, Ubisoft's Anno, Dungeons & Dragons, and Magic: The Gathering.
items.zh: 他曾为诸如索尼的《地平线：零之曙光》、育碧的《安诺》、《龙与地下城》以及《万智牌》等游戏制作过插图。

items.en: And he's become a sudden hit in the new world of text-to-image AI generation.
items.zh: 他最近在文本生成图像的AI新世界中突然爆红。

items.en: His distinctive style is now one of the most commonly used prompts in the new open-source AI art generator Stable Diffusion, which was launched late last month.
items.zh: 他独特的画风现在已成为新推出的开源AI艺术生成器Stable Diffusion中最常用的提示词之一，该生成器是在上个月末发布的。

items.en: The group is in its early days of mobilization, which could involve pushing for new policies or regulation.
items.zh: 该组织正处于动员的早期阶段，这可能涉及推动新的政策或法规。

items.en: One suggestion is that AI models could be trained on images in the public domain, and AI companies could forge partnerships with museums and artists, Ortiz says.
items.zh: 奥尔蒂斯表示，一个建议是让人工智能模型在公共领域的图像上进行训练，人工智能公司可以与博物馆和艺术家建立合作伙伴关系。

items.en: The miracle of the Chesapeake Bay lies not in its depths, but in the complexity of its natural construction, the interaction of fresh and saline waters, and the mix of land and water.
items.zh: 切萨皮克湾的奇迹不在于其深度，而在于其自然构造的复杂性，淡水与咸水的相互作用，以及陆地与水域的混合。

items.en: The shallows provide homes for hundreds of species while storing floodwaters, filtering pollutants from water, and protecting nearby communities from potentially destructive storm surges.
items.zh: 浅滩为数百种物种提供了栖息地，同时还能储存洪水水位、过滤水中的污染物，并保护附近的社区免受可能具有破坏性的风暴潮的影响。

items.en: All this was put at great risk late last month, when the u.s. Supreme Court issued a ruling in an Idaho case that provides the u.s. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) far less authority to regulate wetlands and waterways.
items.zh: 上个月晚些时候，这一切都面临巨大风险，当时美国最高法院在一项爱达荷州案件中作出裁决，该裁决赋予美国环境保护局（EPA）对湿地和水道进行监管的权限大大减少。

items.en: Specifically, a 5-4 majority decided that wetlands protected by the EPA under its Clean Water Act authority must have a "continuous surface connection to bodies of water.
items.zh: 具体而言，5比4的多数意见裁定，环境保护局根据《清洁水法》授权保护的湿地，必须与水域有"连续的表面连接"。

items.en: This narrowing of the regulatory scope was a victory for builders, mining operators and other commercial interests often at odds with environmental rules.
items.zh: 这种监管范围的缩小对建筑商、采矿运营商和其他经常与环保法规发生冲突的商业利益方来说是一次胜利。

items.en: And it carries "significant repercussions for water quality and flood control throughout the United States," as Justice Brett Kavanaugh observed.
items.zh: 正如布雷特·卡瓦诺法官所指出的，这将对美国全国范围内的水质和洪水控制产生"重大影响"。

items.en: In Maryland, the good news is that there are many state laws in place that provide wetlands protections.
items.zh: 在马里兰州，好消息是已经有许多州法律在实施，为湿地提供了保护。

items.en: But that's a very shortsighted view, particularly when it comes to the Chesapeake Bay.
items.zh: 但这是一种非常短视的观点，尤其是在切萨皮克湾方面。

items.en: The reality is that water, and the pollutants that so often come with it, don't respect state boundaries.
items.zh: 现实情况是，水以及常伴随而来的污染物，并不会尊重州界。

items.en: The Chesapeake draws from a 64,000-square-mile watershed that extends into Virginia, Pennsylvania, New York, West Virginia, the District of Columbia and Delaware.
items.zh: 切萨皮克湾的流域面积达64,000平方英里，范围延伸至弗吉尼亚州、宾夕法尼亚州、纽约州、西弗吉尼亚州、哥伦比亚特区和特拉华州。

items.en: Will those jurisdictions extend the same protections now denied under Sackett v.
items.zh: 这些司法管辖区是否会现在就给予萨克特诉案（Sackett v.）中目前被拒绝的相同保护？

items.en: Perhaps some, but all?
items.zh: 也许有一些会，但全部都会吗？

items.en: That seems unlikely.
items.zh: 这似乎不太可能。

items.en: It is too easy, and misleading, to see such court rulings as merely standing up for the rights of land owners when the consequences can be so dire for their neighbors.
items.zh: 将此类法院裁决简单地视为只是维护土地所有者的权利，这既容易又具有误导性，因为这些裁决对他们的邻居可能带来非常严重的后果。

items.en: And it's a reminder that the EPA's involvement in the Chesapeake Bay Program has long been crucial as the means to transcend the influence of deep-pocketed special interests in neighboring states.
items.zh: 这提醒我们，环保局（EPA）参与切萨皮克湾计划长期以来一直是超越邻近州财力雄厚的特殊利益集团影响的重要手段。

items.en: Pennsylvania farmers, to use one telling example, aren't thinking about next year's blue crab harvest in Maryland when they decide whether to spread animal waste on their fields, yet the runoff into nearby creeks can have enormous impact downstream.
items.zh: 以宾夕法尼亚州的农民为例，当他们决定是否在田地里撒播动物粪便时，并不会考虑明年马里兰州的蓝蟹捕获量，然而这些径流进入附近的溪流后，会对下游产生巨大的影响。

items.en: And so we would call on state lawmakers from Richmond to Albany to consider reviewing their own wetlands protections and see for themselves the enormous stakes involved.
items.zh: 因此，我们呼吁从里士满到奥尔巴尼的各州立法者重新审视他们自身的湿地保护政策，并亲自了解其中涉及的巨大利害关系。

items.en: We can offer them a visit to Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge in Dorchester County where bald eagles fly over tidal marshes so shallow you could not paddle a boat across them but teeming with aquatic life.
items.zh: 我们可以带他们去多切斯特县的布莱克沃特国家野生动物保护区参观，那里的白头海雕在潮汐沼泽上空飞翔，沼泽浅得你甚至无法用船划过，但却充满了丰富的水生生物。

items.en: It's worth the scenic drive.
items.zh: 这趟风景优美的旅程值得一去。

items.en: Anger over AI’s role in exacerbating inequality could endanger the technology’s future.
items.zh: 对人工智能加剧不平等现象的愤怒可能会危及这项技术的未来发展。

items.en: In her new book Cogs and Monsters: What Economics Is, and What It Should Be, Diane Coyle, an economist at Cambridge University, argues that the digital economy requires new ways of thinking about progress.
items.zh: 在她的新书《齿轮与怪物：经济学是什么，以及它应该是什么》中，剑桥大学的经济学家黛安·科伊尔认为，数字经济需要新的思维方式来衡量进步。

items.en: Whatever we mean by the economy growing, by things getting better, the gains will have to be more evenly shared than in the recent past,” she writes.
items.zh: 她写道：'无论我们如何定义经济增长或事情变好，未来的收益必须比近期更加均衡地分配。'

items.en: An economy of tech millionaires or billionaires and gig workers, with middle-income jobs undercut by automation, will not be politically sustainable.
items.zh: 一个由科技百万富翁或亿万富翁以及零工工作者组成的经济，当中等收入工作被自动化取代时，将不会在政治上具有可持续性。

items.en: Improving living standards and increasing prosperity for more people will require greater use of digital technologies to boost productivity in various sectors, including health care and construction, says Coyle.
items.zh: 科伊尔表示，要提高生活标准并让更多人实现繁荣，需要更广泛地使用数字技术来提升各个领域的生产率，包括医疗保健和建筑业。

items.en: But people can’t be expected to embrace the changes if they’re not seeing the benefits—if they’re just seeing good jobs being destroyed.
items.zh: 但如果人们看不到这些变化带来的好处，而只是看到优质工作被摧毁，就无法指望他们接受这些变化。

items.en: In a recent interview with MIT Technology Review, Coyle said she fears that tech’s inequality problem could be a roadblock to deploying AI.
items.zh: 在最近一次与《麻省理工科技评论》的采访中，科伊尔表示，她担心科技领域的不平等问题可能会成为部署人工智能的障碍。

items.en: We’re talking about disruption,” she says.
items.zh: 她说：‘我们谈论的是颠覆。’

items.en: These are transformative technologies that change the ways we spend our time every day, that change business models that succeed.” To make such “tremendous changes,” she adds, you need social buy-in.
items.zh: 这些是变革性技术，它们改变了我们每天的时间分配方式，也改变了成功的企业模式。’她补充道，要实现如此‘巨大的变化’，需要社会的广泛认同。

items.en: Instead, says Coyle, resentment is simmering among many as the benefits are perceived to go to elites in a handful of prosperous cities.
items.zh: 相反，科伊尔说，随着人们认为这些好处只流向少数富裕城市的精英阶层，许多人的不满情绪正在酝酿。

items.en: According to the Brookings Institution, a short list of eight American cities that included San Francisco, San Jose, Boston, and Seattle had roughly 38% of all tech jobs by 2019.
items.zh: 根据布鲁金斯学会的数据，到2019年，包括旧金山、圣何塞、波士顿和西雅图在内的美国八个城市，占据了所有科技工作的约38%。

items.en: A more immediate response is to broaden our digital imaginations to conceive of AI technologies that don’t simply replace jobs but expand opportunities in the sectors that different parts of the country care most about, like health care, education, and manufacturing.
items.zh: 一个更直接的回应是，拓展我们的数字想象力，设想出那些不仅仅取代工作岗位，还能在国家各地区最关注的领域（如医疗保健、教育和制造业）中扩大机会的人工智能技术。

items.en: The UK is facing a future construction crisis because of a failure to plant trees to produce wood, Confor has warned.
items.zh: Confor警告称，由于未能种植树木以生产木材，英国正面临未来的建筑危机。

items.en: The forestry and wood trade body has called for urgent action to reduce the country’s reliance on timber imports and provide a stable supply of wood for future
items.zh: 林业和木材贸易机构呼吁立即采取行动，减少英国对木材进口的依赖，并为未来提供稳定的木材供应。

items.en: Currently only 20 percent of the UK’s wood requirement is home-grown while it remains the second-largest net importer of timber in the world.
items.zh: 目前，英国仅20%的木材需求是本国生产的，而它仍然是全球第二大木材净进口国。

items.en: Coming at a time of fresh incentives from the UK government for landowners to grow more trees, the trade body says these don’t go far enough and fail to promote the benefits of planting them to boost timber supplies.
items.zh: 在英国政府近期出台的新激励措施鼓励土地所有者种植更多树木的背景下，该贸易机构表示这些措施力度不足，未能充分宣传种植树木以增加木材供应的好处。

items.en: Not only are we facing a carbon crisis now, but we will also be facing a future construction crisis because of failure to plant trees to produce wood.” said Stuart Goodall, chief executive of Confor.
items.zh: Confor的首席执行官Stuart Goodall表示：'我们不仅现在正面临碳危机，而且由于未能种植树木以生产木材，未来还将面临建筑危机。’

items.en: For decades we have not taken responsibility for investing in our domestic wood supply, leaving us exposed to fluctuating prices and fighting for future supplies of wood as global demand rises and our own supplies fall.
items.zh: 几十年来，我们没有承担起投资本国木材供应的责任，导致我们暴露在价格波动的风险中，并在未来木材供应上与全球需求上升、本国供应下降的趋势相抗衡。

items.en: The UK has ideal conditions for growing wood to build low-carbon homes and is a global leader in certifying that its forests are sustainably managed, Confor says.
items.zh: Confor表示，英国拥有理想的木材生长条件，可以用来建造低碳住宅，并且在认证其森林可持续管理方面是全球的领导者。

items.en: Some states require physicians to report, others allow but do not mandate reports, while a few consider a report breach of confidentiality.
items.zh: 一些州要求医生进行报告，另一些州允许但不强制要求报告，而少数州则认为报告会违反保密原则。

items.en: There could be liability and penalties if a physician does not act in accordance with state laws on reporting and confidentiality ” she counseled.
items.zh: 她告诫说，如果医生不按照各州关于报告和保密的法律行事，可能会面临责任和处罚。

items.en: Part of the problem in keeping older drivers safe is that the difficulties are addressed piecemeal by different professions with different focuses, including gerontologists, highway administration officials, automotive engineers and others, said gerontologist Elizabeth Dugan.
items.zh: 老年驾驶员安全问题的部分难点在于，不同职业从各自不同的角度，包括老年学家、公路管理部门官员、汽车工程师等，对这些问题进行零散的处理，”老年学家伊丽莎白·杜甘说道。

items.en: There’s not a National Institute of Older Driver Studies,” she said.
items.zh: 她说：‘并没有一个全国性的老年驾驶员研究机构。’

items.en: We need better evidence on what makes drivers unsafe” and what can help, said Dugan.
items.zh: 杜甘表示：‘我们需要更确切的证据来了解哪些因素会使驾驶员变得不安全，以及哪些措施能够有所帮助。’

items.en: One thing that does seem to work is requiring drivers to report in person for license renewal.
items.zh: 似乎有效的一项措施是要求驾驶员亲自到场办理驾照更新手续。

items.en: Mandatory in-person renewal was associated with a 31 percent reduction in fatal crashes involving drivers 85 or older, according to one study.
items.zh: 根据一项研究，强制性亲自到场更新驾照与85岁及以上驾驶员致命性车祸减少了31%相关。

items.en: Passing vision tests also produced a similar decline in fatal crashes for those drivers, although there appeared to be no benefit from combining the two.
items.zh: 通过视力测试也能使这些驾驶员的致命性车祸数量出现类似的下降，尽管将两者结合似乎并没有带来额外的好处。

items.en: While around three quarters of Scottish homes are built from Scottish timber, the use of home-grown wood in England is only around 25 percent.
items.zh: 虽然苏格兰约四分之三的住宅是用苏格兰本地木材建造的，但在英格兰，使用本地木材建造住宅的比例仅为约25%。

items.en: While productive tree planting can deliver real financial benefits to rural economies and contribute to the UK's net-zero strategy, the focus of government support continues to be on food production and the rewinding and planting of native woodland solely for biodiversity.
items.zh: 尽管高产的植树活动可以为农村经济带来真正的经济效益，并有助于英国实现净零排放战略，但政府支持的重点仍然放在粮食生产以及仅为了生物多样性的本土森林的恢复和种植上。

items.en: Goodall add： “ While food production and biodiversity are clearly of critical importance, we need our land to also provide secure supplies of wood for construction, manufacturing and contribute to net zero.
items.zh: 古德说："虽然粮食生产和生物多样性显然至关重要，但我们也需要土地能够为建筑、制造等行业提供稳定的木材供应，并为实现净零排放做出贡献。"

items.en: While the UK government has stated its ambition for more tree planting, there has been little action on the ground.
items.zh: 尽管英国政府表示希望增加植树数量，但在实际操作中却鲜有行动。

items.en: Confor is now calling for much greater impetus behind those aspirations to ensure we have enough wood to meet increasing demand.
items.zh: Confor 现在呼吁对这些目标给予更大的推动，以确保有足够的木材来满足日益增长的需求。

items.en: One big challenge in keeping unsafe aging drivers off the road is convincing them that it is time to turn over the key.
items.zh: 让不安全的老年驾驶员远离道路的一大挑战是说服他们认识到该把车钥匙交出来了。

items.en: It is a complete life-changer when someone stops—or is forced to stop—driving, said former risk manager Anne M.
items.zh: 前风险管理专家安妮·M. 说："当有人停止驾驶，或者被迫停止驾驶时，这对他来说是一个彻底的人生转折点。"

items.en: The American Medical Association advises physicians that in situation where clear evidence of substantial driving impairment implies a strong threat to patient and public safety, and where the physician’s advice to discontinue driving privileges is ignored, it is desirable and ethical to notify the Department of Motor Vehicles, Menke wrote.
items.zh: 门克写道，美国医学会建议医生，在存在明显证据表明驾驶能力严重受损并对患者和公众安全构成重大威胁的情况下，如果医生建议停止驾驶权限却被忽视，那么通知机动车管理局是合情合理且符合伦理的。

items.en: New AI technologies are particularly concentrated: Brookings’s Mark Muro and Sifan Liu estimate that just 15 cities account for two-thirds of the AI assets and capabilities in the United States (San Francisco and San Jose alone account for about one-quarter).
items.zh: 新的AI技术特别集中：布鲁金斯学会的马克·穆罗和刘思凡估计，仅15个城市就占美国AI资产和能力的三分之二（仅旧金山和圣何塞两地就占约四分之一）。

items.en: The dominance of a few cities in the invention and commercialization of AI means that
items.zh: 少数城市在AI的发明和商业化方面的主导地位意味着

items.en: geographical disparities in wealth will continue to soar.
items.zh: 财富的地理差距将持续扩大。

items.en: Not only will this foster political and
items.zh: 这不仅会加剧政治和

items.en: social unrest, but it could, as Coyle suggests, hold back the sorts of AI technologies needed for regional economies to grow.
items.zh: 社会动荡，而且正如科伊尔所指出的，可能会阻碍区域经济需要的AI技术的发展。

items.en: Part of the solution could lie in somehow loosening the stranglehold that Big Tech has on defining the AI agenda.
items.zh: 部分解决方案可能在于以某种方式放松大科技公司对定义AI议程的垄断。

items.en: That will likely take increased federal funding for research independent of the tech giants.
items.zh: 这可能需要增加联邦政府对独立于科技巨头的研究的资金支持。

items.en: Muro and others have suggested hefty federal funding to help create US regional innovation centers, for example.
items.zh: 穆罗等人曾建议提供大量联邦资金，以帮助创建美国的区域性创新中心，例如。

items.en: Many old drivers don't see eye doctors or can't afford to.
items.zh: 许多老司机不去看眼科医生，或者负担不起。

items.en: Primary care providers have their hands full and may not be able to follow through with patients who have trouble driving because they can't turn their heads or remember where they are going—or have gotten shorter and haven't changed their seat settings sufficiently to reach car pedals easily,
items.zh: 初级保健医生已经忙得不可开交，可能无法跟进那些因无法转头、记不住要去哪里，或者身体变矮而没有充分调整座椅设置以方便踩踏汽车踏板的患者。

items.en: As long as there are other cars on the roads, self-driving cars won't solve the problems of crashes, said Dugan.
items.zh: 杜甘说，只要还有其他车辆在道路上行驶，自动驾驶汽车就无法解决车祸问题。

items.en: Avoiding dangers posed by all those human drivers would require to many algorithms, she said.
items.zh: 她说，要避免所有这些人类驾驶员带来的危险，需要大量的算法。

items.en: But we need to do more to improve safety, said Dugan.
items.zh: 但杜甘表示，我们需要做更多来提高安全性。

items.en: If we're going to have 100-year lives, we need cars that a 90-year-old can drive comfortably.
items.zh: 如果我们能活到100岁，我们就需要能让90岁老人舒适驾驶的汽车。

items.en: If you look at the apps on your phone, chances are you have at least one related to your health—and probably several.
items.zh: 如果你看看手机上的应用程序，很可能你至少有一个与健康相关的应用——甚至可能有好几个。

items.en: Whether it is a mental health app, a fitness tracker, a connected health device or something else, many of us are taking advantage of this technology to keep better track of our health in some shape or form.
items.zh: 无论是心理健康应用、健身追踪器、联网健康设备还是其他东西，我们中的许多人正在以某种方式利用这些技术来更好地关注自己的健康状况。

items.en: Recent research from the Organization for the Review of Care and Health Applications found that 350,000 health apps were available on the market, 90,000 of which launched in 2020 alone.
items.zh: 最近，健康护理与应用审查组织的一项研究发现，市场上有35万款健康类应用程序可供使用，其中9万款是在2020年这一年推出的。

items.en: While these apps have a great deal to offer, it is not always clear how the personal information we input is collected, safeguarded and shared online.
items.zh: 尽管这些应用程序提供了诸多便利，但我们输入的个人信息是如何被收集、保护和在线共享的，却并不总是清晰明了。

items.en: Existing health privacy law, such as the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, is primarily focused on the way hospitals, doctors ’ offices, clinics and insurance companies store health records online.
items.zh: 现有的健康隐私法律，如《健康保险可携带性和责任法案》，主要关注医院、医生办公室、诊所和保险公司如何在线存储健康记录。

items.en: The health information these apps and health data tracking wearables are collecting typically does not receive the same legal protections.
items.zh: 这些应用程序和健康数据追踪可穿戴设备所收集的健康信息，通常不会受到同样的法律保护。

items.en: Without additional protections in place, companies may share (and potentially monetize) personal health information in a way consumers may not have authorized or anticipated.
items.zh: 如果没有额外的保护措施，公司可能会以消费者未授权或未预料到的方式共享（甚至可能变现）个人健康信息。

items.en: In 2021, Flo Health faced a Federal Trade Commission（FTC） investigation.
items.zh: 2021年，Flo Health面临美国联邦贸易委员会（FTC）的调查。

items.en: The FTC alleged in a complaint that "despite express privacy claims, the company took control of users' sensitivity fertility data and shared it with third parties.” Flo Health and the FTC settled the matter with a Consent Order requiring the company to get app users' express affirmative consent before sharing their health information as well as to instruct the third parties to delete the data they had obtained.
items.zh: FTC在一份投诉中指控称："尽管该公司明确提出了隐私声明，但其仍掌控了用户的敏感生育数据，并将其与第三方共享。" Flo Health与FTC达成和解，签署了一项同意令，要求该公司在与第三方共享用户健康信息之前，必须获得用户的明确同意，并要求第三方删除其已获取的数据。

items.en: Section 5 of the FTC Act empowers the FTC to initiate enforcement action against unfair or deceptive acts, meaning the FTC can only act after the fact if a company's privacy practices are misleading or cause unjustified consumer harm.
items.zh: 《FTC法案》第5条赋予FTC对不公平或欺骗行为采取执法行动的权力，这意味着如果一家公司的隐私做法具有误导性或导致消费者受到不合理的伤害，FTC只能在事后再采取行动。

items.en: While the FTC is doing what it can to ensure apps are keeping their promises to consumers around the handling of their sensitive health information, the rate at which these health apps are hitting the market demonstrates just how immense of a challenge this is.
items.zh: 尽管FTC正在尽其所能确保这些应用程序在处理敏感健康信息时兑现对消费者的承诺，但这些健康应用程序进入市场的速度表明，这是一项多么巨大的挑战。

items.en: As to the prospects for federal legislation, commentators suggest that comprehensive federal privacy legislation seems unlikely in the short term.
items.zh: 至于联邦立法的前景，评论人士认为短期内出台全面的联邦隐私立法似乎不太可能。

items.en: States have begun implementing their own solutions to shore up protections for consumer-generated health data.
items.zh: 各州已经开始实施自己的解决方案，以加强消费者生成的健康数据的保护。

items.en: California has been at the forefront of state privacy efforts with the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018.
items.zh: 加州在州隐私努力方面一直处于领先地位，其代表是2018年的《加州消费者隐私法案》。

items.en: Virginia ， Colorado and Utah have also recently passed state consumer data privacy legislation.
items.zh: 弗吉尼亚州、科罗拉多州和犹他州也最近通过了各自州的消费者数据隐私立法。

items.en: The grammar school boy from Stratford-upon-Avon has landed a scholarly punch after groundbreaking research showed that Shakespeare does benefit children's literacy and emotional development.
items.zh: 这位来自斯特拉特福镇的文法学校男孩在一项开创性研究之后，获得了学术上的重大突破，该研究显示莎士比亚确实有助于儿童的读写能力和情感发展。

items.en: But only if you act him out.
items.zh: 但前提是你要将他表演出来。

items.en: A study found that a "rehearsal room" approach to teaching Shakespeare broadened children's vocabulary, and the complexity of their writing as well as their emotional literacy.
items.zh: 一项研究发现，采用"排练室"方式教授莎士比亚，有助于拓宽儿童的词汇量，同时提升他们写作的复杂性和情感素养。

items.en: She added: "The emotional understanding was very evident and it is probably related to the [rehearsal room process] where you are used to trying to imagine your way through.
items.zh: 她补充道："情感理解非常明显，这可能与[排练室过程]有关，因为在排练室中你习惯于尝试通过想象来应对。"

items.en: They were comfortable in describing different emotional states and part of what you do in drama is put yourself in different shoes.
items.zh: 他们很自如地描述了不同的情感状态，而戏剧的一部分就是让自己置身于不同的处境中。"

items.en: The study showed the importance of embedding arts in education, she said.
items.zh: 她说，这项研究显示了将艺术融入教育的重要性。"

items.en: But could the results be replicated with any old dramatist?
items.zh: 但是，这些结果是否能用任何普通的戏剧家来重复呢？"

items.en: O'Hanlon said more research would be needed but suggested that Shakespeare's use of 20,000 words, compared with the everyday 2,000 words, gave a "massive expansion of language into children's lives", which was combined with children "using their whole bodies to bring words to life".
items.zh: 奥汉隆表示需要更多的研究，但她指出，与日常使用的2000个单词相比，莎士比亚使用了20000个单词，这为孩子们的生活带来了"语言使用的巨大扩展"，同时孩子们也"用全身来赋予语言生命"。"

items.en: I was shocked to learn recently that some scientists want to scale back their research in an effort to decrease carbon emissions.
items.zh: 我最近震惊地得知，一些科学家希望缩减他们的研究规模，以努力减少碳排放。"

items.en: The crisis is here, they said, and we need to cut back on our energy-intensive modelling.
items.zh: 他们说，危机已经来临，我们需要减少能源密集型的建模工作。"

items.en: At the very least, we need to make our energy use far more sustainable.
items.zh: 至少，我们需要使能源使用变得更加可持续。

items.en: The research shows that the way actors work makes a big difference to the way children use language and also how they think about themselves," Jacqui O'Hanlon of the Royal Shakespeare Company (RSC), which commissioned the study, said.
items.zh: 皇家莎士比亚剧团（RSC）委托进行这项研究的雅琪·奥汉伦表示：'研究表明，演员的工作方式对儿童使用语言的方式以及他们对自己的思考方式都有很大影响。'

items.en: The randomised control trial involved hundreds of year 5 pupils—aged nine and ten—at 45 state primary schools that had not been "previously exposed to RSC pedagogy".
items.zh: 这项随机对照试验涉及 45 所“此前未接触过 RSC 教学法”的公立小学中数百名五年级学生，这些学生年龄为九到十岁。

items.en: They were split into target and control groups and asked to write, for example, a message in a bottle as Ferdinand after the shipwreck in The Tempest.
items.zh: 他们被分为目标组和对照组，并被要求例如以《暴风雨》中船难后的费迪南德的身份写一封瓶中信。

items.en: The target group was given a 30-minute drama-based activity to accompany the passage.
items.zh: 目标组的学生被给予一个30分钟的基于戏剧的活动来配合这段文字。

items.en: The peer-reviewed results showed that the target group of pupils drew on a wider vocabulary, used words "classed as more sophisticated or rarer", and wrote at greater length.
items.zh: 经过同行评审的结果显示，目标组的学生使用了更广泛的词汇，使用了'被归类为更复杂或更罕见的词汇'，并且写得更长。

items.en: They also "appear to be more comfortable writing in role...while [control] pupils imagine how they themselves would react to being shipwrecked, [target] children put themselves in the shoes of a literary character and express that character's emotion".
items.zh: 他们还'似乎在角色写作中更加自如……对照组学生想象自己遭遇船难时的反应，而目标组学生则设身处地代入文学人物，表达该人物的情感。'

items.en: The Time to Act study also found that while control pupils relied on "desert island cliches" such as palm trees, target pupils were "more expansive [giving] a broader picture of the sky, the sea and the atmospheric conditions".
items.zh: 《Time to Act》研究还发现，对照组学生依赖诸如棕榈树之类的'荒岛陈词滥调'，而目标组学生则'更加丰富地描绘了天空、大海和大气条件的全貌。'

items.en: O'Hanlon said she had been most surprised by the "emotional literacy that was evident in the [target] children's writing" and that they were "more resilient in their writing, more hopeful".
items.zh: 奥汉伦表示，她最惊讶的是'目标组儿童写作中表现出的情感素养'，并且他们'在写作中更加坚韧，更加充满希望。'

items.en: It is unarguable that our laboratories, scientific instruments, rockets and satellites—the tools we scientists need to measure the planet's pulse—demand significant amounts of energy both in their construction and operation.
items.zh: 不可否认的是，我们的实验室、科学仪器、火箭和卫星——科学家们用来测量地球脉动的工具——在建造和运行过程中都需要消耗大量的能源。

items.en: And it is equally true that science's unrelenting appetite for information has caused a mushrooming of energy-intensive data centres around the world.
items.zh: 同样真实的是，科学对信息永不满足的渴望，已经导致全球范围内能源密集型的数据中心迅速增长。

items.en: According to the International Energy Agency, these buildings now consume about 1 per cent of the world's electricity.
items.zh: 根据国际能源署的数据，这些建筑物现在消耗了全球约1%的电力。

items.en: However, this is a price we must pay for understanding the world.
items.zh: 然而，这是我们为了理解世界必须付出的代价。

items.en: How can we inform decision makers about the best ways to bring down carbon emissions if we can't track the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, where it's coming from and who's producing it?
items.zh: 如果我们无法追踪大气中的二氧化碳含量、它的来源以及是谁排放的，又怎能向决策者提供最佳减少碳排放方式的信息呢？

items.en: The carbon emissions from technological research are well spent: ultimately this research will safeguard the future of our planet.
items.zh: 科技研究产生的碳排放是值得的：最终，这项研究将保障我们星球的未来。

items.en: It can be hard for scientists to make the case because our work is complex, often takes place behind closed doors and does not always lend itself to easy interpretation or explanation.
items.zh: 科学家们很难说服他人，因为我们的工作很复杂，通常在封闭的环境中进行，并不总是易于解释或理解。

items.en: But demonstrating the efficacy of science will be crucial if we are to solve humanity's greatest challenges.
items.zh: 但如果我们要解决人类面临的最大挑战，展示科学的有效性将是至关重要的。

items.en: Recognising the hope that science and engineering can bring was the impetus behind the creation of the Millennium Technology Prize, which is now entering its 20th year as a celebration of human ingenuity.
items.zh: 认识到科学和工程能够带来的希望，是设立千年技术奖的初衷，如今该奖项已进入第20个年头，作为对人类智慧的庆祝。

items.en: One of the past winners, Professor Martin Green from the University of New South Wales, Australia, is the inventor of the Passivated Emitter and Rear Cell technology which is now found in most of the world's solar panels.
items.zh: 过去的一位获奖者，来自澳大利亚新南威尔士大学的马丁·格林教授，是钝化发射极和背面电池（Passivated Emitter and Rear Cell）技术的发明者，这种技术现在被世界上大多数太阳能板所采用。

items.en: Thanks to his invention, we have a real chance to decrease the world's carbon emissions.
items.zh: 得益于他的发明，我们真正有机会减少全球的碳排放。

items.en: Every day, scientists, technologists and engineers are discovering new ways to exploit renewable energy sources and develop techniques not just to use power more intelligently but to power our intelligence.
items.zh: 每天，科学家、技术人员和工程师都在发现新的方法来利用可再生能源，并开发技术，不仅更智能地使用电力，还用电力推动我们的智慧。

items.en: A great example of this is Europe's largest supercomputer, LUMI in Finland, which is astonishingly carbon-negative.
items.zh: 这方面的一个绝佳例子是欧洲最大的超级计算机——位于芬兰的LUMI，它令人惊讶地实现了碳负排放。

items.en: Established in an old paper mill, it is powered by a nearby river and its remote heat warms the people who live in the surrounding town of Kajaani.
items.zh: 它建在一座旧纸厂内，由附近的河流供电，其远程热能还为周边城镇凯亚尼（Kajaani）的居民供暖。

items.en: If the world is to meet its net-zero ambitions, we must think hard about how we can deliver sustainable computing and deliver more LUMIs.
items.zh: 如果世界要实现其净零排放的目标，我们必须认真思考如何提供可持续的计算方式，并打造更多像LUMI这样的项目。

items.en: Ever since taking on Netflix inc. at its own game, old Hollywood has struggled to turn a profit in streaming, with the likes of Disney+, Peacock and Paramount+ losing billions of dollars each year, sparking concerns that the services will never be as profitable as cable once was.
items.zh: 自从老好莱坞在流媒体领域与Netflix公司正面竞争以来，它一直难以盈利，迪士尼+、Peacock和Paramount+等平台每年亏损数十亿美元，引发了人们对这些服务是否能像有线电视那样盈利的担忧。

items.en: But the age of streaming has been a boon for some unintended winners: pirates that use software to rip a film or television show in seconds from legitimate online video platforms and host the titles on their own, illegitimate services, which rake in about $2 billion annually from ads and subscriptions.
items.zh: 然而，流媒体时代对一些意想不到的赢家来说是一次福音：这些盗版网站利用软件在几秒钟内从合法的在线视频平台下载电影或电视剧，并将其托管在自己的非法服务平台上，每年通过广告和订阅获得约20亿美元的收入。

items.en: With no video production costs, illegal streaming sites have achieved profit margins approaching 90%, according to the Motion Picture Association (MPA), a trade group representing Hollywood studios that's working to crack down on the thousands of illegal platforms that have cropped up in recent years.
items.zh: 据代表好莱坞制片公司的行业协会——电影协会（MPA）称，这些非法流媒体网站没有视频制作成本，因此实现了接近90%的利润率，该协会正在努力打击近年来涌现的数千个非法平台。

items.en: Initially the rise of legitimate online businesses such as Netflix actually helped curb digital piracy, which had largely been based on file uploads.
items.zh: 最初，合法的在线企业如Netflix的兴起实际上有助于遏制基于文件上传的数字盗版。

items.en: But now piracy involving illegal streaming services as well as file-sharing costs the US economy about $30 billion in lost revenue a year and some 250,000 jobs, estimates the US Chamber of Commerce's Global Innovation Policy Center.
items.zh: 但现在，据美国商会全球创新政策中心估计，涉及非法流媒体服务和文件共享的盗版每年使美国经济损失约300亿美元的收入，并导致约25万个就业岗位流失。

items.en: The global impact is about $71 billion annually.
items.zh: 全球的经济损失约为每年710亿美元。

items.en: The people who are stealing our movies and our television shows and operating piracy sites are not mom and pop operations," says Charlie Rivkin, chief executive officer of the MPA.
items.zh: MPA首席执行官查理·里夫金（Charlie Rivkin）表示："那些盗取我们的电影和电视剧并运营盗版网站的人，并不是普通的家庭式小作坊。"

items.en: This is organized crime.
items.zh: 这是有组织的犯罪。

items.en: Rivkin joined the MPA in 2017 after the organization failed five years earlier to build consensus between Hollywood and Silicon Valley to win passage of legislation in Congress aimed at stopping online piracy.
items.zh: 里夫金于2017年加入MPA，此前该组织在五年前未能在好莱坞和硅谷之间达成共识，以推动国会通过旨在遏制网络盗版的立法。

items.en: For millennia, we've known what we've known due to artifacts that have survived, often despite their original creators' neglect.
items.zh: 在数千年的时间里，我们所知道的一切都是通过那些得以保存下来的文物，而这些文物往往即使在原作者忽视的情况下也依然留存下来。

items.en: The thing itself is the medium that delivers the information.
items.zh: 物品本身即是传递信息的媒介。

items.en: At the time of creation, no attempts were made at intentional preservation, yet analog materials have a chance of surviving and serving as the historical record that biographers, historians, and novelists rely on.
items.zh: 在创作之时，并未有人刻意尝试去保存它们，但模拟材料仍有机会留存下来，并作为传记作家、历史学家和小说家所依赖的历史记录。

items.en: Libraries and archives have traditionally shouldered the responsibility of organization, preservation, and access to information.
items.zh: 传统上，图书馆和档案馆承担着信息的组织、保存和获取的责任。

items.en: Librarians digitize the tangible so that researchers the world over can quickly search and access their holdings.
items.zh: 图书管理员将有形的资料数字化，以便全球的研究人员能够快速地搜索和获取馆藏资源。

items.en: The result is an embarrassment of historical riches, which brings its own needle-and-haystack problems.
items.zh: 其结果是历史财富的过剩，这也带来了自己特有的大海捞针式的问题。

items.en: Librarians' selfless devotion can act against us when users point to universality of access by holding up a cell phone and saying, "it's all in here" as evidence that libraries are less vital for researchers today.
items.zh: 然而，当用户举起手机并说"所有内容都在这里"，以此证明如今图书馆对研究人员的重要性降低时，图书管理员无私的奉献反而可能对我们不利。

items.en: Yet how was that universality of access made possible and, perhaps more importantly, how is it maintained?
items.zh: 然而，这种获取信息的普遍性是如何实现的？更重要的是，它又是如何被维持的？

items.en: Who curates what is preserved?
items.zh: 谁来负责保存哪些内容？

items.en: When it comes to born-digital information, the terrifying answer can be: if not librarians and archivists, then no one.
items.zh: 当涉及到原生数字信息时，令人不寒而栗的答案可能是：如果不是图书管理员和档案管理员，那就没有人了。

items.en: Digital information requires a great deal more care than analog.
items.zh: 数字信息比模拟信息需要更多的细心呵护。

items.en: Even when a digital object is preserved, it may only be the carrier that's saved, not the information itself.
items.zh: 即使一个数字对象被保存下来，保存的可能只是载体，而不是信息本身。

items.en: As technology advances and a format becomes obsolete, the object is useless.
items.zh: 随着技术的发展和一种格式变得过时，这个对象就变得毫无用处了。

items.en: Have you ever stared helplessly at a ZIP disk, thinking: how do I get the files off this?
items.zh: 你有没有曾经无助地盯着一个ZIP磁盘，想着：我该怎么把里面的文件取出来？

items.en: Without constant migration of digital assets, a nightmare about the foreseeable future is what keeps historians up at night: a historical record that abruptly stops when digital replaces analog.
items.zh: 如果没有持续不断地迁移数字资产，历史学家们就会被一个关于未来的噩梦困扰：当数字技术取代模拟技术时，历史记录会突然中断。

items.en: As a librarian whose day job revolves around special collections and digital assets, I share the night terrors of historians, and I'd be lying if I said a comprehensive preservation solution currently exists.
items.zh: 作为一名日常工作的核心围绕特藏和数字资产的图书管理员，我与历史学家们共享这种夜晚的恐惧，如果我说目前存在一个全面的保存解决方案，那我就是在撒谎。

items.en: In 2017 the association formed the Alliance for Creativity and Entertainment (ACE), an enforcement task force of about 100 detectives circling the globe to help local authorities arrest streaming pirates.
items.zh: 2017年，该协会成立了创意与娱乐联盟（ACE），这是一个由约100名侦探组成、在全球范围内行动的执法特别行动组，旨在协助地方当局逮捕盗版流媒体传播者。

items.en: ACE says it's helped shrink the number of illegal streaming services in North America to 126, from more than 1,400 in 2018, aided in part by the MPA's support for a 2020 federal law that made large-scale streaming of copyrighted material a serious crime.
items.zh: ACE表示，在MPA支持2020年联邦法律的部分帮助下，北美地区的非法流媒体服务平台数量已从2018年的1400多家减少到目前的126家，该法律将大规模传播受版权保护内容的行为定为严重犯罪。

items.en: Consulting firm Parks Associates predicts that legitimate US streaming services' cumulative loss from piracy since 2022 will reach $113 billion in the next two years.
items.zh: 咨询公司Parks Associates预测，自2022年以来，美国合法流媒体服务平台因盗版造成的累计损失将在未来两年内达到1130亿美元。

items.en: While there is some optimism that emerging countermeasures and best practices may see piracy begin to plateau by 2027, there is no consensus among stakeholders as to when it may begin to decline," says analyst Steve Hawley.
items.zh: 分析师史蒂夫·霍利（Steve Hawley）表示："尽管有一些乐观情绪认为，随着新兴的反盗版措施和最佳实践的出现，盗版可能在2027年前后开始趋于稳定，但利益相关方对于盗版何时可能开始下降尚无共识。"

items.en: Visit any antiques store and you'll encounter artifacts from the past: photographs, letters, a brochure detailing the Sinclair dinosaur exhibit from the 1964—65 World's Fair, the ephemera of history.
items.zh: 走进任何一家古董店，你都会看到来自过去的物品：照片、信件，还有1964—65年世界博览会期间关于辛克莱尔恐龙展览的宣传册，这些都是历史的短暂痕迹。

items.en: Yet these objects aren't truly ephemeral, because they're still here, decades, even centuries later.
items.zh: 然而，这些物品并非真正短暂，因为它们至今仍然存在，甚至几十年、几个世纪之后依然如此。

items.en: Because they're tangible.
items.zh: 因为它们是有形的。

items.en: Have you pondered the life cycle of intangible formats, digital information, given that those who produce these artifacts seldom make provision for their long-term preservation?
items.zh: 你是否曾思考过无形格式和数字信息的生命周期？毕竟，这些物品的制作者很少为它们的长期保存做出安排。

items.en: Yet researchers can take some comfort in the fact that there are a multitude of librarians devoted to discovering, organizing, and preserving digital information for researchers current and future.
items.zh: 然而，研究人员可以从这样一个事实中得到一些安慰：有许多图书管理员致力于为当前和未来的研究人员发现、整理和保存数字信息。

items.en: While future researchers may find the digital realm a challenging place to ply their trade, they won't find it an impossible one.
items.zh: 虽然未来的研究人员可能会发现数字领域是一个充满挑战的工作场所，但他们不会发现它是一个无法完成任务的地方。

items.en: u.s. customers historically tipped people they assumed were earning most of their income via tips, such as restaurant servers earning less than the minimum wage.
items.zh: 历史上，美国顾客通常会给那些他们认为大部分收入来自小费的人小费，比如那些赚取的工资低于最低工资的餐厅服务员。

items.en: In the early 2010s, a wide range of businesses started processing purchases with iPads and other digital payment systems.
items.zh: 在2010年代初，各种各样的企业开始使用iPad和其他数字支付系统处理购买交易。

items.en: These systems prompted customers to tip for services that were not previously tipped.
items.zh: 这些系统促使顾客为那些以前不给小费的服务支付小费。

items.en: Today's tip requests are often not connected to the salary and service 3
items.zh: 如今的小费请求往往与决定人们何时以及如何给小费的薪资和服务3

items.en: norms that used to determine when and how people tip.
items.zh: 过去用来决定人们何时以及如何给小费的规范。

items.en: Customers in the past nearly always paid tips after receiving a service, such as at the conclusion of a restaurant meal, after getting a haircut or once a pizza was delivered.
items.zh: 过去的顾客几乎总是在接受服务之后支付小费，比如在餐厅用餐结束时、理发之后或披萨送达后。

items.en: That timing could reward high-quality service and give workers an incentive to provide it.
items.zh: 这种时机安排可能会奖励高质量的服务，并给员工提供提供此类服务的动力。

items.en: It's becoming more common for tips to be requested beforehand.
items.zh: 提前要求小费的情况正变得越来越普遍。

items.en: And new tipping technology may even automatically add tips.
items.zh: 而且，新的小费支付技术甚至可以自动添加小费。

items.en: The prevalence of digital payment devices has made it easier to ask customers for a tip.
items.zh: 数字支付设备的普及使得向顾客请求小费变得更加容易。

items.en: That helps explain why tip requests are creeping into new kind of services.
items.zh: 这在一定程度上解释了为什么小费请求正逐渐渗透到新的服务类型中。

items.en: Customers now routinely see menus of suggested default options-often well above 70% of what they owe.
items.zh: 现在顾客经常能看到建议的小费默认选项菜单，通常高达他们应付金额的70%以上。

items.en: The amounts have risen from 10% or less in the 1950s to 15% around the year 2000 to 20% or higher today.
items.zh: 小费比例从20世纪50年代的10%或更低，上升到2000年左右的15%，如今则达到20%或更高。

items.en: This increase is sometimes called tipflation-the expectation of ever-higher tip amounts.
items.zh: 这种增长有时被称为‘小费膨胀’（tipflation），即对越来越高小费金额的预期。

items.en: Heat action plans, or HAPs, have been proliferating in India in the past few years.
items.zh: 近年来，印度各地的高温应对计划（Heat Action Plans，简称HAPs）迅速增加。

items.en: In general, a HAP spells out when and how officials should issue heat warnings and alert hospitals and other institutions.
items.zh: 一般来说，HAP会明确规定官员应在何时以及如何发布高温预警，并通知医院和其他机构。

items.en: Nagpur's plan, for instance, calls for hospitals to set aside "cold wards" in the summer for treating heatstroke patients, and advises builders to give construction laborers a break from work on very hot days.
items.zh: 例如，那格浦尔的计划要求医院在夏季设立"冷病房"，专门用于治疗中暑患者，并建议建筑商在非常炎热的日子里让建筑工人暂停工作。

items.en: But implementation of existing HAPs has been uneven, according to a report from the Centre for Policy Research.
items.zh: 然而，根据政策研究中心的一份报告，现有HAP的实施情况参差不齐。

items.en: Many lack adequate funding, it found.
items.zh: 该报告发现，许多计划缺乏充足的资金支持。

items.en: And their triggering thresholds often are not customized to the local climate.
items.zh: 而且它们的触发阈值往往没有根据当地气候进行定制。

items.en: In some areas, high daytime temperatures alone might serve as an adequate trigger for alerts.
items.zh: 在一些地区，仅白天的高温就可能作为发布预警的充分依据。

items.en: But in other places, nighttime temperatures or humidity might be as important a gauge of risk as daytime highs.
items.zh: 但在其他地方，夜间温度或湿度可能与白天高温一样，是衡量风险的重要指标。

items.en: Mumbai's April heatstroke deaths highlighted the need for more nuanced and localized warnings, researchers say.
items.zh: 研究人员表示，孟买四月的热射病死亡事件凸显了需要更加细致和本地化的预警措施。

items.en: temperature of roughly 36℃ was 1℃ shy of the heat wave alert threshold for coastal cities set by national meteorological authorities.
items.zh: 大约36℃的温度距离国家气象部门为沿海城市设定的热浪预警阈值还差1℃。

items.en: But the effects of the heat were amplified by humidity—an often neglected factor in heat alert systems -and the lack of shade at the late-morning outdoor ceremony.
items.zh: 但热浪的影响因湿度而加剧——这是热警报系统中经常被忽视的一个因素——而且上午晚些时候户外仪式缺乏遮荫。

items.en: To help improve HAPs, urban planner Rajashree Kotharkar's team is working on a model plan that outlines best practices and could be adapted to local conditions.
items.zh: 为了帮助改进热应激预警系统（HAPs），城市规划师拉贾什丽·科塔卡尔的团队正在制定一个模型计划，概述最佳实践，并可根据当地情况进行调整。

items.en: Among other things, she says, all cities should create a vulnerability map to help focus responses on the populations most at risk.
items.zh: 她说，除了其他措施外，所有城市都应绘制脆弱性地图，以帮助将响应重点放在风险最大的人群中。

items.en: Such mapping doesn't need to be complex, Kotharkar says.
items.zh: 科塔卡尔表示，这种地图并不需要过于复杂。

items.en: A useful map can be created by looking at even a few key parameters.
items.zh: 通过查看几个关键参数，就可以创建一张有用的地图。

items.en: For example, neighborhoods with a large elderly population or informal dwellings might be poorer with heat could get special warnings or be bolstered with cooling centers.
items.zh: 例如，老年人口较多或存在非正式居住区的社区可能在应对高温方面更为薄弱，可以得到特别警告或增设降温中心来加强支持。

items.en: The Nagpur project has already created a risk and vulnerability map, which enabled Kotharkar to tell officials which neighborhoods to focus on in the event of a heat wave this summer.
items.zh: 纳吉浦尔项目已经创建了一张风险和脆弱性地图，这使得科塔卡尔能够告诉官员们今年夏天热浪来临时应该重点关注哪些社区。

items.en: HAPs shouldn't just include short-term emergency responses, researchers say, but also recommend medium-to long-term measures that could make communities cooler.
items.zh: 研究人员表示，HAPs不应该只包括短期的应急响应，还应推荐中长期的措施，使社区变得更凉爽。

items.en: In Nagpur, for example, Kotharkar's team has been able to advise city officials about where to plant trees to provide shade.
items.zh: 例如，在纳吉浦尔，科塔卡尔的团队已经能够向城市官员建议在哪些地方种植树木以提供遮荫。

items.en: HAPs could also guide efforts to retrofit homes or modify building regulations.
items.zh: HAPs还可以指导对住宅进行改造或修改建筑规范的努力。

items.en: Reducing deaths in an emergency is good target to have, but it's the lowest target," says climate researcher Chandri Singh.
items.zh: 气候研究员钱德里·辛格表示："在紧急情况下减少死亡人数是一个不错的目標，但这却是最低的目標。"

items.en: Navigating beyond the organised pavements and parts of our urban spaces, desire paths are the unofficial footprints of a community, revealing the unspoken preferences, shared shortcuts and collective choices of humans.
items.zh: 在我们城市空间中，除了有组织的步道之外，还有欲望路径，这是社区非正式的足迹，揭示了人类未言明的偏好、共享的捷径和集体的选择。

items.en: Often appearing as trodden dirt tracks through otherwise neat green spaces, these routes of collective disobedience cut corners, bisect lawns and cross hills, representing the natural capability of people cand, animals, to go from point A to point B most effectively.
items.zh: 这些体现集体不服从的路线常常以踩踏出的泥路形式出现在原本整洁的绿色空间中，它们绕开角落、穿过草坪、跨越山丘，代表着人和动物从A点到B点最有效率的自然能力。

items.en: Urban planners interpret desire paths as more than just convenient shortcuts; they offer valuable insights into the dynamics between planning and behaviour.
items.zh: 城市规划者认为，欲望路径不仅仅是方便的捷径；它们还提供了关于规划与行为之间关系的宝贵见解。

items.en: This trail, when Dutch colonists arrived, was widened and made into one of the main trade roads across the island, known at the time as de Heere Straat, or Gentlemen’s Street.
items.zh: 当荷兰殖民者到达时，这条小路被拓宽，并成为岛上的主要贸易道路之一，当时被称为de Heere Straat，即绅士街。

items.en: Following the British assumption of control in New York, the street was renamed
items.zh: 在英国接管纽约之后，这条街道被重新命名。

items.en: Notably, Broadway stands out as one of the few areas in NYC that defies the grid-based system applied to the rest of the city, cutting a diagonal across parts of the city.
items.zh: 值得注意的是，百老汇是纽约市少数几个不遵循应用于全市其他地区的网格化系统的区域之一，它穿过城市部分地区，呈对角线延伸。

items.en: In online spaces, desire paths have sparked a fascination that can approach obsession, with the Reddit page serving as a hub.
items.zh: 在网络空间中，欲望路径激发了一种近乎痴迷的兴趣，Reddit页面则成为了这一现象的中心。

items.en: Contributors offer a wide array of stories, from little-known new shortcuts to long-established alternate routes.
items.zh: 投稿者提供了各种各样的故事，从鲜为人知的新捷径到早已存在的替代路线。

items.en: Animal desire paths, such as ducks forging trails through frozen ponds or dogs carving direct routes in gardens, highlight the adaptability of these trails in both human and animal experiences.
items.zh: 动物的欲望路径，例如鸭子在结冰的池塘中开辟的小路，或者狗在花园里走出的直接路线，突显了这些路径在人类和动物体验中的适应性。

items.en: As desire paths criss-cross through both physical and virtual landscapes, they stand as a proof of the collective insistence on forging unconventional routes and embracing the spirit of communal choice.
items.zh: 随着欲望路径在物理和虚拟景观中纵横交错，它们成为集体坚持开辟非传统路线和接受共同选择精神的证明。

items.en: For thousands of years, donkeys have been critical for propelling human civilizations forward.
items.zh: 几千年来，驴子一直是推动人类文明前进的关键力量。

items.en: They've helped pull wheeled vehicles, carry travelers and move goods across the world.
items.zh: 它们帮助拖拽带轮的车辆、运送旅客以及将货物运送到世界各地。

items.en: But where and when these animals first became intertwined with humans has been a mystery.
items.zh: 但这些动物最初在何时何地与人类产生交集，一直是个谜。

items.en: Now, researchers have used the genomes of over 200 donkeys to trace their domestication back to a single event around 7,000 years ago in East Africa - about 3,000 years before humans tamed horses.
items.zh: 现在，研究人员利用了200多匹驴的基因组，追溯它们的驯化历史，发现大约在7000年前的东非发生了一次单一的驯化事件——这比人类驯化马早了约3000年。

items.en: The team published their findings in the journal Science this month.
items.zh: 这个团队本月在《科学》期刊上发表了他们的研究成果。

items.en: Through their DNA, the animals are telling their history themselves," co-author Samantha Brooks, an equine researcher at the University of Florida, says in a statement.
items.zh: 共同作者、佛罗里达大学的马类研究员萨曼莎·布鲁克斯在一份声明中说："通过它们的DNA，这些动物正在讲述自己的历史。"

items.en: We usually only get the human's side of history through written accounts, but of course written history does not always record exactly how something happened.
items.zh: 我们通常只能通过书面记录了解人类视角的历史，但当然，书面历史并不总是准确地记录了事情发生的全过程。

items.en: Looking at these DNA sequences, we get a biological testimony to the environment these animals lived in and the experiences they survived.
items.zh: 通过观察这些DNA序列，我们得到了这些动物所生活的环境以及它们经历过的事件的生物学证据。

items.en: The researchers examined 207 genomes from modern donkeys living in 31 countries across the globe.
items.zh: 研究人员检查了来自全球31个国家的现代驴的207个基因组。
