items.zh: 你的翻译应工整书写在答题纸上。

items.en: It is speculated that gardens arise from a basic human need in the individuals who made them: the need for creative expression.
items.zh: 据推测，花园源自那些建造花园的人的基本需求：即创造性表达。

items.en: There is no doubt that gardens evidence an irrepressible urge to create, express, fashion, and beautify and that self-expression is a basic human urge; (46) yet when one looks at the photographs of the gardens created by the homeless, it strikes one that, for all their diversity of styles, these gardens speak of various other fundamental urges, beyond that of decoration and creative expression.
items.zh: 毫无疑问，花园体现了人类无法抑制的创造、表达、塑造和美化冲动，自我表达是基本的人类需求；（46）然而当人们看到无家可归者所建花园的照片时，会发现这些花园尽管风格各异，却反映出超越装饰和创造表达范畴的其他基本冲动。

items.en: One of these urges has to do with creating a state of peace in the midst of turbulence, a "still point of the turning world," to borrow a phrase from T.
items.zh: 这些冲动之一与在动荡中创造一种和平状态有关，借用T.的一句话，"动荡世界中的静止点"。

items.en: Eliot.
items.zh: 艾略特。

items.en: (47) A sacred place of peace, however crude it may be, is a distinctly human need, as opposed to shelter, which is a distinctly animal need.
items.zh: (47) 无论多么简陋，一个神圣的宁静之地都是人类特有的需求，与庇护所这种动物特有的需求相对。

items.en: This distinction is so much so that where the latter is lacking, as it is for these unlikely gardeners, the former becomes all the more urgent.
items.zh: 这种区别如此之甚，以至于在后者缺失的情况下，如这些不太可能的园丁所面临的那样，前者变得愈发紧迫。

items.en: Composure is a state of mind made possible by the structuring of one's relation to one's environment.
items.zh: 镇定是一种由个人与环境的关系结构化所实现的心理状态。

items.en: (48) The gardens of the homeless, which are in effect homeless gardens, introduce form into an urban environment where it either didn't exist or was not discernible as such.
items.zh: （48）无家可归者花园将形式引入城市环境，这些花园实际上即无家可归者花园，所在城市环境中这种形式要么不存在，要么无法被识别为形式。

items.en: In so doing they give composure to a segment of the inarticulate environment in which they take their stand.
items.zh: 这样做他们赋予了所处无声环境以镇定。

items.en: Another urge or need that these gardens appear to respond to, or to arise from, is so intrinsic that we are barely ever conscious of its abiding claims on us.
items.zh: 这些花园似乎回应或源于另一种冲动或需求，这种需求如此内在，以至于我们几乎从未意识到它对我们持续不断的诉求。

items.en: When we are deprived of green, of plants, of trees, (49) most of us give in to a demoralization of spirit which we usually blame on some psychological conditions, until one day we find ourselves in a garden and feel the oppression vanish as if by magic.
items.zh: 当我们被剥夺了绿色、植物和树木时，大多数人会屈服于一种精神萎靡，通常将其归咎于某些心理状况，直到有一天我们发现自己置身花园，那种压迫感仿佛魔法般消散。

items.en: In most of the homeless gardens of New York City the actual cultivation of plants is unfeasible, yet even so the compositions often seem to represent attempts to call forth the spirit of plant and animal life, if only symbolically, through a clumplike arrangement of materials, an introduction of colors, small pools of water, and a frequent presence of petals or leaves as well as of stuffed animals.
items.zh: 在纽约市大多数无家可归者花园中，实际的植物栽培并不可行，尽管如此，这些花园的布置往往似乎试图通过堆砌状的材料布置、引入色彩、设置小型水池以及频繁出现花瓣、叶片和填充动物来象征性地唤起植物和动物生命的精神。

items.en: On display here are various fantasy elements whose reference, at some basic level, seems to be the natural world.
items.zh: 这里展示的是各种幻想元素，它们的参考在某种程度上似乎源于自然世界。

items.en: The hugely popular blog the Skint Foodie chronicles how Tony balances his love of good food with living on benefits.
items.zh: 广受欢迎的博客 the Skint Foodie 记录 Tony 如何在对美食的热爱与领取救济金生活之间取得平衡。

items.en: After bills, Tony has £ 60 a week to spend, £ 40 of which goes on food, but 10 years ago he was earning £ 130,000 a year working in corporate communications and eating at London’s best restaurants at least twice a week.
items.zh: 支付账单后，Tony每周有60英镑可支配，其中40英镑用于食物，但十年前他每年收入13万英镑，在企业传播领域工作，每周至少两次光顾伦敦最好的餐厅。

items.en: Then his marriage failed, his career burned out and his drinking became serious.
items.zh: 随后他的婚姻破裂，事业陷入困境并且酗酒严重。

items.en: “The community mental health team saved my life.
items.zh: 社区心理健康团队挽救了我的生命。

items.en: And I felt like that again, to a certain degree, when people responded to the blog so well.
items.zh: 当人们如此积极地回应这篇博客时，我再次在某种程度上感受到了那种感觉。

items.en: It gave me the validation and confidence that I’d lost.
items.zh: 它给了我曾经失去的确认和信心。

items.en: But it’s still a day-by-day thing.
items.zh: 但仍然是每天的事情。

items.en: Now he’s living in a council flat and fielding offers from literary agents.
items.zh: 现在他住在公营公寓里，并处理来自文学代理人的报价。

items.en: He’s feeling positive, but he’ ll carry on blogging – not about eating as cheaply as you can – “there are so many people in a much worse state, with barely any money to spend on food” – but eating well on a budget.
items.zh: 他感觉积极，但会继续写博客——不是关于如何尽可能便宜地吃饭——有太多人处境更差，几乎没钱购买食物——而是关于如何在预算内吃得健康。

items.en: Here’s his advice for economical foodies.
items.zh: 这是他给节俭美食爱好者的建议。

items.en: Impulsive spending isn’t an option, so plan your week’s menu in advance, making shopping lists for your ingredients in their exact quantities.
items.zh: 冲动消费不可行，因此提前规划一周的菜单，并按精确数量为食材制定购物清单。

items.en: I have an Excel template for a week of breakfast, lunch and dinner.
items.zh: 我有一个用于一周早餐、午餐和晚餐的Excel模板。

items.en: Stop laughing: it’s not just cost effective but helps you balance your diet.
items.zh: 别笑了：这不仅成本效益高，还能帮助你平衡饮食。

items.en: It’s also a good idea to shop daily instead of
items.zh: 也建议每天购物而不是

items.en: weekly, because, being human, you’ll sometimes change your mind about what you fancy.
items.zh: 每周，因为作为人类，你有时会改变对喜欢事物的主意。

items.en: This is where supermarkets and their anonymity come in handy.
items.zh: 这就是超市及其匿名性派上用场的地方。

items.en: With them, there’s not the same embarrassment as when buying one carrot in a little greengrocer.
items.zh: 有了它们，就不会像在小蔬果商那里买一根胡萝卜那样感到尴尬。

items.en: And if you plan properly, you’ll know that you only need, say, 350g of shin of beef and six rashers of bacon, not whatever weight is pre-packed in the supermarket chiller.
items.zh: 如果你计划得当，就会知道你只需要，比如，350克牛腿肉和六片培根，而不是超市冷藏柜中预包装的重量。

items.en: You may proudly claim to only have frozen peas in the freezer – that’s not good enough.
items.zh: 你可能自豪地声称冷冻柜里只有冷冻豌豆——这还不够好。

items.en: Mine is filled with leftovers, bread, stock, meat and fish.
items.zh: 我的冰箱里装满了剩菜、面包、肉汤、肉类和鱼类。

items.en: Planning ahead should eliminate wastage, but if you have surplus vegetables you’ll do a vegetable soup, and all fruits threatening to “go off” will be cooked or juiced.
items.zh: 提前计划应能消除浪费，但如果你有剩余的蔬菜，就会做蔬菜汤，所有威胁要变坏的水果都会被烹饪或榨汁。

items.en: Everyone says this, but it really is a top tip for frugal eaters.
items.zh: 人人都这么说，但对节俭的食客来说，这确实是一个重要提示。

items.en: Shop at butchers, delis and fish-sellers regularly, even for small things, and be super friendly.
items.zh: 经常去肉铺、熟食店和鱼贩那里购物，即使是为了小事，也要超级友好。

items.en: Soon you’ll feel comfortable asking if they’ve any knuckles of ham for soups and stews, or beef bones, chicken carcasses and fish heads for stock which, more often than not, they’ll let you have for free.
items.zh: 很快你就会习惯询问他们是否有用于汤和炖菜的火腿关节，或者用于高汤的牛骨、鸡架和鱼头，通常他们会免费提供给你。

items.en: You won’t be eating out a lot, but save your pennies and once every few months treat yourself to a set lunch at a good restaurant – £ 1.75 a week for three months gives you £ 21 – more than enough for a three-course lunch at Michelin-starred Arbutus.
items.zh: 你不会经常外出就餐，但节省开支，每隔几个月就犒劳自己一顿好的餐厅套餐午餐——每周存1.75英镑，连续三个月就能存下21英镑——足够在米其林星级餐厅Arbutus享用一顿三道菜的午餐。

items.en: It’s £ 16.95 there – or £ 12.99 for a large pizza from Domino’s: I know which I’d rather eat.
items.zh: 在那里是16.95英镑——或者从Domino’s买一个大披萨只需12.99英镑：我知道我更想吃哪个。

items.en: Most archaeological sites have been located by means of careful searching, while many others have been discovered by accident.
items.zh: 大多数考古遗址是通过仔细搜索确定的，而许多其他遗址则是偶然发现的。

items.en: Olduvai Gorge, an early hominid site in Tanzania, was found by a butterfly hunter who literally fell into its deep valley in 1911.
items.zh: 奥杜威峡谷，一个位于坦桑尼亚的早期人类遗址，于1911年由一位蝴蝶采集者意外发现，当时他真的掉入了其深谷。

items.en: Thousands of Aztec artifacts came to light during the digging of the Mexico City subway in the 1970s.
items.zh: 在1970年代挖掘墨西哥城地铁时，数千件阿兹特克文物被发现。

items.en: At its peak around AD 600, this city was one of the largest human settlements in the world.
items.zh: 在公元600年左右的鼎盛时期，这座城市是世界上最大的人类聚居地之一。

items.en: The researchers mapped not only the city's vast and ornate ceremonial areas, but also hundreds of simpler apartment complexes where common people lived.
items.zh: 研究人员不仅绘制了这座城市广阔而华丽的仪式区，还绘制了数百个普通居民居住的简朴公寓群。

items.en: Typically, they survey and sample (make test excavations on) large areas of terrain to determine where excavation will yield useful information.
items.zh: 通常，他们会勘测和采样（进行试掘）大范围地形，以确定何处挖掘能提供有用信息。

items.en: Surveys and test samples have also become important for understanding the larger landscapes that contain archaeological sites.
items.zh: 调查和测试样本也已成为理解包含考古遗址的更大范围景观的重要手段。

items.en: In one case, many researchers working around the ancient Maya city of Copan, Honduras, have located hundreds of small rural villages and individual dwellings by using aerial photographs and by making surveys on foot.
items.zh: 在洪都拉斯古玛雅城市科潘附近工作的许多研究人员通过使用航空照片和进行徒步调查，已经发现了数百个小型农村村庄和单个住宅。

items.en: The resulting settlement maps show how the distribution and density of the rural population around the city changed dramatically between AD 500 and 850, when Copan collapsed.
items.zh: 由此产生的聚落地图显示，城市周边农村人口的分布和密度在公元500年至850年之间发生了巨大变化，当时科潘城衰落。

items.en: Airborne technologies, such as different types of radar and photographic equipment carried by airplanes or spacecraft, allow archaeologists to learn about what lies beneath the ground without digging.
items.zh: 空中技术，如由飞机或航天器携带的不同类型的雷达和摄影设备，使考古学家能够在不挖掘的情况下了解地下隐藏的遗迹。

items.en: Aerial surveys locate general areas of interest or larger buried features, such as ancient buildings or fields.
items.zh: 航空勘测定位感兴趣的区域或较大的埋藏特征，例如古代建筑或农田。

items.en: Such searches can take years.
items.zh: 这样的搜索可能需要数年时间。

items.en: British archaeologist Howard Carter knew that the tomb of the Egyptian pharaoh Tutankhamun existed from information found in other sites.
items.zh: 英国考古学家霍华德·卡特知道埃及法老图坦卡蒙的墓存在，是根据在其他遗址发现的信息。

items.en: Carter sifted through rubble in the Valley of the Kings for seven years before he located the tomb in 1922.
items.zh: 卡特在1922年发现这座墓穴之前，在国王谷的废墟中搜寻了七年。

items.en: In the late 1800s British archaeologist Sir Arthur Evans combed antique dealers' stores in Athens, Greece.
items.zh: 19世纪末期，英国考古学家艾尔文爵士在希腊雅典搜寻古董商的店铺。

items.en: He was searching for tiny engraved seals attributed to the ancient Mycenaean culture that dominated Greece from the 1400s to 1200s BC.
items.zh: 他正在寻找属于古代迈锡尼文化的微型雕刻印章，这些印章主导了希腊从公元前1400年至公元前1200年。

items.en: Evans's interpretations of these engravings eventually led him to find the Minoan palace at Knossos, on the island of Crete, in 1900.
items.zh: 埃文斯对这些雕刻的解读最终引导他于1900年在克里特岛的克诺索斯发现了米诺斯宫殿。

items.en: Most ground surveys involve a lot of walking, looking for surface clues such as small fragments of pottery.
items.zh: 大多数地面调查涉及大量步行，寻找地表线索，如陶片碎片。

items.en: They often include a certain amount of digging to test for buried materials at selected points across a landscape.
items.zh: 他们通常包括一定量的挖掘，以在景观的特定区域检测埋藏材料。

items.en: Archaeologists also may locate buried remains by using such technologies as ground radar, magnetic-field recording, and metal detectors.
items.zh: 考古学家还可以通过使用地面雷达、磁场记录和金属探测器等技术来定位埋藏的遗骸。

items.en: Archaeologists commonly use computers to map sites and the landscapes around sites.
items.zh: 考古学家通常使用计算机来绘制遗址地图以及遗址周围的景观。

items.en: Two- and three-dimensional maps are helpful tools in planning excavations, illustrating how sites look, and presenting the results of archaeological research.
items.zh: 二维和三维地图是规划挖掘工作、展示遗址外观以及呈现考古研究成果的有用工具。

items.en: Music means different things to different people and sometimes even different things to the same person at different moments of his life.
items.zh: 音乐对不同的人意味着不同的事物，并且有时甚至对同一个人来说在生命的不同时刻也可能意味着不同的事物。

items.en: It might be poetic, philosophical, sensual, or mathematical, but in any case it must, in my view, have something to do with the soul of the human being.
items.zh: 它可能是诗意的、哲学的、感性的或数学的，但无论如何，我认为它必须与人类的灵魂有关。

items.en: Hence it is metaphysical; but the means of expression is purely and exclusively physical: sound.
items.zh: 因此它是形而上学的；但表达方式纯粹且唯一地属于物理层面：声音。

items.en: I believe it is precisely this permanent coexistence of metaphysical message through physical means that is the strength of music.
items.zh: 我相信，正是这种通过物质媒介传达形而上学信息的持久共存，构成了音乐的力量。

items.en: (46) It is also the reason why when we try to describe music with words, all we can do is articulate our reactions to it, and not grasp music itself.
items.zh: (46) 这也是当我们试图用文字描述音乐时，我们所能做的只是表达对它的反应，而无法真正把握音乐本身的原因。

items.en: Beethoven's importance in music has been principally defined by the revolutionary nature of his compositions.
items.zh: 贝多芬在音乐领域的重要性主要由其作品的革命性所定义。

items.en: He freed music from hitherto prevailing conventions of harmony and structure.
items.zh: 他使音乐摆脱了以往盛行的和声与结构传统。

items.en: Sometimes I feel in his late works a will to break all signs of continuity.
items.zh: 有时我在他的晚期作品中感受到一种打破所有连续性迹象的意愿。

items.en: The music is abrupt and seemingly disconnected, as in the last piano sonata.
items.zh: 音乐突兀且看似不连贯，如最后一首钢琴奏鸣曲。

items.en: In musical expression, he did not feel restrained by the weight of convention.
items.zh: 在音乐表达方面，他并未感到传统惯例的束缚。

items.en: (47) By all accounts he was a freethinking person, and a courageous one, and I find courage an essential quality for the understanding, let alone the performance, of his works.
items.zh: 据各方评价，他是一位自由思想的人，也是一位勇敢的人，我认为勇气是他作品理解的关键品质，更不用说其演绎了。

items.en: This courageous attitude in fact becomes a requirement for the performers of Beethoven's music.
items.zh: 这种勇敢的态度实际上已成为贝多芬音乐演奏者的要求。

items.en: His compositions demand the performer to show courage, for example in the use of dynamics.
items.zh: 他的作品要求表演者展现出勇气，例如在力度变化的使用上。

items.en: (48) Beethoven's habit of increasing the volume with an extreme intensity and then abruptly following it with a sudden soft passage was only rarely used by composers before him.
items.zh: (48) 贝多芬习惯将音量提升到极高强度，随后突然接上一个柔和的乐段，这一手法在他之前的作曲家中极少被使用。

items.en: Beethoven was a deeply political man in the broadest sense of the word.
items.zh: 贝多芬在广义上是一个极具政治性的人。

items.en: He was not interested in daily politics, but concerned with questions of moral behavior and the larger questions of right and wrong affecting the entire society.
items.zh: 他对日常政治不感兴趣，但关注道德行为的问题以及影响整个社会的更广泛的是非对错问题。

items.en: (49) Especially significant was his view of freedom, which, for him, was associated with the rights and responsibilities of the individual: he advocated freedom of thought and of personal expression.
items.zh: (49) 他关于自由的观点尤为重要，这在他看来与个人的权利和责任相关联：他倡导思想自由和个人表达自由。

items.en: Beethoven's music tends to move from chaos to order as if order were an imperative of human existence.
items.zh: 贝多芬的音乐往往从混乱走向秩序，仿佛秩序是人类存在的必然要求。

items.en: For him, order does not result from forgetting or ignoring the disorders that plague our existence; order is a necessary development, an improvement that may lead to the Greek ideal of spiritual elevation.
items.zh: 对他而言，秩序并非源于忘记或忽视那些困扰我们存在的混乱；秩序是一种必要的发展，一种可能导向希腊精神升华理想的进步。

items.en: It is not by chance that the Funeral March is not the last movement of the Eroica Symphony, but the second, so that suffering does not have the last word.
items.zh: 葬礼进行曲并非《英雄交响曲》的最后一个乐章，而是第二个乐章，以便苦难不会成为最后的决定。

items.en: (50) One could interpret much of the work of Beethoven by saying that suffering is inevitable, but the courage to fight it renders life worth living.
items.zh: (50) 人们可以这样解读Beethoven的许多作品：苦难是不可避免的，但与之抗争的勇气使生命变得值得。

items.en: Directions: Write a letter of about 100 words to the president of your university, suggesting how to improve students' physical condition.
items.zh: 写作指导：撰写一封约100字的信件，给大学校长，提出改善学生体质的建议。

items.en: You should write neatly on the ANSWER SHEET.
items.zh: 你应该在答题卡上工整书写。

items.en: Thinner isn’t always better.
items.zh: 更瘦并不总是更好。

items.en: A number of studies have 1 that normal-weight people are in fact at higher risk of some diseases compared to those who are overweight.
items.zh: 多项研究显示1正常体重人群实际上比超重人群面临更高的某些疾病风险。

items.en: And there are health conditions for which being overweight is actually 2.
items.zh: 并且存在一些健康状况，超重实际上是2。

items.en: For example, heavier women are less likely to develop calcium deficiency than thin women.
items.zh: 例如，体重较重的女性比体型较瘦的女性不太可能患上钙缺乏。

items.en: 3, among the elderly, being somewhat overweight is often an 4 of good health.
items.zh: 3，对于老年人来说，略微超重通常是健康状况良好的一个 4。

items.en: Of even greater 5 is the fact that obesity turns out to be very difficult to define.
items.zh: 甚至更为重要的5是，肥胖结果证明是非常难以定义的。

items.en: It is often defined 6 body mass index, or BMI.
items.zh: 它通常被定义为6体重指数，或BMI。

items.en: BMI 7 body mass divided by the square of height.
items.zh: BMI 7 体重除以身高的平方。

items.en: An adult with a BMI of 18 to 25 is often considered to be normal weight.
items.zh: 一个成年人的身体质量指数在18至25之间时，通常被认为属于正常体重。

items.en: Between 25 and 30 is overweight.
items.zh: 25到30之间属于超重。

items.en: And over 30 is considered obese.
items.zh: 超过30岁的人被认为肥胖。

items.en: Obesity, 8, can be divided into moderately obese, severely obese, and very severely obese.
items.zh: 肥胖，8，可分为中度肥胖、重度肥胖和极重度肥胖。

items.en: While such numerical standards seem 9, they are not.
items.zh: 虽然这些数字标准似乎9，但并非如此。

items.en: Obesity is probably less a matter of weight than body fat.
items.zh: 肥胖可能与其说是体重问题，不如说是体脂问题。

items.en: Some people with a high BMI are in fact extremely fit, 10 others with a low BMI may be in poor 11.
items.zh: 一些身体质量指数（BMI）较高的人实际上非常健康，10 而身体质量指数较低的其他人可能处于较差的 11 状态。

items.en: For example, many collegiate and professional football players 12 as obese, though their percentage body fat is low.
items.zh: 例如，许多大学和职业橄榄球运动员被 12为肥胖，尽管他们的体脂百分比很低。

items.en: Conversely, someone with a small frame may have high body fat but a 13 BMI.
items.zh: 相反的是，体型较小的人可能体脂率很高，但BMI仅为13。

items.en: Today we have a(n) 14 to label obesity as a disgrace.
items.zh: 今天我们有 14 将肥胖视为一种耻辱。

items.en: The overweight are sometimes 15 in the media with their faces covered.
items.zh: 超重的人有时在媒体中被以15的方式呈现，且脸部被遮盖。

items.en: Stereotypes 16 with obesity include laziness, lack of will power, and lower prospects for success.
items.zh: 与肥胖相关的刻板印象16包括懒惰、缺乏意志力和较低的成功前景。

items.en: Teachers, employers, and health professionals have been shown to harbor biases against the obese.
items.zh: 研究表明，教师、雇主和健康专业人士对肥胖者存在偏见。

items.en: 17 very young children tend to look down on the overweight, and teasing about body build has long been a problem in schools.
items.zh: 17 年龄很小的孩子往往看不起超重的人，而对体型的嘲笑在学校里早就成了一个问题。

items.en: Negative attitudes toward obesity, 18 in health concerns, have stimulated a number of anti-obesity 19.
items.zh: 对肥胖的负面态度，18在健康担忧方面，已经激发了多种反肥胖19。

items.en: My own hospital system has banned sugary drinks from its facilities.
items.zh: 我自己的医院系统已经禁止在其设施中销售含糖饮料。

items.en: Many employers have instituted weight loss and fitness initiatives.
items.zh: 许多雇主已经推出减重和健身计划。

items.en: Michelle Obama has launched a high-visibility campaign 20 childhood obesity, even claiming that it represents our greatest national security threat.
items.zh: 米歇尔·奥巴马发起了一场针对儿童肥胖的高曝光度活动，甚至声称这代表我们最大的国家安全威胁。

items.en: This slim volume is packed with tips to help wage slaves as well as lottery winners get the most “happiness bang for your buck.
items.zh: 这本薄薄的小书塞满了各种技巧，帮助工薪族以及彩票中奖者获得最大的幸福感回报。

items.en: It seems most people would be better off if they could shorten their commutes to work, spend more time with friends and family and less of it watching television (something the average American spends a whopping two months a year doing, and is hardly jollier for it).
items.zh: 如果人们能缩短上下班通勤时间，多花时间与朋友和家人相处，少花时间看电视（美国人平均每年竟花去整整两个月看电视，但因此变得更快乐却很难说），那么大多数人会过得更好。

items.en: “It’s a reflection simply of people generally thinking well of themselves.
items.zh: 这仅仅是人们普遍对自己有良好看法的反映。

items.en: If you are depressed, you won’t be self-enhancing.
items.zh: 如果你情绪低落，你就不会自我提升。

items.en: Why is that?
items.zh: 为什么是这样？

items.en: It is hard
items.zh: 这是困难的

items.en: Read the following text and match each of the numbered items in the left column to its corresponding information in the right column.
items.zh: 阅读以下文字，并将左边列中的每个编号项目与其右边列中对应的相应信息进行匹配。

items.en: Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEERT.
items.zh: 在ANSWER SHEET上标记你的答案。

items.en: Emerging in the late Sixties and reaching a peak in the Seventies, Land Art was one of a range of new forms, including Body Art, Performance Art, Action Art and Installation Art, which pushed art beyond the traditional confines of the studio and gallery.
items.zh: Land Art 于六十年代末出现，并在七十年代达到顶峰，它是包括 Body Art、Performance Art、Action Art 和 Installation Art 在内的一系列新形式之一，这些形式将艺术扩展到了传统画室和画廊之外。

items.en: Rather than portraying landscape, land artists used the physical substance of the land itself as their medium.
items.zh: 土地艺术家并非描绘景观，而是将土地本身的物质作为他们的媒介。

items.en: The British land art, typified by Richard Long’s piece, was not only more domestically scaled, but a lot quirkier than its American counterpart.
items.zh: 英国大地艺术以理查德·朗的作品为代表，不仅规模更小，而且比其美国同类更加古怪。

items.en: Indeed, while you might assume that an exhibition of Land Art would consist only of records of works rather than the works themselves, Long’s photograph of his work is the work.
items.zh: 确实，虽然你可能认为大地艺术展览只包含作品记录而非作品本身，但朗拍摄的作品照片即为作品。

items.en: Since his “action” is in the past, the photograph is its sole embodiment.
items.zh: 由于他的“行为”已成为过去，照片成为其唯一的体现。

items.en: That might seem rather an obscure point, but it sets the tone for an exhibition that contains a lot of black-and-white photographs and relatively few natural objects.
items.zh: 这似乎有些晦涩，但它为一个包含大量黑白照片和相对较少自然物体的展览定下基调。

items.en: Long is Britain’s best-known Land Artist and his Stone Circle, a perfect ring of purplish rocks from Portishead beach laid out on the gallery floor, represents the elegant, rarefied side of the form.
items.zh: Long是英国最著名的大地艺术家，他的作品Stone Circle由波特希德海滩的紫色岩石在画廊地板上铺设成一个完美圆环，代表了这种艺术形式优雅而高雅的一面。

items.en: The Boyle Family, on the other hand, stand for its dirty, urban aspect.
items.zh: 另一方面，The Boyle Family 代表其肮脏的都市一面。

items.en: Comprising artists Mark Boyle and Joan Hills and their children, they recreated random sections of the British landscape on gallery walls.
items.zh: 由艺术家Mark Boyle和Joan Hills及其子女组成，他们在画廊墙壁上再现了英国乡村的随机片段。

items.en: Their Olaf Street Study, a square of brick-strewn waste ground, is one of the few works here to embrace the commonplaceness that characterises most of our experience of the landscape most of the time.
items.zh: 他们的奥拉夫街研究，一片砖块散落的废墟，是这里少数几个接纳我们大部分时间对景观的体验所具有的平凡性的作品之一。

items.en: Parks feature, particularly in the earlier works, such as John Hilliard’s very funny Across the Park, in which a long-haired stroller is variously smiled at by a pretty girl and unwittingly assaulted in a sequence of images that turn out to be different parts of the same photograph.
items.zh: 公园的特色在早期作品中尤为突出，例如约翰·希利亚德非常有趣的《Across the Park》，其中一位长发推婴儿车的人被一位漂亮女孩以不同方式微笑注视，并在一系列图像中被意外地攻击，这些图像最终被揭示为同一张照片的不同部分。

items.en: Generally however British land artists preferred to get away from towns, gravitating towards landscapes that are traditionally considered beautiful such as the Lake District or the Wiltshire Downs.
items.zh: 然而总体而言英国大地艺术家更倾向于远离城镇，选择那些传统上被认为美丽的景观如湖区或威尔特郡丘陵。

items.en: While it probably wasn’t apparent at the time, much of this work is permeated by a spirit of romantic escapism that the likes of Wordsworth would have readily understood.
items.zh: 尽管当时可能并不明显，但这项工作的大部分都充满了浪漫主义逃避现实的精神，这种精神是像Wordsworth这样的人会轻易理解的。

items.en: Derek Jarman’s yellow-tinted film Towards Avebury, a collection of long, mostly still shots of the Wiltshire landscape, evokes a tradition of English landscape painting stretching from Samuel Palmer to Paul Nash.
items.zh: Derek Jarman的泛黄电影《Towards Avebury》由一系列长时间、大多为静态镜头组成的威尔特郡风景集锦，唤起了一种从Samuel Palmer到Paul Nash延续的英国风景画传统。

items.en: In the case of Hamish Fulton, you can’t help feeling that the Scottish artist has simply found a way of making his love of walking pay.
items.zh: 以哈米什·富尔顿为例，你不禁会感到这位苏格兰艺术家只是找到了一种让他的步行爱好获得回报的方式。

items.en: A typical work, such as Seven Days, consists of a single beautiful black-and-white photograph taken on an epic walk, with the mileage and number of days taken listed beneath.
items.zh: 典型的作品如Seven Days由一张美丽的黑白照片组成，该照片拍摄于一次壮丽的徒步旅行中，下方列出了里程数和所用天数。

items.en: British Land Art as shown in this well selected, but relatively modestly scaled exhibition wasn’t about imposing on the landscape, more a kind of landscape-orientated light conceptual art created passing through.
items.zh: 英国大地艺术如本次精心挑选但规模相对较小的展览所示，并非对景观进行强加，而更像是一种以景观为导向的轻概念艺术，通过某种方式创作而成。

items.en: It had its origins in the great outdoors, but the results were as gallery-bound as the paintings of Turner and Constable.
items.zh: 它起源于户外，但结果却像特纳和康斯特布尔的画作一样只能在画廊展出。

items.en: Stone Circle illustrates a kind of landscape-orientated light conceptual art.
items.zh: 石圈，体现了一种以景观为导向的光概念艺术。

items.en: Olaf Street Study reminds people of the English landscape painting tradition.
items.zh: Olaf Street Study，使人们想起英国风景画传统。

items.en: Across the Park represents the elegance of the British land art.
items.zh: 跨过公园，代表了英国大地艺术的优雅。

items.en: Towards Avebury depicts the ordinary side of the British land art.
items.zh: 朝向埃弗伯里，描绘了英国大地艺术的普通一面。

items.en: Seven Days embodies a romantic escape into the Scottish outdoors.
items.zh: Seven Days，体现了浪漫的逃离苏格兰户外。

items.en: Most people would define optimism as being endlessly happy, with a glass that’s perpetually half full.
items.zh: 大多数人会将乐观定义为总是快乐，杯子里永远装着一半的水。

items.en: But that’s exactly the kind of false cheerfulness that positive psychologists wouldn’t recommend.
items.zh: 但这正是积极心理学家不会推荐的那种虚假乐观。

items.en: “Healthy optimism means being in touch with reality,” says Tal Ben-Shahar, a Harvard professor.
items.zh: 健康的乐观意味着正视现实，哈佛大学教授塔尔·本-沙哈尔说。

items.en: According to Ben-Shahar, realistic optimists are those who make the best of things that happen, but not those who believe everything happens for the best.
items.zh: 根据Ben-Shahar的观点，现实乐观者是指那些尽可能利用发生的事情的人，但不是那些认为一切都会向好的方向发展的人。

items.en: Ben-Shahar uses three optimistic exercises.
items.zh: Ben-Shahar采用3个乐观练习。

items.en: When he feels down – say, after giving a bad lecture – he grants himself permission to be human.
items.zh: 当他情绪低落——比如，讲了一堂糟糕的课之后——他允许自己做一个普通人。

items.en: He reminds himself that not every lecture can be a Nobel winner; some will be less effective than others.
items.zh: 他提醒自己，并非每场讲座都能达到诺贝尔奖得主的水平；有些讲座的效果不如其他的。

items.en: Next is reconstruction.
items.zh: 接下来是重建。

items.en: He analyzes the weak lecture, learning lessons for the future about what works and what doesn’t.
items.zh: 他分析了效果不佳的讲座，为未来吸取教训，了解哪些方法有效、哪些无效。

items.en: Finally, there is perspective, which involves acknowledging that in the grand scheme of life, one lecture really doesn’t matter.

items.en: How does your reading proceed?
items.zh: 你的阅读是如何进行的？

items.en: Clearly you try to comprehend, in the sense of identifying meanings for individual words and working out relationships between them, drawing on your implicit knowledge of English grammar.
items.zh: 显然你在试图理解，即为单个单词确定含义并理清它们之间的关系，依靠你对英语语法的隐性知识。

items.en: (41) You begin to infer a context for the text, for instance by making decisions about what kind of speech event is involved: Who is making the utterance, to whom, when and where.
items.zh: （41）你开始为文本推断一个语境，例如通过决定涉及哪种言语事件：谁在发出话语，对谁发出，何时何地。

items.en: The ways of reading indicated here are without doubt kinds of comprehension.
items.zh: 此处指出的阅读方式毫无疑问属于理解方式。

items.en: But they show comprehension to consist not just of passive assimilation but of active engagement in inference and problem-solving.
items.zh: 但他们表明，理解不仅仅是被动吸收，而是对推理和解决问题的主动参与。

items.en: You infer information you feel the writer has invited you to grasp by presenting you with specific evidence and clues.
items.zh: 你通过作者提供的具体证据和线索来推断作者邀请你把握的信息。

items.en: (42) Conceived in this way, comprehension will not follow exactly the same track for each reader.
items.zh: 以这种方式理解的话，每个读者的理解路径都不会完全相同。

items.en: What is in question is not the retrieval of an absolute, fixed or "true" meaning that can be read off and checked for accuracy, or some timeless relation of the text to the world.
items.zh: 问题所在并非是检索一种绝对的、固定的或“真实”的意义，这种意义可以被读取并验证准确性，或文本与世界之间某种永恒的关系。

items.en: (43) Such background material inevitably reflects who we are.
items.zh: (43) 这样的背景资料必然反映我们是谁。

items.en: (44) This doesn't, however, make interpretation merely relative or even pointless.
items.zh: 然而，这并不意味着解释仅仅是相对的，甚至毫无意义。

items.en: Precisely because readers from different historical periods, places and social experiences produce different but overlapping readings of the same words on the page - including for texts that engage with fundamental human concerns - debates about texts can play an important role in social discussion of beliefs and values.
items.zh: 正是由于来自不同历史时期、地点和社会背景的读者对同一页上的文字会产生不同的但重叠的解读——包括那些探讨基本人性问题的文本——关于文本的争论可以在社会对信仰和价值观的讨论中发挥重要作用。

items.en: How we read a given text also depends to some extent on our particular interest in reading it.
items.zh: 我们阅读某段文字的方式在某种程度上取决于我们对该文字的特定兴趣。

items.en: (45) Such dimensions of reading suggest - as others introduced later in the book will also do - that we bring an implicit (often unacknowledged) agenda to any act of reading.
items.zh: 阅读的这些维度表明——正如书中后面介绍的其他内容也将表明的那样——我们在任何阅读行为中都会带着一种隐含的（常常未被承认的）议程。

items.en: It doesn't then necessarily follow that one kind of reading is fuller, more advanced or more worthwhile than another.
items.zh: 因此，并不必然意味着某种阅读比另一种更充实、更高级或更有价值。

items.en: Ideally, different kinds of reading inform each other, and act as useful reference points for and counterbalances to one another.
items.zh: 理想情况下，不同类型的阅读相互启发，并作为彼此的有用参考点和平衡力量。

items.en: Together, they make up the reading component of your overall literacy, or relationship to your surrounding textual environment.
items.zh: 它们共同构成了你的整体读写能力，即你与周围文本环境的关系。

items.en: Within the span of a hundred years, in the seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries, a tide of emigration - one of the great folk wanderings of history - swept from Europe to America.
items.zh: 在17世纪和18世纪初的一百年间，一场移民浪潮——历史上最伟大的民间迁徙之一——席卷了从欧洲到美洲。

items.en: (46) This movement, driven by powerful and diverse motivations, built a nation out of a wilderness and, by its nature, shaped the character and destiny of an uncharted continent.
items.zh: (46) 这一运动由强大而多样的动机驱动，在荒野中建立了一个国家，并因其本质塑造了未被开发的大陆的品格与命运。

items.en: (47) The United States is the product of two principal forces - the immigration of European peoples with their varied ideas, customs, and national characteristics and the impact of a new country which modified these traits.
items.zh: （47）美国是两种主要力量的产物——欧洲各民族带着各自不同的思想、习俗和民族特征的移民，以及一个新国家对这些特征的改变所产生的影响。

items.en: Of necessity, colonial America was a projection of Europe.
items.zh: 出于必要，殖民地美国是欧洲的延伸。

items.en: Across the Atlantic came successive groups of Englishmen, Frenchmen, Germans, Scots, Irishmen, Dutchmen, Swedes, and many others who attempted to transplant their habits and traditions to the new world.
items.zh: 一批又一批的英国人、法国人、德国人、苏格兰人、爱尔兰人、荷兰人和瑞典人跨过大西洋来到新大陆，试图将他们的习惯和传统移植到新世界。

items.en: (48) But the force of geographic conditions peculiar to America, the interplay of the varied national groups upon one another, and the sheer difficulty of maintaining old-world ways in a raw, new continent caused significant changes.
items.zh: 但美国特有的地理条件的力量、各种民族群体之间的相互作用，以及在原始的新大陆上维持旧世界传统方式的巨大困难导致了重大变化。

items.en: These changes were gradual and at first scarcely visible.
items.zh: 这些变化是逐渐发生的，起初几乎难以察觉。

items.en: But the result was a new social pattern which, although it resembled European society in many ways, had a character that was distinctly American.
items.zh: 但结果却形成了一种新的社会模式，尽管它在许多方面与欧洲社会相似，却具有鲜明的美国特色。

items.en: (49) The first shiploads of immigrants bound for the territory which is now the United States crossed the Atlantic more than a hundred years after the 15th- and 16th-century explorations of North America.
items.zh: (49) 第一批前往如今成为美国的领土的移民船队，是在15世纪和16世纪的北美探险之后一百多年才横渡大西洋的。

items.en: In the meantime, thriving Spanish colonies had been established in Mexico, the West Indies, and South America.
items.zh: 与此同时，西班牙已在墨西哥、西印度群岛和南美洲建立了繁荣的殖民地。

items.en: These travelers to North America came in small, unmercifully overcrowded craft.
items.zh: 这些前往北美的旅行者乘坐的是小型且残酷地过度拥挤的船只。

items.en: During their six-to-twelve-week voyage, they survived on barely enough food allotted to them.
items.zh: 在为期六至十二周的航行中，他们仅靠分配给他们的勉强足够的食物维持生命。

items.en: Many of the ships were lost in storms, many passengers died of disease, and infants rarely survived the journey.
items.zh: 许多船只在风暴中失散，许多乘客死于疾病，婴儿很少能幸存下来。

items.en: Sometimes storms blew the vessels far off their course, and often calm brought unbearably long delay.
items.zh: 有时风暴会将船只吹离原定航线，而平静的天气常导致难以忍受的漫长延误。

items.en: To the anxious travelers the sight of the American shore brought almost inexpressible relief.
items.zh: 对焦虑的旅客来说，看到美国海岸几乎难以言表的宽慰。

items.en: Said one recorder of events, "The air at twelve leagues' distance smelt as sweet as a new-blown garden.
items.zh: 一位事件记录者说，十二里外的空气闻起来和一个新开放的花园一样甜美。

items.en: The colonists' first glimpse of the new land was a sight of dense woods.
items.zh: 殖民者第一次看到新大陆时，映入眼帘的是茂密的森林。

items.en: (50) The virgin forest with its richness and variety of trees was a real treasure-house which extended from Maine all the way down to Georgia.
items.zh: 原始森林以其树木的丰富多样，是一个真正的宝库，从缅因州一直延伸到佐治亚州。

items.en: Here was abundant fuel and lumber.
items.zh: 此处燃料和木材充足。

items.en: Here was the raw material of houses and furniture, ships and potash, dyes and naval stores.
items.zh: 这里就是住房、家具、船只、钾肥、染料和海军储备的原材料。

items.en: Some Old Truths to Help You Overcome Tough Times
items.zh: 一些老生常谈帮助你克服困难时刻

items.en: Unfortunately, life is not a bed of roses.
items.zh: 不幸的是，人生并非一帆风顺。

items.en: We are going through life facing sad experiences.
items.zh: 我们经历人生时正面对悲伤的经历。

items.en: Moreover, we are grieving various kinds of loss: a friendship, a romantic relationship or a house.
items.zh: 此外，我们正在哀悼各种各样的丧失：一段友谊、一段浪漫关系或一所房子。

items.en: Hard times may hold you down at what usually seems like the most inopportune time, but you should remember that they won’t last forever.
items.zh: 艰难时期可能在你通常认为最不合适的时机把你压倒，但你应该记住它们不会永远持续。

items.en: When our time of mourning is over, we press forward, stronger with a greater understanding and respect for life.
items.zh: 当我们的哀悼期结束时，我们继续前进，带着对生命的更深刻理解和尊重，更加坚强。

items.en: Furthermore, these losses make us mature and eventually move us toward future opportunities for growth and happiness.
items.zh: 此外，这些损失使我们变得成熟，并最终引导我们走向未来成长和幸福的机会。

items.en: I want to share these old truths I’ve learned along the way.
items.zh: 我想分享这些在旅途中学到的古老真理。

items.en: Fear is both useful and harmful.
items.zh: 恐惧既有用处又有害处。

items.en: This normal human reaction is used to protect us by signaling danger and preparing us to deal with it.
items.zh: 这种正常的人类反应被用来保护我们，通过发出危险信号并准备我们应对它。

items.en: Unfortunately, people create inner barriers with a help of exaggerating fears.
items.zh: 不幸的是，人们通过夸大恐惧来制造内在障碍。

items.en: My favorite actor Will Smith once said, “Fear is not real.
items.zh: 我最喜欢的演员Will Smith曾说，恐惧并非真实。

items.en: It is a product of thoughts you create.
items.zh: 它是你创造的思想的产物。

items.en: Do not misunderstand me.
items.zh: 不要误解我。

items.en: Danger is very real.
items.zh: 危险确实存在。

items.en: But fear is a choice.
items.zh: 但恐惧是一种选择。

items.en: I do completely agree that fears are just the product of our luxuriant imagination.
items.zh: 我确实完全同意，恐惧只是我们丰富想象力的产物。

items.en: If you are surrounded by problems and cannot stop thinking about the past, try to focus on the present moment.
items.zh: 如果你被问题包围且总想着过去，试着专注于当下。

items.en: Many of us are weighed down by the past or anxious about the future.
items.zh: 我们中许多人被过去所压垮，或对未来感到焦虑。

items.en: You may feel guilt over your past, but you are poisoning the present with the things and circumstances you cannot change.
items.zh: 你可能会为过去感到愧疚，但你正用那些无法改变的事物和处境来毒害现在。

items.en: Value the present moment and remember how fortunate you are to be alive.
items.zh: 珍惜当下时刻并记住你活着是多么幸运。

items.en: Enjoy the beauty of the world around and keep the eyes open to see the possibilities before you.
items.zh: 欣赏周围世界的美丽并保持警觉以发现眼前的机会。

items.en: Happiness is not a point of future and not a moment from the past, but a mindset that can be designed into the present.
items.zh: 幸福不是未来的某个时刻，也不是过去的某个瞬间，而是可以融入当下的心态。

items.en: Sometimes it is easy to feel bad because you are going through tough times.
items.zh: 有时候你会因为正在经历艰难时期而很容易感到糟糕。

items.en: You can be easily caught up by life problems that you forget to pause and appreciate the things you have.
items.zh: 你可能会被生活中的问题所困扰，以至于忘记停下来欣赏你所拥有的东西。

items.en: Only strong people prefer to smile and value their life instead of crying and complaining about something.
items.zh: 只有坚强的人更倾向于微笑并珍惜生命，而不是哭泣和抱怨某事。

items.en: No matter how isolated you might feel and how serious the situation is, you should always remember that you are not alone.
items.zh: 无论你可能感到多么孤立，无论情况多么严重，你都应该始终记住你并不孤单。

items.en: Try to keep in mind that almost everyone respects and wants to help you if you are trying to make a good change in your life, especially your dearest and nearest people.
items.zh: 请记住，如果你正在努力改善生活，几乎每个人都会尊重并愿意帮助你，尤其是你最亲爱和最亲近的人。

items.en: You may have a circle of friends who provide constant good humor, help and companionship.
items.zh: 你可能拥有一群朋友，他们能持续带来欢乐、提供帮助并给予陪伴。

items.en: If you have no friends or relatives, try to participate in several online communities, full of people who are always willing to share advice and encouragement.
items.zh: 如果你没有朋友或亲戚，尝试参与几个在线社区，这些社区充满乐于分享建议和鼓励的人。

items.en: Today many people find it difficult to trust their own opinion and seek balance by gaining objectivity from external sources.
items.zh: 如今许多人发现难以信任自己的观点，转而通过从外部来源获取客观性来寻求平衡。

items.en: This way you devalue your opinion and show that you are incapable of managing your own life.
items.zh: 这样你会贬低自己的观点并表明你无法管理自己的生活。

items.en: When you are struggling to achieve something important you should believe in yourself and be sure that your decision is the best.
items.zh: 当你努力实现重要目标时，应该相信自己并确信自己的决定是最好的。

items.en: You live in your skin, think your own thoughts, have your own values and make your own choices.
items.zh: 你以自己的身体生活，思考自己的想法，拥有自己的价值观并做出自己的选择。

items.en: Think about driving a route that’s very familiar.
items.zh: 想想驾驶一条非常熟悉的路线。

items.en: It could be your commute to work, a trip into town or the way home.
items.zh: 可能是你上班的通勤，也可能是进城的行程，或者是回家的路。

items.en: Whichever it is, you know every twist and turn like the back of your hand.
items.zh: 不管是什么，你都对每一个曲折和转折了如指掌。

items.en: On these sorts of trips it’s easy to lose concentration on the driving and pay little attention to the passing scenery.
items.zh: 在这些类型的旅行中，很容易在驾驶时分心，对沿途风景也关注甚少。

items.en: The consequence is that you perceive that the trip has taken less time than it actually has.
items.zh: 结果是你觉得这次旅行所花的时间比实际所花的时间要少。

items.en: This is the well-travelled road effect: People tend to underestimate the time it takes to travel a familiar route.
items.zh: 这是熟路效应：人们倾向于低估走熟悉路线所需的时间。

items.en: The effect is caused by the way we allocate our attention.
items.zh: 这种效果源于我们分配注意力的方式。

items.en: When we travel down a well-known route, because we don’t have to concentrate much, time seems to flow more quickly.
items.zh: 当我们沿着熟悉的路线旅行时，由于不需要集中太多注意力，时间似乎过得更快。

items.en: And afterwards, when we come to think back on it, we can’t remember the journey well because we didn’t pay much attention to it.
items.zh: 之后当我们回想起来时，我们无法很好地记住这段旅程，因为我们当时没有给予太多关注。

items.en: So we assume it was shorter.
items.zh: 因此我们假设它更短。

items.en: Suppose your university is going to host a summer camp for high school students.
items.zh: 假设你们大学将举办一个针对高中生的暑期夏令营。

items.en: Write a notice to briefly introduce the camp activities, and call for volunteers.
items.zh: 撰写一则通知，简要介绍夏令营活动并招募志愿者。

items.en: Do not use your name or the name of your university.
items.zh: 不要使用你的名字或你所在大学的名称。

items.en: In Cambodia, the choice of a spouse is a complex one for the young male.
items.zh: 在柬埔寨，年轻男性选择配偶是个复杂的问题。

items.en: It may involve not only his parents and his friends, 1 those of the young woman, but also a matchmaker.
items.zh: 它可能不仅涉及他的父母和朋友，1女方的亲友，还可能涉及一名媒人。

items.en: A young man can 2 a likely spouse on his own and then ask his parents to 3 the marriage negotiations, or the young man's parents may make the choice of a spouse, giving the child little to say in the selection.
items.zh: 年轻男子可以自己 2 一位可能的配偶，然后请父母来 3 婚姻谈判，或者年轻男子的父母可能做出选择配偶的决定，让孩子在选择中几乎没有发言权。

items.en: 4 a girl may veto the spouse her parents have chosen.
items.zh: 4 一个女孩可能否决父母为她选择的配偶。

items.en: 5 a spouse has been selected, each family investigates the other to make sure its child is marrying 6 a good family.
items.zh: 5 一旦选定配偶，每个家庭都会调查对方，以确保自己的孩子能与 6一个好家庭联姻。

items.en: The traditional wedding is a long and colorful affair.
items.zh: 传统婚礼是一个漫长而丰富多彩的活动。

items.en: Formerly it lasted three days, 7 by the 1980s it more commonly lasted a day and a half.
items.zh: 以前它持续三天，7到20世纪80年代，它通常持续一天半。

items.en: Buddhist priests offer a short sermon and 8 prayers of blessing.
items.zh: 佛教僧侣提供一次简短的布道和 8 个祝福祈祷。

items.en: Parts of the ceremony involve ritual hair cutting, 9 cotton threads soaked in holy water around the bride's and groom's wrists, and 10 a candle around a circle of happily married and respected couples to bless the 11 .
items.zh: 仪式部分包括仪式性理发、9根浸过圣水的棉线缠绕在新娘和新郎的手腕上，以及10将蜡烛环绕在一群幸福美满且受人尊敬的夫妻周围以祝福11。

items.en: Newlyweds traditionally move in with the wife's parents and may 12 with them up to a year, 13 they can build a new house nearby.
items.zh: 新婚夫妇传统上会搬去和妻子的父母同住，可能与他们同住长达一年，13他们可以在附近建新房。

items.en: Divorce is legal and easy to 14 , but not common.
items.zh: 离婚是合法且易于14，但并不常见。

items.en: Divorced persons are 15 with some disapproval.
items.zh: 离婚人士中有15人不赞同。

items.en: Each spouse retains 16 property he or she 17 into the marriage, and jointly-acquired property is 18 equally.
items.zh: 每名配偶保有其在婚姻中带入的16财产，共同财产则按18进行分割。

items.en: Divorced persons may remarry, but a gender prejudice 19 up: The divorced male doesn't have a waiting period before he can remarry 20 the woman must wait ten months.
items.zh: 离婚人士可以再婚，但存在一种性别偏见19：离婚男性再婚前无需等待期，而女性必须等待十个月。

items.en: That's a start.
items.zh: 那是一个开始。

items.en: There are two extra subheadings.
items.zh: 有两个额外的子标题。

items.en: Mental health is our birthright.
items.zh: 心理健康是我们的天赋权利。

items.en: (46) We don't have to learn how to be mentally healthy; it is built into us in the same way that our bodies know how to heal a cut or mend a broken bone.
items.zh: 我们不必学习如何保持心理健康；它与生俱来，就像我们的身体知道如何愈合伤口或修复骨折的骨头一样。

items.en: Mental health can't be learned, only reawakened.
items.zh: 心理健康无法学习，只能重新唤醒。

items.en: It is like the immune system of the body, which under stress or through lack of nutrition or exercise can be weakened, but which never leaves us.
items.zh: 它就像人体的免疫系统，在压力下或因缺乏营养和锻炼而可能被削弱，但永远不会离开我们。

items.en: When we don't understand the value of mental health and we don't know how to gain access to it, mental health will remain hidden from us.
items.zh: 当我们不理解心理健康的价值且不知道如何获得其帮助时，心理健康对我们而言仍然是隐藏的。

items.en: (47) Our mental health doesn't really go away; like the sun behind a cloud, it can be hidden but not extinguished, and it is always there to guide us.
items.zh: (47)我们的心理健康并不会真正消失；就像云层后的太阳，它可能被遮蔽但不会熄灭，始终在那里指引我们。

items.en: Mental health is the seed that contains self-esteem - confidence in ourselves and an ability to trust in our common sense.
items.zh: 心理健康是包含自尊的种子——对自己有信心以及相信自己常识的能力。

items.en: It allows us to have perspective on our lives - the ability to not take ourselves too seriously, to laugh at ourselves, to see the bigger picture, and to see that things will work out.
items.zh: 它让我们能够以更开阔的视角看待生活——不把事情看得太重，学会自嘲，看到大局，并相信事情终会好转。

items.en: It's a form of innate or unlearned optimism.
items.zh: 这是一种天生的或未经学习的乐观主义。

items.en: (48) Mental health allows us to view others with sympathy if they are having troubles, with kindness if they are in pain, and with unconditional love no matter who they are.
items.zh: 心理健康使我们能够以同情心看待遇到困难的人，以善意对待身处痛苦的人，以及无论对方是谁都给予无条件的爱。

items.en: Mental health is the source of creativity for solving problems, resolving conflict, making our surroundings more beautiful, managing our home life, or coming up with a creative business idea or invention to make our lives easier.
items.zh: 心理健康是解决问题、化解冲突、美化环境、管理家庭生活，或提出创新商业构想和发明以简化生活的创造力源泉。

items.en: It gives us patience for ourselves and toward others as well as patience while driving, catching a fish, working on our car, or raising a child.
items.zh: 它给予我们对自己和对他人的耐心，以及在驾驶、钓鱼、修理汽车或养育孩子时的耐心。

items.en: It allows us to see the beauty that surrounds us each moment in nature, in culture, in the flow of our daily lives.
items.zh: 它让我们看到每一刻存在于自然、文化以及日常生活的流动中的美丽。

items.en: (49) Although mental health is the cure-all for living our lives, it is perfectly ordinary as you will see that it has been there to direct you through all your difficult decisions.
items.zh: （49）尽管心理健康是生活的万能药，但正如你将看到的，它一直都在帮助你度过所有困难的决定。

items.en: It has been available even in the most mundane of life situations to show you right from wrong, good from bad, friend from foe.
items.zh: 它甚至在最普通的生活中也能帮助你分辨对错、好坏、朋友与敌人。

items.en: Mental health has commonly been called conscience, instinct, wisdom, common sense, or the inner voice.
items.zh: 心理健康通常被称为良知、本能、智慧、常识或内心声音。

items.en: We think of it simply as a healthy and helpful flow of intelligent thought.
items.zh: 我们仅仅将其视为一种健康且有益的智能思维流动。

items.en: (50) As we can learn to think in a healthy way, we can also unlearn it, and that is what we need to focus on - to relearn how to be mentally healthy.
items.zh: 随着我们学会以健康的方式思考，我们也可以忘记这种思考方式，而我们需要关注的是——重新学习如何保持心理健康。

items.en: Directions: Suppose you are a librarian in your university.
items.zh: 说明：假设你是大学的一名图书管理员。

items.en: Write a notice of about 100 words, providing the newly-enrolled international students with relevant information about the library.
items.zh: 写一份约100字的通知，向新入学的国际学生提供有关图书馆的相关信息。

items.en: Directions: Write an essay of 160-200 words based on the following pictures.
items.zh: 写作说明：根据下图写一篇160至200词的作文。

items.en: In your essay, you should 1) describe the pictures briefly, 2) interpret the meaning, and 3) give your comments.
items.zh: 在你的作文中，你应该1）简要描述图片，2）阐释其含义，3）发表你的评论。

items.en: Happy people work differently.
items.zh: 快乐的人工作方式不同。

items.en: They’re more productive, more creative, and willing to take greater risks.
items.zh: 他们更高效，更具创造力，以及更愿意承担更大风险。

items.en: And new research suggests that happiness might influence 1 firms work, too.
items.zh: 新的研究表明，幸福感可能也会影响1企业的运营。

items.en: Companies located in places with happier people invest more, according to a recent research paper.
items.zh: 根据最近的一篇研究论文，位于人们更快乐地区的企业投资更多。

items.en: 2, firms in happy places spend more on R&D (research and development).
items.zh: 2，幸福地区的企业在研发（research and development）上花费更多。

items.en: That’s because happiness is linked to the kind of longer-term thinking 3 for making investments for the future.
items.zh: 这是因为幸福感与那种为未来进行投资的长远思维3相关。

items.en: The researchers wanted to know if the 4 and inclination for risk-taking that come with happiness would 5 the way companies invested.
items.zh: 研究人员想知道伴随幸福的 4和冒险倾向是否会 5公司投资的方式。

items.en: So they compared U.S. cities’ average happiness 6 by Gallup polling with the investment activity of publicly traded firms in those areas.
items.zh: 因此他们将美国城市居民的平均幸福感6通过盖洛普民意调查与这些地区上市公司的投资活动进行比较。

items.en: 7 enough, firms’ investment and R&D intensity were correlated with the happiness of the area in which they were 8 .
items.zh: 7 足够，企业的投资和研发强度与他们所在的地区的幸福指数相关。

items.en: But is it really happiness that’s linked to investment, or could something else about happier cities 9 why firms there spend more on R&D?
items.zh: 但真正与投资相关的是幸福，还是更幸福的城市中存在其他因素导致这些公司更愿意在研发上投入更多资金？

items.en: To find out, the researchers controlled for various 10 that might make firms more likely to invest – like size, industry, and sales – and for indicators that a place was 11 to live in, like growth in wages or population.
items.zh: 为查明这一点，研究人员控制了可能使企业更可能投资的各种10，如规模、行业和销售额，以及一个地方是否适合居住的指标11，如工资或人口的增长。

items.en: The link between happiness and investment generally 12 even after accounting for these things.
items.zh: 幸福与投资之间的关联通常在12即使考虑了这些因素

items.en: The correlation between happiness and investment was particularly strong for younger firms, which the authors 13 to “less codified decision making process” and the possible presence of “younger and less 14 managers who are more likely to be influenced by sentiment.
items.zh: 幸福感与投资之间的相关性在年轻企业中尤为显著，这被作者归因于“决策流程不够制度化”以及可能存在“年轻且缺乏经验的管理者，他们更容易受到情绪影响”。

items.en: The relationship was 15 stronger in places where happiness was spread more 16.
items.zh: 关系在15处更强，在幸福传播得更16的地方。

items.en: Firms seem to invest more in places where most people are relatively happy, rather than in places with happiness inequality.
items.zh: 公司似乎更倾向于在大多数人相对幸福的地方投资，而不是在存在幸福不平等的地方投资。

items.en: 17 this doesn’t prove that happiness causes firms to invest more or to take a longer-term view, the authors believe it at least 18 at that possibility.
items.zh: 17 这并不能证明幸福感导致企业投资更多或采取更长远的观点，作者认为它至少 18 这种可能性。

items.en: It’s not hard to imagine that local culture and sentiment would help 19 how executives think about the future.
items.zh: 它不难想象，本地文化和情感会影响 19高管们如何思考未来。

items.en: “It surely seems plausible that happy people would be more forward-thinking and creative and 20 R&D more than the average,” said one researcher.
items.zh: 快乐的人显然更具有前瞻性且更有创造力，其研发比平均水平多20%。

items.en: The web’s full of articles offering tips on making time to read: “Give up TV” or “Carry a book with you at all times.
items.zh: 网络上有很多文章提供如何腾出时间阅读的建议：放弃看电视或随时随身带一本书。

items.en: But in my experience, using such methods to free up the odd 30 minutes doesn’t work.
items.zh: 但根据我的经验，使用这些方法来腾出零散的30分钟并不奏效。

items.en: The modern mind, Tim Parks, a novelist and critic, writes, “is overwhelmingly inclined toward communication.
items.zh: 现代人的思维，小说家兼评论家蒂姆·帕克斯写道，极度倾向于交流。

items.en: It is not simply that one is interrupted; it is that one is actually inclined to interruption.
items.zh: 问题不在于某人被中断；而在于某人实际上倾向于被中断。

items.en: Deep reading requires not just time, but a special kind of time which can’t be obtained merely by becoming more efficient.
items.zh: 深度阅读不仅需要时间，还需要一种无法仅通过提高效率来获得的特殊时间。

items.en: “The future comes at us like empty bottles along an unstoppable and nearly infinite conveyor belt,” writes Gary Eberle in his book Sacred Time, and “we feel a pressure to fill these different-sized bottles (days, hours, minutes) as they pass, for if they get by without being filled, we will have wasted them.
items.zh: Gary Eberle在《Sacred Time》一书中写道：未来像空瓶子一样沿着一条无法停止且几乎无限的传送带向我们涌来，我们感受到一种压力，必须在它们经过时填满这些不同大小的瓶子（天、小时、分钟），因为如果它们未被填满而通过，我们就会浪费了它们。

items.en: No mind-set could be worse for losing yourself in a book.
items.zh: 没有比沉浸在书中更糟糕的心态了。

items.en: You’d think this might fuel the efficiency mind-set, but in fact, Eberle notes, such ritualistic behaviour helps us “step outside time’s flow” into “soul time.
items.zh: 你可能会认为这会促进效率心态，但事实上，Eberle指出，这种仪式化行为帮助我们脱离时间的流动，进入“灵魂时间”。

items.en: You could limit distractions by reading only physical books, or on single-purpose e-readers.
items.zh: 你可以通过只读纸质书或使用单一用途的电子阅读器来减少干扰。

items.en: Even now that he is working steadily, he said, “I can’t afford to pay my monthly mortgage payments on my own, so I have to rent rooms out to people to make that happen.
items.zh: 即使现在他工作稳定了，他说，我无法独自承担每月的按揭贷款，所以必须把房间租给别人来实现这一点。

items.en: Looking back, he is struck that his parents could provide a comfortable life for their children even though neither had completed college when he was young.
items.zh: 回想起来，他感到惊讶的是，尽管他年轻时父母都没有完成大学学业，他们却能为孩子提供舒适的生活。

items.zh: 变得愚蠢

items.zh: 请求帮助

items.zh: 表达你的情绪

items.en: Don’t overthink it
items.zh: 不要过度思考

items.zh: 注意事物

items.en: As adults, it seems that we are constantly pursuing happiness, often with mixed results.
items.zh: 作为成年人，我们似乎一直在追求幸福，但结果往往参差不齐。

items.en: Yet children appear to have it down to an art – and for the most part they don’t need self-help books or therapy.
items.zh: 然而，孩子们似乎已经将它掌握得非常娴熟——大多数情况下他们并不需要自助书籍或心理治疗。

items.en: Instead, they look after their wellbeing instinctively, and usually more effectively than we do as grownups.
items.zh: 相反，他们本能地照顾自己的福祉，而且通常比我们作为成年人做得更有效。

items.en: Perhaps it’s time to learn a few lessons from them.
items.zh: 也许该从他们身上吸取一些教训了。

items.en: What does a child do when he’s sad?
items.zh: 当孩子感到悲伤时，他会做什么？

items.en: He cries.
items.zh: 他哭了。

items.en: When he’s angry?
items.zh: 他什么时候生气？

items.en: He shouts.
items.zh: 他大喊。

items.en: Scared?
items.zh: 害怕吗？

items.en: Probably a bit of both.
items.zh: 可能两者都有。

items.en: As we grow up, we learn to control our emotions so they are manageable and don’t dictate our behaviours, which is in many ways a good thing.
items.zh: 随着我们成长，我们学会了控制情绪，使其变得可控且不支配我们的行为，这在很多方面都是好事。

items.en: But too often we take this process too far and end up suppressing emotions, especially negative ones.
items.zh: 但人们常常把这个过程推进得太远，结果压抑了情绪，尤其是负面情绪。

items.en: That’s about as effective as brushing dirt under a carpet and can even make us ill.
items.zh: 这和把脏东西扫到地毯下一样有效，甚至可能让我们生病。

items.en: What we need to do is find a way to acknowledge and express what we feel appropriately, and then – again, like children – move on.
items.zh: 我们需要做的是找到一种适当承认和表达我们感受的方式，然后——就像孩子一样——继续前进。

items.en: A couple of Christmases ago, my youngest stepdaughter, who was nine years old at the time, got a Superman T-shirt for Christmas.
items.zh: 几年前的一个圣诞节，我最小的继女当时才九岁，收到了一件超人T恤作为圣诞礼物。

items.en: It cost less than a fiver but she was overjoyed, and couldn’t stop talking about it.
items.zh: 它花费不到5英镑但她却欣喜若狂，并且不停地谈论它。

items.en: Too often we believe that a new job, bigger house or better car will be the magic silver bullet that will allow us to finally be content, but the reality is these things have very little lasting impact on our happiness levels.
items.zh: 我们常常认为一份新工作、更大的房子或更好的汽车会成为让我们最终感到满足的灵丹妙药，但现实是这些事物对我们的幸福水平几乎没有持久影响。

items.en: Instead, being grateful for small things every day
items.zh: 相反，每天对小事心怀感恩

items.en: is a much better way to improve wellbeing.
items.zh: 是一种更有效的方法来提升幸福感。

items.en: Have you ever noticed how much children laugh?
items.zh: 你有没有注意到孩子们笑得多？

items.en: If we adults could indulge in a bit of silliness and giggling, we would reduce the stress hormones in our bodies, increase good hormones like endorphins, improve blood flow to our hearts and even have a greater chance of fighting off infection.
items.zh: 如果成年人能偶尔放纵一下傻气和傻笑，就能减少体内的压力荷尔蒙，增加如内啡肽等有益荷尔蒙，改善心脏的血液流动，甚至更有可能抵抗感染。

items.en: All of which would, of course, have a positive effect on our happiness levels.
items.zh: 所有这些都会对我们的幸福感产生积极影响。

items.en: The problem with being a grownup is that there’s an awful lot of serious stuff to deal with – work, mortgage payments, figuring out what to cook for dinner.
items.zh: 成为成年人的问题在于，你得面对一大堆严肃的事情——工作、按揭还款、决定晚餐做什么菜。

items.en: But as adults we also have the luxury of being able to control our own diaries and it’s important that we schedule in time to enjoy the things we love.
items.zh: 但作为成年人，我们也有控制自己日程安排的特权，重要的是我们要安排时间去享受自己喜爱的事物。

items.en: Those things might be social, sporting, creative or completely random (dancing around the living room, anyone?) – it doesn’t matter, so long as they’re enjoyable, and not likely to have negative side effects, such as drinking too much alcohol or going on a wild spending spree if you’re on a tight budget.
items.zh: 这些事情可能是社交、运动、创意或完全随机的（比如在客厅跳舞，谁没试过？）——这并不重要，只要它们令人愉快且不太可能产生负面副作用，例如过度饮酒或在预算紧张时疯狂消费。

items.en: Having said all of the above, it’s important to add that we shouldn’t try too hard to be happy.
items.zh: 鉴于上述，需要补充的是我们不应过分努力追求快乐。

items.en: Scientists tell us this can backfire and actually have a negative impact on our wellbeing.
items.zh: 科学家告诉我们，这可能会适得其反，对我们的福祉产生负面影响。

items.en: As the Chinese philosopher Chuang Tzu is reported to have said: “Happiness is the absence of striving for happiness.
items.zh: 据中国哲学家庄子所言：幸福是不追求幸福的状态。

items.en: And in that, once more, we need to look to the example of our children, to whom happiness is not a goal but a natural byproduct of the way they live.
items.zh: 在这一点上，我们再次需要以孩子们为例，对他们来说，幸福不是目标，而是他们生活方式的自然结果。

items.en: The supermarket is designed to lure customers into spending as much time as possible within its doors.
items.zh: 超市旨在诱使顾客尽可能多地在店内停留。

items.en: The reason for this is simple: The longer you stay in the store, the more stuff you’ll see, and the more stuff you see, the more you’ll buy.
items.zh: 原因很简单：你在商店停留的时间越长，看到的商品就越多，看到的商品越多，购买的东西也就越多。

items.en: And supermarkets contain a lot of stuff.
items.zh: 而且超市有很多东西。

items.en: The average supermarket, according to the Food Marketing Institute, carries some 44,000 different items, and many carry tens of thousands more.
items.zh: 根据美国食品营销协会的数据，普通超市约拥有44000种不同商品，许多超市还拥有数万种更多商品。

items.en: The sheer volume of available choice is enough to send shoppers into a state of information overload.
items.zh: 可选商品数量庞大，足以让购物者陷入信息过载的状态。

items.en: According to brain-scan experiments, the demands of so much decision-making quickly become too much for us.
items.zh: 根据脑扫描实验，如此多的决策需求很快对我们来说变得太多。

items.en: After about 40 minutes of shopping, most people stop struggling to be rationally selective, and instead begin shopping emotionally – which is the point at which we accumulate the 50 percent of stuff in our cart that we never intended buying.
items.zh: 购物大约40分钟后，大多数人停止理性选择，转而开始情绪化购物，这时我们购物车里已有50%的东西是原本没有打算购买的。

items.en: Suppose you won a translation contest and your friend, Jack, wrote an email to congratulate you and ask for advice on translation.
items.zh: 假设你赢得了一场翻译比赛，你的朋友Jack给你写了一封电子邮件，祝贺你并请求翻译方面的建议。

items.en: Write him a reply to thank him, and give your advice.
items.zh: 给他回信感谢他，并给出你的建议。

items.zh: 根据下图写一篇作文。

items.zh: 每天一个拥抱能赶走医生吗？

items.en: The answer may be a resounding "yes!
items.zh: 答案可能是一个响亮的是！

items.zh: 1 帮助你与关心的人建立亲密感和 2 ，结果发现拥抱可以给你的身体和心理带来 3 的健康益处。

items.en: Believe it or not, a warm embrace might even help you 4 getting sick this winter.
items.zh: 信不信由你，一个温暖的拥抱甚至可能帮助你4在这个冬天生病。

items.en: In a recent study 5 over 400 healthy adults, researchers from Carnegie Mellon University in Pennsylvania examined the effects of perceived social support and the receipt of hugs 6 the participants' susceptibility to developing the common cold after being 7 to the virus.
items.zh: 在一项针对500多名健康成年人的近期研究中，来自宾夕法尼亚州卡内基梅隆大学的研究人员考察了感知到的社会支持和接受拥抱对参与者在被7到病毒后发展成普通感冒的易感性的影响。

items.en: People who perceived greater social support were less likely to come 8 with a cold, and the researchers 9 that the stress-reducing effects of hugging 10 about 32 percent of that beneficial effect.
items.zh: 感知到更多社会支持的人更不容易患上感冒，研究人员9认为拥抱的减压效果10了大约32%的有益效果。

items.en: 11 among those who got a cold, the ones who felt greater social support and received more frequent hugs had less severe 12 .
items.zh: 在那些感冒的人中，感受到更多社会支持并更频繁接受拥抱的人，其12症状更轻微。

items.en: "Hugging protects people who are under stress from the 13 risk for colds that's usually 14 with stress," notes Sheldon Cohen, a professor of psychology at Carnegie.
items.zh: 拥抱可以保护处于压力下的人们免受通常与压力相关的13感冒风险，卡内基大学心理学教授Sheldon Cohen指出

items.en: Hugging "is a marker of intimacy and helps 15 the feeling that others are there to help 16 difficulty.
items.zh: 拥抱是亲密关系的标志，并有助于15他人在困难时会提供帮助的这种感觉。

items.en: Some experts 17 the stress-reducing, health-related benefits of hugging to the release of oxytocin, often called "the bonding hormone" 18 it promotes attachment in relationships, including that between mothers and their newborn babies.
items.zh: 一些专家将拥抱的减压和健康相关益处归因于催产素的释放，这种激素常被称为“联结激素”，因为其能促进人际关系中的依附，包括母亲与新生儿之间的关系。

items.en: Oxytocin is made primarily in the central lower part of the brain, and some of it is released into the bloodstream.
items.zh: 催产素主要在大脑中央下部产生，其中一部分会释放到血液中。

items.en: But some of it 19 in the brain, where it 20 mood, behavior and physiology.
items.zh: 但其中一些19在大脑中，在那里它20情绪、行为和生理机能。

items.zh: 罗伯特 F.

items.en: Paragraphs B and D have been correctly placed.
items.zh: B和D段已经正确放置。

items.en: From then on his sketches, which appeared under the pen name "Boz" in The Evening Chronicle, earned him a modest reputation.
items.zh: 从那时起，他以“Boz”为笔名在《The Evening Chronicle》上发表的速写为他赢得了一定的声誉。

items.en: There were Pickwick coats and Pickwick cigars, and the plump, spectacled hero, Samuel Pickwick, became a national figure.
items.zh: 有皮克wick大衣和皮克wick雪茄，而圆润、戴眼镜的英雄萨缪尔·皮克wick成为全国知名人物。

items.en: With characteristic confidence, Dickens successfully insisted that Seymour's pictures illustrate his own story instead.
items.zh: 以一贯的自信，狄更斯成功坚持让塞缪尔的插图诠释他自己的故事，而非其他人的。

items.en: After the first installment, Dickens wrote to the artist and asked him to correct a drawing Dickens felt was not faithful enough to his prose.
items.zh: 第一期连载之后，狄更斯给画家写信，要求他修改一幅他认为未能充分忠实于自己文字的插图。

items.en: Seymour made the change, went into his backyard, and expressed his displeasure by committing suicide.
items.zh: Seymour做出改变，进入他的后院，通过自杀来表达他的不满。

items.en: Dickens and his publishers simply pressed on with a new artist.
items.zh: 狄更斯和他的出版商继续使用一位新艺术家。

items.en: The comic novel, The Posthumous Papers of the Pickwick Club, appeared serially in 1836 and 1837 and was first published in book form in 1837.
items.zh: 幽默小说《The Posthumous Papers of the Pickwick Club》于1836年和1837年连载出版，并于1837年首次以书本形式发行。

items.en: A moralist, satirist, and social reformer, Dickens crafted complex plots and striking characters that capture the panorama of English society.
items.zh: 作为道德家、讽刺作家和社会改革者，狄更斯创作了复杂的情节和鲜明的人物形象，生动展现了英国社会的全景。

items.en: He taught himself shorthand to get an even better job later as a court stenographer and as a reporter in Parliament.
items.zh: 他自学速记，以便日后能获得更好的工作，成为一名法庭速记员和议会记者。

items.en: At the same time, Dickens, who had a reporter's eye for transcribing the life around him, especially anything comic or odd, submitted short sketches to obscure magazines.
items.zh: 同时，狄更斯凭借记者般敏锐的眼光记录他周围的生活，尤其是任何滑稽或奇特的事物，向冷门杂志投稿短篇速写。

items.en: His father was a clerk in the British Navy pay office - a respectable position, but with little social status.
items.zh: 他父亲是英国海军军饷办公室的一名职员——一个体面的职位，但社会地位不高。

items.en: His paternal grandparents, a steward and a housekeeper, possessed even less status, having been servants, and Dickens later concealed their background.
items.zh: 他的父方祖父母，一位管家和一位管家，地位更低，因为他们曾是仆人，而狄更斯后来隐瞒了他们的背景。

items.en: Dickens's mother supposedly came from a more respectable family.
items.zh: Dickens的母亲据说来自一个更体面的家庭。

items.en: Yet two years before Dickens's birth, his mother's father was caught stealing and fled to Europe, never to return.
items.zh: 然而在狄更斯出生前两年，他母亲的父亲因偷窃被捕并逃往欧洲，再未返回。

items.en: The family's increasing poverty forced Dickens out of school at age 12 to work in Warren's Blacking Warehouse, a shoe-polish factory, where the other working boys mocked him as "the young gentleman.
items.zh: 狄更斯12岁时因家庭日益贫困被迫辍学，进入沃伦的鞋油工厂工作，那里其他打工的男孩们戏称他为"年轻绅士"。

items.en: His father was then imprisoned for debt.
items.zh: 他父亲当时因债务被关押。

items.en: The humiliations of his father's imprisonment and his labor in the blacking factory formed Dickens's greatest wound and became his deepest secret.
items.zh: 他父亲被监禁以及他在鞋油厂的劳作所遭受的屈辱构成了狄更斯最大的创伤，并成为他最深的秘密。

items.en: He could not confide them even to his wife, although they provide the unacknowledged foundation of his fiction.
items.zh: 他甚至无法向妻子透露这些事，尽管它们为他的小说提供了未被承认的基础。

items.en: In Oliver Twist, he traces an orphan's progress from the workhouse to the criminal slums of London.
items.zh: 在《Oliver Twist》中，他描绘了一个孤儿从济贫院到伦敦犯罪贫民窟的历程。

items.en: Nicholas Nickleby, his next novel, combines the darkness of Oliver Twist with the sunlight of Pickwick.
items.zh: 他的下一部小说《Nicholas Nickleby》融合了《Oliver Twist》的黑暗与《Pickwick》的阳光。

items.en: The popularity of these novels consolidated Dickens' as a nationally and internationally celebrated man of letters.
items.zh: 这些小说的流行巩固了狄更斯作为全国和国际上备受赞誉的文学家的地位。

items.en: The growth of the use of English as the world's primary language for international communication has obviously been continuing for several decades.
items.zh: 英语作为世界主要的国际交流语言的使用增长显然已经持续了几十年。

items.en: (46) But even as the number of English speakers expands further there are signs that the global predominance of the language may fade within the foreseeable future.
items.zh: (46) 但即使英语使用者数量进一步增长，也有迹象表明该语言的全球主导地位可能在未来可预见的时间内减弱。

items.en: Complex international, economic, technological and cultural changes could start to diminish the leading position of English as the language of the world market, and UK interests which enjoy advantage from the breadth of English usage would consequently face new pressures.
items.zh: 复杂的国际、经济、科技和文化变化可能开始削弱英语作为世界市场语言的主导地位，而那些因英语广泛使用而受益的英国利益将因此面临新的压力。

items.en: Those realistic possibilities are highlighted in the study presented by David Graddol.
items.zh: 这些现实的可能性在David Graddol提出的研究中被强调。

items.en: (47) His analysis should therefore end any self-contentedness among those who may believe that the global position of English is so stable that the young generations of the United Kingdom do not need additional language capabilities.
items.zh: 他的分析因此应该终结那些人的自满情绪，这些人可能认为英语的全球地位如此稳定以至于英国年轻一代不需要额外语言能力。

items.en: David Graddol concludes that monoglot English graduates face a bleak economic future as qualified multilingual youngsters from other countries are proving to have a competitive advantage over their British counterparts in global companies and organisations.
items.zh: 大卫·格雷多尔得出结论，单语英语毕业生将面临黯淡的经济前景，因为来自其他国家的合格多语青年正在证明他们在跨国公司和组织中对英国同龄人具有竞争优势。

items.en: Alongside that, (48) many countries are introducing English into the primary-school curriculum but British schoolchildren and students do not appear to be gaining greater encouragement to achieve fluency in other languages.
items.zh: 与此同时，（48）许多国家正在将英语纳入小学课程，但英国的中小学生似乎并未获得更多鼓励去掌握其他语言的流利程度。

items.en: If left to themselves, such trends will diminish the relative strength of the English language in international education markets as the demand for educational resources in languages, such as Spanish, Arabic or Mandarin grows and international business process outsourcing in other languages such as Japanese, French and German, spreads.
items.zh: 如果任其发展，这些趋势将削弱英语在国际教育市场中的相对优势，随着对西班牙语、阿拉伯语或普通话等语言教育资料的需求增长，以及国际业务流程外包在日语、法语和德语等其他语言中的扩展。

items.en: (49) The changes identified by David Graddol all present clear and major challenges to the UK's providers of English language teaching to people of other countries and to broader education business sectors.
items.zh: （49）David Graddol所识别的变化都对英国向其他国家提供英语语言教学的机构以及更广泛的教育产业部门带来了明确且重大的挑战。

items.en: The English language teaching sector directly earns nearly £1.3 billion for the UK in invisible exports and our other education related exports earn up to £10 billion a year more.
items.zh: 英国英语教学行业通过无形出口直接创造近13亿英镑收入，并且我们的其他教育相关出口每年还能带来高达100亿英镑的收入。

items.en: As the international education market expands, the recent slowdown in the numbers of international students studying in the main English-speaking countries is likely to continue, especially if there are no effective strategic policies to prevent such slippage.
items.zh: 随着国际教育市场的扩大，近期主要英语国家国际学生数量的放缓可能将持续，尤其是如果没有有效的战略政策来防止这种滑坡。

items.en: The anticipation of possible shifts in demand provided by this study is significant: (50) It gives a basis to all organisations which seek to promote the learning and use of English, a basis for planning to meet the possibilities of what could be a very different operating environment.
items.zh: 本研究提供的需求变化预期具有重要意义：它为所有致力于推动英语学习和使用的组织提供了规划依据，以应对可能截然不同的运营环境。

items.en: That is a necessary and practical approach.
items.zh: 那是一种必要且实际的方法。

items.en: In this as in much else, those who wish to influence the future must prepare for it.
items.zh: 正如在许多其他方面一样，想要影响未来的人必须为它做准备。

items.en: Directions: You are to write an email to James Cook, a newly-arrived Australian professor, recommending some tourist attractions in your city.
items.zh: 说明：你将要给新到的澳大利亚教授James Cook写一封电子邮件，推荐你所在城市的一些旅游景点。

items.en: Please give reasons for your recommendation.
items.zh: 请说明你推荐的理由。

items.en: Do not sign your own name at the end of the email.
items.zh: 不要在邮件末尾签上自己的名字。

items.en: People have speculated for centuries about a future without work.
items.zh: 人们已经推测了几个世纪关于没有工作的未来。

items.en: Today is no different, with academics, writers, and activists once again 1 that technology is replacing human workers.
items.zh: 今天也不例外，学术界人士、作家和活动家再次1技术正在取代人类工人。

items.en: Some imagine that the coming work-free world will be defined by 2: A few wealthy people will own all the capital, and the masses will struggle in an impoverished wasteland.
items.zh: 一些人认为，即将到来的无工世界将由2：少数富人将拥有全部资本，而大众将在贫困荒原中挣扎。

items.en: A different and not mutually exclusive 3 holds that the future will be a wasteland of a different sort, one 4 by purposelessness: Without jobs to give their lives 5, people will simply become lazy and depressed.
items.zh: 一种不同的且不互相排斥的 3认为，未来将是一种不同类型的荒原，一种由无目的感所 4的荒原：没有工作来赋予他们生活以 5，人们将变得懒惰和沮丧。

items.en: 6, today’s unemployed don’t seem to be having a great time.

items.en: The decline in American manufacturing is a common refrain, particularly from Donald Trump.
items.zh: 美国制造业的衰退是一个经常被提及的话题，尤其是来自唐纳德·特朗普的言论。

items.en: “We don’t make anything anymore,” he told Fox News, while defending his own made-in-Mexico clothing line.
items.zh: 我们现在已经不再生产任何东西了，他对福克斯新闻表示，同时为他自己的墨西哥制造服装系列进行辩护。

items.en: Without question, manufacturing has taken a significant hit during recent decades, and further trade deals raise questions about whether new shocks could hit manufacturing.
items.zh: 毋庸置疑，制造业在最近几十年里遭受了重大打击，进一步的贸易协议引发关于新的冲击是否会对制造业造成影响的疑问。

items.en: But there is also a different way to look at the data.
items.zh: 但也有另一种看待数据的方式。

items.en: Across the country, factory owners are now grappling with a new challenge: Instead of having too many workers, they may end up with too few.
items.zh: 全国各地的工厂主现在正面临一个新的挑战：他们可能最终面临工人数量过少的问题，而不是过多。

items.en: Despite trade competition and outsourcing, American manufacturing still needs to replace tens of thousands of retiring boomers every year.
items.zh: 尽管面临贸易竞争和外包，美国制造业每年仍需替换数以万计的退休婴儿潮一代。

items.en: Millennials may not be that interested in taking their place.
items.zh: 千禧一代可能并不特别热衷于接班。

items.en: Other industries are recruiting them with similar or better pay.
items.zh: 其他行业正在以相似或更高的薪酬招聘他们。

items.en: For factory owners, it all adds up to stiff competition for workers – and upward pressure on wages.
items.zh: 对工厂主来说，这都意味着对工人的激烈竞争——以及工资上行压力。

items.en: “They’re harder to find and they have job offers,” says Jay Dunwell, president of Wolverine Coil Spring, a family-owned firm, “They may be coming [into the workforce], but they’ve been plucked by other industries that are also doing as well as manufacturing.
items.zh: 他们更难找到，而且他们有工作机会，杰伊·邓威尔说，他是家族企业Wolverine Coil Spring的总裁，他们可能正在进入职场，但已经被其他行业挖走，而这些行业也发展得和制造业一样好。

items.en: Mr. Dunwell has begun bringing high school juniors to the factory so they can get exposed to its culture.
items.zh: 邓韦尔先生已开始带高二学生到工厂，让他们接触其文化。

items.en: At RoMan Manufacturing, a maker of electrical transformers and welding equipment that his father cofounded in 1980, Robert Roth keeps a close eye on the age of his nearly 200 workers.
items.zh: 在1980年由其父亲共同创立的电气变压器和焊接设备生产商RoMan Manufacturing，Robert Roth密切关注着其近200名工人的年龄。

items.en: Five are retiring this year.
items.zh: 今年有五人将退休。

items.en: Mr. Roth has three community-college students enrolled in a work-placement program, with a starting wage of $13 an hour that rises to $17 after two years.
items.zh: 罗思先生有三名社区学院学生参加了实习项目，起薪为每小时13美元，两年后涨至17美元。

items.en: At a worktable inside the transformer plant, young Jason Stenquist looks flustered by the copper coils he’s trying to assemble and the arrival of two visitors.
items.zh: 在变压器工厂的一张工作台上，年轻的Jason Stenquist因试图组装的铜线圈和两位访客的到来而显得慌乱。

items.en: It’s his first week on the job.
items.zh: 这是他工作的第一周。

items.en: Asked about his choice of career, he says at high school he considered medical school before switching to electrical engineering.
items.zh: 当被问及职业选择时，他说在高中时曾考虑过医学院，但后来转而选择了电气工程。

items.en: “I love working with tools.

items.en: These concerns aren’t misplaced: Employment in manufacturing has fallen from 17 million in 1970 to 12 million in 2015.

items.en: Now shortages are appearing at the mid-skill levels.
items.zh: 现在，中等技能岗位出现短缺。

items.en: “The gap is between the jobs that take no skills and those that require a lot of skill,” says Rob Spohr, a business professor at Montcalm Community College.
items.zh: 差距存在于不需要技能的工作和需要大量技能的工作之间，蒙卡尔姆社区学院的商业教授Rob Spohr说。

items.en: It’s that gap in between, and that’s where the problem is.
items.zh: 问题就出在中间的差距上。

items.en: (46) By the date of his birth Europe was witnessing the passing of the religious drama, and the creation of new forms under the incentive of classical tragedy and comedy.
items.zh: 在他出生时，欧洲正目睹宗教戏剧的消亡，以及在古典悲剧和喜剧激励下新形式的诞生。

items.en: These new forms were at first mainly written by scholars and performed by amateurs, but in England, as everywhere else in western Europe, the growth of a class of professional actors was threatening to make the drama popular, whether it should be new or old, classical or medieval, literary or farcical.
items.zh: 这些新形式起初主要由学者撰写并由业余爱好者表演，但在英格兰，如同西欧其他地区一样，职业演员阶层的兴起正威胁着使戏剧变得流行，无论其是新剧还是旧剧，古典剧还是中世纪剧，文学剧还是闹剧。

items.en: Court, school, organizations of amateurs, and the traveling actors were all rivals in supplying a widespread desire for dramatic entertainment; and (47) no boy who went to a grammar school could be ignorant that the drama was a form of literature which gave glory to Greece and Rome and might yet bring honor to England.
items.zh: 法庭、学校、业余组织和巡回演员都是满足人们广泛戏剧娱乐需求的竞争者；而且（47）每个上过文法学校的学生都清楚戏剧是一种文学形式，曾为希腊和罗马带来荣耀，未来也可能为英格兰带来荣誉。

items.en: When Shakespeare was twelve years old the first public playhouse was built in London.
items.zh: 当莎士比亚十二岁时，伦敦建起了第一个公共剧院。

items.en: For a time literature showed no interest in this public stage.
items.zh: 曾有一段时间，文学对这个公共舞台毫无兴趣。

items.en: Plays aiming at literary distinction were written for schools or court, or for the choir boys of St. Paul's and the royal chapel, who, however, gave plays in public as well as at court.
items.zh: 旨在获得文学成就的戏剧是为学校或宫廷，或是为圣保罗教堂和皇家礼拜堂的唱诗班男孩创作的，然而这些唱诗班男孩也会在公共场所和宫廷上演戏剧。

items.en: (48) But the professional companies prospered in their permanent theaters, and university men with literary ambitions were quick to turn to these theaters as offering a means of livelihood.
items.zh: (48) 但专业剧团在固定的剧院中繁荣发展，有文学抱负的大学文人也迅速转向这些剧院，将其视为谋生的途径。

items.en: By the time that Shakespeare was twenty-five, Lyly, Peele, and Greene had made comedies that were at once popular and literary; Kyd had written a tragedy that crowded the pit; and Marlowe had brought poetry and genius to triumph on the common stage - where they had played no part since the death of Euripides.
items.zh: 到莎士比亚25岁时，Lyly、Peele和Greene已经创作了既通俗又具有文学性的喜剧；Kyd创作了一部挤满前排座位的悲剧；而Marlowe则让诗歌和天才在普通舞台上取得胜利——自欧里庇得斯去世以来，他们就没有在普通舞台上扮演过任何角色。

items.en: (49) A native literary drama had been created, its alliance with the public playhouses established, and at least some of its great traditions had been begun.
items.zh: 一种本土文学戏剧已被创作出来，与公共剧院的联盟得以建立，并且至少其中一些伟大的传统已被开启。

items.en: The development of the Elizabethan drama for the next twenty-five years is of exceptional interest to students of literary history, for in this brief period we may trace the beginning, growth, blossoming, and decay of many kinds of plays, and of many great careers.
items.zh: 伊丽莎白时代戏剧在接下来的25年的发展对文学史研究者具有特别重要的意义，因为在这短暂的时期内，我们可以追溯许多戏剧类型的兴起、发展、繁荣与衰落，以及许多伟大职业生涯的起起落落。

items.en: We are amazed today at the mere number of plays produced, as well as by the number of dramatists writing at the same time for this London of two hundred thousand inhabitants.
items.zh: 我们今天对所创作的戏剧数量感到惊讶，同时也对同时为这座拥有二十万居民的伦敦创作的剧作家数量感到惊叹。

items.en: (50) To realize how great was the dramatic activity, we must remember further that hosts of plays have been lost, and that probably there is no author of note whose entire work has survived.
items.zh: （50）要认识到戏剧活动的规模有多大，我们还必须记住大量戏剧作品已经失传，可能没有哪位著名作者的全部作品得以流传下来。
