items.en: Five ways to make conversation with anyone
items.zh: 与任何人交谈的五种方法

items.en: Conversations are links, which means when you have a conversation with a new person a link gets formed and every conversation you have after that moment will strengthen the link.
items.zh: 对话是链接，这意味着当你与新的人交谈时，就会形成一个链接，而此后你进行的每一次交谈都会加强这个链接。

items.en: You meet new people every day: the grocery worker, the cab driver, new people at work or the security guard at the door.
items.zh: 你每天都会遇到新的人：杂货店员工、出租车司机、工作中的新人或门口的保安。

items.en: Simply starting a conversation with them will form a link.
items.zh: 仅仅与他们开始交谈就会建立联系。

items.en: Here are five simple ways that you can make the first move and start a conversation with strangers.
items.zh: 这里有五种简单的方法，你可以主动迈出第一步，与陌生人开始交谈。

items.en: Suppose you are in a room with someone you don’t know and something within you says “I want to talk with this person” – this is something that mostly happens with all of us.
items.zh: 假设你和一个你不认识的人在同一个房间里，你内心有什么东西在说"我想和这个人交谈"——这种情况在我们所有人身上大多都会发生。

items.en: You wanted to say something – the first word – but it just won’t come out, it feels like it is stuck somewhere.
items.zh: 你想说点什么——第一个词——但就是说不出口，感觉它卡在某个地方了。

items.en: I know the feeling and here is my advice: just get it out.
items.zh: 我明白这种感受，这是我的建议：把它说出来。

items.en: Just think: what is the worst that could happen?
items.zh: 想想看：最坏的情况会是什么？

items.en: They won’t talk with you?
items.zh: 他们不会和你说话？

items.en: Well, they are not talking with you now!
items.zh: 好吧，他们现在没有和你交谈！

items.en: I truly believe that once you get that first word out everything else will just flow.
items.zh: 我真心相信，一旦你说出第一句话，其他一切都会随之顺畅。

items.en: So keep it simple: “Hi”, “Hey”or “Hello” – do the best you can to gather all of the enthusiasm and energy you can, put on a big smile and say “Hi”.
items.zh: 所以保持简单：‘Hi’、‘Hey’或‘Hello’——尽你所能调动所有热情和精力，露出灿烂笑容，然后说‘Hi’。

items.en: It is a problem all of us face; you have limited time with the person that you want to talk with and you want to make this talk memorable.
items.zh: 这是一个我们所有人都面临的问题；你与想交谈的人相处的时间有限，你希望这次谈话令人难忘。

items.en: Honestly, if we got stuck in the rut of “hi”, “hello”, “how are you?
items.zh: 老实说，如果我们陷入“你好”、“您好”、“你怎么样？”这样的固定模式。

items.en: and “what is going on?”, you will fail to give the initial jolt to the conversation that can make it so memorable.
items.zh: 如果你只是问“发生了什么？”，你将无法给予对话最初的推动力，使其变得如此难忘。

items.en: So don’t be afraid to ask more personal questions.
items.zh: 因此不要害怕提出更个人化的问题。

items.en: Trust me, you’ll be surprised to see how much people are willing to share if you just ask.
items.zh: 相信我，你会惊讶于人们愿意分享多少，只要你去问。

items.en: When you meet a person for the first time, make an effort to find the things which you and that person have in common so that you can build the conversation from that point.
items.zh: 当你第一次见到一个人时，努力寻找你们共同拥有的事物，以便以此为起点展开对话。

items.en: When you start conversation from there and then move outwards, you’ll find all of a sudden that the conversation becomes a lot easier.
items.zh: 当你从那里开始对话并逐步向外扩展时，你会发现突然之间对话变得容易得多。

items.en: Imagine you are pouring your heart out to someone and they are just busy on their phone, and if you ask for their attention you get the response “I can multitask”.
items.zh: 想象一下你正向某人倾诉心事，而他们只是忙着玩手机，如果你请求他们的注意，得到的回应却是"我能多任务处理"。

items.en: So when someone tries to communicate with you, just be in that communication wholeheartedly.
items.zh: 因此当有人试图与你沟通时，就全心全意地进行沟通。

items.en: Make eye contact.
items.zh: 进行眼神交流。

items.en: Trust me, eye contact is where all the magic happens.
items.zh: 相信我，眼神交流是所有魔力发生的地方。

items.en: When you make eye contact, you can feel the conversation.
items.zh: 当你进行眼神交流时，就能感受到对话的氛围。

items.en: You all came into a conversation where you first met the person, but after some time you may have met again and have forgotten their name.
items.zh: 你们都参与了一场对话，你们第一次见到那个人的地方，但一段时间后你们可能再次见面却忘记了他们的名字。

items.en: Isn’t that awkward!
items.zh: 这不是很尴尬吗！

items.en: So, remember the little details of the people you met or you talked with; perhaps the places they have been to, the places they want to go, the things they like, the things they hate – whatever you talk about.
items.zh: 所以，记住你遇到或交谈过的人的小细节；或许他们去过的地方、他们想去的地方、他们喜欢的事物、他们讨厌的事物——无论你谈到什么。

items.en: When you remember such things you can automatically become investor in their wellbeing.
items.zh: 当你记住这些事时你就能自动成为他们福祉的投资者。

items.en: So they feel a responsibility to you to keep that relationship going.
items.zh: 因此他们对你感到有责任维持这段关系。

items.en: That’s it.
items.zh: 就是这样。

items.en: Five amazing ways that you can make conversation with almost anyone.
items.zh: 与几乎所有人开启对话的5种令人惊叹的方法。

items.zh: 每个人其实都是一本非常棒的书，值得阅读，或与之交谈！

items.en: A fifth grader gets a homework assignment to select his future career path from a list of occupations.

items.en: He ticks “astronaut” but quickly adds “scientist” to the list and selects it as well.
items.zh: 他勾选了“宇航员”，但迅速将“科学家”加入列表并选中它。

items.en: The boy is convinced that if he reads enough, he can explore as many career paths as he likes.
items.zh: 这个男孩坚信，如果他读得足够多，他就可以探索他喜欢的尽可能多的职业道路。

items.en: And so he reads – everything from encyclopedias to science fiction novels.
items.zh: 于是他阅读——从百科全书到科幻小说的一切内容。

items.en: He reads so passionately that his parents have to institute a “no reading policy” at the dinner table.
items.zh: 他读得如此充满激情，以至于他的父母不得不在餐桌制定一项“禁止阅读”政策。

items.en: That boy was Bill Gates, and he hasn’t stopped reading yet – not even after becoming one of the most successful people on the planet.
items.zh: 那个男孩就是比尔·盖茨，他尚未停止阅读——甚至在他成为全球最成功的人之一之后也未曾停止。

items.en: Nowadays, his reading material has changed from science fiction and reference books: recently, he revealed that he reads at least 50 nonfiction books a year.
items.zh: 如今，他的阅读材料已从科幻小说和参考书转变为非虚构类书籍：最近他透露，自己每年至少阅读50本非虚构类书籍。

items.en: Gates chooses nonfiction titles because they explain how the world works.
items.zh: 盖茨选择非虚构类书籍，因为它们解释了世界如何运作。

items.en: “Each book opens up new avenues of knowledge to explore”, Gates says.
items.zh: 每本书都开辟了知识的新途径供探索，Gates说。

items.en: Suppose you have to cancel your travel plan and will not be able to visit Professor Smith.
items.zh: 假设你不得不取消旅行计划，将无法拜访史密斯教授。

items.en: Write him an email to apologize and explain the situation, and suggest a future meeting.
items.zh: 给他写封电子邮件道歉并解释情况，同时建议未来的会议。

items.en: At night, scan the horizon for 17 light sources, such as fires and streetlights, then walk toward the glow of light pollution.
items.zh: 在夜晚，在地平线上搜寻 17 个光源，如篝火和路灯，然后朝着光污染的光亮走去。

items.en: 18 , assuming you're lost in an area humans tend to frequent, look for the 19 we leave on the landscape.
items.zh: 18 ，假设你迷失在一个人类倾向于频繁出没的地区，寻找我们留在景观上的 19 。

items.en: Trail blazes, tire tracks, and other features can 20 you to civilization.
items.zh: 小径标记、车辙和其他特征可以20你到文明社会。

items.en: Learning why they disagree with us and learning to talk and work together with them.
items.zh: 了解他们为何与我们有分歧和学会与他们沟通与合作。

items.en: If we readjust our view of arguments - from a verbal fight or tennis game to a reasoned exchange through which we all gain mutual respect, and understanding - then we change the very nature of what it means to "win" an argument.
items.zh: 如果我们调整对争论的看法——从言语争吵或网球比赛转变为有理有据的交流，从而让我们彼此获得相互尊重和理解——那么我们就改变了争论中"赢"的含义。

items.en: Still, we need to be careful not to accuse opponents of bad arguments too quickly.
items.zh: 不过，我们需要谨慎，不要过早指责对手的论点有误。

items.en: We need to learn how to evaluate them properly.
items.zh: 我们需要学会正确地评估它们。

items.en: A large part of evaluation is calling out bad arguments, but we also need to admit good arguments by opponents and to apply the same critical standards to ourselves.
items.zh: 评估的很大一部分在于指出错误的论点，但我们也需要承认对手提出的正确论点，并对自己应用相同的批判标准。

items.en: Humility requires you to recognize weakness in your own arguments and sometimes also to accept reasons on the opposite side.
items.zh: 谦逊要求你承认自己论点中的弱点，有时也要求你接受对方观点的理由。

items.en: Next time you state your position, formulate an argument for what you claim and honestly ask yourself whether your argument is any good.
items.zh: 下次你表达观点时，为你的主张构建一个论点并诚实地问自己你的论点是否有说服力。

items.en: Next time you talk with someone who takes a stand, ask them to give you a reason for their view.
items.zh: 下次和有明确立场的人交谈时，请他们给你一个理由说明他们的观点。

items.en: Spell out their argument fully and charitably.
items.zh: 全面且公正地阐述他们的论点。

items.en: Assess its strength impartially.
items.zh: 公正地评估它的力量。

items.en: Raise objections and listen carefully to their replies.
items.zh: 提出异议并仔细倾听他们的回应。

items.en: Like physical fights, verbal fights can leave both sides bloodied.
items.zh: 和肢体冲突一样，言语冲突也会让双方都受到伤害。

items.en: Even when you win, you end up no better off.
items.zh: 即使你赢了，最终也没有变得更好。

items.en: Your prospects would be almost as dismal if arguments were even just competitions - like, say, tennis games.
items.zh: 你的前景几乎同样暗淡，如果争论仅仅是竞争，比如网球比赛。

items.en: Pairs of opponents hit the ball back and forth until one winner emerges from all who entered.
items.zh: 对手们两两对决，来回击球，直到所有参赛者中产生一位胜者。

items.en: Everybody else loses.
items.zh: 其他人都会输。

items.en: This kind of thinking is why so many people try to avoid arguments, especially about politics and religion.
items.zh: 这种思维方式正是许多人试图避免争论，尤其是关于政治和宗教的争论的原因。

items.en: to get the best of an argument - and that is to avoid it.
items.zh: 要在争论中占上风，最好的办法就是避免争论。

items.en: This aversion to arguments is common, but it depends on a mistaken view of arguments that causes profound problems for our personal and social lives - and in many ways misses the point of arguing in the first place.
items.zh: 对争论的厌恶是常见的，但这种厌恶基于对争论的误解，导致我们个人和社会生活中出现严重问题——而且在很多方面偏离了争论的初衷。

items.en: If you see a conversation as a fight or competition, you can win by cheating as long as you don't get caught.
items.zh: 如果你把对话视为一场战斗或竞争，你可以通过作弊获胜，只要你没有被抓住。

items.en: You will be happy to convince people with bad arguments.
items.zh: 你将会为用错误的论据说服他人而感到高兴。

items.en: You can call their views stupid, or joke about how ignorant they are.
items.zh: 你可以称他们的观点愚蠢，或者取笑他们的无知。

items.en: None of these tricks will help you understand them, their positions or the issues that divide you, but they can help you win - in one way.
items.zh: 这些手段无法帮助你理解他们、他们的立场或导致你们分歧的问题，但它们可以帮助你赢——仅以一种方式。

items.en: Imagine that you favor increasing the minimum wage in our state, and I do not.
items.zh: 假设你支持提高我们州的最低工资，而我不支持。

items.en: If you yell, "Yes," and I yell, "No," neither of us learns anything.
items.zh: 如果你喊“是”，而我喊“否”，我们都没学到任何东西。

items.en: We neither understand nor respect each other, and we have no basis for compromise or cooperation.
items.zh: 我们既不理解也不尊重彼此，和我们没有妥协或合作的基础。

items.en: In contrast, suppose you give a reasonable argument: that full-time workers should not have to live in poverty.
items.zh: 相反，假设你提出一个合理的论点：全职员工不应该陷入贫困。

items.en: Then I counter with another reasonable argument: that a higher minimum wage will force businesses to employ fewer people for less time.
items.zh: 然后我再用另一个合理的论点进行反驳：更高的最低工资将迫使企业雇佣更少的人并让他们工作更少的时间。

items.en: Now we can understand each other's positions and recognize our shared values, since we both care about needy workers.
items.zh: 现在我们能够理解彼此的立场并认识到共同的价值观，因为我们都在乎需要帮助的工人。

items.en: It was only after I started to write a weekly column about the medical journals, and began to read scientific papers from beginning to end, that I realised just how bad much of the medical literature frequently was.
items.zh: 直到我开始撰写关于医学期刊的每周专栏，并开始从头到尾阅读科学论文，我才意识到医学文献中很多内容经常是如此糟糕。

items.en: I came to recognise various signs of a bad paper: the kind of paper that purports to show that people who eat more than one kilo of broccoli a week were 1.17 times more likely than those who eat less to suffer late in life from pernicious anaemia.
items.zh: 我逐渐认识到一些表明论文质量低劣的迹象：那种声称证明每周食用超过一千克西兰花的人比食用更少者在晚年患恶性贫血的可能性高出1.17倍的论文。

items.en: (46) There is a great deal of this kind of nonsense in the medical journals which, when taken up by broadcasters and the lay press, generates both health scares and short-lived dietary enthusiasms.
items.zh: 医学期刊中充斥着大量这种无稽之谈，当被广播媒体和通俗媒体采用时，会引发健康恐慌和短暂的饮食热潮。

items.en: Why is so much bad science published?
items.zh: 为什么会有这么多伪科学被发表？

items.en: A recent paper, titled "The Natural Selection of Bad Science", published on the Royal Society's open science website, attempts to answer this intriguing and important question.
items.zh: 最近发表在Royal Society开放科学网站上的一篇题为《The Natural Selection of Bad Science》的论文，试图回答这个引人入胜且重要的问题。

items.en: It says that the problem is not merely that people do bad science, but that our current system of career advancement positively encourages it.
items.zh: 它指出问题不仅仅在于人们从事劣质科研，而在于我们当前的职业晋升体系积极鼓励这种行为。

items.en: What is important is not truth, but publication, which has become almost an end in itself.
items.zh: 重要的不是真相，而是发表，发表本身几乎已成为目的。

items.en: There has been a kind of inflationary process at work: (47) nowadays anyone applying for a research post has to have published twice the number of papers that would have been required for the same post only 10 years ago.
items.zh: 有一种膨胀过程在起作用：如今申请研究职位的人必须已经发表了两倍于十年前申请同一职位所需的论文数量。

items.en: Never mind the quality, then, count the number.
items.zh: 别管质量，只看数量。

items.en: (48) Attempts have been made to curb this tendency, for example, by trying to incorporate some measure of quality as well as quantity into the assessment of an applicant's papers.
items.zh: （48）人们试图通过在评估申请人的论文时纳入质量与数量的指标来遏制这一趋势。

items.en: This is the famed citation index, that is to say the number of times a paper has been quoted elsewhere in the scientific literature, the assumption being that an important paper will be cited more often than one of small account.
items.zh: 这就是著名的引用指数，也就是说该论文在科学文献中被其他文献引用的次数，其假设是重要论文会被引用的次数多于影响力较小的论文。

items.en: (49) This would be reasonable if it were not for the fact that scientists can easily arrange to cite themselves in their future publications, or get associates to do so for them in return for similar favours.
items.zh: (49) 如果不是因为科学家可以轻松地在未来的出版物中引用自己，或者让同事这样做以换取类似的回报，这将是合理的。

items.en: Boiling down an individual's output to simple metrics, such as number of publications or journal impacts, entails considerable savings in time, energy and ambiguity.
items.zh: 将个人的产出简化为简单的指标，如论文数量或期刊影响力，可以显著节省时间、精力和歧义。

items.en: Unfortunately, the long-term costs of using simple quantitative metrics to assess researcher merit are likely to be quite great.
items.zh: 不幸的是，使用简单的定量指标来评估研究人员学术价值的长期代价可能相当大。

items.en: (50) If we are serious about ensuring that our science is both meaningful and reproducible, we must ensure that our institutions encourage that kind of science.
items.zh: 如果我们认真致力于确保我们的科学既具有意义又可重复，我们必须确保我们的机构鼓励这种类型的科学。

items.zh: 说明：假设你正在参与你所在大学的“Aiding Rural Primary School”项目。

items.en: Weighing yourself regularly is a wonderful way to stay aware of any significant weight fluctuations.
items.zh: 定期称重是保持对任何显著体重波动警觉的绝佳方法。

items.en: 1, when done too often, this habit can sometimes hurt more than it 2.
items.zh: 1 当过于频繁时，这个习惯有时会造成的伤害比它 2 的好处还要多。

items.en: As for me, weighing myself every day caused me to shift my focus from being generally healthy and physically active, to focusing 3 on the scale.
items.zh: 对我来说，每天称体重让我把关注点从保持总体健康和身体活跃，转移到了体重秤上的数字3上。

items.en: That was bad to my overall fitness goals.
items.zh: 这对我的整体健身目标不利。

items.en: I had gained weight in the form of muscle mass, but thinking only of 4 the number on the scale, I altered my training program.
items.zh: 我以增加肌肉质量的形式增重了，但只考虑体重秤上的4这个数字，我调整了我的训练计划。

items.en: That conflicted with how I needed to train to 5 my goals.

items.en: I also found that weighing myself daily did not provide an accurate 6 of the hard work and progress I was making in the gym.
items.zh: 我还发现每天称重并未提供一个准确的6来衡量我在健身房里所做的辛勤工作和进步。

items.en: It takes about three weeks to a month to notice significant changes in your weight 7 altering your training program.
items.zh: 需要大约三周到一个月的时间才能注意到体重的显著变化7改变你的训练计划。

items.en: The most 8 changes will be observed in skill level, strength and inches lost.
items.zh: 最8的变化将观察到在技能水平、力量和失去的英寸中。

items.en: For these 9, I stopped weighing myself every day and switched to a bimonthly weighing schedule 10.
items.zh: 对于这 9 个，我停止每天称重，改为每两个月称一次 10。

items.en: Since weight loss is not my goal, it is less important for me to 11 my weight each week.
items.zh: 由于减肥不是我的目标，每周11我的体重对我来说不那么重要。

items.en: Weighing every other week allows me to observe and 12 any significant weight changes.
items.zh: 每两周称一次体重让我观察并12任何显著的体重变化。

items.en: That tells me whether I need to 13 my training program.
items.zh: 这告诉我是否需要13我的训练计划。

items.en: I use my bimonthly weigh-in 14 to get information about my nutrition as well.
items.zh: 我也会利用每两个月一次的称重14来获取关于我营养状况的信息。

items.en: If my training intensity remains the same, but I’m constantly 15 and dropping weight, this is a 16 that I need to increase my daily caloric intake.
items.zh: 如果我的训练强度保持不变，但我在持续 15并减重，这是一个 16信号，表明我需要增加每日的热量摄入。

items.en: The 17 to stop weighing myself every day has done wonders for my overall health, fitness and well-being.
items.zh: 停止每天称重的第 17 条建议极大地改善了我的整体健康、体能和幸福感。

items.en: I’m experiencing increased zeal for working out since I no longer carry the burden of a 18 morning weigh-in.
items.zh: 自从我不再承担早上18点称重的负担，我对锻炼的热情增加了。

items.en: I’ve also experienced greater success in achieving my specific fitness goals, 19 I’m training according to those goals, not the numbers on a scale.
items.zh: 我也在实现特定健身目标方面取得了更大的成功，19 我是根据这些目标进行训练，而不是体重秤上的数字。

items.en: Rather than 20 over the scale, turn your focus to how you look, feel, how your clothes fit and your overall energy level.
items.zh: 与其关注体重秤上的20，不如将注意力转向你的外表、感受、衣服是否合身以及整体精力水平。

items.zh: 在答题卡上填写答案。（40分）

items.en: India has just announced it will “eliminate all single-use plastic in the country by 2022.
items.zh: 印度刚刚宣布将于2022年前全面禁止国内所有一次性塑料制品。

items.en: There are also incentive-based ways of making better environmental choices easier, such as ensuring recycling is at least as easy as trash disposal.
items.zh: 还有基于激励的方法可以使更好的环保选择更容易实现，例如确保回收利用至少和垃圾处理一样容易。

items.en: In choosing a new home, Camille McClain’s kids have a single demand: a backyard.
items.zh: 在选择新家时，Camille McClain的孩子们只有一个要求：一个后院。

items.en: McClain’s little ones aren’t the only kids who have an opinion when it comes to housing, and in many cases youngsters’ views weigh heavily on parents’ real estate decisions, according to a 2018 Harris Poll survey of more than 2,000 U.S. adults.
items.zh: McClain的小孩并非唯一在住房问题上有自己看法的孩子，根据2018年Harris Poll对2000多名美国成年人的调查，许多情况下孩子们的观点对父母的房地产决策产生重大影响。

items.en: While more families buck an older-generation proclivity to leave kids in the dark about real estate decisions, realty agents and psychologists have mixed views about the financial, personal and long-term effects kids’ opinions may have.
items.zh: 尽管越来越多的家庭反对老一辈让孩子对房地产决策一无所知的倾向，但房地产经纪人和心理学家对孩子们意见可能带来的财务、个人和长期影响看法不一。

items.en: The idea of involving children in a big decision is a great idea because it can help them feel a sense of control and ownership in what can be an overwhelming process, said Ryan Hooper, clinical psychologist in Chicago.
items.zh: 芝加哥临床心理学家瑞安·胡珀表示，让儿童参与重大决策是个好主意，因为它可以帮助他们在可能令人感到压倒的过程中感受到控制感和归属感。

items.en: “Children may face serious difficulties in coping with significant moves, especially if it removes them from their current school or support system,” he said.
items.zh: 他说，儿童在应对重大变动时可能会遇到严重困难，特别是如果这使他们离开当前学校或支持系统的话。

items.en: Greg Jaroszewski, real estate broker with Gagliardo Realty Associates, said he’s not convinced that kids should be involved in selecting a home – but their opinions should be considered in regards to proximity to friends and social activities, if possible.
items.zh: 格雷格·贾罗夫斯基（Greg Jaroszewski），Gagliardo Realty Associates房地产经纪公司经纪人，表示他并不确信孩子应该参与选择住房，但如果可能的话，应考虑他们的意见，尤其是住所与朋友和社交活动的接近程度。

items.en: Younger children should feel like they’re choosing their home – without actually getting a choice in the matter, said Adam Bailey, real estate attorney based in New York.
items.zh: 年幼的孩子应该感觉自己在选择自己的家——但实际上他们并没有选择权，纽约的房地产律师亚当·贝利（Adam Bailey）表示。

items.en: Asking them questions about what they like about the backyard of a potential home will make them feel like they’re being included in the decision-making process, Bailey said.
items.zh: 贝利表示，询问他们对潜在住宅后院的哪些方面感兴趣，会让他们感觉自己被纳入了决策过程。

items.en: Many of the aspects of homebuying aren’t a consideration for children, said Tracey Hampson, a real estate agent based in Santa Clarita, Calif.
items.zh: 据加利福尼亚州圣克拉利塔市的房地产经纪人Tracey Hampson所说，购房的许多方面都不是孩子们考虑的因素。

items.en: And placing too much emphasis on their opinions can ruin a fantastic home purchase.
items.zh: 过分重视他们的意见可能会毁掉一次绝佳的购房机会。

items.en: “Speaking with your children before you make a real estate decision is wise, but I wouldn’t base the purchasing decision solely on their opinions.
items.zh: 在做出房地产决策前与孩子沟通是明智的，但我不建议仅根据他们的意见做出购买决策。

items.en: Hampson said.
items.zh: 汉普森说。

items.en: The other issue is that many children – especially older ones – may base their real state knowledge on HGTV shows, said Aaron Norris of The Norris Group in Riverside, Calif.
items.zh: 另一个问题是，许多儿童——尤其是年长一些的——可能基于HGTV节目来获取他们的房地产知识，据加利福尼亚州里弗赛德The Norris Group的Aaron Norris所说。

items.en: “They love Chip and Joanna Gaines just as much as the rest of us,” he said.
items.zh: 他们和我们其他人一样喜欢Chip和Joanna Gaines，他说。

items.en: “HGTV has seriously changed how people view real estate.
items.zh: HGTV 严重地改变了人们看待房地产的方式。

items.en: It’s not shelter, it’s a lifestyle.
items.zh: 这不是庇护所，而是生活方式。

items.en: With that mindset change come some serious money consequences.
items.zh: 这种心态转变带来了一些严重的经济后果。

items.en: Kids tend to get stuck in the features and the immediate benefits to them personally, Norris said.
items.zh: 诺里斯表示，孩子们往往容易关注产品的特点和直接的好处。

items.en: Parents need to remind their children that their needs and desires may change over time, said Julie Gurner, a real estate analyst with FitSmallBusiness.com.
items.zh: 据房地产分析师Julie Gurner表示，父母需要提醒孩子，他们的需求和愿望可能会随着时间而改变。

items.en: “Their opinions can change tomorrow,” Gurner said.
items.zh: 他们的观点明天可能会改变，Gurner说。

items.en: “Harsh as it may be to say, that decision should likely not be made contingent on a child’s opinions, but rather made for them with great consideration into what home can meet their needs best–and give them an opportunity to customize it a bit and make it their own.
items.zh: 尽管这听起来可能很苛刻，但那个决定很可能不应取决于孩子的意见，而是应为他们慎重考虑哪种家庭环境最能满足他们的需求，并给予他们一定的机会来定制并使其成为自己的空间。

items.en: This advice is more relevant now than ever before, even as more parents want to embrace the ideas of their children, despite the current housing crunch.
items.zh: 这些建议现在比以往任何时候都更相关，尽管越来越多的父母希望接受孩子的想法，尽管当前住房紧张。

items.en: Ryan Hooper says that it is wise to leave kids in the dark about real estate decisions.
items.zh: Ryan Hooper，表示对房地产决策让孩子们保持无知是明智的。

items.en: Adam Bailey advises that home purchases should not be based only on children’s opinions.
items.zh: Adam Bailey，建议购房不应仅基于孩子的意见。

items.en: Tracey Hampson thinks that children should be given a sense of involvement in homebuying decisions.
items.zh: Tracey Hampson，认为儿童应在购房决策中获得参与感。

items.en: Aaron Norris notes that aspects like children’s friends and social activities should be considered upon homebuying.
items.zh: 亚伦·诺里斯指出，在购房时应考虑孩子的朋友和社会活动等因素。

items.en: Julie Gurner believes that homebuying decisions should be based on children’s needs rather than their opinions.
items.zh: 朱莉·格纳，认为购房决策应基于孩子的需要而不是他们的意见。

items.en: It is easy to underestimate English writer James Herriot.
items.zh: 低估英国作家詹姆斯·赫里奥特很容易。

items.en: He had such a pleasant, readable style that one might think that anyone could imitate it.

items.en: James Herriot, contrary to popular opinion, did not find it easy in his early days of, as he put it, “having a go at the writing game”.

items.en: While he obviously had an abundance of natural talent, the final, polished work that he gave to the world was the result of years of practicing, re-writing and reading.
items.zh: 虽然他显然拥有丰富的天赋，但他最终呈现给世界的作品是多年练习、重写和阅读的结果。

items.en: Like the majority of authors, he had to suffer many disappointments and rejections along the way, but these made him all the more determined to succeed.
items.zh: 和大多数作者一样，他在创作过程中不得不经历许多失望和拒绝，但这些经历反而使他更加决心取得成功。

items.en: Everything he achieved in life was earned the hard way and his success in the literary field was no exception.
items.zh: 他一生中所取得的一切成就都是通过艰苦努力获得的，而他在文学领域的成功也不例外。

items.en: Following the explosion of creativity in Florence during the 14th century known as the Renaissance, the modern world saw a departure from what it had once known.
items.zh: 随着14世纪佛罗伦萨文艺复兴时期创造力的爆发，现代世界开始摆脱过去所熟知的一切。

items.en: It turned from God and the authority of the Roman Catholic Church and instead favoured a more humanistic approach to being.
items.zh: 它转向了上帝和罗马天主教会的权威，转而青睐一种更人文主义的存在方法。

items.en: Renaissance ideas had spread throughout Europe well into the 17th century, with the arts and sciences flourishing extraordinarily among those with a more logical disposition.
items.zh: 文艺复兴时期的思想在17世纪初已广泛传播至整个欧洲，在那些更倾向于逻辑思维的人群中，艺术和科学蓬勃发展。

items.en: (46) With the Church's teachings and ways of thinking eclipsed by the Renaissance, the gap between the Medieval and modern periods had been bridged, leading to new and unexplored intellectual territories.
items.zh: 随着教会的教义和思维方式被文艺复兴所超越，中世纪与现代时期之间的鸿沟已被弥合，从而开辟了新的、未被探索的智力领域。

items.en: During the Renaissance, the great minds of Nicolaus Copernicus, Johannes Kepler and Galileo Galilei demonstrated the power of scientific study and discovery.
items.zh: 文艺复兴时期，尼古拉·哥白尼、约翰内斯·开普勒和伽利略·伽利莱这三位杰出人物展示了科学研究和发现的力量。

items.en: (47) Before each of their revelations, many thinkers at the time had sustained more ancient ways of thinking, including the geocentric view that the Earth was at the centre of our universe.
items.zh: 在每次启示之前，当时的许多思想家都坚持更古老的思想方式，包括认为地球是宇宙中心的地心说。

items.en: Copernicus theorized in 1543 that all of the planets that we knew of revolved not around the Earth, but the Sun, a system that was later upheld by Galileo at his own expense.
items.zh: 1543年哥白尼提出理论认为我们已知的所有行星并非围绕地球运转而是围绕太阳运转这一理论后来被伽利略以自己的代价捍卫

items.en: Offering up such a theory during a time of high tension between scientific and religious minds was branded as heresy and any such heretics that continued to spread these lies were to be punished by imprisonment or even death.
items.zh: 在科学界与宗教界人士关系紧张的时期提出这样的理论被指控为异端，任何继续传播这些谎言的异端分子都将被判处监禁甚至死刑。

items.en: (48) Despite attempts by the Church to suppress this new generation of logicians and rationalists, more explanations for how the universe functioned were being made at a rate that the people could no longer ignore.
items.zh: (48) 尽管教会试图压制新一代逻辑学家和理性主义者，但关于宇宙如何运作的更多解释正以人们再也无法忽视的速度被提出。

items.en: It was with these great revelations that a new kind of philosophy founded in reason was born.
items.zh: 正是这些重大启示催生了以理性为基础的新哲学。

items.en: The Church's long-standing dogma was losing the great battle for truth to rationalists and scientists.
items.zh: 教会长期坚持的教义正在在与理性主义者和科学家对真理的斗争中节节败退。

items.en: This very fact embodied the new ways of thinking that swept through Europe during most of 17th century.
items.zh: 这一事实体现了17世纪大部分时间席卷欧洲的新思维方式。

items.en: (49) As many took on the duty of trying to integrate reasoning and scientific philosophies into the world, the Renaissance was over and it was time for a new era - the Age of Reason.
items.zh: 当许多人承担起将推理和科学哲学融入世界的职责时，文艺复兴结束了，迎来了一个新时代——理性时代。

items.en: The 17th and 18th centuries were times of radical change and curiosity.

items.en: Scientific method, reductionism and the questioning of Church ideals was to be encouraged, as were ideas of liberty, tolerance and progress.

items.en: (50) Such actions to seek knowledge and to understand what information we already knew were captured by the Latin phrase 'sapere aude' or 'dare to know' after Immanuel Kant used it in his essay An Answer to the Question: What is Enlightenment?
items.zh: (50) 在伊曼努尔·康德在其论文《An Answer to the Question: What is Enlightenment?》中使用它之后，这些寻求知识和理解我们已知信息的行为被拉丁语短语'sapere aude'或'dare to know'所概括。

items.en: It was the purpose and responsibility of great minds to go forth and seek out the truth, which they believed to be founded in knowledge.

items.en: Five Ways to Win Over Everyone in the Office
items.zh: 五种方法赢得办公室所有人

items.en: Is it possible to like everyone in your office?
items.zh: 你能在办公室里喜欢每个人吗？

items.en: Think about how tough it is to get together 15 people, much less 50, who all get along perfectly.
items.zh: 想想看召集15个人，更不用说50个人，让他们都相处融洽有多难。

items.en: But unlike in friendships, you need coworkers.
items.zh: 与友谊不同，你需要同事。

items.en: You work with them every day, and you depend on them just as they depend on you.
items.zh: 你每天和他们一起工作，并且你依赖他们，就像他们依赖你一样。

items.en: Here are some ways that you can get the whole office on your side.
items.zh: 以下是一些让你赢得整个办公室支持的方法。

items.en: If you have a bone to pick with someone in your workplace, you may try to stay tight-lipped around them.
items.zh: 如果你在职场中有与某人需要解决的分歧，你可能会试图在他们面前保持沉默。

items.en: But you won’t be helping either one of you.
items.zh: 但你们中的任何一个都不会得到帮助。

items.en: A Harvard Business School study found that observers consistently rated those who were upfront about themselves more highly, while those who hid lost trustworthiness.
items.zh: 哈佛商学院的一项研究发现，观察者始终对那些坦率表达自己的人给予更高的评价，而隐瞒的人则失去了可信度。

items.en: The lesson is not that you should make your personal life an open book, but rather, when given the option to offer up details about yourself or studiously stash them away, you should just be honest.
items.zh: 这节课的教训不是你应该把个人生活当作一本公开的书，而是当你可以选择透露自己的细节或谨慎地将它们藏起来时，你只需诚实即可。

items.en: Just as important as being honest about yourself is being receptive to others.
items.zh: 与对自己诚实同样重要的是对他人开放。

items.en: We often feel the need to tell others how we feel, whether it's a concern about a project, a stray thought, or a compliment.
items.zh: 我们常常有向他人表达自己感受的需要，无论是对某个项目的担忧、一个零散的想法，还是一句赞美。

items.en: Those are all valid, but you need to take time to hear out your coworkers, too.
items.zh: 那些都是合理的，但你也需要花时间听完同事的话。

items.en: In fact, rushing to get your own ideas out there can cause colleagues to feel you don’t value their opinions.
items.zh: 事实上，急于表达自己的想法可能会让同事觉得你不重视他们的意见。

items.en: Do your best to engage coworkers in a genuine, back-and-forth conversation, rather than prioritizing your own thoughts.
items.zh: 尽你所能与同事进行真诚的、双向交流，而不是优先考虑你自己的想法。

items.en: It's common to have a “cubicle mate” or special confidant in a work setting.
items.zh: 在职场中拥有一个“隔间同事”或特别知己是很常见的。

items.en: But in addition to those trusted coworkers, you should expand your horizons and find out about all the people around you.
items.zh: 除了那些值得信赖的同事之外，你还应该拓展视野，了解你周围的所有人。

items.en: Use your lunch and coffee breaks to meet up with colleagues you don’t always see.
items.zh: 利用午餐和咖啡时间与不常见面的同事见面。

items.en: Find out about their lives and interests beyond the job.
items.zh: 了解他们工作之外的生活和兴趣。

items.en: It requires minimal effort and goes a long way.
items.zh: 它只需付出最小的努力，却能发挥巨大作用。

items.en: This will help to grow your internal network, in addition to being a nice break in the work day.
items.zh: 这将有助于扩展你的内部网络，同时也能在工作日中提供一个不错的休息时间。

items.en: Positive feedback is important for anyone to hear.
items.zh: 积极反馈对任何人都很重要。

items.en: And you don’t have to be someone’s boss to tell them they did an exceptional job on a particular project.
items.zh: 你不需要成为某人的上司就能告诉他们他们在某个特定项目上做得非常出色。

items.en: This will help engender good will in others.
items.zh: 这将有助于在他人中产生善意。

items.en: But don't overdo it or be fake about it.
items.zh: 但不要过分或在这方面做作。

items.en: One study found that people responded best to comments that shifted from negative to positive, possibly because it suggested they had won somebody over.
items.zh: 一项研究发现人们最积极响应从负面转向正面的评论，可能因为这暗示他们说服了某人。

items.en: This one may be a bit more difficult to pull off, but it can go a long way to achieving results.

items.en: Remember in dealing with any coworker what they appreciate from an interaction.

items.en: Watch out for how they verbalize with others.

items.en: Some people like small talk in a meeting before digging into important matters, while others are more straightforward.
items.zh: 有些人喜欢在会议中先闲聊，然后再深入讨论重要事项，而另一些人则更直接。

items.en: Jokes that work on one person won’t necessarily land with another.
items.zh: 对某个人有效的笑话不一定对另一个人有效。

items.en: So, adapt your style accordingly to type.
items.zh: 因此，根据类型相应调整你的风格。

items.en: Consider the person that you’re dealing with in advance and what will get you to your desired outcome.
items.zh: 提前考虑你所面对的人以及什么能帮助你达成预期结果。

items.en: It's almost impossible to go through life without experiencing some kind of failure.
items.zh: 几乎不可能不经历某种失败就度过一生。

items.en: But, the wonderful thing about failure is that it's entirely up to us to decide how to look at it.
items.zh: 但失败的美妙之处在于，我们完全由自己决定如何看待它。

items.en: We can choose to see failure as “the end of the world”.
items.zh: 我们可以选择将失败视为世界末日。

items.en: Or, we can look at failure as the incredible learning experience that it often is.
items.zh: 或者，我们可以把失败视为常常是不可思议的学习经历。

items.en: Every time we fail at something, we can choose to look for the lesson we’re meant to learn.
items.zh: 每次我们在某事上失败，我们都可以选择寻找我们应学习的教训。

items.en: These lessons are very important; they’re how we grow, and how we keep from making that same mistake again.
items.zh: 这些教训非常重要；它们是我们成长的方式，也是我们避免再次犯同样错误的方法。

items.en: Failures stop us only if we let them.
items.zh: 失败只有在我们允许它们的时候才会阻止我们。

items.en: Failure can also teach us things about ourselves that we would never have learned otherwise.
items.zh: 失败也能教会我们一些关于自己的事情，这些事情在其他情况下我们永远无法学到。

items.en: For instance, failure can help you discover how strong a person you are.
items.zh: 例如，失败可以帮助你发现你有多坚强。

items.en: Failing at something can help you discover your truest friends, or help you find unexpected motivation to succeed.
items.zh: 在某事上失败可以帮助你发现你最真诚的朋友，或帮助你找到意想不到的成功动力。

items.en: In the movies and on television, artificial intelligence is typically depicted as something sinister that will upend our way of life.
items.zh: 在电影和电视中，人工智能通常被描绘成某种邪恶的东西，将会颠覆我们的生活方式。

items.en: When it comes to AI in business, we often hear about it in relation to automation and the impending loss of jobs, but in what ways is AI changing companies and the larger economy that don't involve doom-and-gloom mass unemployment predictions?
items.zh: 当谈到商业中的人工智能时，我们经常听到与自动化和即将到来的失业危机相关的末日论，但人工智能在哪些方面正在改变公司和整个经济，而不涉及大规模失业的悲观预测？

items.en: A recent survey of manufacturing and service industries from Tata Consultancy Services found that companies currently use AI more often in computer-to-computer activities than in automating human activities.
items.zh: 最近一项来自塔塔咨询服务公司的对制造业和服务行业的调查发现，公司目前更常将AI用于计算机之间的活动，而不是用于自动化人类活动。

items.en: Here are a few ways AI is aiding companies without replacing employees:
items.zh: 以下是一些人工智能帮助公司而不取代员工的方式：

items.en: If you're doing research, you can have AI go out and look for relevant sources and information that otherwise you just wouldn't have time for.
items.zh: 如果你正在进行研究，让人工智能去查找那些否则你根本就没有时间去查找的相关资料和信息。

items.en: This process, along with employees reviewing the contracts, is faster and more accurate.
items.zh: 这一流程加上员工审查合同，更快捷、更准确。

items.en: World War I was the watershed event for higher education in modern Western societies.
items.zh: 第一次世界大战是现代西方社会高等教育的分水岭事件。

items.en: (46) Those societies came out of the war with levels of enrollment that had been roughly constant at 3-5% of the relevant age groups during the decades before the war.
items.zh: (46) 这些社会战后入学率水平在战前几十年间大致稳定在适龄群体的3-5%。

items.en: But after the war, great social and political changes arising out of the successful war against Fascism created a growing demand in European and American economies for increasing numbers of graduates with more than a secondary school education.
items.zh: 但战后，源于成功抗击法西斯主义的战争带来的重大社会和政治变革，导致欧洲和美国经济中对拥有超过中学教育水平的毕业生的需求不断增长。

items.en: (47) And the demand that rose in those societies for entry to higher education extended to groups and social classes that had not thought of attending a university before the war.
items.zh: 随着这些社会对高等教育需求的增加，一些此前从未想过战前上大学的群体和社会阶层也开始寻求入学机会。

items.en: These demands resulted in a very rapid expansion of the systems of higher education, beginning in the 1960s and developing very rapidly (though unevenly) during the 1970s and 1980s.
items.zh: 这些需求导致了高等教育体系的迅速扩张，始于1960年代，并在1970年代和1980年代期间迅速发展（尽管发展不均衡）。

items.en: The growth of higher education manifests itself in at least three quite different ways, and these in turn have given rise to different sets of problems.
items.zh: 高等教育的增长至少以三种截然不同的方式表现出来，而这些方式反过来又导致了不同的问题集合。

items.en: There was first the rate of growth: (48) in many countries of Western Europe, the numbers of students in higher education doubled within five-year periods during the 1960s and doubled again in seven, eight, or 10 years by the middle of the 1970s.
items.zh: 首先是增长速度：在许多西欧国家，20世纪60年代期间高等教育学生人数在五年内翻了一番，到20世纪70年代中期又在七到八年或十年内再次翻番。

items.en: Second, growth obviously affected the absolute size both of systems and individual institutions.
items.zh: 其次，增长显然影响了系统和个别机构的绝对规模。

items.en: And third, growth was reflected in changes in the proportion of the relevant age group enrolled in institutions of higher education.
items.zh: 第三，增长体现在相应年龄段进入高等教育机构的比例变化上。

items.en: Each of these manifestations of growth carried its own peculiar problems in its wake.
items.zh: 这些增长的各种表现形式都带来了各自特有的问题。

items.en: For example, a high growth rate placed great strains on the existing structures of governance, of administration, and above all of socialization.
items.zh: 例如，高增长率对现有的治理体系、行政体系以及尤其是社会化体系造成了巨大压力。

items.en: When a faculty or department grows from, say, five to 20 members within three or four years, (49) and when the new staff are predominantly young men and women fresh from postgraduate study, they largely define the norms of academic life in that faculty.
items.zh: 当一个学院或系在三到四年间成员从五人增至二十人时，（49）当新教职员工主要由刚完成研究生学习的年轻人组成时，他们很大程度上定义了该学院学术生活的规范。

items.en: And if the postgraduate student population also grows rapidly and there is loss of a close apprenticeship relationship between faculty members and students, the student culture becomes the chief socializing force for new postgraduate students, with consequences for the intellectual and academic life of the institution — this was seen in America as well as in France, Italy, West Germany, and Japan.
items.zh: 如果研究生人数也迅速增长且师生之间亲密的学徒关系丧失，学生文化将成为新研究生的主要社会化力量，对机构的学术和智力生活产生影响——这在美国以及法国、意大利、西德和日本都曾出现过。

items.en: (50) High growth rates increased the chances for academic innovation; they also weakened the forms and processes by which teachers and students are admitted into a community of scholars during periods of stability or slow growth.
items.zh: （50）高增长率为学术创新提供了更多机会；它们也削弱了在稳定或缓慢增长时期教师和学生被接纳进入学术共同体的形式和过程。

items.en: In the 1960s and 1970s, European universities saw marked changes in their governance arrangements, with empowerment of junior faculty and to some degree of students as well.
items.zh: 在1960年代和1970年代，欧洲大学经历了治理结构的显著变化，初级教职员工在一定程度上也被赋予权力。

items.en: How to disagree with someone more powerful than you
items.zh: 如何反对比你更有权势的人

items.en: Your boss proposes a new initiative you think won’t work.
items.zh: 你的老板提出了一项你认为不会成功的倡议。

items.en: Your senior colleague outlines a project timeline you believe is unrealistic.
items.zh: 你的资深同事概述了一个你认为不现实的项目时间表。

items.en: What do you say when you disagree with someone who has more power than you do?
items.zh: 当你与比你更有权力的人意见不同时，你会说什么？

items.en: How do you decide whether it’s worth speaking up?
items.zh: 你如何决定是否值得发言？

items.en: And if you do, what exactly should you say?
items.zh: 如果这样做，究竟应该说什么？

items.en: Here's how to disagree with someone more powerful than you.
items.zh: 以下是与比你更有权势的人意见不合的方法。

items.en: You may decide it’s best to hold off on voicing your opinion.
items.zh: 你可能会决定推迟表达你的观点。

items.en: Maybe you haven’t finished thinking the problem through, or you want to get a clearer sense of what the group thinks.If you think other people are going to disagree, too, you might want to gather your army first.
items.zh: 也许你还没彻底思考这个问题，或者你想更清楚地了解小组的想法。如果你认为其他人也会不同意，你可能需要先拉拢支持者。

items.en: People can contribute experience or information to your thinking—all the things that would make the disagreement stronger or more valid.
items.zh: 人们可以将经验或信息贡献给你的思考——所有能让分歧更强烈或更合理的事物。

items.en: It’s also a good idea to delay the conversation if you are in a meeting or other public space.
items.zh: 这也是个好主意，若你身处会议或其他公共场合，可推迟谈话。

items.en: Discussing the issue in private will make the powerful person feel less threatened.
items.zh: 私下讨论这个问题会让有权力的人感到威胁减少。

items.en: Before you share your thoughts, think about what the powerful person cares about—it may be the credibility of their team or getting a project done on time.You’re more likely to be heard if you can connect your disagreement to a higher purpose.
items.zh: 在分享你的想法之前，考虑一下权力者关心什么——可能是他们的团队信誉或按时完成项目。如果你能将你的不同意见与更高的目标联系起来，你更可能被采纳意见。

items.en: When you do speak up, don’t assume the link will be clear.
items.zh: 当你发言时，不要以为联系会很明确。

items.en: You’ll want to state it overtly, contextualizing your statements so that you’re seen not as a disagreeable subordinate but
items.zh: 你需要明确地表达这一点，结合具体情境来陈述，以确保你不会被视为一个不讨喜的下属，而是

items.en: as a colleague who’s trying to advance a common objective.
items.zh: 作为一位试图推进共同目标的同事

items.en: The discussion will then become more like a chess game than a boxing match.
items.zh: 讨论将更像一场棋局，而非拳赛。

items.en: This step may sound overly deferential, but it’s a smart way to give the powerful person psychological safety and control.
items.zh: 这一步可能显得过于顺从，但这是给予有权力的人心理安全感和控制感的聪明做法。

items.en: You can say something like, “I know we seem to be moving toward a first-quarter commitment here.I have reasons to think that won’t work.I’d like to lay out my reasoning.
items.zh: 你可以这样说：“我知道我们似乎正在朝着这里的第一季度承诺迈进。我有理由认为这行不通。我想阐述我的理由。”

items.en: Would that be OK?

items.en: This gives the person a choice, allowing him to verbally opt in.

items.en: You might feel your heart racing or your face turning red, but do whatever you can to remain neutral in both your words and actions.

items.en: When your body language communicates reluctance or anxiety, it undercuts the message.It sends a mixed message,and your counterpart gets to choose what signals to read.

items.en: Deep breaths can help,as can speaking more slowly and deliberately.

items.en: When we feel panicky, we tend to talk louder and faster.

items.en: Simply slowing the pace and talking in an even tone helps the other person cool down and does the same for you.
items.zh: 只需放慢语速并用平稳语调说话，就能帮助对方冷静下来，同样也能帮助你冷静。

items.en: It also makes you seem confident, even if you aren’t.

items.en: Emphasize that you’re only offering your opinion, not gospel truth.It may be a well-informed, well-researched opinion, but it’s still an opinion, so talk tentatively and slightly understate your confidence.
items.zh: 强调你只是在表达个人观点，而非绝对真理。这可能是一个信息充分且经过深入研究的观点，但它仍然是一个观点，因此要试探性地表达，并略微降低自信程度。

items.en: Instead of saying: “If we set an end-of-quarter deadline, we will never make it,” say, “ This is just my opinion, but I don’t see how we will make that deadline.

items.en: Having asserted your opinion (as a position, not as a fact),demonstrate equal curiosity about other views.

items.en: Remind the person that this is your point of view, and then invite critique.

items.en: While that may well be true, researchers have also recently found that interacting with strangers actually brings a boost in mood and feelings of belonging that we didn’t expect.

items.en: In one series of studies, researchers instructed Chicago-area commuters using public transportation to strike up a conversation with someone near them.

items.en: On average, participants who followed this instruction felt better than those who had been told to stand or sit in silence.
items.zh: 平均而言，遵循该指示的参与者感觉比那些被要求站立或静坐的参与者更好。

items.en: The researchers also argued that when we shy away from casual interactions with strangers, it is often due to a misplaced anxiety that they might not want to talk to us.
items.zh: 研究人员还指出，当我们回避与陌生人的随意互动时，通常是因为存在一种错误的焦虑，担心他们可能不想与我们交谈。

items.en: Much of the time,however, this belief is false.As it turns out, many people are actually perfectly willing to talk — and may even be flattered to receive your attention.
items.zh: 很多时候，然而，这种信念是错误的。实际上，许多人完全愿意交谈——甚至可能因为受到你的关注而感到荣幸。

items.en: The Man Who Broke Napoleon's Codes — Mark Urban
items.zh: 破解拿破仑密码的人 —— Mark Urban

items.en: Between 1807 and 1814 the Iberian Peninsula (comprising Spain and Portugal) was the scene of a titanic and merciless struggle.
items.zh: 1807年至1814年间，伊比利亚半岛（包括西班牙和葡萄牙）爆发了一场惨烈而无情的斗争。

items.en: It took place on many different planes: between Napoleon's French army and the angry inhabitants; between the British, ever keen to exacerbate the emperor's difficulties, and the marshals sent from Paris to try to keep them in check; between new forces of science and meritocracy and old ones of conservatism and birth.
items.zh: 它发生在多个不同层面：拿破仑的法国军队与愤怒的居民之间；英国人，总是急于加剧皇帝的困境，与从巴黎派来的元帅之间，后者试图遏制他们；新出现的科学与功绩主义力量与旧有的保守主义和出身观念之间。

items.en: (46) It was also, and this is unknown even to many people well read about the period, a battle between those who made codes and those who broke them.
items.zh: (46) 这也是一场制定密码者与破解密码者之间的较量，这一点甚至对许多对该时期有深入了解的人而言都是未知的。

items.en: I first discovered the Napoleonic cryptographic battle a few years ago when I was reading Sir Charles Oman's epic History of the Peninsular War.
items.zh: 我几年前在阅读查尔斯·欧曼爵士的巨著《半岛战争史》时首次发现了拿破仑密码战。

items.en: In volume V he had attached an appendix, The Scovell Ciphers.
items.zh: 在第五卷中，他附上了《The Scovell Ciphers》附录。

items.en: (47) It listed many documents in code that had been captured from the French army of Spain, and whose secrets had been revealed by the work of one George Scovell, an officer in British headquarters.
items.zh: (47) 它列出许多从法国驻西班牙军队缴获的加密文件，这些文件的秘密被英国总部一名军官乔治·斯科维尔的工作所揭露。

items.en: Oman rated Scovell's significance highly, but at the same time, the general nature of his History meant that (48) he could not analyze carefully what this obscure officer may or may not have contributed to that great struggle between nations or indeed tell us anything much about the man himself.
items.zh: 阿曼高度评价斯科维尔的重要性，但同时，他所著《历史》一书的总体性质意味着48他无法仔细分析这位鲜为人知的军官可能或可能没有为国家间的重大斗争做出什么贡献，甚至无法向我们提供关于这位军官本人的太多信息。

items.en: I was keen to read more, but was surprised to find that Oman's appendix, published in 1914, was the only considered thing that had been written about this secret war.
items.zh: 我很想阅读更多，却惊讶地发现，1914年出版的《Oman附录》是唯一被认可的关于这场秘密战争的著作。

items.en: I became convinced that this story was every bit as exciting and significant as that of Enigma and the breaking of German codes in the Second World War.
items.zh: 我确信这个故事与恩尼格玛密码机和二战期间德国密码的破解一样令人兴奋且意义重大。

items.en: The question was, could it be told?
items.zh: 问题是，它能否被讲述？

items.en: Studying Scovell's papers at the Public Record Office, London, I found that he had left an extensive journal and copious notes about his work in the Peninsula.
items.zh: 在伦敦公共档案办公室研究斯科维尔的文件时，我发现他留下了一份详尽的日记和大量关于他在半岛工作的笔记。

items.en: What was more, many original French dispatches had been preserved in this collection, which I realized was priceless.
items.zh: 更重要的是，许多原始的法国电报已经被保存在这份收藏中，我意识到它无价。

items.en: (49) There may have been many spies and intelligence officers during the Napoleonic Wars, but it is usually extremely difficult to find the material they actually provided or worked on.
items.zh: （49）在拿破仑战争期间可能有许多间谍和情报官员，但通常很难找到他们实际提供的资料或处理的材料。

items.en: Furthermore, Scovell's story involved much more than just intelligence work.
items.zh: 此外，Scovell的故事涉及远不止情报工作。

items.en: His status in Lord Wellington's headquarters and the recognition given to him for his work were all bound up with the class politics of the army at the time.
items.zh: 他在威灵顿勋爵总部的地位以及因工作而获得的认可，都与当时军队的阶级政治密切相关。

items.en: His tale of self-improvement and hard work would make a fascinating biography in its own right, but represents something more than that.
items.zh: 他关于自我提升和努力工作的故事本身就足以成为一部引人入胜的传记，但还象征着比这更多的东西。

items.en: (50) Just as the code breaking has its wider relevance in the struggle for Spain, so his attempts to make his way up the promotion ladder speak volumes about British society.
items.zh: (50) 正如密码破译在西班牙的斗争中具有更广泛的意义，他的晋升阶梯上的努力也充分反映了英国社会的情况。

items.en: The story of Wellington himself also gripped me.
items.zh: 温特沃斯本人的故事也吸引了我。

items.en: Half a century ago his campaigns were considered a central part of the British historical mythology and spoon-fed to schoolboys.
items.zh: 半个世纪前，他的战役被视为英国历史神话的重要组成部分，并被灌输给男学生。

items.en: More recently this has not been the case, which is a great shame.

items.en: A generation has grown up.

items.en: How to Get Active Again

items.en: Getting back into exercise can be a challenge in the best of times, but with gyms and in-person exercise classes off-limits to many people these days, it can be tricky to know where to start.
items.zh: 在最好的时候，重新开始锻炼也可能是一项挑战，但在如今许多健身房和线下运动课程都无法进入的情况下，要确定从哪里开始可能会很困难。

items.en: And it’s important to get the right dose of activity.
items.zh: 重要的是获得适量的活动。

items.en: “Too much too soon either results in injury or burnout,” says Mary Yoke, PhD, a faculty member in the kinesiology department at Indiana University in Bloomington.
items.zh: 印第安纳大学布卢明顿分校运动科学系的Mary Yoke博士表示：过早过度要么导致受伤，要么导致倦怠。

items.en: The following simple strategies will help you return to exercise safely after a break.
items.zh: 以下简单策略将帮助你在休息后安全恢复锻炼。

items.en: Don’t try to go back to what you were doing before your break.
items.zh: 不要试图回到你休假前做的事情。

items.en: If you were walking 3 miles a day, playing 18 holes of golf three times a week, or lifting 10-pound dumbbells for three sets of 10 reps, reduce activity to half a mile every other day, or nine holes of golf once a week with short walks on other days, or use 5-pound dumbbells for one set of 10 reps.
items.zh: 如果你每天步行3英里，每周打三次18洞高尔夫球，或每周三次进行三组10次10磅哑铃训练，可减少为每两天步行半英里，或每周打一次九洞高尔夫球并在其他时间短途散步，或使用5磅哑铃进行一组10次训练。

items.en: Increase time, distance, and intensity gradually.
items.zh: 逐渐增加时间、距离和强度。

items.en: “This isn’t something you can do overnight,” says Keri L.
items.zh: 这不是短时间内能完成的事情，凯莉·L.说。

items.en: Denay, MD, lead author of a recent American College of Sports Medicine advisory that encourages Americans to not overlook the benefits of activity during the pandemic.
items.zh: 丹尼（Denay），医学博士，是美国运动医学会近期一份建议的主要作者，该建议鼓励美国人不要忽视疫情期间活动的好处。

items.en: But you will reap benefits such as less anxiety and improve sleep right away.
items.zh: 但你将立即获得减少焦虑和改善睡眠等益处。

items.en: If you’re breathing too hard to talk in complete sentences, back off.
items.zh: 如果你呼吸得太急促以至于无法完整地说出句子，就退后一步。

items.en: If you feel good, go a little longer or faster.
items.zh: 如果你感觉良好，就再坚持一会儿或加快速度。

items.en: Feeling wiped out after a session?
items.zh: 参加完一次课程后感到筋疲力尽吗？

items.en: Go easier next time.
items.zh: 下次轻松点。

items.en: And stay alert to serious symptoms, such as chest pain or pressure, severe shortness of breath or dizziness, or faintness, and seek medical attention immediately.
items.zh: 并留意诸如胸痛或胸压、严重呼吸困难、头晕或昏厥等严重症状，立即就医。

items.en: Consistency is the key to getting stronger and building endurance and stamina.
items.zh: 坚持是增强力量和培养耐力与耐久力的关键。

items.en: Ten minutes of activity per day is a good start, says Marcus Jackovitz, DPT, a physical therapist at the University of Miami Hospital.
items.zh: 每天进行10分钟的活动是一个好的开始，迈阿密大学医院的物理治疗师Marcus Jackovitz，DPT表示。

items.en: All the experts we spoke with highly recommend walking because ifs the easiest, most accessible form of exercise.
items.zh: 我们采访的所有专家都强烈推荐步行，因为它是最容易、最易获得的锻炼方式。

items.en: Althoughit can be a workout on its own, if your goal is to get back to Zumba classes, tennis, cycling, or any other activity, walking is also a great first step.
items.zh: 虽然它本身就是一个锻炼，但如果你的目标是重新参加尊巴课程、网球、骑自行车或任何其他活动，步行也是一个很好的第一步。

items.en: Even if you can’t yet do a favorite activity, you can practice the moves.
items.zh: 即使你目前还不能做最喜欢的活动，也可以练习动作。

items.en: With or without a club or racket, swing like you’re hitting the ball.
items.zh: 无论有没有球杆或球拍，都要像击球那样挥动。

items.en: Paddle like you’re in a kayak or canoe.
items.zh: 像在独木舟或皮划艇中一样划桨。

items.en: Mimic your favorite swimming strokes.
items.zh: 模仿你最喜欢的游泳动作。

items.en: The action will remind you of the joy the activity brought you and prime your muscles for when you can get out there again.
items.zh: 这个动作会提醒你这项活动曾带给你的快乐，并激活你的肌肉为再次行动做好准备。

items.en: Exercising with others “ can keep you accountable and make it more fun, so you’re more likely to do it again,” Jackovitz says.
items.zh: 和他人一起锻炼可以让你保持责任感并增加乐趣，因此你更有可能再次进行锻炼，Jackovitz说。

items.en: You can do activities such as golf and tennis or take a walk with others and still be socially distant.
items.zh: 你可以进行高尔夫、网球等活动，或者与他人一起散步，同时仍然保持社交距离。

items.en: But when you can’t connect in person, consider using technology.
items.zh: 但当你无法当面交流时，不妨考虑使用技术。

items.en: Chat on the phone with a friend while you walk around your neighborhood.
items.zh: 在你的社区里散步时打电话和朋友聊天。

items.en: FaceTime with a relative as you strength train or stretch at home.
items.zh: 当你在家进行力量训练或拉伸时，和亲戚进行FaceTime视频通话。

items.en: You can also join a livestream or on-demand exercise class.
items.zh: 你也可以参加直播或点播的健身课程。

items.en: Although we try our best, sometimes our paintings rarely turn out as originally planned.
items.zh: 尽管我们尽了最大努力，有时我们的画作很少能达到最初计划的效果。

items.en: Changes in the light, the limitations of your painting materials, and the lack of experience and technique mean that what you start out trying to achieve may not come to life the way that you expected.
items.zh: 光线变化、绘画材料的限制以及缺乏经验和技巧意味着你最初试图实现的效果可能不会以你预期的方式呈现出来。

items.en: Although this can be frustrating and disappointing, it turns out that this can actually be good for you.
items.zh: 尽管这可能令人沮丧和失望，事实证明这其实对你有好处。

items.en: Unexpected results have two benefits: you pretty quickly learn to deal with disappointment, and realise that when one door closes, another opens.
items.zh: 意外的结果有两个好处：你很快学会应对失望，并意识到当一扇门关闭时，另一扇门会打开。

items.en: You also quickly learn to adapt and come up with creative solutions to the problems the painting presents, and thinking outside the box will become your second nature.
items.zh: 你也会迅速学会适应并想出创造性的解决方案来应对绘画所呈现的问题，并且跳出思维定式将成为你的本能。

items.en: In fact, creative problem-solving skills are incredibly useful in daily life, with which you’re more likely to be able to find a solution when a problem arises.
items.zh: 事实上，创造性解决问题的技能在日常生活中非常有用，有了这些技能，当问题出现时你更有可能找到解决方案。

items.en: Suppose you are planning a campus food festival.
items.zh: 假设你正在计划一场校园美食节。

items.en: Write an e-mail to the international students in your university to 1) introduce the food festival, and 2) invite them to participate.
items.zh: 写一封电子邮件给你们大学的国际学生，1）介绍美食节，2）邀请他们参加。

items.en: In your writing, you should 1) interpret the chart, and 2) give your comments.
items.zh: 在你的写作中，你应该1）解释图表，2）发表你的评论。

items.en: Caravanserais were roadside inns that were built along the Silk Road in areas including China, North Africa and the Middle East.
items.zh: 驿站是沿丝绸之路在包括中国、北非和中东在内的地区建造的路边旅馆。

items.en: They were typically 1 outside the walls of a city or village and were usually funded by governments or 2 .
items.zh: 它们通常位于1城市或村庄的城墙外，并且通常由政府或2资助。

items.en: This word "Caravanserais" is a 3 of the Persian word "karvan", which means a group of travellers or a caravan, and "seray", a palace or enclosed building.
items.zh: 这个词"Caravanserais"是波斯语单词"karvan"的3，意为一群旅行者或商队，以及"seray"，即宫殿或封闭建筑。

items.en: The term caravan was used to 4 groups of people who travelled together across the ancient network for safety reasons, 5 merchants, travellers or pilgrims.
items.zh: 商队一词用于指代4人群，他们出于安全原因一起穿越古代网络，5商人、旅行者或朝圣者。

items.en: From the 10th century onwards, as merchant and travel routes became more developed, the 6 of the caravanserais increased and they served as a safe place for people to rest at night.
items.zh: 从 10世纪起，随着商路和旅行路线的发展，驿站的 6增加，它们成为人们夜间休息的安全场所。

items.en: Travellers on the Silk Road 7 possibility of being attacked by thieves or being 8 to extreme weather conditions.
items.zh: 丝绸之路的旅行者面临7被盗贼袭击或8极端天气条件的可能性。

items.en: For this reason, caravanserais were strategically placed 9 they could be reached in a day's travel time.
items.zh: 因此，驿站被战略性地设置在9它们可以在一天的行程内到达的位置。

items.en: Caravanserais served as an informal 10 point for the various people who travelled the Silk Road.
items.zh: 驿站曾作为非正式的 10 个点，供不同的人们在丝绸之路旅行时使用。

items.en: 11 , these structures became important centers for cultural 12 and interaction, with travellers sharing their cultures, ideas and beliefs, 13 taking knowledge with them, greatly 14 the development of several civilisations.
items.zh: 11 ，这些结构成为文化 12 和交流的重要中心，旅行者分享他们的文化、思想和信仰， 13 带走知识，极大地 14 了几个文明的发展。

items.en: Caravanserais were also an important marketplace for commodities and 15 in the trade of goods along the Silk Road.
items.zh: 驿站也是丝绸之路上商品贸易的重要市场，15在商品贸易中扮演了重要角色。

items.en: 16 , it was frequently the first stop for merchants looking to sell their wares and 17 supplies for their own journeys.
items.zh: 16 ，它经常是商人们出售商品和为自己的旅程准备 17 补给的第一站。

items.en: It is 18 that around 12,000 to 15,000 caravanserais were built along the Silk Road, 19 only about 3,000 are known to remain today, many of which are in 20 .
items.zh: 据估计，丝绸之路沿线曾建有约12000至15000座驿站，19 如今仅约3000座仍存，许多已处于20状态。

items.en: Horn said.
items.zh: 霍恩说。

items.zh: 第41至45题，要求你从A至H的选项中选择段落，重新排列成连贯的文本，并填入编号的方框中。

items.en: He captured the first-ever shots of iconic landmarks such as the Tetons, Old Faithful and the Colorado Rockies.
items.zh: 他首次拍摄到了诸如提顿山脉、老忠实泉和科罗拉多洛基山脉等标志性地标。

items.en: Jackson snapped them on a late 19th-century expedition through the Yellowstone Basin that was conducted by the head of the U.S. Geological and Geographical Survey of the Territories, Ferdinand V.
items.zh: 杰克逊在19世纪末由美国领土地质与地理勘测局负责人费迪南德·V. 主持的黄石盆地探险中拍摄了它们。

items.en: Hayden.
items.zh: 海登。

items.en: The team included a meteorologist, a zoologist, a mineralogist, and an agricultural statistician.
items.zh: 团队包括一名气象学家、一名动物学家、一名矿物学家和一名农业统计学家。

items.en: One of the turning points in public support for land conservation efforts—and recognizing the magnificence of the Yellowstone region in particular—came in the form of vivid photographs.
items.zh: 公众对土地保护努力的支持——特别是对黄石地区壮丽景色的认可——的一个转折点以生动的照片形式出现。

items.en: He asked Jackson to print out large copies and distributed them, along with reproductions of Moran's paintings, to each member of Congress.
items.zh: 他让杰克逊打印大尺寸的副本并分发给每位国会议员，同时附上莫兰画作的复制品。

items.en: "The visualization, particularly those photographs, really hit home that this is something that has to be protected," says Murphy.
items.zh: Murphy说：“这些可视化展示，尤其是那些照片，让人深有感触，这说明有些东西必须加以保护。”

items.en: The crude technique required educated guesses on exposure times, and involved heavy, awkward equipment—several men had to assist in its transportation.
items.zh: 这种粗糙的技术需要根据经验估计曝光时间，并且需要多人协助运输笨重而不灵便的设备。

items.en: Despite these challenges, Jackson captured dozens of striking photos, ranging from majestic images like his now-famous snapshot of Old Faithful, to casual portraits of expedition members at the camp.
items.zh: 尽管面临这些挑战，杰克逊拍摄了数十张引人注目的照片，从诸如他如今著名的Old Faithful快照等壮观画面，到营地里探险队员的随意肖像。

items.en: While veterans of previous expeditions wrote at length about stunning trail sights, these vivid photographs were another thing entirely.
items.zh: 虽然有经验的探险者们详细描述了令人惊叹的徒步路线景色，但这些生动的照片则是另一回事。

items.en: Over nearly four months, dozens of men made their way on horseback into Montana and traversed along the Yellowstone River and around Yellowstone Lake.
items.zh: 历时近四个月，几十名男子骑马前往蒙大拿州，沿着黄石河行进并环绕黄石湖。

items.en: That fall, they concluded the survey in Fort Bridger, Wyoming.
items.zh: 那个秋天，他们结束了在怀俄明州福尔特·布里杰的调查。

items.en: That's why Hayden's expedition aimed to produce a fuller understanding of the Yellowstone River region, from its hot springs and waterfalls to its variety of flora and fauna.
items.zh: 这就是为什么海登的探险队旨在对该地区从温泉瀑布到动植物多样性产生更全面的理解。

items.en: In addition to the entourage of scientists, the team also included artists: Painter Thomas Moran and photographer William Henry Jackson were charged with capturing this astounding natural beauty and sharing it with the world.
items.zh: 除了科学家团队，该团队还包括艺术家：画家托马斯·莫兰和摄影师威廉·亨利·杰克逊负责记录这一令人惊叹的自然美景并将其与世界分享。

items.en: In quick succession, the Senate and House passed legislation protecting Yellowstone in early 1872.
items.zh: 参议院和众议院接连不断地在1872年初通过了保护黄石公园的立法。

items.en: That March, President Ulysses S.
items.zh: 那年三月，总统Ulysses S.

items.en: Grant signed an act into law that established Yellowstone as the world's first national park.
items.zh: 格兰特签署了将法案变为法律，设立Yellowstone为世界第一个国家公园。

items.en: Soon, some locals opposed the designation.
items.zh: 不久之后，一些当地人反对这一指定。

items.en: Still, the decision was largely accepted—and Jackson's photos played a key role in the fight to protect the area.
items.zh: 不过，这一决定还是被广泛接受——杰克逊的照片在保护该地区的斗争中发挥了关键作用。

items.en: "I don't believe that the legal protection would have happened in the timeframe that it did without those images," says Hansen, journalist and author of Prophets and Moguls, Rangers and Rogues, Bison and Bears: 100 Years of the National Park Service.
items.zh: 汉森说：“如果没有那些图片，我认为法律保护不会在它实际发生的时间框架内实现。”汉森是记者，也是《先知与大亨、护林员与恶棍、野牛与熊：国家公园管理局100年史》一书的作者。

items.en: Weeks after completing the expedition, Hayden collected his team's observations into an extensive report aimed at convincing Senators and Representatives, along with colleagues at government agencies like the Department of the Interior that Yellowstone ought to be preserved.
items.zh: 完成探险数周后，Hayden将团队的观察整理成一份详尽报告，旨在说服参议员和众议员以及政府机构如内政部的同事，黄石公园应当被保护。

items.en: There has been some exploration around the use of AI in digital marketing.
items.zh: 在数字营销中使用人工智能方面已有一些探索。

items.en: For example, AI can be used to analyse what type of advertising content or copy would be appropriate to 'speak' to a specific target customer group by revealing information about trends and preferences through the analysis of big data.
items.zh: 例如，AI可以通过分析大数据揭示趋势和偏好信息，从而确定适合特定目标客户群体的广告内容或文案。

items.en: (46) AI can also be used to identify the lifestyle choices of customers regarding their hobbies, favourite celebrities, music choices, and fashions to provide unique content in marketing messages put out through social media.
items.zh: 人工智能也可以被用来识别客户在兴趣爱好、喜爱的名人、音乐选择和时尚方面的生活方式，以在通过社交媒体发布的营销信息中提供独特内容。

items.en: At the same time AI can also be used to generate content for social media posts and chat sites.
items.zh: 同时AI也可以用于生成社交媒体帖子和聊天网站的内容。

items.en: AI can also provide a bridge between the need of the brand to communicate emotionally with the customer and identifying their rapidly changing needs.
items.zh: 人工智能也可以架起一座桥梁，连接品牌与客户进行情感沟通的需求以及识别客户快速变化的需求。

items.en: The main disadvantage of using AI to respond to customers is that there are concerns about trusting personal interactions to machines, which could lead not only to the subsequent loss of interpersonal connections, but also to a decrease in marketing personnel.
items.zh: 使用AI回复客户的主要缺点是人们担心将个人互动交由机器处理，这不仅可能导致后续人际关系的丧失，还会导致营销人员减少。

items.en: (47) Some believe that AI is negatively impacting on the marketer's role by reducing creativity and removing jobs, but they are aware that it is a way of reducing costs and creating new information.
items.zh: 一些人认为AI正在通过减少创造力和消除职位对营销人员的角色产生负面影响，但他们意识到这是降低成本和创造新信息的一种方式。

items.en: By allowing AI to develop content some brand marketers may find that they are losing control over the brand narrative.
items.zh: 通过允许AI生成内容，一些品牌营销人员可能会发现他们正在失去对品牌叙事的控制。

items.en: (48) Algorithms that are used to simulate human interactions are creating many of these concerns, especially as no-one is quite sure what the outcomes of using AI to interact with customers will be.
items.zh: (48) 用于模拟人类互动的算法正在引发许多这些担忧，尤其是因为没有人完全确定使用AI与客户互动的结果会是什么。

items.en: For AI to be successful, data needs to be accessible, but the use of personal data is becoming more regulated and the automated sharing of data is becoming more difficult.
items.zh: 人工智能要取得成功，数据需要易于获取，但个人数据的使用正变得越来越受监管，数据的自动共享也正变得越来越困难。

items.en: (49) If customers are not willing to share data, AI will be starved of essential information and will not be able to function effectively or employ machine learning to improve its marketing content and communication.
items.zh: 如果顾客不愿意分享数据，人工智能将缺乏必要的信息，无法有效运作或利用机器学习来改进其营销内容和沟通。

items.en: Therefore, unless customers are prepared to sign release agreements, the use of AI may become somewhat restricted in the future.
items.zh: 因此，除非客户准备好签署免责协议，否则未来AI的使用可能会受到一定程度的限制。

items.en: Not only can AI help to create the marketing content, but it can also provide a non-intrusive way of delivering the content to the target customers.
items.zh: 人工智能不仅可以帮助创建营销内容，还能以一种非侵入式的方式将内容传递给目标客户。

items.en: Data can be gathered on where the customer can be engaged, such as location, devices used, website interactions, and sites visited, to display marketing messages in appropriate forms, including emails, social media posts, pop-up advertisements, and banners at an appropriate frequency.
items.zh: 可以收集客户参与的地点数据，例如地理位置、使用的设备、网站互动和访问的网站，以适当的形式展示营销信息，包括电子邮件、社交媒体帖子、弹出广告和横幅，并以适当的频率进行推送。

items.en: (50) The non-intrusive delivery of the marketing messages in a way that is sensitive to the needs of the target customer is one of the critical challenges to the digital marketer.
items.zh: （50）以一种敏感于目标客户需求的方式非侵入式传递营销信息是数字营销者面临的关键挑战之一。

items.zh: 撰写一份通知招募一名学生参与史密斯教授关于校园体育活动的研究项目。

items.zh: 明确工作的职责和要求。

items.en: Here’s a common scenario that any number of entrepreneurs face today: you’re the CEO of a small business and though you're making a nice 1, you need to find a way to take it to the next level.
items.zh: 今天众多企业家面临的常见场景是：你是某家小企业的首席执行官，虽然你正在获得不错的1，但你需要找到一种方法将其提升到更高层次。

items.en: what you need to do is 2 growth by establishing a growth team.
items.zh: 你需要做的就是2增长通过建立一个增长团队。

items.en: A growth team is made up of members from different departments within your company, and it harnesses the power of collaboration to focus 3 on finding ways to grow.
items.zh: 增长团队由来自公司不同部门的成员组成，它发挥协作的力量，聚焦于3寻找增长的方法。

items.en: Let's look at a real-world 4.
items.zh: 让我们看看现实世界中的4。

items.en: Prior to forming a growth team, the software company BitTorrent had 50 employees.Working in the 5 departments of engineering, marketing and product development.
items.zh: 在组建增长团队之前，软件公司BitTorrent有50名员工。在工程、市场和产品开发这5个部门工作。

items.en: New building regulations aimed at improving energy efficiency are set to increase the price of new homes, as well as those of extensions and loft conversions on existing ones.
items.zh: 旨在提高能源效率的新建筑法规将提高新建住宅的价格，以及现有房屋的扩建和阁楼改造的价格。

items.en: The rules, which came into effect on Wednesday in England, are part of government plans to reduce the UK’s carbon emissions to net zero by 2050.
items.zh: 这些规则于周三在英格兰生效，是政府计划到2050年将英国碳排放减少至净零的一部分。

items.en: They set new standards for ventilation, energy efficiency and heating, and state that new residential buildings must have charging points for electric vehicles.
items.zh: 他们制定了新的通风、能源效率和供暖标准，并规定新建住宅必须配备电动汽车充电点。

items.en: The moves are the most significant change to building regulations in years, and industry experts say they will inevitably lead to higher prices at a time when a shortage of materials and high labour costs is already driving up bills.
items.zh: 这些举措是数年来建筑规范最重大的变革，行业专家表示它们将不可避免地导致价格上涨，而目前材料短缺和高劳动力成本已经推高了费用。

items.en: Brian Berry, chief executive of the Federation of Master Builders, a trade group for small and medium-sized builders, says the measures will require new materials, testing methods, products and systems to be installed.
items.zh: 建筑商协会联合会首席执行官Brian Berry表示，这些措施将需要安装新材料、测试方法、产品和系统。

items.en: “All this comes at an increased cost during a time when prices are already sky high.
items.zh: 所有这些在物价已经高得离谱的时期都需要付出更高的代价。

items.en: Inevitably, consumers will have to pay more,” he says.
items.zh: 不可避免地，消费者将不得不支付更多。他说。

items.en: Gareth Belsham, of surveyors Naismiths, says people who are upgrading, or extending their home, will be directly affected.
items.zh: 纳伊斯米斯公司的加雷斯·贝尔沙姆表示，升级或扩建住房的人将直接受影响。

items.en: “The biggest changes relate to heating and insulation,” he says.
items.zh: 他说最大的变化涉及供暖和隔热。

items.en: “There are new rules concerning the amount of glazing used in extensions, and any new windows or doors must be highly insulated.
items.zh: 有关扩建中使用的玻璃面积有新的规定，任何新安装的窗户或门都必须高度隔热。

items.en: The changes could mean an extra £3,000 added to the bill of an average home extension, according to Jonathan Rolande of the National Association of Property Buyers, a group of professionals aimed at raising construction standards.
items.zh: 据国家房产买家协会的乔纳森·罗兰德称，这些变化可能意味着普通住宅扩建的费用将额外增加3000英镑，该协会是一个旨在提高建筑标准的专业人士团体。

items.en: Homeowners extending may see the amount of space they have decrease, as walls will have to be thicker in order to comply with requirements for better insulation.
items.zh: 正在扩建房屋的房主可能会发现他们拥有的空间减少，因为墙壁必须更厚以满足更好的隔热要求。

items.en: Andrew Mellor, of PRP architects, says external walls will need to be about 7cm thicker than previously.
items.zh: PRP建筑师的安德鲁·梅尔说，外墙需要比之前厚约7厘米。

items.en: Windows and doors will have to adhere to higher standards, while there are new limits on the amount of glazing you can have to reduce unwanted heat from the sun.
items.zh: 窗户和门必须遵守更高标准，同时对玻璃面积的数量有新限制，以减少太阳带来的不必要热量。

items.en: Thomas Goodman, of My Job Quote, a site which sources quotes, says this will bring in new restrictions for extensions.
items.zh: My Job Quote网站的托马斯·古德曼表示，这将带来新的扩建限制。

items.en: “Glazing on windows, doors and roof lights must cover no more than 25% of the floor area to prevent heat loss, ” he says.
items.zh: 他指出，窗户、门和天窗的玻璃覆盖不得超过地板面积的25%，以防止热量损失。

items.en: As properties become more airtight, there are also measures to ensure proper airflow, such as having small openings (trickle vents) on windows that allow ventilation when a window is closed.
items.zh: 随着房产变得更密封，也有措施确保空气流通，比如在窗户上设置小开口（trickle vents）当窗户关闭时允许通风。

items.en: For people extending their homes, they may be required to install a new, or replacement, heating system depending on the size of the build, says Belsham.
items.zh: 贝尔沙姆表示，对于扩建住宅的人，他们可能需要根据扩建规模安装新的或更换的供暖系统。

items.en: These will have to use lower temperature water to deliver the same heat, which will require increased insulation of pipes.
items.zh: 这些必须使用较低温度的水来传递相同的热量，这将需要增加管道的保温。

items.en: “We’ll see more insulation, better lighting design and restrictions on the amount of glass used in some areas.
items.zh: 我们将看到更多隔热措施、更优的照明设计以及对某些区域玻璃用量的限制。

items.en: But with more thermal-efficient homes can come the risk of overheating due to solar gain, and so ventilation is also covered,” says Rolande.
items.zh: 但更节能的住宅可能带来因太阳能增益导致的过热风险，因此通风也被纳入考虑，”罗兰德说。

items.en: “As a result, double-glazed windows will require trickle vents to let heat escape and also to provide fresh air for health reasons and, of course, to reduce the risk of condensation build up in an ever-more airtight property.
items.zh: 因此，双层玻璃窗将需要 trickle 通风口来散热，同时为健康原因提供新鲜空气，并且当然，也能减少密封性越来越好的房屋中冷凝物积聚的风险。

items.en: As the rules came into effect last Wednesday, property developers were rushing to file plans just before the deadline, according to Belsham.
items.zh: 随着规则上周三生效，据Belsham称，房地产开发商正急于在截止日期前提交计划。

items.en: Any plans submitted before that date are considered to be under the previous rules, and can go ahead as long as work starts before 15 June next year.
items.zh: 在该日期之前提交的计划被视为适用旧规则，只要在明年6月15日前开始工作，即可继续进行。

items.en: An average extension will probably see around £3,000 additional cost thanks to the new regs
items.zh: 平均扩建项目可能会因新规产生约3000英镑的额外费用。

items.en: Builders which have costed projects, but have not filed the paperwork, may need to go back and submit fresh estimates, says Marcus Jefford of Build Aviator, which prices projects.
items.zh: 据Build Aviator的Marcus Jefford称，那些已经估算过项目但未提交文件的建筑商可能需要重新提交新的估算。

items.en: As the changes are aimed to make homes more energy efficient, they will eventually drive down heating bills.
items.zh: 这些变化旨在提高住宅的能源效率，最终将降低取暖费用。

items.en: But in the short-term homeowners are likely to face higher costs for work.
items.zh: 但短期内房主可能面临更高的工作成本。

items.en: Materials prices are already up 25% in the last two years, according to figures from the Construction Products Association.
items.zh: 根据建筑材料协会的数据，材料价格在过去两年中已经上涨了25%。

items.en: How much overall prices will increase as a result of the rule changes is not clear.
items.zh: 规则变更导致总体价格上升的程度尚不清楚。

items.en: “While admirable in their intentions, they will add to the cost of housebuilding at a time when many already feel that they are priced out of homeownership,” says Rolande.
items.zh: 尽管他们的初衷值得称赞，但它们会在许多人已经感到自己买不起房的时刻增加住房建设的成本，”罗兰德说。

items.en: “An average extension will probably see around £3,000 additional cost thanks to the new regs.
items.zh: 平均扩建项目可能会产生约3000英镑的额外费用，这归因于新规。

items.en: John Kelly, a construction lawyer at Freeths law firm, believes prices will eventually come down.
items.zh: 弗里思律师事务所的建筑工程律师John Kelly认为价格最终会下降。

items.en: But not in the immediate future.
items.zh: 但不是在短期内。

items.en: “As the marketplace adapts to the new requirements, and the technologies that support them, the scaling up of these technologies will eventually bring costs down, but in the short term, we will all have to pay the price of the necessary transition,” he says.
items.zh: 随着市场适应新的要求及其支持技术，这些技术的扩大应用最终会降低成本，但短期内，我们所有人都必须承担必要转型的代价。

items.en: However, the long-term effects of the changes will be more comfortable and energy-efficient homes, adds Mellor.
items.zh: 然而，这些变化的长期影响将是更舒适节能的住宅，梅尔补充道。

items.en: “Homeowners will probably recoup that cost over time in energy bill savings.
items.zh: 房主可能随着时间推移通过节省能源账单来收回这笔费用。

items.en: It will obviously be very volatile at the moment, but they will have that benefit over time.
items.zh: 显然，目前它会非常波动，但随着时间的推移，他们会获得这种好处。

items.en: Its energy and rhythm can capture a reader, transport them to another world and make them see things differently.
items.zh: 其活力和节奏能够吸引读者，带他们进入另一个世界并让他们以不同的视角看待事物。

items.en: No one knows for sure when poetry began but it has been around for thousands of years, even before people could write.
items.zh: 没有人确切知道诗歌起源于何时但它已经存在了数千年甚至在人类能够书写之前

items.zh: 这是一种讲述故事和传承历史的方式。

items.en: It is closely related to song and even when written it is usually created to be performed out loud.
