items.en: The following comments are given by several people on the issue of returning artifacts to their countries of origin.
items.zh: 以下评论由几位人士针对归还文物至其原属国家的问题发表。

items.en: Hannah Simply there are people in Nigeria who cannot travel to the Smithsonian Institution to see that part of their history and culture represented by the Benin Bronzes.
items.zh: 汉娜只是说在尼日利亚有一些人无法前往史密森尼学会观看代表他们历史和文化的贝宁青铜器部分。

items.en: These should be available to them as part of their cultural heritage and history and as a source of national pride.
items.zh: 这些应向他们开放，作为其文化遗产和历史的一部分，并作为民族自豪感的来源。

items.en: There is no good reason that these artifacts should be beyond the ordinary reach of the educational objectives or inspiration of the generations to which they were left.
items.zh: 没有充分的理由让这些文物超出教育目标或后代所受启发的常规范围。

items.en: They serve no purpose in a museum in the United States or elsewhere except as curious objects.
items.zh: 在美国或其他地方的博物馆中，它们除了作为奇特的物品外没有其他用途。

items.en: They cannot be compared to works of art produced for sale which can be passed from hand to hand and place by purchase.
items.zh: 它们无法与那些为出售而创作的艺术品相提并论，这些艺术品可以辗转传递并通过购买来转移位置。

items.en: Buck We know very exact reproductions of artwork can be and are regularly produced.
items.zh: 巴克 我们知道艺术品的非常精确的复制品可以并且经常被生产。

items.en: Perhaps museums and governments might explore some role for the use of nearly exact reproductions as a means of resolving issues relating to returning works of art and antiquities.
items.zh: 或许博物馆和政府可以探讨利用几乎精确的复制品作为解决涉及归还艺术品和文物问题的方法。

items.en: The context of any exhibit is more important to me than whether the object being displayed is 2000 years old or 2 months old.
items.zh: 对我来说，展品的背景比展品本身是2000年还是2个月的历史更重要。

items.en: In many cases the experts have a hard time agreeing on what is the real object and what is a forgery.
items.zh: 在许多情况下，专家们很难就什么是真品和什么是赝品达成一致。

items.en: Again, the story an exhibit is trying to tell is what matters.
items.zh: 再者，展览试图传达的故事才是关键。

items.en: The monetary value of the object on display is a distant second place in importance.
items.zh: 该展品的货币价值在重要性上仅居第二位，远不及其他因素。

items.en: Sara When visiting the Baltimore Museum of Art, I came across a magnificent 15th-century Chinese sculpture.
items.zh: 莎拉参观巴尔的摩艺术博物馆时，我偶然发现了一件精美的15世纪中国雕塑。

items.en: It inspired me to learn more about the culture that it represented.
items.zh: 它促使我深入了解它所代表的文化。

items.en: Artifacts in museums have the power to inspire, and perhaps spark that need to learn and understand the nature of their creators.
items.zh: 博物馆中的文物具有启发的力量，并可能激发那种学习和理解其创造者本质的渴望。

items.en: Having said that, I do feel that whatever artifacts find their way to public museums should, in fact, be sanctioned as having been obtained on loan, legally purchased or obtained by treaty.
items.zh: 话虽如此，我认为无论通过何种方式进入公共博物馆的文物，实际上都应被认可为是通过贷款、合法购买或条约获得的。

items.en: Stealing artifacts from other peoples' cultures is obscene; it robs not only the physical objects, but the dignity and spirit of their creators.
items.zh: 盗取其他民族的文化文物令人发指；它不仅剥夺了实物，还剥夺了创作者的尊严和精神。

items.en: Victor Ancient art that is displayed in foreign countries by all means should be returned to the original country.
items.zh: Victor认为，无论如何在外国被展示的古代艺术品都应归还给原属国家。

items.en: The foreign countries have no right to hold back returning the items.
items.zh: 外国没有权利阻碍归还这些物品。

items.en: I would ask that the foreign nations and the original country discuss the terms of transfer.
items.zh: 我要求外国国家和原产国讨论转让条款。

items.en: Yes, there is the risk that the original will not have as good security as do the foreign countries.
items.zh: 是的，原产国的安全性可能不如外国国家。

items.en: But look at what happened to Boston's Gardner Museum theft in 1990, including the loss of Rembrandt, Vermeer, Manet and other masterpieces.
items.zh: 但看看1990年波士顿盖蒂博物馆盗窃案发生时的情况，包括伦勃朗、维米尔、马奈等杰作的失窃。

items.en: Nothing is absolutely safe nowhere, and now Climate Change agitators are attacking publicly displayed work in European museums.
items.zh: 任何地方都没有绝对安全的事物，现在气候变化活动人士正在攻击欧洲博物馆中公开展出的作品。

items.en: Julia To those of you in the comments section who are having strong feelings about artifacts being removed from cities in the US and Britain and returned to their countries of origin, I would ask you to consider: why do you think Americans have more of a right to easily access the Benin Bronzes than people of Nigeria?
items.zh: Julia 对那些在评论区对美国和英国城市中的文物被移回原籍国一事有强烈看法的人，我想请你们考虑：为什么你们认为美国人比尼日利亚人更有权利轻松接触贝宁青铜器？

items.en: Why are people who live within a day's drive of London entitled to go and see the Elgin Marbles whenever they want, but the people of Athens aren't?
items.zh: 为什么住在伦敦一天车程内的人有资格随时去参观埃尔金大理石像，但雅典的居民却没有？

items.en: What intrinsic factors make the West a suitable home for these artifacts but preclude them from being preserved and displayed by their countries of origin?
items.zh: 哪些内在因素使西方成为这些文物的合适保存地，却阻止了它们的原产国进行保存和展示？

items.en: If your conclusion is that the West is better able to preserve these artifacts, think about why you're assuming that to be true.
items.zh: 如果你的结论是西方更能保存这些文物，请思考你为何认为这一结论是正确的。

items.en: "Elephants never forget" - or so they say - and that piece of folklore seems to have some foundation.
items.zh: 大象从不忘记——据说如此——而这个民间传说似乎有其道理。

items.en: The African savanna elephant, also known as the African bush elephant, is distributed across 37 African countries.
items.zh: 非洲草原象，又称非洲丛林象，分布于37个非洲国家。

items.en: They move between a variety of habitats, including forests, grasslands, woodlands, wetlands.
items.zh: 它们在各种栖息地之间迁徙，包括森林、草原、林地、湿地。

items.en: (46) They sometimes travel more than sixty miles to find food or water, and are very good at working out where other elephants are - even when they are out of sight.
items.zh: 它们有时会跋涉超过六十英里寻找食物或水源，并且非常擅长判断其他大象的位置——即使它们不在视线范围内。

items.en: What is more, they almost always seem to choose the nearest waterhole.
items.zh: 更重要的是，他们几乎总是选择最近的水源地。

items.en: (47) The researchers are convinced that the elephants always know precisely where they are in relation to all the resources they need, and can therefore take shortcuts, as well as following familiar routes.
items.zh: 研究人员确信大象总是能准确知道自己相对于所有所需资源的位置，因此可以走捷径，以及遵循熟悉的路线。

items.en: Although the cues used by African elephants for long-distance navigation are not yet understood, smell may well play a part.
items.zh: 尽管非洲象用于长距离导航的线索尚未被理解，但嗅觉可能起作用。

items.en: Elephants are very choosy eaters, but until recently little was known about how they selected their food.
items.zh: 大象是非常挑剔的食性动物，但直到最近才有人了解它们如何选择食物。

items.en: (48) One possibility was that they merely used their eyes and tried out the plants they found, but that would probably result in a lot of wasted time and energy, not least because their eyesight is actually not very good.
items.zh: (48) 一种可能性是他们只是依靠眼睛尝试他们找到的植物，但这可能会导致大量浪费的时间和精力，尤其是因为他们的视力实际上并不好。

items.en: (49) The volatile chemicals produced by plants can be carried a long way, and they are very characteristic: each plant or tree has its own particular odor signature.
items.zh: （49）植物产生的挥发性化学物质可以传播很远，且它们非常有特征性：每种植物或树木都有其独特的气味特征。

items.en: What is more, they can be detected even where they are not actually visible.
items.zh: 此外，它们甚至可以在实际上不可见的地方被检测到。

items.en: New research suggests that smell is a crucial factor in guiding elephants - and probably other herbivores - to the best food resources.
items.zh: 新研究显示气味是引导大象——及可能其他食草动物——寻找最佳食物资源的关键因素。

items.en: The researchers first established what kinds of plant the elephants preferred either to eat or avoid when foraging freely.
items.zh: 研究人员首先确定了大象在自由觅食时偏好的植物种类，要么吃，要么避开。

items.en: They then set up a food station experiment, in which they gave the elephants a series of choices based only on smell.
items.zh: 他们随后设立了食物站实验，在实验中他们给大象一系列仅基于气味的选择。

items.en: (50) The experiment showed that elephants may well use smell to identify patches of trees that are good to eat, and secondly to assess the quality of the trees within each patch.
items.zh: 实验显示，大象可能用气味来识别可食用的树丛，并其次评估每个树丛中树木的质量。

items.en: Free-ranging elephants presumably also use this information to locate their preferred food.
items.zh: 野生大象据推测也利用这些信息寻找它们偏好的食物。

items.en: Their well-developed hippocampal structures may enable elephants, like rats and people, to construct cognitive maps.
items.zh: 它们高度发达的海马体结构可能使大象像老鼠和人类一样构建认知地图。

items.en: High school students eager to stand out in the college application process often participate in a litany of extracurricular activities hoping to bolster their chances of admission a selective undergraduate institution.
items.zh: 渴望在大学申请过程中脱颖而出的高中生们常常参与大量课外活动，以增强他们被有选择性的本科院校录取的机会。

items.en: However, college admissions experts say that the quality of a college hopeful's extracurricular activities matter more than the number of activities he or she participates in.
items.zh: 然而，大学招生专家表示，大学申请者的课外活动质量比其参与的活动数量更重要。

items.en: Sue Rexford, the director of college guidance at the Charles.
items.zh: 苏·雷克斯福德是查尔斯大学申请指导主任。

items.en: Smith Jewish Day School, says it is not necessary for a student,filling out the Common Application to list 10 activities in the application
items.zh: 史密斯犹太日校表示，学生填写通用申请表时不需要在申请中列出10项活动。

items.en: “No” college will expect that a student has a huge laundry list of extracurricular that they have been passionately involved in each for an tended period of time, " Rexford wrote in an email.
items.zh: “没有”一所大学会期望学生拥有一个长长的课外活动清单，每个活动他们都曾热情参与并持续了一段时间，Rexford在一封电子邮件中写道。

items.en: Experts say it is tougher to distinguish oneself in a school-affiliated extracurricular activity that is common among high school students than it is to stand out while doing an uncommon activity.
items.zh: 专家表示，在高中生普遍参与的学校附属课外活动中脱颖而出，比在从事不常见的活动中更难。

items.en: “The competition to stand out and make an impact is going to be much stiffer, and so if they’re going to do a popular activity, I’d say, be the best at it.
items.zh: 要脱颖而出并产生影响的竞争将更加激烈，因此如果他们要从事流行的活动，我会说，要做到最好。

items.en: says Sara Harherson, a college admission consultant.
items.zh: 大学招生顾问Sara Harherson表示。

items.en: High school students who have an impressive personal project they are working on independently often impress colleges, experts say.
items.zh: 专家表示，那些正在独立完成令人印象深刻的个人项目的高中生常常会给大学留下深刻印象。

items.en: “For example, a student with an interest in entrepreneurship could demonstrate skills and potential by starting a profitable small business.
items.zh: 例如，对创业感兴趣的学生可以通过创办一家盈利的小企业来展示其技能和潜力。

items.en: Olivia Valdes, the founder of Zen Admissions consulting firm, wrote in an email.
items.zh: Zen Admissions 咨询公司创始人 Olivia Valdes 在一封邮件中写道。

items.en: Joseph Adegboyega-Edun, a Maryland High school guidance counselor, says unconventional, extracurricular activities can help students, impress college admissions offices, assuming they demonstrated, serious commitment.
items.zh: 马里兰州高中辅导员Joseph Adegboyega-Edun表示，非传统课外活动可以帮助学生给大学招生办公室留下印象，前提是他们展示了认真的承诺。

items.en: “Again, since one of the big questions high school seniors must consider is ‘What makes you unique? ’ having an uncommon, extracurricular activity, a conventional one is an advantage,” he wrote in an email.
items.zh: 同样，由于高中生必须考虑的一个重大问题是“什么使你与众不同”，参加不常见的课外活动，或者参加传统的课外活动，都是优势，他在一封电子邮件中写道。

items.en: Experts say demonstrating talent in at least one extracurricular activity can help in the college admissions process, especially at top-tier undergraduate institutions.
items.zh: 专家表示在至少一项课外活动中展示才能有助于大学录取流程，尤其是顶尖本科院校。

items.en: “Distinguishing yourself in one focused type of extracurricular activity can be a positive in the admissions process, especially for highly selective institutions, where having top grades and test scores is not enough,” Katie Kelley admissions counselor at Ivy Wise admissions consultancy, wrote in an email.
items.zh: 在某一特定类型的课外活动中脱颖而出可能在招生流程中是一个加分项，尤其是对于高度选择性的院校而言，仅拥有优异的成绩和考试分数是不够的，Ivy Wise招生咨询公司顾问Katie Kelley在一封电子邮件中写道。

items.en: “Students need to have that quality or hook that will appeal to admissions officers and allow them to visualize how the student might come and enrich their campus community.
items.zh: 学生需要具备某种特质或亮点，能够打动招生官并让他们想象该学生如何加入并丰富校园社区。

items.en: Extracurricular activities related to the college major declared on a college application are beneficial, experts suggest.
items.zh: 专家建议，在大学申请中声明的与大学专业相关的课外活动是有益的。

items.en: “If you already know your major, having an extracurricular that fits into that major can be a big plus,” says Mayghin Levine, the manager of educational opportunities with The Cabbage Patch Settlement House, a Louisville, Kentucky, nonprofit community center.
items.zh: 如果你已经确定了自己的专业，选择一个与该专业相关的课外活动会是一个显著优势，”肯塔基州路易斯维尔非营利社区中心“凯奇帕奇收容所”教育机会经理梅格欣·莱文说。

items.en: High school students who have had a strong positive influence on their community through an extracurricular activity may impress a college and win a scholarship, says Erica Gwyn, a
items.zh: 通过课外活动对社区产生强烈积极影响的高中生可能会给大学留下深刻印象并赢得奖学金，埃里卡·格温表示

items.en: former math and science magnet program assistant at a public high school who is now executive director of the Kaleidoscope Careers Academy in Atlanta, a nonprofit organization.
items.zh: 曾是公立高中数学和科学磁校项目助理，现为亚特兰大非营利组织Kaleidoscope Careers Academy的执行主任。

items.en: Students who stand out in a specific extracurricular activity will be favored by top-tier institutions.
items.zh: 在特定课外活动中表现突出的学生会受到顶尖院校的青睐。

items.en: Sue Rexford.
items.zh: 苏·雷克斯福德

items.en: Students whose extracurricular activity has benefited their community are likely to win a scholarship.
items.zh: 那些课外活动对社区有益的学生可能获得奖学金。

items.en: Sara Harberson.
items.zh: 萨拉·哈伯森

items.en: Undertaking too many extracurricular activities will hardly be seen as a plus by colleges.
items.zh: 参与过多课外活动几乎不会被学院视为优势。

items.zh: 凯蒂·凯利

items.en: Student who exhibits activity in doing business can impress colleges.
items.zh: 积极从事商业活动的学生会给大学留下深刻印象。

items.en: Mayghin Levine.
items.zh: 梅金·莱文

items.en: High school students participating in popular activity should excel in it.
items.zh: 参与流行活动的高中生应当在其中表现出色。

items.en: Erica Gwyn.
items.zh: 埃里卡·格温

items.en: Engaging in uncommon activity can demonstrate Students ’ determination and dedication.
items.zh: 参与不常见的活动可以展示学生的决心和奉献。

items.en: It is advisable for students to choose an extracurricular activity that is related to their future study at college.
items.zh: 建议学生选择与未来大学学业相关的课外活动。

items.en: With the smell of coffee and fresh bread floating in the air, stalls bursting with colorful vegetables and tempting cheeses, and the buzz of friendly chats, farmers ’ markets are a feast for the senses.
items.zh: 空气中飘散着咖啡和新鲜面包的香气，摊位上摆满了色彩鲜艳的蔬菜和诱人的奶酪，友好的交谈声此起彼伏，农贸市场是一场感官盛宴。

items.en: They also provide an opportunity to talk to the people responsible for growing or raising your food, support your local economy and pick up fresh seasonal produce — all at the same time.
items.zh: 它们还提供了一个与负责种植或培育你食物的人交谈的机会，支持当地经济并购买新鲜时令农产品——所有这些都可以同时完成。

items.en: Farmers ’ markets are usually weekly or monthly events, most often with outdoor stalls, which allow farmers or producers to sell their food directly to customers.
items.zh: 农贸市场通常是每周或每月一次的活动，通常设有户外摊位，使农民或生产者能够直接向顾客销售他们的食品。

items.en: The size or regularity of markets can vary from season to season, depending on the area's agricultural calendar, and you’re likely to find different produce on sale at different times of the year.
items.zh: 市场的规模或规律性可能因季节而异，取决于该地区的农业日历，你可能在一年中不同时期发现不同的农产品在出售。

items.en: By cutting out the middlemen, the farmers secure more profit for their produce.
items.zh: 通过消除中间商，农民能为他们的农产品获得更多的利润。

items.en: Shoppers also benefit from seeing exactly where — and to who — their money is going.
items.zh: 购物者也能从确切知道他们的钱流向了哪里——以及流向了谁——中受益。

items.en: Suppose you and Jack are going to do a survey on the protection of old houses in an ancient town.

items.en: Butterflies may not pollinate as many plants as wild bees and hoverflies, but because British butterflies are the best-studied group of insects in the world, they are an extremely useful indicator of the wider declines in flying insects.
items.zh: 蝴蝶可能不如野蜂和食蚜蝇那样为众多植物传粉，但因为英国的蝴蝶是全球研究最充分的昆虫群体，它们成为飞行昆虫整体数量下降的极佳指标。

items.en: "I was waiting for surgery, feeling really ill, sitting in my garden.

items.en: At such high shutter speeds, the depth of field is tiny, and as butterflies do not fly in a straight line they swiftly flutter out of focus.

items.en: Innovation and research have relied on public participation in science for centuries.
items.zh: 创新和研究数百年来一直依靠公众参与科学。

items.en: It was a musician who discovered the planet Uranus in the 18th century by making his own telescope with mirrors composed of copper and tin.
items.zh: 18世纪，一位音乐家通过自制望远镜发现了天王星，望远镜的镜片由铜和锡制成。

items.en: (46) Recent decades have seen science move into a convention where engagement in the subject can only be done through institutions such as a university.
items.zh: 近年来，科学已进入一个惯例，即对这一领域的参与只能通过大学等机构来实现。

items.en: Citizen science provides an opportunity for greater public engagement and the democratisation of science.
items.zh: 公民科学为更大的公众参与和科学民主化提供了机会。

items.en: In the information era, large data sets, small teams and financial restrictions have slowed scientific process.
items.zh: 在信息时代，大型数据集、小型团队和资金限制减缓了科学进程。

items.en: (47) But by utilising the natural curiosity of the general public it is possible to overcome many of these challenges by engaging non-scientists directly in the research process.
items.zh: 但通过利用公众的天然好奇心，可以克服这些挑战中的许多，通过让非科学家直接参与研究过程。

items.en: Anyone can be a citizen scientist, regardless of age, nationality or academic experience.
items.zh: 任何人都可以成为公民科学家，无论年龄、国籍或学术经验如何。

items.en: You don't even need any formal training, just an inquisitive mind and the enthusiasm to join one of the thousands of citizen science projects to generate new knowledge and the means to understand a genuine scientific outcome.
items.zh: 你甚至不需要任何正式培训，只需一颗好奇的心和加入成千上万公民科学项目以生成新知识并理解真正科学成果的热情。

items.en: (48) Scientists have employed a variety of ways to engage the general public in their research, such as making data analysis into an online game or sample collection into a smartphone application.
items.zh: (48) 科学家们已经采用多种方法让公众参与他们的研究，比如将数据分析转化为在线游戏，或将样本采集变成智能手机应用程序。

items.en: They've implored citizen scientists to help with bug counting and categorising cancer cells, and even identifying distant galaxies.
items.zh: 他们恳求公民科学家帮助进行虫子计数、对癌细胞进行分类，以及识别遥远的星系。

items.en: This form of accessible science means that great minds are able to join the race to create and develop projects with the potential to change the world.
items.zh: 这种普及科学的形式意味着杰出人才能够参与竞赛，创建和发展具有改变世界潜力的项目。

items.en: A citizen science-based approach can extend the field of vision and include more ideas and different brains to problem-solve and create, making innovation faster and more effective.
items.zh: 基于公民科学的方法可以扩展视野，纳入更多想法和不同的人脑来解决问题和创造，使创新更快更有效。

items.en: The rise of citizen science has grown alongside the rise of do-it-yourself biology laboratories around the world.
items.zh: 公民科学的兴起与全球范围内DIY生物实验室的兴起同时发生。

items.en: (49) These groups of people are part of a rapidly expanding biotechnological social movement of citizen scientists and professional scientists seeking to take discovery out of institutions and put it into the hands of anyone with the enthusiasm.
items.zh: （49）这些人群是快速扩展的生物技术社会运动的一部分，该运动由公民科学家和专业科学家组成，试图将发现从机构中带出，交到任何有热情的人手中。

items.en: There are around 40 official do-it-yourself biology centres across the globe in locations including Paris, London, Sydney, and Tel Aviv.
items.zh: 全球约有40个官方自助生物中心，分布在包括巴黎、伦敦、悉尼和特拉维夫在内的地点。

items.en: (50) They pool resources, collaborate, think outside the box, and find solutions and ways around obstacles to explore science for the sake of science without the traditional boundaries of working inside a formal setting.
items.zh: 他们汇集资源、协作、跳出思维定式，寻找解决方案并克服障碍，以不受传统正式环境限制的方式，纯粹为了科学本身而探索科学。

items.en: Five Steps to Suggesting a Change at Work That'll Actually Get Taken
items.zh: 五个步骤：在工作中提出一个实际上会被采纳的改变

items.en: Seriously
items.zh: 认真地

items.en: Everyone wants to be that person—the one who looks at the same information as everyone else, but who sees a fresh, innovative solution.
items.zh: 每个人都想成为那个人——那个看到和每个人一样的信息但能发现新颖创新解决方案的人。

items.en: However, it takes more than simply having a good idea.
items.zh: 然而，仅仅有一个好主意是不够的。

items.en: How you share it is as important as the suggestion itself.
items.zh: 你如何分享它与建议本身同样重要。

items.en: Because writing a new script-literally or figuratively-means that other team members will have to adapt to something new.
items.zh: 因为撰写一个新剧本——无论是字面意义上的还是比喻意义上的——意味着其他团队成员必须适应新事物。

items.en: So whether you're suggesting a (seemingly)benign change like streamlining outdated protocol, or a bigger change like adding an hour to each workday so people can leave early on Fridays, you're asking others to reimagine their workflow or schedule.
items.zh: 无论你是建议看似无害的改变，比如简化过时的协议，还是更大的改变，比如每天增加一小时工作时间以便人们周五能提前下班，你都在要求他人重新规划他们的工作流程或日程。

items.en: Not to mention, if
items.zh: 更不用说，如果

items.en: the process your scrapping is one someone else suggested, there's the possibility of hurt feelings.
items.zh: 你正在舍弃的过程是某人建议的，可能伤害感情。

items.en: To gain buy-in on an innovative, new idea, follow these steps:
items.zh: 要获得对创新新想法的支持，遵循以下步骤：

items.en: Great ideas don’t stand alone.
items.zh: 伟大的想法不会独立存在。

items.en: In other words, you can’t mention your suggestion once and expect it to be adopted.
items.zh: 换句话说，你不能提一次建议就指望它被采纳。

items.en: To see a change, you’ll need to champion your plan and sell its merits.
items.zh: 要看到变化，你需要积极倡导你的计划并宣传其优势。

items.en: In addition, you need to be willing to stand up to scrutiny and criticism and be prepared to explain your innovation in different ways for various audiences.
items.zh: 此外，你需要愿意经受审查和批评，并准备好用不同方式向不同受众解释你的创新。

items.en: Sometimes it makes sense to go to your boss first.
items.zh: 有时候先找老板是合理的。

items.en: But other times, it’s useful to build a coalition among your co-workers or other stakeholders.
items.zh: 但有时在你的同事或其他利益相关者之间建立联盟是有用的。

items.en: When it works, it works great—because you’re ready for your stubborn supervisor’s pushback with answers like, “Actually, I connected with a few people in our tech department to discuss how much time these kinds of website updates would take, and they suggested they have the bandwidth.
items.zh: 当它起作用时，效果很好——因为你可以用诸如"实际上，我联系了我们技术部门的几个人讨论这类网站更新需要多长时间，他们建议他们有带宽"这样的回答来应对顽固上司的反对

items.en: However, just be certain you can explain your end-around approach as one that built your case, rather than simply circumvented your manager.
items.zh: 然而，务必确保你能将你的迂回策略解释为建立你的论点，而不是仅仅绕过你的经理。

items.en: The last thing you want is for your boss to feel embarrassed he wasn’t informed—which could lead him to quash the idea before it even takes off.
items.zh: 你最不想看到的就是你的老板因为未被告知而感到尴尬——这可能会导致他在该想法甚至开始之前就扼杀它。

items.en: One of the biggest barriers to gaining buy-in occurs when the owner
items.zh: 获得支持的最大障碍之一是当业主...时

items.en: of an idea is viewed as argumentative, defensive, or close-minded.
items.zh: 一个想法被视为好争论的、防御性的或思想封闭的。

items.en: Because, let’s be honest: No one likes a know-it-all.
items.zh: 因为，说实在的：没人喜欢爱显摆的人。

items.en: So, if people disagree with you, don’t be indignant.
items.zh: 因此，如果人们不同意你的观点，不要感到愤怒。

items.en: Instead, listen to their concerns fully, try to understand their perspective, and include their concerns (and possible remedies) in
items.zh: 相反，充分倾听他们的担忧，努力理解他们的观点，并将他们的担忧（以及可能的解决方案）纳入

items.en: future discussions.
items.zh: 后续讨论。

items.en: So, instead of saying, “Martha, our current slogan is confusing and should be updated,” you could try, “Martha raises a great point that our current slogan has a long history for our stakeholders, but I wonder if we might able to brainstorm a tagline that could build on that—and be clearer for new customers.
items.zh: 与其说“玛莎，我们目前的标语令人困惑，需要更新”，不如尝试说“玛莎提出了一个很好的观点，我们目前的标语对我们利益相关者来说有着悠久的历史，但我想知道我们是否能够集思广益，设计一个可以延续这一点并对新客户更清晰的标语”。

items.en: New ideas are the grandchildren of old ones.
items.zh: 新思想是旧思想的孙子。

items.en: In other words, don’t throw old solutions under the bus to make your improvement stand out.
items.zh: 换句话说，不要为了突出自己的改进而抛弃旧的解决方案。

items.en: Remember that in light of whatever the problem the old system solved—or, maybe, has failed to solve in recent memory—it was a great idea at the time.
items.zh: 请记住，无论旧系统解决了什么问题——或者，也许，最近记忆中未能解决的问题——在当时看来都是个好主意。

items.en: Appreciating the older contributions as you suggest future innovations helps bolster the credibility of your idea.
items.zh: 正如你建议的那样，欣赏早期贡献有助于增强你想法的可信度。

items.en: When pitching a new idea, it’s important use the language of abundance instead of the language of deficit.
items.zh: 提出新想法时，重要使用丰裕的语言而非匮乏的语言。

items.en: Instead of saying what is wrong, broken, or suboptimal, talk about what is right, fixable, or ideal.
items.zh: 与其指出哪里有问题、有缺陷或不理想，不如谈论正确的地方、可修复之处或理想的状态。

items.en: For example, try, “I can see lots of applications for this new approach” rather than, “This innovation is the only way.
items.zh: 例如，可以说"我能看到这种方法的很多应用"，而不是"这种创新是唯一的方法"。

items.en: Be optimistic but realistic, and you will stand out.
items.zh: 保持乐观但现实，你将脱颖而出。

items.en: You know the moment - the conversation.
items.zh: 你知道那个时刻——对话。

items.en: Slows, then there's a pause.

items.zh: 在对话中存在短暂停顿时，人们会感到与他们的对话伙伴更加亲近。

items.en: But such feeing of connection markedly dip when entering a long gap.
items.zh: 但这种连接感在进入长时间的间隔时会明显下降。

items.en: Long gaps between strangers are likely to be followed by a change in topic.
items.zh: 陌生人之间的长时间沉默可能引发话题的改变。

items.en: But the opposite seems to be true for conversations between friends.
items.zh: 但朋友之间的对话似乎情况相反。

items.en: Long gaps there saw increased connection.
items.zh: 那里的长时间间隔出现了更多连接。

items.en: Between friends, longer gaps seem to provide natural moments for reflection and expression.
items.zh: 朋友之间，更长的间隔似乎能提供自然的时机进行反思和表达。

items.en: In his Oxford lectures, Seamus Heaney argued that a poem draws a picture of reality, a "glimpsed alternative" that sets up a contradiction with your own, in ways little and large.
items.zh: 在牛津的讲座中，谢默斯·希尼认为，一首诗描绘现实，一种"瞥见的替代现实"，以各种方式，无论大小，与你自身的现实形成矛盾。

items.en: The negotiation, between you and it, is the heart of the matter.

items.en: Forget self-help books; reading is self-help in action.
items.zh: 忘记自助书籍；阅读就是将自助付诸实践。

items.en: I have yet to meet a chief executive who reads regularly.
items.zh: 我尚未遇到一位定期阅读的首席执行官。

items.en: Many skip newspapers, and magazines are a stretch.
items.zh: 许多人不看报纸，而杂志则更进一步。

items.en: They don't have time, they say.
items.zh: 他们没有时间，他们说。

items.en: It's inefficient; they can get the information they need from those around them.
items.zh: 效率低下；他们可以从周围的人那里获取所需的信息。

items.en: At a pinch, they might pick up a business book before a long flight, in the hope that, like a cookbook, it will provide a foolproof recipe.
items.zh: 在万不得已时，他们可能会在长途飞行前拿起一本商业书籍，希望它能像食谱一样提供无懈可击的方法。

items.en: Some are drawn to what I think of as "business car crash" books - the stories of Theranos, Purdue, or WeWork.
items.zh: 有些人被吸引去读我称之为"商业车祸"的书籍——Theranos、Purdue 或 WeWork 的故事。

items.en: But outside those narrow pools of interest, a vast ocean awaits, bountiful with simmering ideas, mental adventure and imaginative refreshment.
items.zh: 但在这狭窄的兴趣池塘之外，一片广阔的海洋等待着，富于酝酿中的想法、精神冒险和富有想象力的更新。

items.en: Reading will keep you better informed about the world but it can also improve our tech-shattered ability to concentrate.
items.zh: 阅读不仅能让你更了解世界，还能提高我们因科技而受损的专注力。

items.en: Standing in the shoes of others fine tunes our social understanding, useful as we struggle to understand friends, neighbours, customers and co-workers.
items.zh: 站在他人的角度能微调我们的社会理解，这在我们努力理解朋友、邻居、客户和同事时尤为有用。

items.en: Different parts of our brain engage as we simulate scenes, characters and mental states.
items.zh: 当我们模拟场景、角色和心理状态时，大脑的不同部分会参与进来。

items.en: Our imagination - remember that? - is rekindled.
items.zh: 我们的想象力——还记得吗？——被重新点燃了。

items.en: The cure is right at hand, reading is cheap, easy and, most important, it's fun.
items.zh: 解决方法近在咫尺，阅读廉价、容易，最重要的是，它很有趣。

items.en: Liberate your imagination this year.
items.zh: 今年释放你的想象力。

items.en: So lucid and accessible that even lay readers can relish the unpredictability of discovery.
items.zh: 如此清晰易懂，以至于即使是普通读者也能享受发现的不可预测性。

items.en: Daunted by uncertainty?
items.zh: 对不确定性感到畏惧吗？

items.en: Stand in the shoes of scientists and witness the degree to which breakthroughs emerge from accidents, conflict and sheer mental stamina.
items.zh: 站在科学家的立场，见证突破性成果在意外、冲突和纯粹脑力耐力中的产生程度。

items.en: "We are never sure of anything," says the physicist (and writer) Carlo Rovelli.
items.zh: ‘我们对任何事情都不确定，’物理学家（兼作家）Carlo Rovelli说。

items.en: If, like most business people, you spend your life dashing from office to plane, train to home, boardroom to washroom, what you really need to do is stay in more.
items.zh: 如果你和大多数商务人士一样，一生都在从办公室到飞机、从火车到家、从会议室到洗手间之间奔波，那么你真正需要做的其实是多待在某个地方。

items.en: Sit down - and read a book.
items.zh: 坐下，然后读一本书。

items.en: (And yes, all these benefits are more closely associated with physical books than digital ones.)
items.zh: 而且没错，所有这些好处都与纸质书比与电子书更密切相关。

items.en: Any fiction.
items.zh: 任何小说。

items.en: Free yourself from algorithms and choose anything you don't need technology for an immersive experience just surrender to narratives across time and place.
items.zh: 摆脱算法并选择任何无需技术即可带来沉浸式体验的事物，只需沉浸在跨越时空的故事中。

items.en: Modern (Sebastian Barry or Olga Tokarczuk), classic (Virginia Woolf or James Baldwin) or genre (Stephen King, Margaret Atwood, Georges Simenon) - it doesn't matter.
items.zh: 现代（Sebastian Barry 或 Olga Tokarczuk）、经典（Virginia Woolf 或 James Baldwin）或类型（Stephen King、Margaret Atwood、Georges Simenon）——无关紧要。

items.en: Fiction invites you to loiter the unseen.
items.zh: 小说邀请你探索不可见之物。

items.en: In the lives of others, we are living through a golden age of translation too, so you can go anywhere in time or place.
items.zh: 在他人生活中，我们也正经历着翻译的黄金时代，因此你可以穿越时空去任何地方。

items.en: Science education today revolves around the idea of scientific literacy - the base-level knowledge about science that non-scientists require to effectively get on in the world.
items.zh: 当今的科学教育围绕科学素养这一概念展开——即非科学家为了有效立足于社会所需的基础科学知识。

items.en: This concept has served as a central goal for curriculum developers, local school boards, business and community leaders, and policymakers ever since its introduction nearly 80 years ago.
items.zh: 这个概念自80年前引入以来，一直是课程开发者、地方学校委员会、企业和社区领袖以及政策制定者的中心目标。

items.en: (46) Tracing the history of the term, we can see how the definition of scientific literacy has shifted over time, muddying the waters when it comes to determining the goals of science education.
items.zh: （46）追溯该术语的历史，我们可以看到科学素养的定义随着时间的推移已经发生了变化，在确定科学教育目标时使问题变得复杂。

items.en: And that's a shame, because there is much to recommend in the idea of scientific literacy as it was originally articulated in 1945, a time when science appeared to be the key to progress and scientists seemingly held the fate of the world in their hands.
items.zh: 这令人遗憾，因为1945年最初提出的科学素养理念有许多值得推崇之处，当时科学似乎被视为进步的关键，科学家似乎掌握着世界命运。

items.en: (47) A return to that version of scientific literacy, which focused more on teaching what science is and how it works and less on memorizing scientific facts, seems like something society today desperately needs.
items.zh: 回归到更注重教授科学本质和运作方式、而非死记硬背科学事实的科学素养版本，似乎正是当今社会迫切需要的。

items.en: In the United States, the desire to provide the public with a general, nontechnical education in science originated as far back as the late 1800s.
items.zh: 在美国，为公众提供非技术性科学教育的愿望早在19世纪末就已出现。

items.en: (48) Educators advanced the idea of having students complete detailed laboratory exercises in high schools in the belief that such work was beneficial primarily as a way to enhance logical reasoning and observational skills.
items.zh: 教育工作者提出了让学生完成详细实验练习的想法，认为这种工作主要是通过提高逻辑推理能力和观察能力来产生益处。

items.en: The development in 1915 of the popular new subject "general science" was another effort to train students to apply the principles of science to everyday, non-science problems.
items.zh: 1915年广受欢迎的新学科"general science"的出现是另一次努力，旨在训练学生将科学原理应用于日常非科学问题。

items.en: Although these efforts were aimed at the non-science-bound student, they never really made their way into mainstream thought and public discourse as a means to rally widespread support for the importance of science teaching in schools.
items.zh: 尽管这些努力旨在针对不打算从事科学领域的学生，但它们从未真正进入主流思想和公共讨论，作为动员公众广泛支持学校科学教学重要性的手段。

items.en: (49) It wasn't until the phrase "scientific literacy" came along in the 1940s that science had the formidable slogan it needed to command public attention and make improving science education an important national goal.
items.zh: 直到1940年代"scientific literacy"这一术语出现，科学才拥有了它所需要的强有力的口号，以吸引公众关注并使提高科学教育成为重要的国家目标。

items.en: (50) The intense focus on scientific literacy in the United States originally grew out of the critical role of science and technology during World War II, as well as the perceived deficiencies of American soldiers.
items.zh: 美国对科学素养的高度重视最初源于二战期间科学与技术发挥的关键作用，以及当时美国士兵被察觉的缺陷。

items.en: As the war unfolded, science rapidly assumed a central role.
items.zh: 随着战争的展开，科学迅速发挥了核心作用。

items.en: Battles increasingly depended on new military technologies such as radar and the proximity fuze.
items.zh: 战斗日益依赖于诸如雷达和近炸引信等新型军事技术。

items.en: Science-based analytical approaches proved remarkably successful in the hunt for German submarines in the Atlantic Ocean.
items.zh: 科学分析方法在大西洋搜寻德国潜艇的行动中成效显著。

items.en: And there was the (then-secret) work building the world's first atomic bomb.
items.zh: 还有（当时机密的）制造世界上第一颗原子弹的工作。

items.en: As a result, scientists - physicists in particular - found themselves in high demand.

items.en: ① In an effort to support restoration programmes, specialists are developing supplies of seeds and seedlings, maintaining gene banks and sequencing the genomes of indigenous trees and other crops.
items.zh: 为支持恢复项目，专家正在开发种子和幼苗的供应，维护基因库，并对本土树木和其他作物的基因组进行测序。

items.en: Their work deals with one of the problems that could block major restoration efforts in different parts of the world.
items.zh: 他们的工作涉及一个可能阻碍全球各地重大修复工作的难题。

items.en: ② “Where’s the planting material going to come from?
items.zh: 种植材料将从哪里来？

items.en: That’s one big bottleneck,” says genetic-resources specialist Rami Jamnadass.
items.zh: 这确实是一个大瓶颈，遗传资源专家Rami Jamnadass说。

items.en: ③ Asia is arguably the region most neglected by global efforts to increase diversity in restoration and to study native species.
items.zh: ③ 亚洲可以说是全球在增加生态恢复多样性及研究本地物种方面最被忽视的地区。

items.en: Christopher Kettle, Bioversity International’s director for forest genetic resources and restoration in Rome, says that the need for infrastructure—things such as mechanisms for collecting and storing seeds, and nurseries to raise seedlings—might be most desperate here because many trees are ‘masting’ species, which don’t produce seeds every year.
items.zh: 罗马Bioversity International森林遗传资源与恢复部门主任Christopher Kettle表示，这里的基础设施需求可能最为迫切，因为许多树木属于“周期性结实”树种，这些树种并非每年都会结果。

items.en: People need to be ready.
items.zh: 人们需要做好准备。

items.en: “Otherwise, you miss the boat, you lose all the seed and you’ve got to wait another seven years,” says Kettle.
items.zh: 否则，你就会错过机会，失去所有种子，还得再等七年，”凯特尔说。

items.en: “This is a really, really critical issue for restoration in Southeast Asia, because many of the most important timber species and tree species—the ones that will lock up the most carbon—they’re all masting species.
items.zh: 这是东南亚生态恢复中一个非常关键的问题，因为许多最重要的木材树种和树种——那些能够封存最多碳的树种——都是周期性结实的树种。

items.en: ④ John Stanturf, a leading forest restoration expert with the US Forest Service, argues that successful forest restoration isn’t just about planting the right trees.
items.zh: ④ 美国林业局知名森林恢复专家 John Stanturf 认为，成功的森林恢复不仅仅是种植合适的树木的问题。

items.en: “We often focus too much on the technical side of seed supply and seedling quality, but we ignore that restoration only works if we also account for human factors—local communities’ needs, land-use rights, and their willingness to participate,” he says.
items.zh: 我们常常过于关注种子供应和幼苗质量的技术层面，却忽略了恢复只有在考虑人为因素——当地社区的需求、土地使用权以及他们的参与意愿时才能奏效。他说。

items.en: “Restoration projects that fail to engage stakeholders from the start will struggle to survive long-term, no matter how good the planting material is.
items.zh: 未能从一开始就参与相关方的生态修复项目将难以长期维持，无论种植材料多么优良。

items.en: ⑤ Pedro Brancalion, a restoration ecologist specializing in the Brazilian Atlantic Forest, echoes this focus on people-centered restoration.
items.zh: ⑤ Pedro Brancalion，一位专攻巴西大西洋森林的生态恢复专家，呼应了这种以社区为中心的生态恢复关注。

items.en: “Many restoration plans are designed based on ecological ideals, but they don’t align with the real needs of local farmers and communities who live on the land,” he notes.
items.zh: 他指出，许多修复计划是基于生态理念设计的，但它们不符合当地农民和社区居民的实际需求。

items.en: “For example, some projects prioritize carbon sequestration trees over species that provide non-timber forest products, which are the main income source for locals.
items.zh: 例如，一些项目优先选择用于碳封存的树木而非提供非木材林产品的物种，这些物种是当地人的主要收入来源。

items.en: This mismatch makes it hard to get long-term community support.
items.zh: 这种不匹配使得长期获得社区支持变得困难。

items.en: ⑥ With so much research left to do, leaders in the field have been doing some soul-searching, and acknowledging that restoration can be motivated by—and designed to meet—different needs.
items.zh: ⑥ 鉴于仍有大量研究工作要做，该领域的领导者一直在进行反思，并承认恢复可以由不同的需求驱动，并且旨在满足这些需求。

items.en: “When you talk about conservation or restoration, the first question has to be restoration by whom, for whom?

items.en: Whether we opt for bold, colorful outfits or prefer more understated styles, our dress choices convey messages about who we are and how we want to be perceived.

items.zh: 他们将八只成年老鼠与两种类型的机器人鼠——一种社交型，一种非社交型——共同饲养了四天。

items.en: The robot rats were quite minimalist, resembling a chunkier version of a computer mouse with wheels to move around and colourful markings.
items.zh: 这些机器人老鼠设计非常极简，类似于一个更粗壮的电脑鼠标，配有轮子用于移动和彩色标记。

items.en: Next, the researchers trapped the robots in cages and gave the rats the opportunity to release them by pressing a lever.
items.zh: 接下来，研究人员将机器人关进笼子并给了老鼠一个通过按下杠杆来释放它们的机会。

items.en: Across 18 trials each, the living rats were 52 per cent more likely on average to set the social robot free than the asocial one.
items.zh: 在每只活鼠的 18次试验中，它们平均更有可能 52%释放社交机器人而非非社交机器人。

items.en: The readiness of the rats to befriend the social robot was surprising given its minimal design.
items.zh: 鉴于其极简设计，老鼠乐于与社交机器人结交朋友令人惊讶。

items.en: The robot was the same size as a regular rat but resembled a simple plastic box on wheels.
items.zh: 这个机器人和普通老鼠一样大小，但看起来像一个装有轮子的简单塑料盒子。

items.en: CEOs must have a good sense of financial markets and maybe even how the company should trade in them.
items.zh: 首席执行官必须具备良好的金融市场意识，并且甚至如何在其中进行交易。

items.en: They also need better public relations skills than their predecessors, as the costs of even a minor slipup can be significant.
items.zh: 他们还需要比前辈更好的公关技能，因为即使是一个小失误的代价也可能很重大。

items.en: Yet it is principally during this period of stronger governance that CEO pay has been high and rising.
items.zh: 然而，高管薪酬主要是在治理更严格的时期保持较高水平并持续上涨。

items.en: That suggests it is in the broader corporate interest to recruit top candidates for increasingly tough jobs.
items.zh: 这表明，从更广泛的企业利益来看，为日益艰难的工作招募顶尖候选人是必要的。

items.en: Travel on a London bus and you’ll 3 see how this works with drivers.
items.zh: 乘坐伦敦巴士，你将 3看到这种机制如何与司机配合。

items.en: Watch people get on and show their tickets.
items.zh: 观看人们上车并出示车票。

items.en: Are they carefully inspected?
items.zh: 它们是否被仔细检查？

items.en: Possibly, but very few.
items.zh: 可能，但很少。

items.en: And people who run for the bus?
items.zh: 那么那些为了赶公交车而奔跑的人呢

items.en: 7 , the number of buses and bus lanes were increased, and drivers were
items.zh: 7 增加了公交车和公交专用道的数量，司机们被

items.en: Airlines have simply changed the time a 14 is meant to take.
items.zh: 航空公司只是改变了 14原本需要的时间。

items.en: A one-hour flight is now billed as a two-hour flight.
items.zh: 一小时的航班现在被计费为两小时的航班。

items.en: Choose one criterion and you may well 16 others.
items.zh: 选择一个标准，你可能忽略其他标准。

items.en: Everything can be done faster and made cheaper, but there is a 17.
items.zh: 一切都可以做得更快、成本更低，但存在一个 17 。

items.en: But it is an argument for exploring consequences first.
items.zh: 但这是一个先探讨后果的论点。

items.en: All good targets should have multiple criteria 18 critical factors such as time, money, quality and customer feedback.
items.zh: 所有好的目标都应有多个标准 18 关键因素，如时间、金钱、质量和客户反馈。

items.en: The trick is not only to 19 just one or even two dimensions of the objective, but also to understand how to help people better 20 the objective.
items.zh: 诀窍不仅是要 19 仅仅 一个或甚至两个维度的目标，还要理解如何帮助人们更好地 20 实现 目标。

items.en: We know we are moving into a period where the jobs in demand will change rapidly, as will the requirements of the jobs that remain.
items.zh: 我们知道我们正进入一个需求量大的工作将迅速变化的时期，同样，那些仍存在的职位的要求也会迅速变化。

items.en: Research by the World Economic Forum finds that on average 42 per cent of the“core skills”within job roles will change by 2022.That is a very short timeline.
items.zh: 世界经济论坛的研究发现，平均而言，职位要求中的 42%的核心技能到 2022年将发生改变。这是一段非常短的时间。

items.en: The question of who should pay for reskilling is a thorny one.
items.zh: 谁应为再培训付费的问题十分棘手。

items.en: For individual companies, the temptation is always to let go of workers whose skills are no longer in demand and replace them with those whose skills are.
items.zh: 对于个别公司而言，诱惑始终是解雇那些技能不再被需要的员工，并用那些技能仍被需要的员工来替代他们。

items.en: That does not always happen.
items.zh: 这并不总是发生。

items.en: AT&T is often given as the gold standard of a company who decided to do a massive reskilling program rather than go with a fire-and-hire strategy.
items.zh: AT&T 通常被视为一家选择实施大规模再培训计划而非采用裁员再招聘策略的公司的典范。

items.en: Other companies including Amazon and Disney had also pledged to create their own plans.
items.zh: 包括亚马逊和迪士尼在内的其他公司也承诺制定自己的计划。

items.en: When the skills mismatch is in the broader economy though, the focus usually turns to government to handle.
items.zh: 尽管技能错配存在于更广泛的经济中，焦点通常会转向政府来处理。

items.en: Efforts in Canada and elsewhere have been arguably languid at best, and have given us a situation where we frequently hear of employers begging for workers, even at times and in regions where unemployment is high.
items.zh: 加拿大及其他地方的努力可以说至多是迟缓的，这使我们经常听到雇主恳求工人，甚至在失业率高的时期和地区。

items.en: In February, at 3.5 per cent and 5.5 per cent respectively, unemployment rates in Canada and the United States were at generational lows and worker shortages were everywhere.
items.zh: 二月，加拿大和美国的失业率分别为 3.5%和 5.5%，处于代际低点，工人短缺现象随处可见。

items.en: As of May, those rates had spiked up to 13.3 per cent and 13.7 per cent, and although many worker shortages had disappeared, not all had done so.
items.zh: 截至 5月，这些比率已飙升至 13.3%和 13.7%，尽管许多劳动力短缺已消失，但并非所有都已消失。

items.en: In the medical field, to take an obvious example, the pandemic meant that there were still clear shortages of doctors, nurses and other medical personnel.
items.zh: 在医疗领域，以显而易见的例子而言，疫情意味着医生、护士和其他医护人员仍存在明显的短缺。

items.en: Of course, it is not like you can take an unemployed waiter and train him to be a doctor in a few weeks, no matter who pays for it.
items.zh: 当然，你不能像几周内就能把一个失业的服务员训练成医生那样，不管谁来支付费用。

items.en: But even if you cannot close that gap, maybe you can close others, and doing so would be to the benefit of all concerned.
items.zh: 但即使你无法弥补那个差距，也许可以弥补其他差距，这样做将使所有相关方受益。

items.en: That seems to be the case in Sweden: When forced to furlough 90 per cent of their cabin staff, Scandinavian Airlines decided to start up a short retraining program that reskilled the laid-off workers to support hospital staff.
items.zh: 这似乎在瑞典是这种情况：当被迫暂时解雇 90%的客舱员工时，斯堪的纳维亚航空公司决定启动一个短期再培训计划，将被裁员的员工重新培训以支持医院工作人员。

items.en: The effort was a collective one and involved other companies as well as a Swedish university.
items.zh: 这次努力是集体的，还涉及其他公司以及瑞典的一所大学。

items.en: With the global population predicted to hit close to 10 billion by 2050, and forecasts that agricultural production in some regions will need to nearly double to keep pace, food security is increasingly making headlines.
items.zh: 随着全球人口预计到 2050年将达到近 100亿，以及一些地区农业产量需要几乎翻倍以保持同步的预测，粮食安全问题正日益受到关注。

items.en: In the UK, it has become a big talking point recently too, for a rather particular reason: Brexit.
items.zh: 在英国，最近这也成为了一个热门话题，原因相当特殊：脱欧。

items.en: The country produces only about 60 per cent of the food it eats, down from almost three-quarters in the late 1980s.
items.zh: 该国仅生产其消耗食物的约百分之六十，较 1980年代末期的几乎四分之三有所下降。

items.en: A move back to self-sufficiency ， the argument goes, would boost the farming industry, political sovereignty and even the nation’s health.
items.zh: 向自给自足的回归，论点认为，会提升农业产业、政治主权和甚至国家的健康。

items.en: Sounds great — but how feasible is this vision?
items.zh: 听起来不错——但这个愿景有多可行？

items.en: 85 per cent of the country’s total land area is associated with meat and dairy production.
items.zh: 该国百分之八十五的国土面积关联于肉类和乳制品生产。

items.en: That supplies 80 per cent of what is consumed, so even covering the whole country in livestock farms wouldn’t allow us to cover all our meat and dairy needs.
items.zh: 这供应了 80%的消费量，因此即使将整个国家都覆盖成畜牧场也无法满足我们所有的肉类和乳制品需求。

items.en: There are many caveats to those figures, but they are still grave.
items.zh: 这些数据有许多注意事项，但它们仍然非常严重。

items.en: To become much more self-sufficient, the UK would need to drastically reduce its consumption of animal foods, and probably also farm more intensively — meaning fewer green fields and more factory-style production.
items.zh: 要变得更加自给自足，英国需要大幅减少动物食品的消费，1 可能也需要更集约化地耕种——这意味着更少的绿色田野和更多的工厂化生产。

items.en: But switching to a mainly plant-based diet wouldn’t help.
items.zh: 但转向以植物为主的饮食并无帮助。

items.en: There is a good reason why the UK is dominated by animal husbandry: most of its terrain doesn’t have the right soil or climate to grow crops on a commercial basis.
items.zh: 英国之所以以畜牧业为主，是有充分理由的：其大部分地形缺乏适合商业种植作物的土壤和气候。

items.en: Just 25 per cent of the country’s land is suitable for crop-growing, most of which is already occupied by arable fields.
items.zh: 仅有 25%的国土适合种植作物，其中大部分已被可耕地占据。

items.en: Even if we converted all the suitable land to fields of fruit and veg — which would involve taking out all the nature reserves and removing thousands of people from their homes — we would achieve only a 30 per cent boost in crop production.
items.zh: 即使我们将所有适合的土地都改造成水果和蔬菜种植区——这将涉及清除所有自然保护区并迫使成千上万的人离开家园——我们也只能实现作物产量 30 的提升。

items.en: Just 23 per cent of the fruit and vegetables consumed in the UK are currently home-grown, so even with the most extreme measures we could meet only 30 per cent of our fresh produce needs.
items.zh: 目前英国消费的水果和蔬菜中只有 23 是本地种植的，因此即使采取最极端的措施，我们也只能满足 30 的新鲜农产品需求。

items.en: That is before we look for the space to grow the grains, sugars, seeds and oils that provide us with the vast bulk of our current calorie intake.
items.zh: 这在我们寻找种植谷物、糖类、种子和油脂的空间之前，这些物质为我们当前大部分热量摄入提供来源。

items.en: When Microsoft bought task management app Wunderlist and mobile calendar Sunrise in 2015,it picked two newcomers that were attracting considerable buzz in Silicon Valley.
items.zh: 当微软于 2015年收购任务管理应用Wunderlist和移动日历应用Sunrise时，它选择了两家当时正引起硅谷相当大关注的新晋公司。

items.en: Microsoft’s own Office dominates the market for “productivity” software, but the start-ups represented a new wave of technology designed from the ground up for the smartphone world.
items.zh: 微软自家的Office在“生产力”软件市场占据主导地位，但这些初创公司代表了专为智能手机世界从头设计的新一轮技术。

items.en: Both apps, however, were later scrapped, after Microsoft said it had used their best features in its own products.
items.zh: 然而，这两款应用后来都被取消，微软表示已将其最佳功能整合到自家产品中。

items.en: Their teams of engineers stayed on, making them two of the many “ acqui-hires”that the biggest companies have used to feed their great hunger for tech talent.
items.zh: 他们的工程师团队继续留任，使他们成为众多"acqui-hires"中的两家，这是最大的公司用来满足他们对科技人才的巨大需求的方式。

items.en: To Microsoft’s critics, the fates of Wunderlist and Sunrise are examples of a remorseless drive by Big Tech to chew up any innovative companies that lie in their path.
items.zh: 对微软的批评者而言，Wunderlist和Sunrise的命运是大科技公司无情扩张过程中吞并任何挡路创新企业的典型案例。

items.en: “They bought the seedlings and closed them down,” complained Paul Arnold, a partner at San Francisco-based Switch Ventures, putting an end to businesses that might one day turn into competitors.
items.zh: 他们收购了这些幼苗并将其关闭，1总部位于旧金山的Switch Ventures合伙人保罗·阿诺德抱怨道，此举终结了可能未来成为竞争对手的企业。

items.en: Microsoft declined to comment.
items.zh: 微软拒绝评论。

items.en: Like other start-up investors, Mr. Arnold’s own business often depends on selling start-ups to larger tech companies, though he admits to mixed feelings about the result: “I think these things are good for me, if I put my selfish hat on.
items.zh: 与其他初创企业投资者一样，阿诺德先生自己的业务通常依赖于将初创企业出售给更大的科技公司，尽管他承认对结果感到矛盾：如果从自私的角度来看，我认为这些事对我有好处。

items.en: But are they good for the American economy?
items.zh: 但它们对美国经济有好处吗？

items.en: I don’t know.
items.zh: 我不知道。

items.en: The US Federal Trade Commission says it wants to find the answer to that question.
items.zh: 美国联邦贸易委员会表示它想要找到这个问题的答案。

items.en: This week, it asked the five most valuable US tech companies for information about their many small acquisitions over the past decade.
items.zh: 本周，它要求美国五大最有价值的科技公司提供过去十年中他们众多小型收购的相关信息。

items.en: Although only a research project at this stage, the request has raised the prospect of regulators wading into early-stage tech markets that until now have been beyond their reach.
items.zh: 尽管目前只是一个研究项目，该请求引发了监管机构介入早期科技市场的前景，这些市场迄今为止一直超出他们的掌控范围。

items.en: Given their combined market value of more than $5.5 trillion, rifling through such small deals—many of them much less prominent than Wunderlist and Sunrise—might seem beside the point.
items.zh: 鉴于它们合计市值超过 5.5万亿美元，翻找这些小交易——其中许多都不如Wunderlist和Sunrise知名——似乎有些偏离重点。

items.en: Between them, the five biggest tech companies have spent an average of only $3.4 billion a year on sub- $ 1 billion acquisitions over the past five years—a drop in the ocean compared with their massive financial reserves, and the more than $130 billion of venture capital that was invested in the US last year.
items.zh: 在它们之间，五大科技公司过去五年平均每年仅花费 34亿美元用于低于 10亿美元的收购——与它们庞大的财务储备相比，这不过是九牛一毛，而去年在美国投入的风险投资就超过了 1300亿美元。

items.en: We’re fairly good at judging people based on first impressions, thin slices of experience ranging from a glimpse of a photo to five-minute interaction, and deliberation can be not only extraneous but intrusive.
items.zh: 我们相当擅长基于第一印象来评判他人，这些短暂经验片段从瞥见一张照片到五分钟的互动不等，而深思熟虑不仅可能是多余的，甚至可能带有侵入性。

items.en: In one study of the ability she called“thin slicing,” the late psychologist Nalini Ambady asked participants to watch silent 10-second video clips of professors and to rate the instructor’s overall effectiveness.
items.zh: 在一项关于她所称的“薄切片”能力的研究中，已故心理学家纳莉妮·安巴迪要求参与者观看教授的无声 10秒视频片段，并评价该讲师的整体教学效果。

items.en: Their ratings correlated strongly with students’ end-of-semester ratings.
items.zh: 他们的评分与学生期末评分高度相关。

items.en: Another set of participants had to count backward from 1,000 by nines as they watched the clips, occupying their conscious working memory.
items.zh: 另一组参与者必须从 1000开始以九为单位倒数，当他们观看这些片段时，占据他们的意识工作记忆。

items.en: Their ratings were just as accurate, demonstrating the intuitive nature of the social processing.
items.zh: 他们的评分同样准确，证明了社会处理的直觉性。

items.en: Critically, another group was asked to spend a minute writing down reasons for their judgment, before giving the rating.
items.zh: 关键的是，另一组人被要求花一分钟写下他们判断的理由，然后给出评分。

items.en: Accuracy dropped dramatically.
items.zh: 准确性急剧下降。

items.en: Ambady suspected that deliberation focused them on vivid but misleading cues, such as certain gestures or utterances, rather than letting the complex interplay of subtle signals form a holistic impression.
items.zh: Ambady怀疑深思熟虑使他们关注生动但具有误导性的线索，比如某些手势或言语，而不是让微妙信号的复杂互动形成整体印象。

items.en: She found similar interference when participants watched 15-second clips of pairs of people and judged whether they were strangers, friends, or dating partners.
items.zh: 她发现当参与者观看 15秒的两人片段并判断他们是否是陌生人、朋友或恋爱伴侣时，出现了类似的干扰。

items.en: But if you go on automatic pilot, you’re fine.
items.zh: 但如果你进入自动驾驶状态，你就会没事。

items.en: Much of our social life is like that.
items.zh: 我们的社会生活大多如此。

items.en: Thinking too much can also harm our ability to form preferences.
items.zh: 过度思考也会损害我们形成偏好的能力。

items.en: College students’ ratings of strawberry jams and college courses aligned better with experts’ opinions when the students weren’t asked to analyze their rationale.
items.zh: 当学生未被要求分析其理由时，大学生对草莓果酱和大学课程的评分更符合专家意见。

items.en: And people made car-buying decisions that were both objectively better and more personally satisfying when asked to focus on their feelings rather than on details, but only if the decision was complex—when they had a lot of information to process.
items.zh: 人们在买车时做出的决定既客观上更好又更令人满意，当被要求关注感受而非细节时，但仅当这个决定是复杂的——当他们需要处理大量信息时。

items.en: Intuition’s special powers are unleashed only in certain circumstances.
items.zh: 直觉的特殊能力只有在特定情况下才会被释放。

items.en: In one study, participants completed a battery of eight tasks, including four that tapped reflective thinking (discerning rules, comprehending vocabulary) and four that tapped intuition and creativity (generating new products or figures of speech).
items.zh: 在一项研究中，参与者完成了一组八个任务，包括四个涉及反思性思维（辨别规则、理解词汇）的任务和四个涉及直觉与创造力（生成新产品或修辞手法）的任务。

items.en: Then they rated the degree to which they had used intuition (“gut feelings,” “ hunches,” “my heart”).
items.zh: 然后他们对自己使用直觉的程度进行了评分（“直觉感受”，“预感”，“我的内心”）。

items.en: Use of their gut hurt their performance on the first four tasks, as expected, and helped them on the rest.
items.zh: 他们依赖直觉在前四个任务中表现受损，正如预期的那样，却在其余任务中得到了帮助。

items.en: Maybe you haven’t finished thinking the problem through, or you want to get a clearer sense of what the group thinks.
items.zh: 也许你还没有彻底思考这个问题，或者你想更清楚地了解这个群体的想法。

items.en: If you think other people are going to disagree, too, you might want to gather your army first.
items.zh: 如果你认为其他人也会不同意，你可能需要先召集你的支持者。

items.en: Before you share your thoughts, think about what the powerful person cares about—it may be the credibility of their team or getting a project done on time.
items.zh: 在分享你的想法之前，先考虑权势者关心什么——可能是他们团队的可信度或按时完成项目。

items.en: You’re more likely to be heard if you can connect your disagreement to a higher purpose.
items.zh: 如果你能将你的不同意见与更高的目标联系起来，你更有可能被倾听。

items.en: You can say something like, “I know we seem to be moving toward a first-quarter commitment here.
items.zh: 你可以这样说：我知道我们似乎正在朝着第一季度的承诺迈进。

items.en: I have reasons to think that won’t work.
items.zh: 我有理由认为那不会奏效。

items.en: I’d like to lay out my reasoning.
items.zh: 我想说明我的理由。

items.en: When your body language communicates reluctance or anxiety, it undercuts the message.
items.zh: 当你肢体语言传达出不情愿或焦虑时，它会削弱所传递的信息。

items.en: It sends a mixed message, and your counterpart gets to choose what signals to read.
items.zh: 它传递了矛盾的信息，而你的对话者可以选择接收哪些信号。

items.en: Deep breaths can help, as can speaking more slowly and deliberately.
items.zh: 深呼吸可以帮助，同样可以放慢并谨慎地说话。

items.en: Emphasize that you’re only offering your opinion, not gospel truth.
items.zh: 强调你只是在提供自己的观点，而不是绝对真理。

items.en: It may be a well-informed, well-researched opinion, but it’s still an opinion, so talk tentatively and slightly understate your confidence.

items.zh: 博物馆参观者在原件之后仍能从文物复制品中学到同样多的知识。

items.en: Reproductions, even if perfectly made, cannot take the place of the authentic object.
items.zh: 复制品，即使制作得 1 完美，也无法替代真品。

items.en: The real value of artifacts can only be recognized in their countries of origin rather than anywhere else.
items.zh: 文物的真实价值只能在其原产国 1 被认可而非其他任何地方

items.en: Ways to get artifacts from other countries must be decent and lawful.
items.zh: 从其他国家获取文物的方式必须正当且合法。

items.en: Concern over security is no excuse for refusing to return artifacts to their countries of origin.
items.zh: 对安全的担忧不能成为拒绝归还文物给原属国家的借口。

items.en: The first and more important is the consumer's growing preference for eating out: the consumption of food and drink in places other than homes has risen from about 32 percent of total consumption in 1995 to 35 percent in 2000 and is expected to approach 38 percent by 2005.
items.zh: 第一个且更为重要的是消费者日益增长的外出就餐偏好：在家庭以外场所的食品饮料消费占比已从 1995年的约 32%上升至 2000年的 35%，预计到 2005年将达到 38%。

items.en: Retail sales of food and drink in Europe's largest markets are at a standstill, leaving European grocery retailers hungry for opportunities to grow.
items.zh: 欧洲最大市场的食品饮料零售销售陷入停滞，使得欧洲杂货零售商渴望寻找增长机会。

items.en: Will such variations bring about a change in the overall structure of the food and drink market?
items.zh: 这些变化会导致食品和饮料市场的整体结构发生改变吗？

items.en: All in all, this clearly seems to be a market in which big retailers could profitably apply their gigantic scale, existing infrastructure, and proven skills in the management of product ranges, logistics, and marketing intelligence.
items.zh: 总体而言，这显然属于一个大型零售商可以有利可图地利用其巨大规模、现有基础设施以及在商品组合、物流和营销情报管理方面成熟技能的市场。

items.en: Despite variations in detail, wholesale markets in the countries that have been closely examined - France, Germany, Italy and Spain - are made out of the same building blocks.
items.zh: 尽管在细节上存在差异，被仔细研究的国家的批发市场 - 法国、德国、意大利和西班牙 - 都由相同的基本组成部分构成。

items.en: For example, wholesale food and drink sales came to $268 billion in France, Germany, Italy, Spain, and the United Kingdom in 2000 - more than 40 percent of retail sales.
items.zh: 例如，2000年法国、德国、意大利、西班牙和英国的食品和饮料批发销售额达到 2680亿美元，超过零售销售的 40%。

items.en: However, none of these requirements should deter large retailers (and even some large food producers and existing wholesalers) from trying their hand, for those that master the intricacies of wholesaling in Europe stand to reap considerable gains.
items.zh: 然而，这些要求不应阻止大型零售商（甚至一些大型食品生产商和现有批发商）尝试涉足，因为那些掌握欧洲批发业务复杂之处的企业有望获得可观收益。

items.en: No disciplines have seized on professionalism with as much enthusiasm as the humanities.
items.zh: 没有哪个学科像人文学科那样热衷于职业化。

items.en: His concern is mainly with the humanities: literature, languages, philosophy and so on.
items.zh: 他的关注主要集中在人文学科：文学、语言、哲学等。

items.en: Equally unsurprisingly, only about half end up with professorships for which they entered graduate school.
items.zh: 同样不出人意料的是，只有大约一半的人最终获得了他们进入研究生院时所追求的教授职位。

items.en: One reason why it is hard to design and teach such courses is that they cut across the insistence by top American universities that liberal-arts education and professional education should be kept separate, taught in different schools.
items.zh: 设计和教授此类课程之所以困难的一个原因是，它们与顶尖美国大学坚持文理教育与专业教育应当保持分离、在不同学院教授的做法相冲突。

items.en: Besides professionalising the professions by this separation, top American universities have professionalised the professor.
items.zh: 除了通过这种分离使专业领域更加专业化外，顶尖美国大学还使教授这一职业更加专业化。

items.en: The key to reforming higher education, concludes Mr. Menand, is to alter the way in which "the producers of knowledge are produced".
items.zh: 门兰先生得出结论，改革高等教育的关键在于改变「知识生产者被生产」的方式。

items.en: The subtle and intelligent little book The Marketplace of Ideas: Reform and Resistance in the American University should be read by every student thinking of applying to take a doctoral degree.
items.zh: 精妙而睿智的小书《The Marketplace of Ideas: Reform and Resistance in the American University》应被每一位打算申请攻读博士学位的学生阅读。

items.zh: 应向快餐生产商如McDonald’s等征收肥胖税。

items.en: the government should strengthen the sense of responsibility among businesses.
items.zh: 政府应在企业中加强责任感。

items.en: Of course, it is precisely these superfluous things that define human culture and ultimately what it is to be human.
items.zh: 当然，正是这些多余的事物定义了人类文化，最终也定义了人类的本质。

items.en: Applications like tumblr.com, which allow users to combine pictures, words and other media in creative ways and then share them, have the potential to add stickiness by amusing, entertaining and enlightening others.
items.zh: 像tumblr.com这样的应用，允许用户以创意方式结合图片、文字和其他媒体并分享，有可能通过娱乐、逗乐和启发他人来增加粘性。

items.en: Not only did they develop such a device but by the turn of the millennium they had also managed to embed it in a worldwide system accessed by billions of people every day.
items.zh: 他们不仅开发了这种设备，而且在 21世纪初已经成功将其嵌入到一个每天被数十亿人访问的全球系统中。

items.en: This is because the networked computer has sparked a secret war between downloading and uploading - between passive consumption and active creation - whose outcome will shape our collective future in ways we can only begin to imagine.
items.zh: 这是因为联网计算机引发了一场秘密战争——在下载与上传之间——在被动消费与主动创造之间——这场战争的结果将以我们只能开始想象的方式塑造我们的集体未来。

items.en: The challenge the computer mounts to television thus bears little similarity to one format being replaced by another in the manner of record players being replaced by CD players.
items.zh: 因此，计算机对电视构成的挑战与一种格式被另一种格式取代的情况 1 留声机被CD播放器取代几乎没有相似之处。

items.en: One reason for the persistence of this pyramid of production is that for the past half-century, much of the world's media culture has been defined by a single medium - television - and television is defined by downloading.
items.zh: 这种生产金字塔之所以持续存在，其中一个原因是过去半个世纪以来，世界大部分媒体文化一直由单一媒介——电视——所定义，而电视则被下载所定义。

items.en: The networked computer offers the first chance in 50 years to reverse the flow, to encourage thoughtful downloading and, even more importantly, meaningful uploading.
items.zh: 联网计算机提供了 50年来首次逆转趋势的机会，鼓励深思熟虑的下载，甚至更重要的是有意义的上传。

items.en: emphasized the virtue of classical heroes.
items.zh: 强调古典英雄的美德。

items.en: depicted the worthy lives of engineers, industrialists and explorers.
items.zh: 描绘了工程师、工业家和探险家的值得尊敬的生活。

items.en: The idea is to force social scientists to integrate their work with other categories, including health and demographic change; food security; marine research and the bio-economy; clean, efficient energy; and inclusive, innovative and secure societies.
items.zh: 这个想法是要迫使社会科学家将他们的工作与其他领域整合，包括健康和人口变化；粮食安全；海洋研究和生物经济；清洁高效的能源；以及包容、创新和安全的社会。

items.en: The solution is to change the mindset of the academic community, and what it considers to be its main goal.
items.zh: 解决方案是改变学术界的心态，以及它所认为的 1 主要目标。

items.en: It could be that we are evolving two communities of social scientists: one that is discipline-oriented and publishing in highly specialized journals, and one that is problem-oriented and publishing elsewhere, such as policy briefs.
items.zh: 我们可能正在形成两个社会科学家群体：一个是学科导向并发表于高度专业化的期刊，另一个是问题导向并发表于其他地方，例如政策简报。

items.en: However, the numbers are still small: in 2010, about 1,600 of the 100,000 social-sciences papers published globally included one of these keywords.
items.zh: 然而，数量仍然很小：2010年，全球发表的 10万篇社会科学论文中约有 1600篇包含这些关键词中的一个。

items.en: These issues all have root causes in human behavior: all require behavioral change and social innovations, as well as technological development.
items.zh: 这些问题的根本原因都在于人类行为：都需要行为改变和社会创新，以及技术发展。

items.en: Despite these factors, many social scientists seem reluctant to tackle such problems.
items.zh: 尽管存在这些因素，许多社会科学家似乎不愿解决此类问题。

items.en: During the late 1990s, national spending on social sciences and the humanities as a percentage of all research and development funds - including government, higher education, non-profit and corporate - varied from around 4% to 25%; in most European nations, it is about 15%.
items.zh: 在 1990年代末，国家在社会科学和人文学科上的支出占所有研发资金（包括政府、高等教育、非营利和企业部门）的百分比 4% 到 25% 不等；在大多数欧洲国家，这一比例约为 15%。

items.en: Some archaeological sites have always been easily observable - for example, the Parthenon in Athens, Greece; the pyramids of Giza in Egypt; and the megaliths of Stonehenge in southern England.
items.zh: 一些考古遗址一直易于观察——例如，希腊雅典的帕特农神庙；埃及吉萨的金字塔；以及英国南部巨石阵的巨石群。

items.en: In another case, American archaeologists René Millon and George Cowgill spent years systematically mapping the entire city of Teotihuacan in the Valley of Mexico near what is now Mexico City.
items.zh: 在另一个案例中，美国考古学家René Millon和George Cowgill花费多年时间系统性地绘制整个特奥蒂瓦坎城的地图，地点位于墨西哥谷，靠近如今的墨西哥城。

items.en: How do archaeologists know where to find what they are looking for when there is nothing visible on the surface of the ground?
items.zh: 考古学家如何知道在地表没有任何可见物的情况下，该在哪里寻找他们要找的东西？

items.en: Surveys can cover a single large settlement or entire landscapes.
items.zh: 调查可以涵盖一个大型定居点或整个景观。

items.en: To find their sites, archaeologists today rely heavily on systematic survey methods and a variety of high-technology tools and techniques.
items.zh: 今天，考古学家严重依赖系统性调查方法和各种高科技工具与技术。

items.en: Most archaeological sites, however, are discovered by archaeologists who have set out to look for them.
items.zh: 然而，大多数考古遗址都是由考古学家发现的，这些考古学家是专门寻找它们的。

items.en: Ground surveys allow archaeologists to pinpoint the places where digs will be successful.

items.en: Factors such as the place and period in which we are reading, our gender, ethnicity, age and social class will encourage us towards certain interpretations but at the same time obscure or even close off others.

items.en: If you are unfamiliar with words or idioms, you guess at their meaning, using clues presented in the context.
items.zh: 如果你对某些词语或习语不熟悉，就根据上下文中的线索来猜测它们的含义。

items.en: In effect, you try to reconstruct the likely meanings or effects that any given sentence, image or reference might have had: These might be the ones the author intended.
items.zh: 实际上，你试图重建任何给定句子、图像或参考可能产生的含义或影响：这些可能是作者意图的那些。

items.en: You make further inferences, for instance, about how the text may be significant to you, or about its validity - inferences that form the basis of a personal response for which the author will inevitably be far less responsible.
items.zh: 你做出进一步的推论，例如，关于文本对你可能有何意义，或关于其有效性——这些推论构成了个人回应的基础，而作者对此必然远不那么负责。

items.en: In plays, novels and narrative poems, characters speak as constructs created by the author, not necessarily as mouthpieces for the author's own thoughts.
items.zh: 在戏剧、小说和叙事诗中，角色作为作者构建的产物而发言，而非必然作为作者自身思想的代言人。

items.en: Rather, we ascribe meanings to texts on the basis of interaction between what we might call textual and contextual material: between kinds of organization or patterning we perceive in a text's formal structures (so especially its language structures) and various kinds of background, social knowledge, belief and attitude that we bring to the text.
items.zh: 相反，我们基于文本内容与上下文信息之间的互动来赋予文本意义，即我们感知到的文本形式结构（尤其是其语言结构）中的组织形式或结构模式，以及我们带入文本的各种背景知识、社会常识、信念和态度之间的互动。

items.en: The first published sketch, "A Dinner at Poplar Walk" brought tears to Dickens's eyes when he discovered it in the pages of The Monthly Magazine.

items.en: Soon after Sketches by Boz appeared, a publishing firm approached Dickens to write a story in monthly installments, as a backdrop for a series of woodcuts by the then-famous artist Robert Seymour, who had originated the idea for the story.

items.en: Charles Dickens is probably the best-known and, to many people, the greatest English novelist of the 19th century.
items.zh: 查尔斯·狄更斯可能是最著名的，并且对许多人来说是 19世纪最伟大的英国小说家。

items.en: Soon after his father's release from prison, Dickens got a better job as errand boy in law offices.

items.en: Dickens was born in Portsmouth, on England's southern coast.

items.en: After Pickwick, Dickens plunged into a bleaker world.
items.zh: 《匹克威克外传》之后，狄更斯陷入了更阴暗的世界。

items.en: In December of 1869, Congress appointed a commission to select a site and prepare plans and cost estimates for a new State Department Building.
items.zh: 1869年 12月，国会任命了一个委员会负责为新的国务院大楼选择地点并制定规划和成本估算。

items.en: Completed in 1875, the State Department's south wing was the first to be occupied, with its elegant four-story library (completed in 1876), Diplomatic Reception Room, and Secretary's office decorated with carved wood, Oriental rugs, and stenciled wall patterns.
items.zh: 1875年完工的国务院南翼大楼是第一个被占用的，其优雅的四层图书馆（1876年完工）、外交接待室和国务卿办公室装饰有雕刻木制品、东方地毯和带有图案的墙纸。

items.en: The State, War, and Navy Building, as it was originally known, housed the three Executive Branch Departments most intimately associated with formulating and conducting the nation's foreign policy in the last quarter of the nineteenth century and the first quarter of the twentieth century - the period when the United States emerged as an international power.
items.zh: 原名"State, War, and Navy Building"的建筑容纳了十九世纪最后四分之一和二十世纪最初四分之一时期最密切相关的三个行政部门，这些部门负责制定和执行国家的外交政策——这一时期美国成为国际强国。

items.en: Many of the most celebrated national figures have participated in historical events that have taken place within the EEOB's granite walls.

items.en: The Eisenhower Executive Office Building (EEOB) commands a unique position in both the national history and the architectural heritage of the United States.

items.en: Construction took 17 years as the building slowly rose wing by wing.

items.en: The history of the EEOB began long before its foundations were laid.
